  both throw a two-ring SHOCKWAVE (16 units, 0.35 s) and break the bar into 28 pieces, with a +10% thump and a max
  shake. The overshield's are yellow.
- **Overshield** is drawn as a tail after the fill, the bar scaled against `max(max, current + overshield)`. It moves
  on a spring with the **same frequency and damping as the reading**, which keeps the fill's end plus the tail's
  length exactly constant while a grant or a loss rescales the bar (the system is linear, so the sum moves only if
  its target moves). A grant pushes the yellow in from the end. Before that the tail snapped, which made the bar
  jump. While a rescale runs, the memory copies the reading, so no white chip band opens as if it were a hit. A
  hit on the overshield whitens the tail and drops yellow chunks. A grant tops up to its amount and does not stack
  (`GrantOvershield`); the bench copies that.
- **A max going down** rescales the same way, with no gesture.

### The raise (the max going up)

BeACastleLord's `CoreHealthUI.Raise`, in pixel units. The server raises the max and then heals by the same amount
(`CharacterService` on `OnPassiveStatChanged`), so a full bar goes from full to full and nothing visibly happened
until this was added.

1. **Charge**, 0.12 s: the bar pulls in 4% and its outline walks toward a green-white.
2. **Sweep**, 0.5 s: the value AND the max are walked by **one share** from what the bar showed to the truth, so
   `(v0 + dv*s) / (m0 + dm*s)` only ever moves from the old share to the new one. A full bar stays full the whole
   way, a hurt one climbs. Checked offline: 100/100 to 120/120 reads 1.000 at every step, and 50/100 to 70/120 only
   rises. Re-basing first and filling after is what slides the fill BACKWARDS on the one event that made it
   bigger. The value is read live, so the heal can land a frame or two after the max (it does, over the network).
   A stepped comet (a two-unit head and three fading trail steps) crosses the whole track with green behind it, on
   a curve already moving on its first frame that pulls into the landing (`pull`). The bar trembles harder as the
   light goes.
3. **Strike** on the frame the numbers arrive: flash, +9% throw, a jolt, two pixel rings off the bar (the second
   smaller and 0.07 s behind, so they read as two), and a green "+N" sliding out past the bar's right end with an
   overshoot, held 1.5 s, then lifted away. Two raises inside one roll show their sum.
4. **A bar raised from a max of 0** (the first Shield pick) would be full on the sweep's first frame, because value
   and max start together at 0. Its fill follows the light instead.

**What triggers it**: any `SetMax` above the current max, except the bar's first call (which lands at once and opens
the bar full) and calls with `instant`. The controllers create each bar once and only change the max through
`OnPassiveStatChanged`, which is the upgrade. If a run reset strips passives and the next run re-adds them, that will
play as a raise; watch for it in a playtest.

**The first `SetMax` opens the bar full.** The controllers spawn the player at max but skip `SetHealth` /
`SetShield` when the value did not change, so a max that moved before the bar existed left the old bar on its
default 100 (100/120). The new bar seeds its value to its first max.

### The bench

`Stories/Vitals` is a generic UI Labs story (render + subscribe; UI Labs has no Fluid mode). It puts `scaleNumber`
into canvas mode at the widget's height while it builds, because in edit mode the camera viewport is the 3D view and
has nothing to do with the widget, and it rebuilds on resize. Each "Do:" switch is one flip, one event, fired by
comparing against the last value: graze, heavy hit, break the shield, regen tick, big heal, refill shield, grant /
hit / break the overshield, upgrade max health / shield, drop to low, reset. The fake fight is off by default, so
an event can be watched alone. `Fight: time scale` slows everything.

### What was tried and lost, and why

| Look | What it was | Why it lost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cells | Bar split into cells; a hit knocks the lost cells off as falling blocks | Not picked; busier than a solid fill at a glance |
| Arcade (HitStop + Hold) | Everything froze white for 60 to 140 ms, then knocked down; orange band stood 0.45 s and drained at a fixed rate | Not picked |
| Neon on health | | Read as a shield; it went on the shield instead |
| Gradient sheen | 45-degree UIGradient on a square | Cut off by a vertical edge (see above) |

### Checked, and how

Linted (StyLua, Selene), compiled with `lune`, place built with Rojo, spring peaks and the raise roll simulated with
`lune`, the sheen rendered as ASCII. **Not played in Studio** by the agent that built it: the user judged it on the
bench.

## Last Wave: carrying the vitals look to the rest of the UI

The vitals are the reference for every Last Wave screen from here on, the way BeACastleLord's skill tree was for its
cut face. This is the recipe, pulled out of `vitalBar.luau` and the five rounds of feedback it took. **Read the vitals
section above first**; this one says what to copy and what to decide per element.

### The look in one paragraph

Pixel-hard and modern at once. Every shape is axis-aligned Frames snapped to one pixel unit, with an ink outline,
a lit top row and a shaded bottom row, and no UICorner, no gradient and no uploaded art. Light is STEPPED: glows
are three stacked solid rings at falling opacity, a sheen is a staircase, particles are unrotated squares that blink
out. Motion is modern: springs that are shoved, not tweened, a quick reading and a slow memory, punches measured to a
percentage, hard-position shakes, flashes that decay. Numbers are Silkscreen bold with a miter ink outline. Two
surfaces exist: **Slab** (solid, inked, a hard drop shadow; things you have) and **Neon** (lit outline, dark well,
glow that follows the content, scanlines; energy and shields). Pick per element; the user picked per bar.

### What to copy, and from where

| Piece | Where it is in `vitalBar.luau` | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pixel unit | `layout`: `p = round(scaleNumber(PixelSize, "y"))`, capped at a sixth of the element's height | Every offset and size is a multiple of `p`. Default 3 design px. |
| Slab frame | `outline` (ink, 1 p) > `well` (trough, a darker top row) + `shadow` (ink at 0.45, offset p, p) | Contents get a light top row and a shade bottom row, each 1 p. |
| Neon frame | `outline` in the colour's Light, `NEON_TROUGH` well, `neonRings` off the content, `scanlines` (1/3 p every 2 p, 0.78) | The glow hangs off what is FILLED, not the box. |
| Stepped glow | `ring()` x3, each 1 p bigger, transparency 0.35 / 0.6 / 0.8 (alarm) or 0.62 / 0.8 / 0.9 (neon) | First ring under an opaque outline is wasted: start rings outside it. |
| Sheen | `sheenRows`: one Frame per p-row, each p left of the one above, 3 p wide, 0.3 | Clip it to what it shines on (`ClipsDescendants` on the fill). Never a turned gradient. |
| Particles | `pixelFx.Particles` (shared pool) | Squares of p or 2 p in the element's own colours plus white. **Go through "Particles: the checklist" below for every spawn**: born outside the outermost glow, moving away, light gravity, smooth fade in and out. |
| Rings thrown off | `throwRings`: four 1 p edges growing out and fading | For a strike, a break, a reward. One ring in this game. |
| Clock | `pixelMotion.Wake` / `Sleep` (lifted out of `vitalBar` when the upgrade card needed it): one module `PreRender` connection, alive only while something moves; `pixelMotion.TimeScale` | Each element's `tick` returns whether it is still busy. |
| Springs | `pixelMotion.Spring`, `Step` (1/240 substeps), `Pop` (non-stacking shove), `Snap`, `Decay` | Per-event reactions use `Pop`, never `+=`. **The spring's value IS the scale added** (`1 + thump.X`): do not multiply it down again. |

**When the SECOND element needs these, lift them into shared modules** (a pixel kit and a clock) instead of copying;
until then they stay inside `vitalBar`. Do not build the kit ahead of the element that needs it: that is how the retro
round ended up with a kit and no element anyone wanted.

### Particles: the checklist (every element so far got this wrong on its first try)

The upgrade cards, the reward cards and the XP bar all shipped their first round with particles that vanished and came
back, or popped out of existence, and the user had to report it each time. A particle is only right when ALL of these
hold. Go through them for every `Spawn` call before calling an element done; do not rely on remembering lesson 9.

1. **It crosses ONE background for its whole life.** A light mote over a light bezel or a lit glow ring is invisible,
   and the same mote over the dark well shows again, so a particle that crosses outline, bezel, glow rings and well
   blinks on and off however smoothly it fades. Work out every layer the element draws (outline, bezel, well, EVERY
   glow ring at its largest, shafts, rims) and find its outermost edge on the side the particle leaves from.
2. **It is born a unit OUTSIDE that edge** (`aboveGlow` in `levelBar`, `pixelFx.OnEdge` plus the glow's reach on the
   cards), not on the border, not inside the well. The only exception is a particle the design pulls INTO the thing
   (the Secret void's light), which still fades smoothly.
3. **It moves AWAY and never comes back.** Gravity pulls a thrown piece back down through the element it left: the
   XP bar's first confetti (gravity 240) fell 44 units back through the bar. Use light gravity under drag (the bar:
   gravity 40 to 60 units/s^2, drag 1.6 to 3) so the piece slows and hangs where it is.
4. **It fades smoothly, in AND out** (`isSteady = true` on `pixelFx.Spawn`: in over the first 15%, out over the last
   30%). A blink, or a fade in two steps, reads as flicker. Blinking is left only on the old fast debris that was
   already there (below); new particles are steady.
5. **It lives long enough to be seen**: a fast spark under 0.3 s is gone before the eye finds it. 0.35 s is the
   floor for a spark, 0.5 s for confetti, 0.6 s for a drifting mote.
6. **It is born where the element IS this frame.** A swell, a lift or a shake moves the element; particles parented
   outside it (so they do not shake with it) must compute their birth from its current top (`barTop()` in `levelBar`).
7. **Check it with numbers, not by eye.** Paste the particle's step out of `pixelFx` into a `lune` script and run the
   WORST case: the slowest launch, the strongest gravity, the longest life. Print the furthest it gets back toward the
   element over its life; it must stay outside the edge from step 1. That is how the 44 units were found.
8. **A puff thrown as something disappears** (a card or button leaving) is the one case that may start at the centre:
   the body is hidden on that frame, so there is nothing left to cross. It should still fade smoothly.

**Known to break this list, not fixed yet** (found while writing it, 2026-10-30; fix them when the user asks or the
element is next touched, and check against every point):

| Where | What is wrong |
| --- | --- |
| `rewardCard` `burst` (flip, pick) | Born ON the edge (`OnEdge` with no push outward), so it starts on the bezel inside the glow; blinks (`isSteady = false`) |
| `rewardCard` and `upgradeCard` `puff` (leaving) | Blinks, and lives only 0.25 to 0.45 s |
| `upgradeCard` landing / pick bursts | Not checked; same shape as `rewardCard`'s burst |
| `actionButton` release burst and puff | Not checked |
| `vitalBar` hit chunks and break pieces | Born inside the bar, fall at gravity 230 and blink: built as falling debris before this rule |

Only the drifting motes on both cards (`sparkle`, `pixelFx`) and everything on `levelBar` pass it today.

### Text rules

1. **Silkscreen bold** (`UITools.FONT_SILKSCREEN_BOLD`) for numbers. Words: open (see the Press Start recipe above).
2. **`TextSize`, never `TextScaled`**, worked out from the box: about 0.7 of the element's height, then CAPPED to fit
   inside its inner area with half a pixel unit (at least 1 px) of air above and below. Silkscreen's capitals are
   ~half the TextSize and its ink (letters plus outline) ~0.77 of it.
3. **Outline: a miter `UIStroke` in ink, 0.1 of the TextSize, at least 1 px, NOT rounded.** A share of the letters,
   never of the pixel unit, or small text gets a heavier outline than big text.
4. **Raise Silkscreen by 0.075 of its TextSize**: it sits low in its line box.
5. **Check every size on the smallest instance.** The shield bar broke every text rule first; health never did.

### Motion vocabulary (measured, keep these numbers)

| Gesture | Use for | Numbers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reading + memory | Any value that changes (a bar, a counter's fill) | Quick 4.1 Hz / 0.72; slow 1.1 Hz / 1.0; memory shoved back 2.2 per share lost |
| Flash | The frame something is hit or lands | White at 0.75, decays 14/s |
| Punch | A number that changed | 3.6 Hz / 0.32; pop 8 = +22% (a loss), 3.6 = +10% (a gain) |
| Thump | The whole element on a big moment | 2.9 Hz / 0.4; 3.2 = +10% (break), 2.9 = +9% (reward), 1.4 = +4% (refill) |
| Shake | A loss | Jumps 30 times a second to whole-px positions, decays 9/s, 0.7 to 3 p by size |
| Roll | A number counting to its value | 3.2 Hz / 1.0, printed rounded |
| Breath | A lasting warning | 1.15 s cosine on stepped red rings and a warming outline. Never strobe. |
| Raise | A ceiling going up, a reward | Charge 0.12 s (pull in 4%, edge lights), sweep 0.5 s (`pull` curve, light crosses), strike (flash, thump, rings, a "+N" that overshoots in, holds 1.5 s, lifts out) |

Under a floor (0.2% of the bar here) a change is a tick, not an event: nothing fires. Rate-limit gains (0.35 s): regen
and lifesteal fire many times a second.

### How to run a round on the next element

1. **One element.** List every way its state changes in the game first (read the controller AND the server: the
   upgrade, the overshield and the break were found only on the second pass).
2. **A UI Labs generic story** like `Stories/Vitals`: the shipped element as the control beside the candidates, one
   fake source driving all of them, a `Do:` flip per event, a time-scale slider, `scaleNumber.setCanvasScale` at the
   widget's height while building. Dropdowns (`UILabs.Choose` in `UILabs.Ordered`), never strings, and give each
   control its own order number.
3. **Candidates differ on the open question.** Hold the rest identical. Offer a Mix of axes, and ASK what the Mix was
   set to.
4. **On feedback with a screenshot, measure it** (PIL: print the rows as characters) before changing anything. Every
   size fix here was found by counting pixels, not by eye: the sheen's vertical cut, the 2x stroke on the shield,
   the 4 px Press Start letters, the ink filling the well.
5. **Check numbers offline with `lune`**: spring peaks, the raise roll, a staircase, text sizes at bench and at
   1080p sizes. The bench widget is smaller than the game: a size that only fails on the bench is still a bug.
6. **Wire it, delete the losers**, update this file, and say it was not played if it was not.

### Pitfalls this round hit, so the next one does not

| Pitfall | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Changing the whole HUD in one round | One element per round |
| Art that has to be uploaded and pasted before anything draws | Frames only |
| Fluid's static props land on a `task.defer` and overwrite hand-written ones | An `isReady` flag set in your own `task.defer` |
| A turned UIGradient for a diagonal | A staircase of rows |
| Stroke sized off the pixel unit | Off the TextSize |
| Text sized off the inner area, then off the outer only | Off the outer, capped to the inner with air |
| A tail snapping when its scale changes | Move it on the reading's own spring so the sum holds |
| A rescale opening a damage band | The memory copies the reading while rescaling |
| A raise that slides the fill backwards | Walk value and max by one share; from 0 the fill follows the light |
| A bar seeded at a default value | The first max opens it full |
| `for _, x in { a, b } do` in a per-frame step | Build the list once |
| A spring target set after the springs step: the tick returns idle and sleeps before the move starts (hover lifted only sometimes) | Set every target BEFORE stepping |
| A spring value multiplied down again (`1 + thump.X * 0.03`): an invisible thump | The spring's value IS the scale added; size the shove |
| `derive` at a story's top level: "cannot call derive without a parent scope" | Derives only inside the mount; plain functions outside |
| A tab hanging over the card's edge under covers sized to the card (banish, dim): half covered, and its ink stayed dark while the outline went red | The tab's ink IS the outline's colour, the tab sits above the covers and carries its own dim |
| A banish that rebuilds the whole hand (the server resends every option, the client cleared and respawned them): every card dropped and revealed again | Stage options from ClearOptions to Appear and keep the OLD table for each option the hand already shows (`for_values` keeps a card while its table is listed); only the swapped card is built, dropping straight in |
| A slow particle that blinks, or step-fades, or drifts across the card | Ease it in and out smoothly, born outside the glow and drifting away |
| A per-item landing sound right after the moment's own sound (ChestCommon after LevelUp): heard as the moment's sound twice | Low tiers land silent; only the rare ones get a flourish |
| Particles born inside the element, or pulled back through it by gravity (XP bar confetti fell 44 units back through the bar) | "Particles: the checklist": born a unit outside the outermost glow, light gravity under drag, smooth fade, worst case simulated in `lune` |
| A size change on a FREQUENT event (the XP bar swelled a unit on every big gem): disliked | Size gestures only for rare moments (a level, a break); frequent events move light and colour, never the element's size |
| A reactive guard that returns before reading a source (`if not isReady then return end` ahead of `read(props.Visible)`): the effect never subscribes to it and never reruns, so buttons stayed white until hovered | Read every source the effect depends on at the TOP of the effect, before any guard |
| Something on the screen's edge that swells or shakes symmetrically: a gap opens between it and the edge | Grow and shake only away from the edge (the XP bar: up only) |

## Last Wave: the level-up screen (`upgradeCard`, `actionButton`, shipped 2026-10-29)

The second element in the vitals' look, three rounds on the bench (`Stories/Upgrades`), then wired: `UpgradeUI` spawns
`UpgradeOption`, which now only works out the stat lines and icons and hands them to `upgradeCard`; the three action
buttons are `actionButton`. The rounds are below in order; **"Shipped" at the end of this section is the state of
it**. Asked for: the juiciest card, rarity told apart at a glance (a player report: Godly's white border
read as the grey "New" one, at half a second a pick), and a rarity climb like the run's chests, with their sounds.

### What it is

- **A Slab card in Frames**: ink outline, a 2-unit rarity bezel with lit and shaded rows, a dark well, hard shadow, a
  rarity tab hanging over the top edge (ink, fill, lit row, Silkscreen fitted to the fill). Content (icon recess,
  title, `LVL`, stat lines, synergy icons) is laid out in px off the card's own size.
- **Rarity reads by shape, not only hue** (`ORNAMENTS`): Common no glow; each tier adds a stepped glow ring up to three
  at Epic; Legendary adds sparkles off the bezel and a staircase sheen every 2.4 s; Mythic breathes; Godly's bezel
  MARCHES (segments in four clipped strips slid one segment every 0.09 s: 4 position writes a step, not hundreds of
  colour writes); Secret is inverted (black fill, white ink and glow) and glitches a red/cyan split. New is a plain
  grey slab with no ornament at all, which is what separates it from Godly now.
- **The climb** (`schedule`): Common upward, one tier per step, each holding `0.07 + 0.012 * tier` s (Godly lands
  0.83 s in, Secret 0.99 s); Epic to Godly sometimes tease the tier above for 0.32 s and fall back. Each step: tab
  punch +16%, card thump +2.5%, flash, a small thrown ring, the stat's `to` rolling by the rarity multiplier
  (`RarityCore.RARITY_MULTIPLIERS[tier] / [target]`), and ChestJump at `1 + 0.05 * tier` pitch (the chest's step,
  steeper). The landing: thump from +3.8% (Common) to +8.5% (Godly), rings, a burst of 3 + 3 per tier motes, a shake
  from Epic, then the rarity's chest sound (`ChestCommon` .. `ChestSecret`, as `ChestClient` uses). New cards skip the
  climb and land with `ObjectPick`. Three cards stepping in lockstep play ONE jump (`SoundGap`).
- Hover lifts 2 units (the shadow drops with it) and whitens the outline; the pick thumps +8%, flashes and bursts; the
  rest dim under a flat black; banish mode reddens the outline and shows the banish mark on the hovered card.
- Clicking mid-climb lands every card (the bench's `pick`): a fast picker is never made to wait for the show.

### Open on the bench

`Climb`: Together (the three step in lockstep after the last drops in) or Cascade (0.14 s apart, a staircase of
sounds). `Godly`: Marching (black and white, the report's own suggestion) or Prism (the rarity hues marching). Not
yet touched: the banish / skip / reroll buttons, and the wiring (`UpgradeUI` spawning `upgradeCard`, its stat lines
built from `UpgradeOption`'s maths, input locked until the last card lands or is clicked through).

### Pitfalls this round

| Pitfall | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Thump multiplied by 0.03 on top of a spring whose value already is the scale: an invisible card thump | Map springs straight to the scale, size the shove instead |
| A UIScale on a top-left anchored frame grows right and down | Anchor what thumps at its centre (the body), the tab at its left middle |
| A tab's lit row placed at (p, p) inside a UIPadding of p | Padding already insets children: place at the padded origin |
| Sounds through SoundsCore are silent on the edit-mode bench | `SoundService:PlayLocalSound` when `RunService:IsRunning()` is false |


### Round 2 (2026-10-29): Secret above Divine, the left panel, the buttons

Feedback on round 1: Divine (then Godly) was drawn richer than Secret, but Secret is the top and should read as
**something that should not be possible**: black, away from the world, undiscovered until it reaches you. "Godly"
reads better as **Divine**. The icon's dark square looked pasted on: the whole left side should be the darker part.
Hover lifted the card only sometimes. Side by side never showed the old card. The buttons needed the same look.

- **Secret is a void** (`ORNAMENTS[Secret].Void`): black bezel and well, white ink, and its glow rings are BLACK at
  0.25 / 0.45 / 0.65, so it darkens the scene around it instead of lighting it. Stars twinkle in its well, motes are
  PULLED IN from outside (`pullIn`) rather than thrown off, a white rim a few units out flickers like a bad signal,
  and every 1.2 to 2.6 s it glitches: a red/cyan split, white tears across it, a one-unit jolt, its name scrambled.
  **Its climb breaks**: it rises like any card to Divine, stalls there 0.55 s coming apart (split doubled, name all
  noise, a ChestJump at 0.55 pitch), then lands with a BLACK flash, black-then-white rings, a pull-in burst, a
  3-unit shake and its name decoded out of noise a letter every 0.06 s. Nothing teases Secret: it is never shown
  until it is yours (the tease is Epic to Mythic only).
- **Divine is the display name of Godly** (`DISPLAY_NAMES`), on the card only: the enum, the sounds and every save
  keep "Godly" (enum names are never renamed). The chests, the codex and the shop still say Godly.
- **The left panel** runs the well's full height in a darker shade with an ink seam on its right; the icon sits in it
  below the tab. Secret's panel is pure black with a lit seam.
- **Hover bug**: the lift's target was set AFTER the springs stepped, so on a frame where everything else rested the
  tick returned "idle" and slept before the lift moved. **Set every target before stepping**.
- **Side by side**: `UpgradeOption` cannot load in edit mode (the weapon data waits on `LocalPlayer`), so the bench draws
  a copy of its look (and of the old buttons) instead of requiring it.
- **The buttons (`actionButton`)**: square Slabs, icon in the well tinted the bezel's light, uses left in an ink chip
  off the bottom-right corner. Hover lifts 2 units with one glow ring; pressing SINKS it a unit onto its shadow;
  release thumps +9%, flashes, throws rings and pixels and plays ClickHud plus the chest's own action sound
  (ChestBanish, ChestSkip, ObjectChange) with a gesture per action: banish's icon shakes, skip's dashes off right and
  springs back, reroll's turns in four quarter steps (90 degree turns keep pixel art crisp). A spent use punches the
  chip +22%, a gained one +14% and lights it. Out of uses or blocked: grey bezel and icon, and a press refuses (red
  flash, shake, BuyRefuse). Banish held on: sunk, bezel lit, two red rings breathing on the alarm's 1.15 s.
- **Sounds** moved to `Components/uiSound` (shared by card and button).
- A `scaleNumber:89 attempt to call a nil value` seen on the bench is most likely an earlier hot-reload's copy of
  scaleNumber whose camera connection outlived UI Labs unloading its modules; it is not raised by the game.

### Round 3 (2026-10-29): Divine takes Secret's old look, steady motes, bigger counts

- **Divine** wears what Secret wore in round 1 (dark fill, white ink, a white stepped glow), with no march and no
  prism: those are gone, with the bench's control. Its own touch is **shafts of light**: columns of white segments
  behind the card, rising off its top edge a segment at a time, transparency stepped 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.68 / 0.84 upward,
  fading in two steps; 2.5 a second while it rests, seven at once when it lands or is picked. Its sparkles rise white.
  The glitch stays Secret's alone.
- **Drifting motes flickered**: a slow mote that BLINKS out (the vitals' fast chunks do) reads as transparency
  flicker. Drifting motes (sparkles, the void's pulled-in light) now fade in two steps (0.4, then 0.7) over their last
  30%; only the fast pieces thrown off a landing blink.
- **The button counts were tiny** next to the old ones (letters ~0.4 of the button): the chip is now 0.52 of the
  button, centred on its bottom edge where the old count sat.
- **No seam on Secret**: the panel's ink seam is hidden on the void; the darker panel alone separates the sides.

### Shipped (2026-10-29): what the game draws, and what was learned

**Wiring.** `UpgradeUI`'s `for_values` builds each option through `UpgradeOption` (the stat maths, synergy and
conflict icons, favourite star, all as before but as DATA: `{ Name, From, To, IsPercent }` or `{ Text }` lines) into
`upgradeCard`, and calls `Reveal` on it the moment it is built, timed off its own slot (drop 0.06 s apart, all three
start climbing 0.16 s after the third would be in), so nothing depends on when Fluid's deferred build lands. A click
while any card is still climbing lands them all and does not pick (`landAll`); the 0.5 s input lock is unchanged. The
climb is **Together** (the user never picked; Cascade is still on the bench). Banish / skip / reroll are `actionButton`s
whose `Enabled` is the old gating (`buttonsVisible`, count, banish blocking skip and reroll) and whose sounds replace
the old ClickHud / HoverHud calls in `UpgradeUI` (the buttons play their own). Not played in Studio.

**The rarity ladder, as it stands** (`ORNAMENTS`, `PALETTES` in `upgradeCard`):

| Rarity | Look |
| --- | --- |
| New | Plain grey slab, nothing else: the absence of ornament is what tells it from the top tiers |
| Common to Epic | Rarity bezel, plus one stepped glow ring per tier up to three |
| Legendary | + sparkles rising off the edge, a staircase sheen every 2.4 s |
| Mythic | + the glow breathes, sheen every 2 s |
| Divine (Godly) | Dark slab, white ink and white glow (Secret's round-1 look), white rising sparkles, sheen, and its own: SHAFTS of light rising off its top edge |
| Secret | A void: black, white ink, a BLACK glow that darkens the scene, stars in its well, light PULLED IN, a flickering rim, glitches (split, tears, jolt, scrambled name); its climb stalls on Divine and breaks before it lands |

**What was learned, for the next element:**

1. **Rarity must read by shape, not hue alone.** The report was Godly (white) mistaken for New (grey) at a half-second
   pick. A count of rings, then motion (sparkles, breath), then a signature effect per top tier separates them for
   anyone, colourblind or rushed.
2. **The top of a ladder gets the most unusual treatment, not the most of the same.** Secret is the rarest: it should
   feel impossible (it eats light) rather than brighter. The user corrected a Godly that outshone it. Divine's
   signature (shafts) and Secret's (the void) are different KINDS of effect, so they never compete.
3. **Display names can change without touching enums**: `DISPLAY_NAMES` maps Godly to "Divine" on the card only. The
   chests, codex and shop still say Godly: renaming those is a separate, asked-for change.
4. **A reveal climbs like the chests**: every tier one step (`0.07 + 0.012 * tier` s), ChestJump rising 0.05 pitch a
   step, the stat's value rolling by `RARITY_MULTIPLIERS[tier] / [target]`, the landing sized by the tier. A tease (one
   tier too high, then back) only below the top; the top tier is never teased.
5. **Never make the player wait for the show**: a click mid-reveal finishes it.
6. **A dark panel beats a dark box**: the icon's recess was disliked as a square pasted on; a full-height panel down the
   left reads as part of the card. Secret needs no seam at all.
7. **Counts in a chip: a SQUARE with a `UIAspectRatioConstraint`**, about 0.4 of the button, centred on its bottom
   edge, letters fitted by height AND by width for the digits it holds (`fitCount`: digit advance 0.7 of TextSize).
   0.36 off the corner was too small, 0.52 too big, an auto-width chip not square.
8. **A button has four moments, each with its own feel**: hover lifts (one ring), press SINKS onto its shadow, release
   thumps and throws (rings, pixels, its own sound) with a per-action icon gesture (shake, dash, quarter-step spin),
   and a press it cannot do REFUSES (red flash, shake, BuyRefuse) rather than doing nothing. Held modes (banish) stay
   sunk and breathe.
9. **Benches in edit mode cannot load run modules** that touch the ECS or wait on `LocalPlayer` (the weapon data does).
   Draw a copy of the old look as the control, and feed the new component made-up data.
10. **Shared now** (lifted when the second element needed them): `Components/pixelMotion` (clock, springs) and
    `Components/uiSound` (UI sounds by name with pitch and volume, deduped per 0.03 s, `PlayLocalSound` in edit mode).
    Rings, particles, sheen and text-fit are still copied per element; lift them when a third needs them.

    **Done with the reward cards (below)**: `Components/pixelFx`. `actionButton` moved to `Components/` once the
    augment screen used it too.

## Last Wave: the augment / ability screen (`rewardCard`, shipped 2026-10-30)

The third element in the vitals' look, and a direct follow-on to the level-up screen: `RewardUI` (the augment moment,
and the run's first forced ability pick) asked to be "just like the level up, only cards without rarities". The one
thing the user disliked in the old screen: **the augment card's animated rainbow border made augments look better
than abilities** (whose border was a flat gold). Bench: `Stories/Rewards`. Built, benched and wired in the same round
(`RewardUI` keeps its whole API, so `RewardsController` is untouched), then five rounds of feedback, all of which
are in the state below. The user signed it off on 2026-10-30. Linted, compiled and built every round; **not played in
Studio**.

### How the rounds ran

| Round | Feedback | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Remake it like the level-up, no rarities; the rainbow made augments look better | `rewardCard`: upright Slab, one palette (Amber), face-down deal |
| 2 | Centre the text and the CD; the star sat closer to the right than the top (on both cards); augments and abilities should differ in colour | Centred, star equal margins (lesson 8), Teal augments / Amber abilities |
| 3 | Motes "disappear and appear again" (as on the level-up) | Born outside the glow, drift away, smooth fade (lesson 9) |
| 4 | A banish re-animates the whole hand (and on the level-up) | Only the swapped card is built (lesson 10) |
| 5 | The tab looks tucked under the banish frame | Tab ink follows the outline, tab above the covers (lesson 11) |

### What it is

- **The level-up card stood upright.** Same Slab (ink outline, 2-unit bezel with lit and shaded rows, dark well, hard
  shadow), the tab centred on the top edge saying AUGMENT or ABILITY, a full-WIDTH darker panel across the top of the
  well holding the icon (the level-up card's left panel turned 90 degrees; the user preferred a whole darker side to a
  dark square), an ink seam under it, then the name, the ability's weapon, the description, and a footer with the
  ability's cooldown and the synergy / conflict icons. The description and the cooldown are CENTRED (round 2: the
  user did not want them on the left). Card shares are the old ones
  (0.21 x 0.5), so the row and the buttons kept their places.
- **One set of ornaments for every reward, one colour per kind.** No rarity, so nothing may rank the cards: every card
  wears the same ornaments. Round 1 gave both kinds one colour; the user wanted them told apart by colour, so
  augments are **Teal** and abilities **Amber** (`rewardCard.AugmentPalette` / `AbilityPalette`, the bench's two colour
  dropdowns offer Violet too). Neither is a rarity's colour (Teal sits between green Common and blue Uncommon, Amber
  between red Epic and yellow Legendary): a reward in a rarity colour would be read as that rarity. Different hues
  of the SAME weight and the same effects; what made the old augment look better was its animated rainbow, not its
  hue.
- **The deal replaces the climb.** There is no rarity to climb, so the reveal is a face-down deal: the hand drops in
  0.06 s apart showing the card BACK (the bezel's shade, an inset border in its fill, a big "?"), then turns over one
  card at a time from the left (0.32 s, then every 0.13 s). A flip: the back closes to its middle row a pixel row at a
  time (0.1 s), flash, thump +5.6%, the icon punches +17%, the tab +14%, two rings and ten pixels thrown, a sheen
  starts, and `ChestItemCycle` (the chest's item tick) plays, 0.07 higher in pitch per card, so a hand is heard as a
  rising run. A click mid-deal turns every card over and does not pick (`landAll`, as the level-up's).
- **Idle, the same on every card**: two glow rings breathe on a 2.4 s cosine, motes rise from just outside the glow at
  2.5 a second (9 on hover, none once dimmed), and a sheen crosses every 3.2 s. Because the cards flip one after another, their
  sheens cross the hand as a wave.
- Hover lifts 2 units, whitens the outline, brightens the rings and gives the icon a small punch (+7%); the pick
  thumps +8%, flashes and bursts; the rest dim (tab included); banish reddens the outline AND the tab's ink and shows
  the mark, as the level-up card. A banish swaps only the banished card, which drops in and flips at once.
- The buttons are the level-up's `actionButton`s with the same gating (plus `actionsVisible`, which the first ability
  pick and Roulette use to hide them).

### What was learned

1. **Tell kinds apart by hue, never by effect.** The old screen gave augments an animated rainbow and abilities a flat
   gold, and players read the extra motion as value. Rewards without rarity get one set of ornaments; the kind is a
   hue of equal weight and a word.
2. **A colour with no rarity meaning** for things that have no rarity. Every Slab colour in this game is read against
   the rarity ladder first.
3. **The reveal follows what the thing has.** Upgrades have a rarity, so they climb; rewards have none, so they are
   dealt face down and turned, which keeps the beat-by-beat reveal (and its rising pitch) without inventing a tier.
4. **The moment's sound plays once.** `LevelUp` opens this moment too, so the flips are the light chest tick, not a
   landing flourish (the level-up's "heard twice" lesson).
5. **The server deals a fixed hand** (`RewardsService` splits one card count between abilities and augments), so the
   row never holds more than the old one did; a bench hand bigger than the game's only tests overflow that cannot
   happen.
6. **A tall card's sheen steps two units a row**: half the Frames, the same 45 degrees.
7. **Lift the kit with the third user, and only what it shares**: particles (with the steady / blink split), thrown
   rings and the staircase sheen went into `Components/pixelFx`. The springs and the clock were already shared;
   per-element pieces (the void, the shafts, the back) stay in their element. `upgradeCard` and `actionButton` still
   carry their own copies of the effects: port them onto `pixelFx` the next time either is touched, not as a
   drive-by.
8. **A corner badge sits as far in from the side as from the top** (round 2, the favourite star sat 2 units from the
   right and the tab's clearance from the top on both cards). The reward card's star is 2 units in each way; the
   level-up card's is the tab's clearance each way, since its top margin must clear the tab.
9. **Drifting motes must only cross ONE background** (round 3, reported on these cards and on the level-up cards
   before): motes born on the border and drifting up crossed the bezel, the glow and the well, so a light mote vanished
   on the bezel and showed again on the dark well, and the stepped fade (0.4, then 0.7) added two more jumps. Now they
   are born a unit outside the outermost glow ring, drift away from the card (bottom-edge ones move to the top edge),
   and ease in over their first 15% and out over their last 30%. Fixed in `pixelFx` and in `upgradeCard` (its sparkles
   and the void's pulled-in light, which still fly INTO the card by design, but now fade smoothly).
10. **A banish swaps ONE card** (round 4, on both screens): `RewardsService` replaces only the banished option and
    resends the hand, and the client used to clear it and spawn it again, so every card dropped in and climbed / flipped
    again. `UpgradeUI` and `RewardUI` now hold the options from `ClearOptions` until `Appear` (`commitOptions`) and
    reuse the previous table for any option with the same key (upgrade: id, level, rarity and slot; reward: kind, id
    and slot), so Fluid's `for_values` keeps those cards as they are. The new card is marked `IsSwapIn` and drops in
    and climbs / flips at once instead of waiting for its slot's stagger. A reroll changes every key, so it still deals
    the whole hand. The Rewards bench swaps one card the same way; the Upgrades bench still redeals on a banish.
11. **A piece that hangs off the frame is part of the frame** (round 5, both cards): the tab kept its ink while the
    outline turned red in banish mode, and the banish and dim covers (sized to the card) cut across its lower half, so
    the label looked tucked under the frame. The tab's ink now follows the outline (red in banish, lit on hover), the
    tab draws above the covers (ZIndex 61 to 64) and has its own dim (65), so it dims with its card.

### Also changed on the level-up screen by these rounds

The level-up section above is its history; these rounds moved it on, so its current state also includes: the star the
tab's clearance in from the top AND the right; Legendary-and-up sparkles born outside the glow and drifting away with a
smooth fade (the void's pulled-in light still flies in, smoothly faded); a banish building only the swapped card, which
drops in and climbs at once; the tab inked like the outline, above the banish and dim covers, with its own dim. Its
cards land silent below Epic (the "heard twice" fix), whatever the round-1 notes say about landing sounds.

### For the next element

1. **Feedback on one element is usually feedback on its sibling.** Every round here found the same flaw on the
   level-up card (star margin, motes, banish rebuild, tab). Check the sibling every time and say what changed there.
2. **Watch the flow, not only the look**: two of five rounds were behaviour on a gameplay event (banish), not drawing.
   Bench the events the screen gets after it opens (banish, reroll, a resend) as `Do:` flips that behave like the
   game, not like a rebuild.
3. **Read the server before wiring**: the fixed hand size (lesson 5) and the swap-one banish (lesson 10) were both in
   `RewardsService`, and both decided how the client should behave.
4. **Copy the user's eye for spacing**: equal margins, centred text in narrow columns, one background per moving
   pixel. They see a 1-unit asymmetry in a screenshot; measure it before replying.

## Last Wave: closing a moment (the pick hold, exits, button entrances; 2026-10-30)

Follow-ups on both reward screens (`UpgradeUI`, `RewardUI`, `RewardsController`), after "the UI disappears right away
and the player cannot see what he picked". Linted, compiled and built; not played in Studio.

- **The screen holds 0.4 s after a pick** (`PICK_HOLD_SEC` in `RewardsController`; the user went 0.9 to 0.6 to 0.4),
  so the chosen card's thump and rings play out. Only a PICK holds: skip and the server's auto-pick still close at
  once. The hold is a real-time `task.delay`, not TimeCore, because a solo moment pauses the game clock; a token
  cancels it if the moment ends another way.
- **The server echoes your own pick** (`FireAll` on `UpgradeCharacterSelected` / `AugmentCharacterSelected`, to the
  picker too), and in solo that echo ran `checkAllSelected`, which ended the moment and cut the hold short.
  `IsHoldingPick` makes `checkAllSelected` leave it to the hold. **When adding a delay to a flow, find every other
  path that ends it** (echoes, timers, aborts) and make each one respect it.
- **Cards leave as they arrived**: each card's `Leave(delay)` swells to 1.08 over the first 0.3 of 0.22 s, then
  falls as `1.08 * (1 - u^2)` (`pixelMotion.LeaveScale`), and puffs when it is gone. The losers go first, 0.05 s
  apart, the picked card last. The screen tidies up (`finishLeave`) 0.7 s later; an `Appear` during a leave finishes
  it at once, so a queued moment cuts the exit short rather than overlapping it.
- **Buttons arrive and leave too** (`actionButton`, driven by its `Visible` prop): showing pops each in, staggered
  by `LayoutOrder` (0.4 s lead, 0.07 s a button, rising 6 units from half size on a 3.4 / 0.55 spring, with a flash
  and a small burst); hiding shrinks each away (0.18 s, 0.04 s apart) and puffs. Presses are ignored while a button
  is entering or leaving, and it keeps its colours on the way out (`paint` skips while hidden) instead of greying.
- **Bug: buttons white until hovered on the first open.** `paint`'s effect returned on `not isReady` before it read
  `props.Visible`, so it never subscribed to it and never repainted when the buttons were shown. Read every source
  an effect depends on at its top, before any guard (also in the pitfalls table above).
- **Bug: a single-card hand (the run's first ability) dimmed the card you picked.** The pick marked slot -1, which
  dims every card. The pick now marks the slot that was clicked, whatever the hand size.

## Last Wave: the XP bar (`levelBar`, built 2026-10-30, unjudged)

The fourth element in the vitals' look. Asked for: the same style as the new screens, still along the bottom edge from
left to right, no level label, as satisfying as it can be. `LevelBarUI` keeps its API (`SetXP`, `SetRainbow`,
`SetLocked`) and now only mounts `Components/levelBar` in a ScreenGui; `SetXP` gained an optional `instant`, which the
run reset (`RewardsController.OnGameRestarting`) passes so a reset is not drawn as a level. Bench: `Stories/LevelBar`.
Built, linted, compiled and built with Rojo; **not played in Studio and not yet judged on the bench**.

### What it is

- **A Slab six units tall** (outline, lit row, two fill rows, shaded row, outline), its height set in pixel units off
  `PixelSize` rather than a share of the screen, so every row is whole. Blue (`levelBar.Blue`), kept clear of the
  shield's cyan; the bench offers Violet.
- **A gain** lights the new XP as a band at once and the fill (critically damped, 90% in 0.24 s) runs into it,
  spitting sparks off its edge as fast as it moves (up to 26 a second). Heat builds with a stream of gems: it lights
  the leading edge and a stepped glow above the fill, and fades when the stream stops. A gain never changes the bar's
  size (round 1 swelled it a unit on big gems; the user disliked it). The level's swell only ever grows the bar
  UPWARD, and the shake never moves it down, because the bar sits on the screen's edge.
- **Every particle is born a unit above the outermost glow ring, only ever rises, and fades smoothly** (round 1
  feedback: "don't disappear instantly", the cards' lesson 9). Round 1 spawned sparks inside the well and motes inside
  the glow, and the confetti's 240 gravity dropped the slow pieces 44 units back through the bar (simulated). Now
  gravity is light under drag, so nothing comes back down within its life (sparks at worst 1.3 units above their
  birth, the slowest confetti 7), and nothing blinks out.
- **Close to a level** (85% and up) the bar charges: edge and glow breathe and motes rise off it.
- **A level** (an `xp` lower than the last call, or the rainbow turning on) runs the fill to the end in 0.16 s, then
  strikes: white flash, outline to white, a 2.6-unit swell, two rings, confetti along the whole bar, a sheen. Held
  0.12 s, then the old fill drains away to the right as a white band while the next level's XP climbs in under it.
- **Rainbow** (a level waiting to be picked) is that strike followed by 14 stepped hues marching along the full bar,
  with motes and a sheen every 1.4 s. The pick drains it the same way. A max that moves with no level (a player
  joining) moves the bar with no gesture.
- **Locked** (a quest blocks levelling) knocks the bar (red flash, shake), turns the fill red over 0.25 s and drops a
  CAGE of ink bars over it, one every 20 units, as a wave from the left; the outline and a red glow breathe on the
  alarm's 1.15 s. Unlocking lifts the cage the same way, with a white flash, a sheen and motes.
- Effects come from `pixelFx` (particles, rings, sheen); no sound, since the level-up moment plays its own.

### What was learned

1. **Particles get their own checklist now** ("Particles: the checklist", in the vitals recipe): this was the third
   element in a row whose first round had them crossing the element or falling back through it.
2. **A frequent event never changes the element's size.** XP arrives many times a second; a one-unit swell on big
   gems read as the bar twitching and the user disliked it. Light and colour answer a gain (band, edge, heat glow,
   sparks); size is kept for the level.
3. **Something on the screen's edge moves only away from it**: the swell grows up, the shake never goes down, or a
   gap opens under it.
4. **Size a pixel element in units, not in screen shares**: the bar is `Rows * p` tall, so every row is whole at any
   resolution. A share of the screen height would leave a part-row somewhere.
5. **Detect an event from the raw value, not the share.** A level is `xp` going DOWN; the share also drops when a
   player joins (the XP needed goes up), which must move the bar quietly. And a value that drops for another reason
   (the run reset) needs `instant`, or it plays the celebration.
6. **Read what the controller suppresses.** `RewardsController.XPSet` ignores XP during a moment, so the last value
   before a level never reaches the bar; the rainbow turning on IS the level, and the bar runs itself to full. After
   the pick, `SetRainbow(false)` is followed by `SetXP(overflow)`, so the bar resets its last value to 0 on the
   rainbow's end to read that as a gain from empty, not another level.
7. **A screen-wide element keeps its instance count fixed**: the cage is a pooled bar every 20 units (about 32 at
   1080p), the rainbow 18 hue segments that MARCH (positions stepped a unit at a time and colours re-indexed), not a
   gradient rebuilt every frame or a stripe per pixel row.
8. **The level-up moment owns the sound**; the bar plays none (the "heard twice" lesson).


## Last Wave: the ability hotbar and the mobile controls (`abilitySlot`, `touchButton`, built 2026-10-30, unjudged)

The fifth element in the vitals' look. Asked for: the hotbar in the new style, the mobile controls with it ("they are
mostly like the hotbar abilities"), as satisfying as it can be, the mobile controls readable, and BeACastleLord's
hotbar as the reference for cooldowns and stamina. Built, wired and benched in one round (`Stories/Hotbar`); linted,
compiled, the place built with Rojo, springs and sparks simulated with `lune`. **Not played in Studio and not yet
judged on the bench.**

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Components/abilitySlot.luau` | One ability: the slot, plus `Registry()` (the API AbilitiesController drives, shared by both UIs) and `ForEntry()` (builds an entry's slot and hands it back so the registry can strike and press it) |
| `Components/touchButton.luau` | Jump, slide, ping and the interact buttons |
| `AbilitiesUI.luau`, `MobileControlsUI.luau` | The two UIs, rebuilt on those. Same API as before plus `Pressed(id)`; every position, size and Instance name the controllers and the tutorial use is kept (`Container.AbilitySlot1.Ability`, the `HitArea` buttons) |
| `Stories/Hotbar.story.luau` | The bench: Desktop / Mobile, a fake AbilitiesController on the bench's clock |

`abilityComponent` was deleted (no users left). `AbilitiesController` changed in one place: a key press now calls
`Pressed` on its slot before the `abilitiesBlocked` guard, so a key on cooldown or under Powerless is seen to refuse.

### What it is

- **The slot is the level-up screen's `actionButton` made into an ability**: ink outline, a 2-unit bezel (Amber, the
  ability card's colour; **Violet on the ultimate**, a different kind told by hue), a dark well with the icon, a hard
  shadow, the key hanging over the top edge, charges in an ink chip on the bottom edge.
- **A cooldown is drawn twice, on purpose.** The well's dark shade covers the share still to wait (in whole rows,
  with a light edge where it ends) and draws back up as it recharges; the bezel goes grey and lights back CLOCKWISE
  FROM TWELVE like a fuse, five Frames walking the bezel. That is BeACastleLord's square League wipe, redone as
  axis-aligned pieces because a turned gradient is not pixel-hard. The number counts down in the middle (Silkscreen,
  ink outline, sized to the well), and its last three seconds punch +10% on each tick.
- **A cast is BeACastleLord's stamina chip.** Two springs chase the shade: a quick loose light one and a slow dark one,
  so a cast drops a LIGHT BAND down the icon with the dark eating it from above, and a recharge moves both together
  (snapped, so the readout never lags the clock). A bar that only slides says where you are; the chip says what just
  happened. Plus a light flash, a +6% thump, the icon squashed -16%, a small ring and a few sparks.
- **Ready strikes it** (the controller's `TriggerShine`: cooldown done, a charge back, a slot added): white flash,
  +9% thump, icon +14%, two rings, 12 sparks, a sheen. A strike on a slot still entering waits for it to land.
- **A press shows before the server answers**: a slot that can cast sinks a unit and flashes (+3%); one that cannot
  (cooling, no charges, locked) refuses with a red flash, a shake and a quiet BuyRefuse. Touch presses come from the
  slot's own button; keyboard and gamepad presses come through `Pressed`.
- **Charges**: the shade is lighter while charges are left (the ability can still be cast), the chip punches +22% on
  a spend and +14% on a gain.
- **Active** (a buff running): the bezel turns to its light colour, two rings breathe (0.9 s), a sheen every 1.2 s,
  the number turns light. A `CooldownAt.End` cooldown starting as the buff ends is NOT a second cast.
- **Locked** (Powerless): red flash and a shake, the well tints red and a cage of ink bars drops in; the outline is
  red. Unlocking lifts the cage with a white flash and a sheen.
- **Info key**: a Slab tooltip (ink, bezel, well, Silkscreen) above the key, popping in.
- **Idle, only the ultimate moves**: one ring breathes on 2.4 s while it is ready, with a sheen every 3.2 s. The bar is
  up for the whole run under combat, so everything else is still unless something happened to it.
- **The row opens**: on desktop each slot's cell holds its width plus its gap and opens from nothing (BeACastleLord's
  hotbar), so a new ability slides its neighbours apart instead of the row jumping half a slot. Slots pop in a beat
  apart on `Appear` and shrink away on `Disappear`.
- **Mobile**: the same slots on the arc, and `touchButton`s in the same Slab for jump, slide, ping (Slate), interact
  (Slate, gold on skip), accept (green) and banish (red, grey and refusing with none left). Opaque wells and big light
  icons so they read over any scene, a hit area 1.15x the art. **A press sinks it, lights one ring and flashes; it
  never changes size** (jump is pressed constantly). Interact buttons pop in and shrink away; a new interact icon
  punches. The thumbstick knob is a small Slab, the trail is inked squares, and a hollow square of one-unit edges marks
  where the thumb landed.

### What was learned

1. **Two readouts of one number can both earn their place** when they answer different questions: the shade says
   how much is left (read on the icon you are looking at), the fuse says it is cooling at all (read from the corner of
   the eye, in a fight). Neither alone did both.
2. **Detect a cast from the state, not the press.** Every input path (touch, keys, gamepad) ends in the same
   `SetCooldown` / `SetAmount` / active flag, so the slot reads a cooldown starting from zero, a charge going down or
   a buff starting. The press itself only gets the tap or the refusal, because only the server knows if it cast.
3. **A HUD that is always up must be still at rest.** Every gesture here answers an event; the one idle motion is
   the ultimate saying "ready", because that is the one a player should notice without looking.
4. **Sparks off a slot in a row go UP and AWAY from the key**, never off the sides or the bottom: side sparks would
   cross the next slot (two backgrounds), bottom sparks would cross the XP bar. Born a unit past the outer glow ring
   on the top edge, outside the key's middle 40%, thrown outward from the middle with an upward float under drag:
   simulated, the worst case never comes back below where it was born.
5. **Frequent presses move light and position, never size** (the XP bar's lesson, applied to jump): sink, ring,
   flash.
6. **Keep the Instance names other systems look up** when rebuilding a UI: the tutorial finds
   `Container.AbilitySlot1.Ability`, the controller wires the `HitArea` buttons and reads `_Thumbstick*` sources.

### Round 2 (2026-10-30): the chest buttons, the top bar, the thumbstick

| Feedback | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Skipping a chest showed the "open chest" button before accept / banish | The interact button's icon is reactive: as the mode went skip to split it swapped to the chest's icon and then played its 0.16 s shrink, so a chest button was seen leaving | `touchButton` keeps its icon and colours while hidden or leaving; only a wanted button takes a new look |
| After accept, the "open chest" button appeared and went again | `OnChestItemPicked` cleared the chest's mode while the prop was still the shown one, so `refreshInteract` read "a prop, no chest mode" as "main" until `CleanupProp` ran a moment later | The prop is cleaned up first, then the mode cleared |
| The level-up and reward cards ran under Roblox's top-left buttons | `ScreenInsets = DeviceSafeInsets` clears the notch, not the core UI | `CoreUISafeInsets` on `UpgradeGui` and `AugmentGui` |
| The thumbstick looked nothing like the rest | A translucent grey square, a thin outline, plain dots | The knob is a small Slab (ink, two-unit bezel with lit and shaded rows, dark well, a light cap), the base is a hollow frame of the same layers round a see-through well, the trail is inked squares growing toward the knob |

**Learned:**

1. **An exit animation makes every transient state visible.** Hiding used to be instant, so a frame of a wrong icon
   or a wrong mode never showed. Once things shrink away or pop in, a source that flips through an in-between value
   draws it for the whole animation. Freeze a leaving element's look, and order the writes so the in-between never
   happens (clean up, THEN clear).
2. **Layers that fade together must sit side by side, not on top of one another.** A Slab built as nested opaque
   Frames is fine until it is faded: the bloom on a nested knob would have darkened where the bezel lies over the ink.
   The knob is built from edge rings round its well instead.
3. **A full-screen modal on mobile wants `CoreUISafeInsets`**, the HUD keeps `DeviceSafeInsets`: the topbar buttons
   sit in the top-left on every device and cards under them cannot be read.

## Last Wave: the status strip (`statusTile`, built 2026-10-30, unjudged)

The bottom-left row of buff / augment tiles (`TimersUI`, driven by `TimersController`), in the ability slots' look.
Bench `Stories/StatusTiles`. Linted, compiled, built; **not played in Studio and not yet judged**. `timerComponent`
was deleted; the rim fuse moved into `pixelFx.Fuse` (the ability slot uses it too).

- **Four kinds, three hues**: augment dials (Magneto, Black Hole) Teal like the augment card; timed buffs (drops,
  support-weapon buffs) Lime; the Greatshield counter Amber. `AddTimer` took an optional `kind`; only
  `tryAddTimer` passes `"Augment"`, the rest default to a buff.
- **A buff is something you HAVE running out**: its bezel is lit and unwinds clockwise from twelve (the lit part is
  the time left), the icon stays bright, a ring marks it active. Its last 3 seconds breathe the outline toward red on
  0.6 s and punch the number on each whole second. Grabbing it again flashes it and sheens.
- **A dial is something CHARGING**: the ability slot's cooldown (dark shade over the icon drawing back up, bezel
  lighting back clockwise). When it fires (the cycle wraps, or its active phase starts) the tile flashes, the icon
  punches, a ring and sparks leave the top. **No size change on a fire**: Black Hole fires every 6 s.
- **Counter**: lit whole, the number punches +10% on each change, the tile never moves.
- **Tiles arrive and leave**: pop in from half size with a fire, shrink away on `RemoveTimer`; the registry keeps
  the entry until the leave and the cell's close are done (0.5 s) and a re-grab mid-leave keeps the tile (a token per
  id, so the old leave cannot drop it). Cells open and close, so the strip slides.

**Learned:**

1. **Removing a list entry instantly kills its exit.** `values()` destroys a tile the moment its entry leaves the
   table, so the registry marks it leaving, waits out the animation, then drops it, and any re-add in between must
   cancel that drop.
2. **Read the meaning of a fill off the kind, not the number**: a buff and a dial both send a 0 to 1 share, but one
   is time LEFT (lit runs down) and one is charge still TO COME (dark runs down). Same pieces, opposite reading.
3. **A shared piece moves to the kit on its second user** (`pixelFx.Fuse`), per the rule in "What was learned" on the
   level-up screen.

## Last Wave: what the hotbar, mobile and status rounds taught (2026-10-30)

The habits from these three rounds (hotbar, mobile controls, status strip), on top of the per-element notes above.

### Cost: a HUD element is updated 30 times a second, so skip what did not change

- **Separate "the number moved" from "the look changed".** `AbilitiesController` and `TimersController` push
  `SetCooldown` / `SetProgress` 30 times a second for as long as anything is cooling. The first build repainted every
  colour (about 20 property writes) and woke the clock on every push, four slots at once. Now each effect builds a
  short LOOK KEY from the states that pick colours (locked, active, usable, hovered, pressed; or active, draining,
  warning) and repaints and wakes only when the key changes; the moving parts (shade, fuse, number) are drawn
  directly. Every Instance property write is a reflection call, the same value or not (CLAUDE.md, Performance Rules).
- **A recharge snaps, a spend springs.** Snapping the shade on a recharge means no clock frame is spent on it at
  all: the effect draws once and returns. Only an event that should be SEEN (a cast's chip band) wakes the clock.
- **Idle means asleep.** Nothing on the bar runs a frame at rest except the ultimate's ready breath, which is the one
  thing meant to be noticed. Check this for every new element: what keeps `pixelMotion` awake when nothing happens?

### Readability: what is still not as clean as it should be

- **The Slab body is now built four times**: `actionButton`, `abilitySlot`, `touchButton`, `statusTile` each make
  their own outline / bezel / lit and shaded rows / well / shadow and lay them out in a `layout()`. That is past the
  "lift on the third user" rule. **`Components/pixelSlab` now exists** (lifted by the quest round, below); move the four
  over to it one element per round, re-benching each. Not done yet because it touches the shipped level-up screen.
- **Two registries** (`abilitySlot.Registry`, `statusTile.Registry`) share their shape (a source of entries, add,
  remove, set) but differ on purpose: tiles leave with an animation, slots are cleared by the controller. Leave them.
- `LoadingScreen` still preloads the old ability frame image (`72008670363476`), which nothing draws now.

### Flow: what broke between elements, not inside one

1. **An exit animation exposes every in-between state** (the chest's "open" button): look for a source that flips
   through a wrong value when you add any leave or enter animation, freeze the leaving element's look, and order
   writes so the in-between never exists.
2. **A UI that the server or another controller feeds must survive their order.** The chest cleared its mode before
   its prop; the controller strikes a slot before it has entered (queued until it lands); a buff is re-grabbed while
   its tile is leaving (a token cancels the drop).
3. **Mobile feedback comes as screenshots of the real device frame**: check the ScreenGui's insets against Roblox's
   own buttons (`CoreUISafeInsets` for modals) and read sizes off the screenshot before replying.
4. **Keep the names other code looks up** (`Container.AbilitySlot1.Ability`, `HitArea`, `_Thumbstick*`), and keep a
   remade UI's API whole so its controller changes by a line at most.

### Editing big files by script

A Python replace anchored on `"\tend)\n"` matched the INNER `end)` of an effect and left a stray `end)` behind;
StyLua and the compile caught it. Anchor scripted edits on text that occurs once (assert the count), and compile the
file straight after.

## Last Wave: the quest UI (built 2026-10-30, unjudged)

Asked for: the quests and objectives in the new style, more readable ("most people don't even know that they have
objectives, it's really tiny"), and Color Dance players not knowing they lost or that they must stay on the colour
until it changes. As satisfying as it can be. Built, wired, benched (`Stories/Quests`); linted, compiled, the place
built with Rojo, springs simulated with `lune`. **Not played in Studio and not yet judged on the bench.**

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Components/pixelSlab.luau` | The Slab lifted out: `Body` (shadow, outline, bezel with lit and shaded rows, well with its dark top row; `Layout(w, h, unit, bezelUnits)` returns the well's size, `Paint(palette)`), `Tab` (the word over the top edge), `Letters` + `Fit` (miter ink outline a tenth of the TextSize, the Silkscreen raise), palettes (Gold, Red, Magenta, Green, Grey) and `FromColor` |
| `QuestsUI.luau` | The objective under the minimap: OBJECTIVE tab, altar icon, "Activate Altars", one pip per altar and the count; turns red into "Activate Boss Altar" on the last one. Takes `{MaxActivations, AltarIcon, BossIcon}` from MinimapUI so the bench can build it without DataCore |
| `QuestActiveUI.luau` | One running quest as a card: QUEST tab (CHALLENGE in red for a challenge's two), icon, name, description, a big countdown and a bar draining along the bottom. API: `Show(name, description, imageId, duration, isChallenge?)`, `SetRemaining`, `Finish(didSucceed, line?)`, `SetOut(line)`, `Hide(onGone?)`, `SetLayoutOrder` |
| `QuestLockWarningUI.luau` | The red ribbon above the cards while a quest runs; knocks in, breathes red, pops away |
| `AnnouncementsUI.luau` | Every banner as a Slab in its header's colour. Same API, plus `flyTo` accepting a GuiObject (the NEW QUEST banner now flies into the objective card, `MinimapController.GetObjectivePanel()`), `MountPinned(build)` for a panel of its own under the cards, `Unmount()` for the bench |
| `ColorDanceUI.luau` | Color Dance's panel, pinned under the cards |
| `Stories/Quests.story.luau` | The bench: stand-in minimap, the column, a fake controller on the bench's clock, "On the colour" for the player's feet |

### What it does

- **The objective is a card, not a caption.** About twice the old height, with a tab saying OBJECTIVE and a pip per
  altar, so the goal reads as progress. An altar lit pops its pip (+24%, simulated), punches the count (+22%) and
  throws sparks off the card's BOTTOM edge (the minimap is above it). The last altar strikes the whole card (flash,
  +9% thump, rings, sparks) 0.35 s later, once its pip has landed, and turns it red. **The NEW QUEST banner flies
  into it** and it strikes as the banner arrives. At rest it is still, except **a nudge every 14 s**: a sheen and the
  next pip blinking once. That breaks the "a HUD at rest is asleep" rule on purpose: the complaint was that nobody
  sees it. Nudges are cheap (a `task.delay` chain, the clock wakes only for the sheen) and skipped while the map is
  open.
- **A quest card** drops in (the reward cards' arrival), the timer bar drains along the whole well's bottom and the
  number sits in its own panel. The last 10 s breathe the outline red; the last 5 punch the number on each second.
  **The end is stamped on the card**: a pixel tick (green) or cross (red) pops in where the number was (+23%), the
  name turns to "Quest complete" / "Quest failed", the tab to COMPLETE! / FAILED; a win flashes, thumps and throws
  sparks off the sides, a loss shakes. The card holds 3 s, or, for a loss while others pick rewards, says "Wait for
  other players to get their rewards." and stays until `RewardsController.OnClosed` (with the old failsafe). **This
  replaced the QUEST FAILED banner**: the card IS the result now, instead of the card vanishing and a banner
  appearing.
- **Color Dance's panel** answers what players missed:
  - **Which colour**: a swatch that is a tile of the colour itself, and its name big in that colour. The bezel is the
    colour too.
  - **When it is checked**: a countdown in its own panel (its "CHECK IN" label was removed in round 3), a bar running out, and the last 3 s ticking
    (`ChestItemCycle`, rising pitch). The server checks only at the END of a round, so "stay until it changes" is
    really "be on it when the bar runs out", and the bar shows exactly that.
  - **Whether you are on it now**: a live line, "STAY ON IT!" in green or "MOVE TO RED!" in red, breathing red (0.5 s)
    with the outline while you are off it, and a jolt on each tick when off. The client works out the colour under
    the player from the rings buffer it already gets (cellIndex to colorIndex), the same way `ColorDanceServer` checks
    (`Grid:GetCellXYFromWorldPos`, `y * Width + x`, an unpainted cell counts as wrong).
  - **Passing a check** says SAFE! (green flash, rings, sparks, `ChestJump`) while the next colour comes in; the last
    one turns the panel to ALL CLEAR.
  - **Failing one** turns it to ELIMINATED / "Wrong color!" / "Quest failed" with a big red shake, plays QuestFailed
    at that moment, and **stays until the quest ends**. The quest card is crossed out too (`SetOut`), its bar still
    running to the end. It used to say ELIMINATED for 2 s and vanish while the quest ran on.
- **Network:** `ColorDanceRoundStarted` gained `roundCount` (u8) and `roundSeconds` (f32, the time to the check),
  so the panel can count down and show ROUND 2/4. Regenerated with `blink/generate.sh` (the local binary handled a
  changed field fine). `ColorDanceClient` falls back to 5 s if the field is missing.
- **Quest client modules' `Start` gets a 4th argument**, the quest's card, so a module can mark it (Color Dance's
  `SetOut`) without requiring QuestsController (which requires the modules).

### What was learned

1. **Ask what the player cannot SEE, not what the UI shows.** Color Dance showed the colour all along; what was
   missing was when the check happens and whether you are on it. Both were knowable on the client (the round's length
   from the server, the colour under the feet from data the client already had), and neither was drawn.
2. **A result belongs on the thing it is the result of.** A card that vanishes and a banner that appears elsewhere
   reads as two events; the card stamping its own outcome reads as one, and it can say what to do next.
3. **A loss that does not end the activity must be shown for as long as the activity runs.** Elimination is
   personal, the quest is not: a 2 s message left eliminated players dancing for nothing.
4. **An always-up element that players MISS may move at rest, rarely.** The "idle means asleep" rule is about cost
   and noise; a 14 s nudge costs nothing and is the only fix for "nobody knows it is there", together with size.
5. **Point a flight at the thing, not at a screen share.** The old banner flew to `(0.93, 0.32)`, which drifts off the
   panel whenever the minimap's aspect or the panel's size changes; it now reads the target's AbsolutePosition.
6. **A freshly mounted list item has no width on its first frame.** Effects that need it (rings sized to the card,
   sparks off its edges) wait for the first AbsoluteSize (`isEnterPending` in the card, a `task.defer` in a banner).
7. **A content-sized Slab measures its content**: the banner lays its text out at the well's width with
   `AutomaticSize.Y`, reads `AbsoluteSize.Y` back on change, rounds it up to whole units and sizes the Slab round it.


### Round 2 (2026-10-30): tabs on the outline, centred scaling, centred text

| Feedback | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The QUEST / OBJECTIVE / ROUND tabs sat above the card, and were too small to read | `Tab.Layout` centred the tab on the body's y = 0, and the body started half a tab ABOVE the Slab, so the whole tab floated over it; 7 to 8 units tall gave letters about 4 units high | `Tab.Layout(x, y, height, unit)` takes a y, and every caller puts the tab's middle on the outline (`round(p / 2)` from the Slab's top), as the reward cards do. 11 to 12 units tall: letters about 7 units, 21 px at 1080p |
| The objective's thump grew from its top-left corner | Its body had the default `AnchorPoint` (0, 0), and **a `UIScale` grows a frame from its AnchorPoint** | Every Slab body (card, objective, Color Dance, banner, lock ribbon) is now the Slab's own box with `AnchorPoint` (0.5, 0.5), placed at its centre (`top + slabHeight / 2`); the tab and the rings hang off it |
| A dark line across the top of Color Dance's swatch | The swatch is a `pixelSlab.Body`, whose well has a darker top row (right for a hole, wrong for a tile of colour) | `TSlab.WellShade` is exposed; the swatch hides it |
| Title, description and the rest read better centred | Left-aligned columns | Names, descriptions, Color Dance's lines and the objective's title are centred; the objective's pips and count are one group centred under the title |
| Hunt had no icon on the bench | The bench's pasted quest data had an empty `ImageId` | The real one (`Data/Quests/Hunt`) |
| The hotbar's charges chip ran over the shield bar when it punched | The chip hangs half below the slot; at `BOTTOM` 0.88 it overlapped the shield (top at 0.894) even at rest. Worst case (slot thump +9% and chip punch +22% together) worked out in `lune`: -14 px at 0.88, +7.5 px at 0.86, +18 px at 0.85 | `AbilitiesUI` `BOTTOM` 0.85, leaving room for the shield's glow |

**Learned:**

1. **Anything that scales gets `AnchorPoint` (0.5, 0.5).** A `UIScale` (or any size gesture) grows a frame from its
   AnchorPoint, so a punch, thump, arrival or leave on a (0, 0) frame grows from the top-left corner and reads as the
   thing sliding, not swelling. Make the body the box being scaled (not a box with extra room above it), anchor it at
   its middle and place it by its middle; hang tabs, rings and sparks off it. Check this on every new element: what
   does each UIScale sit on, and where is that frame's AnchorPoint?
2. **A tab sits ON the outline**, its middle on the Slab's top edge, not on the edge of whatever frame holds it. When
   a frame grows "room for the tab" above the Slab, every child placed at that frame's y = 0 is now in the wrong spot.
3. **A hanging piece (chip, tab, key) needs its clearance worked out at its WORST size**: the element's own thump and
   the piece's punch together, plus the neighbour's glow. Checking it at rest is how the chip ended up over the shield.

**Round 3:** the tab hangs half into the well, so the text under it starts lower: the quest card's name and Color
Dance's first line start 5 units down the well (`TextTopUnits`, was 3), and both wells grew 2 units to keep the room
under the text. Color Dance's "CHECK IN" label is gone; the countdown sits centred in its panel. A first try added the
air ABOVE the tab instead (between cards); the user meant inside the card, between the tab and the text.

**Round 4:** the timer's panel is a square the well's height, the same as the icon's (swatch's) on the other side, so
the centred text is centred on the card. **Round 5:** the timer bar is drawn in the palette's Light, not its Fill: in
the Fill it sat against the bezel and read as part of the outline.

## Last Wave: altar reminder completion (2026-11-05)

The "ACTIVATE AN ALTAR" banner kept appearing after the team activated all eight regular altars. The server's
reminder timer checked whether each player had contributed, but never checked whether the team had finished.
The boss altar is a separate objective; leaving it inactive must not keep the regular-altar reminder alive.

- **Guard the event producer with authoritative completion state.** In
  `src/Survivors/Server/Props/AltarServer.luau`, the Heartbeat callback returns when
  `totalActivations >= PropsCore.ALTAR_MAX_ACTIVATIONS`, immediately after the running-game guard and before
  `Players:GetPlayers()`. This avoids the player lookup, loop and reminder packets once the objective is complete.
- **Reuse existing state and limits.** No second completion counter, client polling, new connection or protocol
  change is needed. Preserve the initial delay, repeat interval, contributor exemption and existing reset path.
- **Check the objective boundary and restart.** Reminders remain eligible below the regular-altar limit, stop at
  and above it even for a noncontributor, and resume after reset with the initial delay. Also check cooldown,
  contributor exemption and a stopped run. Visual styling alone cannot establish that a reminder is still valid.

This fix passed an offline execution of the source callback covering those cases, full-module Luau compilation,
full-tree StyLua and a Selene comparison with no added diagnostics. It was not playtested in Studio or profiled;
these checks establish the guard's behavior, not a measured frame-time improvement.

## Last Wave: what the quest rounds taught (2026-10-30)

The habits from the quest UI's five rounds, on top of the per-round notes above.

### Shape: what the user corrected, so the next card starts right

1. **A tab sits on the outline, and the text inside starts clear of it.** The tab's middle goes on the Slab's top
   edge (`Tab.Layout(x, round(p / 2), height, unit)`), so half of it hangs into the well: whatever is first in the well
   starts about 5 units down (`TextTopUnits`), not 3. Tabs 11 to 12 units tall, letters about 7 units, or they cannot
   be read.
2. **Everything that scales is anchored at its centre** (round 2's lesson, above): the body IS the Slab's box, placed
   by its middle.
3. **A card with a panel on each side makes both panels the same square** (the well's height), and centres its text,
   so the middle column is centred on the card.
4. **A bar against the bezel is not the bezel's colour.** Draw it in the palette's Light (or another colour); in the
   Fill it merges with the outline.
5. **A well that is a colour, not a hole** (a swatch) hides the well's dark top row (`TSlab.WellShade`).
6. **"More space" can mean two places.** Round 3's first try added air between cards when the user meant between the
   tab and the text inside the card. When the screenshot shows a gap problem, say which gap you will change before
   changing it, or change the one INSIDE the element first: that is the one a single element owns.

### Cost: what keeps this cheap

- **Every per-frame push is guarded.** `SetRemaining` and `SetCheck` run every Heartbeat; they redraw the bar only when
  its whole-unit width changes and the number only when its whole second changes. `SetOnColor` returns at once when
  the answer did not change. The live colour check reads one property (`PrimaryPart.Position`) and one table lookup a
  frame, and only while a round is running.
- **The clock sleeps at rest**, except where a warning is meant to be seen: a card's last 10 s, Color Dance while the
  player is off the colour, the lock ribbon while a quest runs. The objective's nudge is a `task.delay` chain that
  wakes the clock for half a second every 14 s.
- **Not done:** each banner builds its own particle pool, rings and sheen rows (about 80 Frames) when it is shown, and
  frees them when it goes. Banners are rare (a few a minute at most), so pooling them was not worth the complexity;
  pool them if a flow ever shows banners in bursts.

### Readability: what was lifted, and what is still copied

- **Lifted this round:** `pixelSlab` (the Slab body, the tab, lettering), `pixelFx.SideSparks` (sparks off a box's
  left and right edges, for anything in a column) and `pixelFx.Shake` (`Kick(amount)`, `Step(dt)`, `.X`). Each was in
  three of the new files before; the shake and the sparks were moved after the build, when a re-read found the copies.
  **Re-read new files side by side before calling a round done**: three elements built in one round copy each other
  more than three built in three rounds, because each is written from the last.
- **Still copied** across the card, Color Dance, the banner and the ribbon: the arrival (drop plus scale springs), the
  leave (`LeaveScale` then the row closing) and the row's open spring, about 20 lines each. They differ in what
