  happens at the end (pool, unmount, destroy), so a shared piece would need callbacks for each; lift them when a fifth
  element needs the same thing. The card and Color Dance also share the "side panel + number + bar" layout.
- The older debt stands: `actionButton`, `abilitySlot`, `touchButton`, `statusTile` still build their own Slab
  instead of `pixelSlab`.

### Editing by script, again

A regex meant to swap a whole function (`local function burst ... end`) used a lazy `.*?` up to the first indented
`end`, which was the inner `for` loop's: it left the function's own `end` and a broken body behind. Compile caught it.
Same lesson as last time, now with regexes: **never match a block's end by pattern; match the whole block's exact
text** (copied from the file), assert it occurs once, and compile right after.

## Last Wave: the clock, kills and souls, and the toasts (built 2026-10-30, unjudged)

Asked for: the timer, the souls and kills counters and the notifications (stat changes, discoveries) in the new style,
as satisfying as they can be; the notifications were unreadable on phones (on the right, under the thumbs and the
buttons, and they stacked); the pick glow off EditableImage if it could be. Bench `Stories/RunHud`. Linted, compiled,
the place built with Rojo, the glow's falloff checked in `lune`. **Not played in Studio and not yet judged on the bench.**

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Components/runClock.luau` | The clock as a Slab at the top centre: the time big, a bar draining along the well's bottom. `ShowRun(secondsLeft, share)`, `ShowOvertime(secondsOver, isBreathing)`, `ShowPick(secondsLeft, share)`, `Reset(secondsLeft)`; called every frame, each returns early when nothing it draws changed |
| `TimerUI.luau` | The same clock logic as before (run clock, overtime, the pick's countdown over it, the red tint); only the drawing moved to `runClock` |
| `TimerBarUI.luau` | The pick glow: the old radial baked to `Assets/ui/glow/TimerGlow.png` and drawn by an ImageLabel instead of an EditableImage, tinted and faded as before. Same API plus `Root` |
| `SelfStatsUI.luau` | Kills (Grey) and souls (Magenta) as two Slab chips hung off the minimap's left edge. Same API plus `Root`; takes an optional minimap frame for the bench |
| `PassiveChangesUI.luau` | Stat changes and discoveries as toasts above the hotbar, newest at the bottom. `AddChange(name, delta, isPercent, imageId?)`, `AddDiscovery(name, imageId?)`, plus `Root` |

### What it does

- **The clock's colour is the phase.** Grey while more than half the run is left, Gold past half, Red in the last
  minute (the outline breathes red in the last 10 s, the number knocks on each second, the last 5 tick with
  `ChestItemCycle` at a rising pitch), Red with "+" in overtime (breathing, unless Infinite, like the tint). A pick's
  countdown takes the clock over in Green, then Gold, then Red, the number knocking each second and harder in the last
  3. **Entering a phase strikes it** (flash, sheen, rings, side sparks, a thump sized to the phase; overtime also
  shakes). A minute passing is a sheen and a knock. Coming back from a pick is a flash only: the player caused it, and
  in a late run it happens every few seconds.
- **The pick glow was first rebuilt as stepped Frames, and the user rejected it**: "I liked it more how it looked
  with editableimage". The radial was baked instead (same centre, radius and `(1 - d)^2` falloff, 256 px, white with
  the falloff in alpha) and uploaded as a Decal; the animation (tint green to red, a brightening pulse each second,
  the fade) is the old one, on `ImageColor3` / `ImageTransparency`. Its Heartbeat is connected only while it shows or
  fades.
- **Kills and souls never change size on a kill** (frequent events move light, not size): souls ROLL to their value
  and light their icon (at most every 0.35 s), a spend of 10 or more flashes and knocks the number (a smaller drop is
  the server correcting the client's own count), and **every 100 kills is a moment**: a gold flash, a sheen, a +9%
  thump, a +22% punch, sparks off the bottom edge.
- **The toasts moved to the middle, above the hotbar** (bottom at 0.74, the hotbar's top is about 0.77): where the
  player looks, and clear of the phone's buttons on the right and the thumbstick on the left. Each is a Slab with the
  stat's icon (now passed from `PassivesController` and `DiscoveryController`) and "+10% Damage" centred. Gains are
  Green with a few side sparks, losses Red, discoveries Gold with a DISCOVERED tab, more sparks and a
  `ChestJump`. **The same stat again adds to its toast** (a flash, timer restarted) instead of stacking, and
  **at most four show**: past that, the oldest leaves early. Toasts pop in from half size and leave with the
  `LeaveScale` pop; rows open and close, so the stack slides.

### What was learned

1. **Where a notice sits decides whether it is read.** The old feed was readable on a monitor and invisible on a
   phone, because the phone's right side is buttons and a thumb. Before placing anything that must be read, map the
   screen on every device: what covers the corners (Roblox's buttons, the thumbstick, the action cluster), and where
   the eye already is (the character, the hotbar, the clock).
2. **A stack that grows needs a cap and a merge, not just a place.** Most of the "they stack a lot" came from one
   level-up firing several changes and the same stat changing twice; merging per stat and capping the count fixes the
   flood without hiding anything new.
3. **A row that opens from nothing should hang its content from the side it grows from.** A toast centred on its row's
   top drew BELOW the stack for the 0.2 s its row took to open (over the hotbar's gap); hung from the row's bottom, it
   rises with the stack.
4. **The pixel rule is for things, not for light that washes the screen.** A screen-wide glow drawn in steps read
   as pixel art and the user wanted the smooth one back. To drop an EditableImage, bake what it drew to a PNG
   (`Assets/ui/glow`, uploaded with `Assets/ui/upload.py`) and animate the ImageLabel's properties; keep the look.
5. **Split the clock from its drawing.** `TimerUI` requires TimeCore and a controller, so a story cannot load it; the
   drawing as a component (`runClock`) with a small Show API can be benched with a fake run, and `TimerUI` keeps its
   tested timing logic untouched. The same idea for the other three: each kept its ScreenGui and API and grew a `Root`
   for the bench.
6. **A change the player caused is quieter than one that happened to them.** The clock strikes on the run's phases
   but only flashes coming back from a pick; a strike on every pick close would fire every few seconds late in a run.

**Round 2 (2026-10-30):** the discovery toast pushed its icon panel and text 3 units down under the tab and grew its
well by 3, so everything sank and the top looked empty. Now the well is 1 unit taller than a stat toast's, the icon
panel fills it from the top as on every other card, and only the text moves: centred between the tab's bottom edge
(about 3 units into the well) and the well's bottom. **Under a tab, move the text, not the panels.**

**Round 3 (2026-10-30):** the text knock on a merge and the shake on a loss were taken out: "wobbles too much... hurts
readability". **A toast is read, so its text never moves**; a change is shown by light (the flash) only. The arrival
pop and the leave stay, since they happen before and after the reading.

**Round 4 (2026-10-30): souls are blue, the chips burn, and the streak is remade.** Souls' chip moved from Magenta to a
new `pixelSlab.Palettes.Blue` (its icon is blue). The old `StreakUI` (two tweened labels at (0.5, 0.2)) is gone:

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Components/streakMeter.luau` | The streak as a Slab hung under the chips (its bonus is souls): a STREAK tab, the count ("x24") in its own panel, "+24% souls" in the souls' blue (gold once the bonus is full), and a bar running down `StreakCore.DECAY_TIMEOUT` of GAME time (it takes `TimeCore.GetDeltaTime`, so it stops with the game, like the server's timer), red and breathing in its last second. Pops in on the first kill, knocks the count each kill (+22% on a jump of 5+), strikes on each tier (10 Red, 25 Magenta where the bonus is full, 50 Blue, 100 Green: flash, thump, rings, sparks, `ChestJump` a step higher each tier), and breaks when the streak ends (red flash, shake, the last count held 0.35 s, then the pop and a puff) |
| `Components/pixelFire.luau` | Pixel flames as a few connected TONGUES (5 crests that sway and rise, each column's height the highest crest over it) with nested layers inside, one per colour given (the chips pass three: dark edge, body, bright; no white core behind white digits), a travelling curl moving the hot layers under each crest. Heights are whole units, redrawn 24 times a second; the whole fire is one Visible switch while out. Phase comes from the palette, not `math.random`, so two fires never burn in step |
| `SelfStatsUI.luau` | Now also owns the streak: `SetStreak(n)`, called by `StatsController.SetStreak` from RewardsController's `StreakChanged` listener. Each chip burns from a streak of 10 (40%) up to 50 (full): red on kills, blue on souls, Balatro's mult and chips. The fire stands in the well, CLIPPED, behind the number only (the panels and number draw over it). Lighting bursts the flames to 2.2x and lets them fall back; each further kill FEEDS it (a short boost, refreshed, never stacked, capped at +0.3) so a horde makes it roar without burying the numbers |

**Learned:**

1. **A shove cannot make a big overshoot on a damped spring.** The lighting "whoosh" as a velocity pop peaked at only
   1.2 to 1.5 times the target however hard it was shoved (simulated: 4 gives x1.17, 12 gives x1.65), because the
   damping that settles it also eats the shove. For a burst, START the value high and let the spring fall onto the
   target.
2. **Two effects side by side share the gap between them.** The first fire also burned behind each whole Slab,
   reaching 2 units past its sides across a 3-unit gap, so the two fires met and an ember thrown into the gap crossed
   the other one (`pixelFx.SideSparks` gained `Side` for it). The fire was then reworked to stay clipped inside the
   well behind the number: a fire you read THROUGH has to stay inside its box, and nothing then crosses anything.
3. **Lifted this round:** `pixelFx.BottomSparks` (sparks off a bottom edge; the chips and the streak meter), and
   `SideSparks` gained `Left` and `Side`. `QuestsUI`'s burst is the same shape plus a spread around one point; move it
   over when it is next touched.
4. **A per-frame effect that only has to LOOK animated can step.** The fire redraws on its own sprite clock (24 Hz
   now) in whole units and writes only the columns whose height changed: it reads as pixel fire and costs a fraction
   of a 60 Hz one.
5. **Pixel fire reads as fire when its columns are CONNECTED.** Independent per-column sines looked like an equalizer.
   A few crests that each lift a run of neighbouring columns (the column takes the highest crest over it) give
   tongues; a curl shifting the hot layers sideways under the crest makes them lick.

**Round 5 (2026-10-30): feeding the kills / souls fire.** `Stories/Fire` compares an exact frozen copy of round 4
(`Before` and `pixelFireBefore`, kept inside the story) with the real current `SelfStatsUI`. Both receive the same
streak, kills and souls on the same frame. The default 10.5 s loop shows 9 -> 10 ignition, single kills, +12
multi-kills, full heat at 50, feeding beyond 50, and extinction. Turn off **Auto demo** to use the Streak slider or
Do flips; **Hold streak** freezes only the meter's game-time drain. Time scale slows both versions; Size changes the
pixel unit. The comparison stacks vertically when the two columns would not fit. `Stories/RunHud` still shows the
current counters in the full HUD composition.

- The columns now share **five moving crests** rather than flickering independently. Nested heat bands travel under
  the crests, so the tongues connect and their cores curl. They redraw at **24 Hz**, in **two-unit columns**, with
  cached heights and no per-redraw tables or Instances. Red and blue use different deterministic phases.
- The outside fire carries all four colours, including the pale hot core. Its base moved from the Slab's middle to
  **two units below its top**, so the opaque chip does not swallow the low fire. Its reach is 10 units above that
  top at full intensity before the crest envelope; the renderer caps intensity at 1.35. The inner fire stays behind
  the number, uses only the three darker colours and reaches 65% of the well.
- Ignition keeps the spring's whoosh and throws five sparks per chip. Further ability kills refresh a **non-stacking
  heat pulse** (cap 0.3, exponential decay 8/s), including beyond streak 50; a multi-kill feeds it harder. Feed sparks
  are limited to once per 0.14 s. The chip and its number keep their existing size behaviour.
- Sparks rise above each chip within its width (the review correction below). The ember accumulator is capped, so a
  hitch cannot leave a backlog. Extinction clears the feed and hides the flame **before** its redraw-rate guard:
  the old guard could miss the last zero when the owner's flame clock stopped, leaving pixels behind.

**Checked offline:** changed files linted and compiled at optimization level 2; Rojo game build. The actual renderer
was exercised with mocked Frames for 2,163 samples at 1 / 2 / 3 px units: snapped heights and X positions, bounded
reach, resize invalidation, extinction and reignition on the same sprite tick. The actual fire spring settles after
extinction. The side-spark integration's slowest launch at the longest lifetime stays outward and upward. Repository
checks still report pre-existing formatting and Selene issues outside these files. **Not played or visually judged
in Studio; the comparison is ready for that review.**

**Round 5 review: keep the fire over the chip.** The screenshot showed the crown hanging past the side outlines.
The outside flame is now inset one pixel unit on both sides, instead of extending two units beyond them. Ambient,
ignition and feed embers launch vertically from the middle half of each chip, above the flame, with no horizontal
velocity. They keep their smooth fade and light upward pull. `Stories/Fire` keeps the original Before and shows
this correction in After. Checked flame bounds and ember travel offline, linted, compiled and built; not replayed

**Round 5 final direction: the fire belongs INSIDE the number wells.** The chips sit near the screen's top, so

including their pools' flame-related spawn paths and tuning. The remaining red / blue tongues climb behind the

that fire. Its three colour bands exclude white, and the existing clipped well contains the overshoot beneath the

above. `Stories/Fire` keeps the original Before and uses this inside-only version for After. Linted, compiled and

**Inside-fire colour review:** the screenshot contained all three bands, but the bright kills band was amber
(`255, 170, 40`), so it still read as orange. It is now warm yellow (`255, 222, 88`), distinct from the red edge and
orange body. The blue souls palette and the clipped geometry are unchanged. Linted, compiled and built; not

**Colour follow-up:** the yellow was too strong. The bright kills band is now a softer peach-gold
(`255, 194, 100`), between the original amber and that yellow. Linted and compiled; not visually replayed in Studio.

**Code review against CLAUDE.md:** the accepted look is unchanged. The flame pool now derives its column count
from the number well's width (38 units / 2 per column = 19), rather than reserving 32 columns per chip. That reduces
the two chips' flame Frames from 192 to 114. The renderer visits only the active prefix; layout still hides any

including the final settling frame. The 24 Hz fire no longer forces unchanged scales, colours and hidden sheen rows
to be written every render frame. The remaining fire field is named `Fire`, and the header is two lines.

**Verified offline:** 3,600 before/after comparisons of visible UI properties at 1 / 2 / 3 px units, using the actual
counter, fire, pixelSlab, pixelFx and spring modules with mocked Instances and a stub streak meter. Gains, spends,
100-kill milestones, ignition, multi-kill feed and extinction matched; the clock disconnected after settling.
Steady burning made 0 chip-chrome assignments over 120 simulated frames instead of 5,280 (44 per frame). This
counts attempted property assignments, not GPU work or live frame time. Linted, compiled and built; not replayed
or profiled in Studio. No claim of absolute optimality or measured FPS gain.

**Round 6 (2026-11-01): the overtime bonus, Megabonk's final swarm.** Past 00:00 the clock turns into a tickets and
stardust multiplier that the run really pays (`RunScoringCore.GetOvertimeMultiplier`, applied in `RunScoringService`
on both payouts, listed as "Overtime xN" on the end screen). x1.00 at the run's end, climbing in a straight line to
`OVERTIME_MAX_MULTIPLIER` (2, RunScoring's `OvertimeMaxMultiplier` on the dashboard, clamped to x5) at the
overdrive wall, 4:40 in, then holding (the base payout freezes at that same wall, so nothing grows past it);
a hundredth every 2.8 s at x2. Infinite never unfolds and pays none. `runClock.ShowBonus(multiplier, share)`:

- **It grows sideways, never down**: the quest column starts at 0.07 of the screen, right under the clock. The Slab
  unfolds 64 -> 94 units on an underdamped spring (1.6 Hz, 0.55: +3.7 units of overshoot, settled in ~0.5 s); the
  time keeps a 36-unit panel on the left (a pick's countdown still shows there, with its bar) and the bonus takes the
  right (no ink seam between them: the user read it as a stray black bar): the ticket over the stardust, the multiplier, and the ramp's bar.
- **It snaps between 00:00 and +00:01** (the user's correction: it first unfolded after "+" numbers were showing).
  TimerUI starts the bonus as the clock reads 00:00, the unfold lands 0.45 s later (white flash, big rings, sparks in
  the tickets' and stardust's colours, the icons spinning in, the number slamming down from +140%), and overtime
  arriving on the next second only flashes.
- **The bezel walks Megabonk's gradient**: a quarter of the ramp each, Green, Blue, Magenta, Red, then Gold at the
  max, each a strike and a `ChestJump` a step higher; the max adds `ScoreComplete` and a sheen every 2.2 s. The bar
  runs the same gradient with a breathing head pixel; the outline breathes in the tier's light (the red screen tint
  still says danger).
- **Each hundredth** knocks the number (+7%) and the icons, and ticks `TicketTick` / `StardustTick` in turn, pitched
  up the ramp. Motes drift off the sides, 0.8 a second rising to 5 at the max (checked in lune: never back toward the
  Slab, never down).

Bench: `Stories/RunHud` ("skip to +1:08 / +3:28 / +4:36", "Overtime max"). Linted, compiled, both places built with
Rojo, the ramp, springs and motes checked in lune. **Not played in Studio and not yet judged on the bench.**

## Last Wave: what the clock, toast and streak rounds taught (2026-10-30)

On top of the per-round notes above. Linted, compiled (every UI file), the place built with Rojo; **not played in
Studio**, and the bench only seen by the user.

### Shape and look: what the user corrected

1. **Smooth light stays smooth.** The pixel rule ("light is STEPPED") is for the things on the HUD, not for a glow
   that washes the screen: the stepped Frame version of the pick glow was rejected for the old soft one. Drop an
   EditableImage by BAKING what it drew (`Assets/ui/glow`, uploaded with `Assets/ui/upload.py`, the image id resolved
   with `InsertService:LoadAsset(decalId)` in Studio's command bar) and animating the ImageLabel's properties.
2. **Text that is read does not move.** The toasts' merge knock and loss shake were taken out ("wobbles too much,
   hurts readability"). Moving gestures go on arrival and leave, and on things that are glanced at (a count); a line
   of words changes by light only.
3. **Under a tab, move the text, not the panels.** The discovery toast pushed its icon panel down with its text and
   the whole card sank. Panels fill the well from the top on every card; only the text centres below the tab.
4. **Colour matches the art.** Souls' chip was Magenta because the altar is; the souls icon is blue. Check the icon
   before giving a counter its palette.
5. **Where a notice sits decides if it is read** (round 1 here): map what covers the screen on a phone (buttons and
   thumbs right, thumbstick left, Roblox's buttons at the top corners) before placing anything that must be read.

### Cost

- Everything pushed every frame returns early when nothing it draws changed (`runClock.Show*`, the chips' draw gate,
  the fire's per-column `Shown` heights, the glow's Heartbeat connected only while it shows or fades).
- The clock sleeps at rest except for warnings meant to be seen: the clock's last 10 s and overtime breath (not in
  Infinite), the streak bar while a streak lives, the fire while it burns.
- 2 x 19 x 3 fire Frames (two chips, 19 columns, three colours: no white core behind white digits) exist for the
  whole run, hidden behind one `Visible` while out.

### Readability: what was lifted, and what is still copied

- **Lifted this round:** `pixelFx.BottomSparks` (chips, streak), `pixelFx.Puff` (the quest card's leave and the
  streak's break), `pixelSlab.FitWidth` (Silkscreen sized to fit a width, counting characters; the clock, both
  chips, the streak count, the quest card's name and number, Color Dance's lines and number), `pixelSlab.Palettes.Blue`,
  and `SideSparks`' `Left` / `Side`. The six `Advance = 0.72` copies are gone; the number lives in `pixelSlab`.
- **Still copied, and now past the lift rule:** the ARRIVAL (a scale spring from about -0.5 or -0.18, plus a drop on
  some) and the LEAVE (`LeaveScale` over about 0.22 s, then hide / close / destroy) are in eight elements: the quest
  card, Color Dance, banners, the lock ribbon, toasts, the streak meter, `rewardCard`, `inspectCard`. They differ in
  what the end does and in the arrival's numbers, so the lift is a small `pixelMotion.Presence` (`Arrive(from)`,
  `Leave(onDone)`, `Step(dt) -> scale, busy`) that each element calls from its own step; do it in its own round, with
  the bench open, because it touches shipped screens.
- `QuestsUI`'s burst (sparks round one point) is `BottomSparks` with a spread; move it over when it is next touched.
- The older debt stands: `actionButton`, `abilitySlot`, `touchButton`, `statusTile` build their own Slab.

### Process

- **Files change under you between turns** (the user, or another session, reworked the fire). Read the current file
  before describing or editing it; never write UI.md from memory of what you built.
- **A scratch script can vanish between turns**: recreate the compile helper rather than assuming it is there.
- **Exact-text edits, asserted once, then compile**, again caught nothing wrong this time; keep doing it.

## Last Wave: the inventory and stats screen (`infoScreen`, `inspectCard`, built 2026-10-30)

Asked for: the inventory and stats in the new style, as juicy as it can be, and a way to read each weapon's, item's
and passive's own name, description and numbers on PC (hover) and on phones (tap), like BeACastleLord's pack card.
The old screen showed only the character's totals, so a weapon's real Damage / Size / Attack Speed was nowhere.
Bench `Stories/Inventory`. Thirteen rounds of screenshots, all on size, spacing, input and the hover / number
styling; the motion and the juice were never sent back. Linted, compiled, the place built with Rojo. **Not played in Studio by me**; the user judged it in play.

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Components/infoScreen.luau` | The whole screen as drawing only (no Cores, so a story mounts it): INVENTORY panel left, STATS right, card and brackets between. Fed through `SetSlot` / `SetUnlocked` / `SetItems` / `AddStat` / `SetStat` / `MarkSeen` |
| `Components/inventorySlot.luau` | One Slab slot: kind palette (weapon Amber, passive Violet, augment Teal, item its rarity), level number in a gap cut from the corner (`MAX` in pink at the cap, small-x `x3` for item stacks), lift + icon pop under the hand, deal-in, strike; outline white when hovered or linked |
| `Components/inspectCard.luau` | The card: kind tab, icon, name, `LV 3/10` (pink at the cap), description typed out, zebra stat lines sliding in. Follows the hand on springs; a new thing lands with a flash, a +7% punch and the icon popping from half size; the same `Key` again only refreshes |
| `Components/focusBrackets.luau` | BeACastleLord's focus marker (5m) in Frames: four L corners, leading corners on a quicker spring, arrive from outside, breathe, pinch on press, linger 0.14 s |
| `InfoUI/init.luau` | Mounts the screen in a ScreenGui (`CoreUISafeInsets`), runs `Stats` then `Inventory` then `MarkSeen` |
| `InfoUI/Inventory.luau`, `InfoUI/Stats.luau` | The feeders: the old signals, now building slot entries (`Key`, `Look`, `Links`, `GetCard`) and stat defs. `InfoUI/StatText.luau` prints every number for both |
| `Controllers/InfoController.luau` | Frees the mouse while open (restored on close unless a reward pick opened over it), pushes pad focus, B closes |

### What it does

- **The card answers "what does this do for me".** A weapon lists its own computed stats (`WeaponsCore.GetStatComputed`
  for each `BasePassives` key; a multiplier stat whose weapon base is not 1, like Damage 2 or Size 20, prints as a
  plain number). A passive: its total and what the next level adds (Armor / Evasion through the diminishing curve, like
  the upgrade cards). An item: `formatItemDescription`, its rarity (Godly reads Divine) and count. A **stat row** is
  inspectable too: its total plus every owned weapon's own value of it.
- **Links.** Inspecting a thing lights the stat rows it scales with (weapon `BasePassives`, augment `Synergies`
  filtered to passive ids, item `Stats`) in its own colour; inspecting a stat lights the slots that feed it.
- **What changed since the last look is shown changing.** On open, slots whose key (`<id>:<level>` / `<id>:<count>`)
  differs from the last open strike one after another, and stat rows roll from the value last seen, green up / red
  down with a punch. `MarkSeen()` after the first feed keeps the starting loadout from striking.
- **Opening** swings the panels in from their sides (stats a beat behind), dims the world to 0.5, deals the slots in
  row by row with a rising `ChestItemCycle` step, and cascades the stat rows in.
- **Input.** Mouse and pad: the card follows the hover / selection only; a click does nothing extra. Touch: `MouseEnter`
  is ignored (a tap fires it and never `MouseLeave`); a tap picks, and a tap on the same thing, the card, a panel's
  empty space or anywhere else puts it away. Hovering along a row of slots plays `HoverHud` a step higher per slot.

### What the rounds taught, as a checklist for the next card or panel

Every correction here was spacing, size or input. Run this list BEFORE showing a screen; it is the seven rounds.

| # | The user said | The rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | "make it bigger, take more space, icons bigger, text more readable" | **Start big.** A full-screen menu uses unit 4 at 1080 (slots 72 px, body text ~18 px), not the HUD's 3. Then cap the unit so everything side by side fits the WIDTH (`fitUnit`: the units across plus margins, `floor(width * 0.96 / across)`), floor 2 for phones, and let a column taller than 0.9 of the screen scroll. Check 1920x1080, 1366x768 and an 844x390 phone in `lune` before sending |
| 2 | "it comes back to where I clicked when I don't hover anything" | **A click is not a hover.** On mouse and pad the card follows the hand and nothing else; only TOUCH picks (`GetLastInputType() == Touch` at `Activated`). A pick needs a way off on every surface: the thing again, the card, the panel's empty space (a `Catch` TextButton at ZIndex 0 under the content) and the world (a full-screen `Catch` shown ONLY while a pick exists, so it never eats the thumbstick) |
| 3 | "the little squares for levels are unnecessary, levels go to the hundreds" | **No pips or per-unit marks for anything unbounded.** `LV 3/10`, pink at the cap. Check the late-game range of every number before drawing it as marks |
| 4 | "why does the image have a line on top" | **No decoration that is not on every sibling.** A lit row on a bare icon box (no outline of its own) read as a stray line. The Slab's lit / shade rows belong to Slabs only |
| 5 | "does it keep clear of Roblox's top-left bar like the level-up and reward screens" | **Full-screen menus use `ScreenInsets = CoreUISafeInsets`** (with `IgnoreGuiInset` and `ClipToDeviceSafeArea = false`), like UpgradeUI / RewardUI. A dim Frame must then overhang the safe area (`Size = UDim2.new(1, 1000, 1, 1000)`, centred) or the top bar stays undimmed |
| 6 | "too much space at the top just for the tab", "a little space at the bottom" (card, then both panels) | **Clearance is computed from what it clears, never a fixed depth.** The tab's bottom in the well is `round(p/2) + round(tabH/2) - 2p`; text that runs under the tab starts 1 unit below that. Things the tab is NOT over (the icon at the left) start at the side padding (3 units). Bottoms: 1 unit under a list of rows, 3 under slots (their chip hangs 1 unit below and they lift). An empty section ends under its header, without the gap its content would have had |
| 7 | "no need for separations between categories, it reads as blank space" | **No blank gaps between groups in a list.** Order carries the grouping; zebra rows carry the rhythm |
| 8 | "this x should be little, like in descriptions" | **Every `x` after a number is small**, everywhere: rich text `<font size="N">x</font>`, and N is ABSOLUTE, so compute it from the label's own TextSize sum (0.65 of it), not from the label after layout (paint can run before layout sets TextSize). Pass counts as data (`Count`) and let the drawer format them |

| 9 | "the scrollbar of the panel doesn't go with the theme" | **Never the engine's ScrollingFrame bar.** `ScrollBarThickness = 0` and the project's `GlobalClient/UI/Components/scrollbar` (draggable, hides itself when nothing overflows), required RELATIVELY (it pulls `InputTypeController`). Style its container as an ink track and its `ScrollbarThumb` as a Slab (fill, lit top row, shaded bottom row), sized in units in the layout. `HideGamepadHint` where a pad walks the items instead of scrolling with the stick |
| 10 | "the little number looks bad", then (after a boxed badge) "I liked how it was removing the strokes and infusing the number there, remove the little box" | **A slot's number sits in a GAP cut out of its bottom-right corner, never in a box of its own.** The gap is painted the panel's background (`pixelSlab.WellColor`), not ink: ink only read as a gap while the outline was ink, and the outline turns white on hover. It starts a unit past the corner so the shadow is cut with the outline. White digits with an ink stroke (MAX pink), TextSize 0.28 of the slot, the gap 0.6 of that plus a unit above and below, its width from the characters (`Advance` 0.72, a small x as 0.65 of one). A boxed, filled badge with a lit row was tried and rejected |
| 11 | "the darker stats don't change on hover" | **A hover must not depend on a background a row may not have.** Zebra rows had a colour to change, the rest were transparent: a hover sets the colour AND the transparency, and puts both back by the row's own parity |
| 12 | "the white stroke was for the inventory, not the stats; a slot lit by a hovered stat should use it instead of another stroke" | **Under the hand, and linked to what is under the hand, is the slot's OWN outline turning white**: never a second ring drawn round it (it costs space and doubles the edge). The brackets are white too. A hovered stat ROW only changes its background (every row, zebra or not); it gets no outline and no brackets |

Also from this round, not corrections but worth keeping:

- **The run locks the mouse to the centre** (`CameraController.LockCamera`). Any screen meant to be hovered must
  unlock it and show the cursor on open, and restore on close, the way `RewardsController` does; skip the restore if
  a reward pick opened on top (it owns the camera now).
- **A selected GuiObject eats the DPad**, so a screen's own DPad toggle cannot close it once a pad has focus: push a
  B handler with `GamepadFocusController.PushBack`, and `PushFocus` / `PopFocus` around the screen.
- **Split drawing from data** (`infoScreen` vs `InfoUI/Inventory` / `Stats`), with entries that carry a `GetCard`
  closure: the card is built only when shown, always fresh, and the bench feeds the same component with made-up data.
- **Files got committed mid-build** between turns (`b7271ed` held the new `Inventory.luau` with the old `init.luau`).
  When a session is cut off, finish the pieces that make the tree consistent first, and tell the user what is broken
  at which commit.

### Cost

- **Idle is asleep:** the screen's tick runs only while panels move, rows reveal, a roll / punch / flash runs or a
  strike waits; the brackets breathe only while they frame something; the card only while it moves or types.
- **Only what moves is written:** in the per-frame row loop, a row reformats its value only when its roll spring
  stepped, and rescales only when its punch stepped (the first build wrote all ~30 rows every frame of any animation).
  Slots repaint behind a look key; the card is re-read on a stat change at most once a frame (`task.defer` gate).
- **Not done:** `paintLinkColor` rewrites every row's link colour on each new shown thing (~60 writes per hover
  change, not per frame); fine at this size.

- **Nothing is written that cannot change:** the brackets' arms are built white and `Target` takes no colour (it
  used to repaint eight Frames to the same white on every hover).

### Process: run every tool from the REPO ROOT

`stylua` and `selene` find `stylua.toml` / `selene.toml` by walking up from the CURRENT DIRECTORY, not from the file.
Run from a subfolder (the shell's cwd had drifted into `Components/`), StyLua silently formatted with its defaults
and expanded every one-line guard clause into three lines (looked like "someone else reformatted it"), and Selene
parsed Luau types as errors (`unexpected token type`, 175 "parse errors") or panicked in its tokenizer while still
printing "0 errors". **`cd` to the repo root (or use absolute paths from it) before every lint / format / compile**,
and treat a Selene panic or a sudden parse-error count as "wrong directory" before anything else.

### Readability: what is still not as clean as it could be

- `Tune.CardUnits` in `infoScreen` copies `inspectCard`'s width (112) to fit the screen; keep them in step, or expose
  the width from `inspectCard` if a second user appears.
- The kind palettes (weapon Amber, passive Violet, augment Teal) were lifted into `pixelSlab.Kinds` when the end screen
  became their second user; `InfoUI/Inventory` reads them from there. The stories still paste their own copy.
- The ARRIVAL / LEAVE copies (see the previous section's debt) now include `inspectCard` and `focusBrackets`.

## Last Wave: the end screen (`finalScreen`, built 2026-10-30, unjudged)

Asked for: the game over / win screen in the new style, as juicy as it can be, with variants to pick from where a
choice is open. The problem it had: the leaderboard's run card (`runView`, lobby) showed MORE about a run than the
end screen did (every player's weapons and passives with levels, augments, trait, items), and the end screen's
buttons and banners covered the screen. A player asked for the leaderboard's stats on the end screen. **The first
thing a player sees must be the ranking among the players.** Bench `Stories/FinalStats`. Linted, compiled, Blink
regenerated, the place built with Rojo. **Not played in Studio and not judged on the bench.**

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Components/finalScreen.luau` | The whole screen as drawing only (no Core, so a story mounts it): title, the run's facts, the RANKING board, the chosen player's run card, the buttons. `Show(run)`, `Hide()`, `SetAvatar`, `SetVote`, `ClearVotes`, `SetCanRevive`, `SetDetailsMode("Tabs" or "Scroll")`, `FirstFocus()`, `Scroll` (for the pad's stick) |
| `FinalStatsUI.luau` | The feeder: the same API as before for `FinalStatsController`. Turns the packets into a `TRun` (names, `DataCore` icons, kind and rarity palettes, `RunStatsCore` labels, `BestsCore` records, facts, the death line), fetches headshots, attaches `gamepadScroll`, focuses Restart for a pad |
| `blink/Server/FinalStats.blink` | New `FinalStatsBuild`: per player, trait id, weapon ids + levels, passive ids + levels, augment ids, item ids + counts (data ids in pick order, not names) |
| `FinalStatsService` / `RunScoringService` | `RunScoringService.GetSnapshot` (the leaderboard snapshot) is exposed, and the service sends each player's build from it, so the end screen and `runView` show the same build |
| `pixelSlab.Kinds` | The kind palettes, lifted (second user) |

### What it does

- **First: the ranking.** The title drops in (Red "GAME OVER" with a low thud; Gold "RUN COMPLETE!" with sparks and
  `ChestJump`), the facts sit under it as chips (survived, level, the payout multipliers, a Red "KILLED BY ..." first
  on a loss, the tip below). The RANKING board deals its rows in one by one. Then the old reveal runs, category by
  category, now in the board's strip ("DAMAGE DEALT", popping in, a progress bar under it): each row's points bar fills
  against the leader's, the rows **re-sort live and slide past each other** (an overtake flashes the row, knocks it +4%
  and ticks `HoverHud` higher the higher it climbs), and each row's tickets and stardust roll up with its share of the
  points (the ticket glyph lights as it gains). A hold anywhere runs it at the fast pace, rows included.
- **Final results:** the category strip goes and the rows glide up into its room; the winner's row strikes (gold flash,
  +9% thump, rings, sparks, `ChestJump`), the local player's row flashes if it did not win. The scoring and the ticket split are the old ones
  (`RunStatsCore` Points, floor to 0.01, tickets by share of the player's own points, snapped to the server's total).
- **Then the run card.** After 1.1 s the board slides left and the card swings in beside it on the local player. Its
  tab is the player's name in their rank's colour. A row is a button now: click / tap / A on another row to read that
  player (the card bounces and its slots deal in again). The selected row's outline is white; a hovered one, its Light.
- **The card's three pages:** BUILD (weapons, passives, augments, trait, items as `inventorySlot`s with level and count
  chips, dealt in one after another; hover, or tap on a phone, prints the name and level under the card), STATS (every
  per-player stat, zebra rows sliding in, a Gold BEST chip on a personal record, a Green TOP chip where the player led
  the party), DAMAGE (each weapon and augment with its icon, damage, share and a share bar).
- **Buttons** are text Slabs at the bottom centre: RESTART (Gold, with the party's headshots inside it lighting as they
  vote; a vote knocks it), MAIN MENU (Grey), REVIVE (Green, gone on a win or once bought). Hover lifts, a press sinks,
  a click flashes and thumps.

### The open question on the bench (answered)

Tabs or one scroll for the run card: the user judged and built on Tabs for four rounds (LB / RB turn them), so the
Scroll layout and its dropdown were deleted in the review round. The card is three tabs: BUILD, STATS, DAMAGE.

### What was learned

1. **"Integrate everything" is a reading order, not one sheet.** The old screen's problem was not too little space but
   showing everyone's everything at once (a 5-column table). One screen can hold all of it when it is staged: the
   ranking first (what everyone wants), then ONE player's card at a time, chosen from the ranking itself.
2. **A row of buttons over the reveal eats the hold.** Rows are buttons, so a press on them arrives `processed`, and the
   old `if processed then return end` would have stopped the speed-up exactly where the eye is. Only a key typed into a
   box is skipped now.
3. **The build was never on the client.** The game place had damage per weapon but not the build; the leaderboard's
   snapshot already gathered it on the server. Send what the other surface already gathers (`GetSnapshot`), as ids.
4. **Blink output is committed RAW.** StyLua on `Network.luau` turned a 900-line diff into 25,000. The Meta network
   regenerates with StyLua formatting differences only, so restore it when its `.blink` did not change.

### Not done / debt

- The button and page-tab Slab (`newButton` in `finalScreen`) is a text button the lobby will want; lift it with its
  second user. `actionButton` is an icon button and does not fit text.
- Leaving is plain: the panels hide and the dim fades. Rows could puff out.
- The client's placement uses the old floor-to-0.01 formula and breaks ties by order; the server's `computePlacements`
  does not floor and breaks ties by damage. Same as before; rare ties can disagree.

### Round 2 (2026-10-30): the slots, the size, the centring, the chips

| The user said | What was wrong | The fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "fix the build window" (slots cut off, under the headers) | `inventorySlot` centres its body in its own button, and the button was never given a size, so every slot drew half a slot up and left | Size the slot's `UI` (`size x size`) as `infoScreen` does. **A component that centres its body in its own button needs the button sized** |
| "plenty of space at the bottom middle, make it bigger on x and y" | The unit was capped at 4 per 1080 (3 on the bench) and the panels were only as tall as five rows | Cap 6 per 1080, then fit to width and height (bench 3 to 4, 1080p 5). Both panels fill the height down to the hint; rows grow from 17 to 22 units to fill the board, their words with them; the card takes the width left (176 to 230 units) |
| "the ranking entries are not centred" | Rows were centred on the board's width, but they live in its well (4 units narrower) | Centre on the well. Vertically, the rows sit in the middle of the room left |

| "BEST and TOP look relatively bad" | Ink letters with no outline on a bare colour box, crammed into a 7-unit row, with a gap to a right-aligned value | Rows 9 units, text 5. The chip is an outlined plate with its own lit row (a full bezel leaves no room for letters at this height), white letters with ink, all chips one width, sitting right against the value's text |
| "the panels have padding top and bottom that could be used" | A fixed 7-unit top under the tab | Content starts a unit under the tab's bottom (UI.md inventory rule 6); empty build sections are left out; the scrollbar shows only when the page scrolls |

Also from the inventory checklist: `ScreenInsets = CoreUISafeInsets` with the dim overhanging it, and the bonus `2x` with a
small `x`. Checked in `lune` at 1519x853, 1920x1080, 1366x768, 844x390 and 2560x1440: everything fits, the panels end
above the buttons. Linted, compiled, built; **not replayed in Studio**.

### Round 3 (2026-10-30): header, middle, footer; nothing that says nothing

| The user said | What was wrong | The fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "TOP and BEST should not have shadows, they should be IN it" | A drop shadow lifts a badge off the row it belongs to | Badges set into a row have no shadow |
| "on mobile the buttons are on top of the panels; header, middle, footer" | The board had a minimum height (five rows) that won over the room left | **The middle band is a hard box**: panels end above the hint and buttons whatever happens; rows shrink (17 down to 12 units) before the board may grow past it |
| "the ranking's space on top and bottom looks awful" | The board filled the height and centred three rows in it | The board is as tall as its rows (a unit under the last, under the tab's clearance); only the run card fills the height |

| (the category strip, round 2) | It took a band of the board for the race only | The race names its category in the board's own tab, popping on each; back to RANKING at the end |
| "the damage page has no stylised bars nor strokes round the images" | Flat frames where everything else is a Slab | Icons in small Slabs of their kind's colour; the share is a vitals-style bar (ink outline, trough, fill with a lit and a shaded row) |
| "the scrollbar does not go with the theme" | The engine's bar | Rule 9: the project's `scrollbar`, ink track, gold Slab thumb |
| "padding at the bottom just to name what you hover; hover and click effects are clipped and tell nothing" | The slot lift was clipped by the scroll frame, and the hint only repeated the icon | **If a hover gives no information the screen does not already show, there is no hover**: the card's slots take no input, and the hint line is gone |

Linted, compiled, built; **not replayed in Studio**.

### Round 4 (2026-10-30): the inspect card under the ranking

Asked for: the inventory's hover information in the free space at the bottom left, for anything any player had, and
fine with five players.

- **`inspectCard` lives in a zone the size of the left column** (under the board's left and right edges, from the panels'
  top to the footer). It sits on the zone's bottom, centred under the board, and grows upward. With one to three
  players it fits under the ranking. With five it would not: its card (about 60 units with two lines) is taller than
  what the rows leave, so it rises over the ranking's last rows. That was chosen over shrinking five rows to 12 units
  for good, since the card is up only while the hand is on a slot. It never goes below the footer.
- **What a card says for ANY player** (built in `FinalStatsUI`, carried on each `TBuildSlot.Card`):
  - Kind, name, `LV x/max`, and the description.
  - For items: the rarity and count, and `formatItemDescription` at that player's build when their character is
    still in the world.
  - For weapons and augments: **damage dealt and its share of the player's damage**. The inventory's live computed
    stats exist only for the local character, so they are not shown here. The run's damage is known for everyone.
- **Input is the inventory's (rule 2):**
  - Mouse and pad follow the hover and the selection only.
  - Only a tap picks. The same slot, the card or anywhere else puts it away: a full-screen `Catch` under everything,
    shown only while a pick exists.
  - Hovering along a row plays `HoverHud` a step higher per column.
  - Switching player or page, and leaving, puts the card away.
- Slots are a unit in from the scroll's edges, so their 10% lift is not clipped.

Linted, compiled, built; **not replayed in Studio**.

### Round 5 (2026-10-30): pad, phone, and the inventory's brackets

- **`focusBrackets` (the inventory's marker)** frames:
  - a slot under the mouse, a slot a tap picked, and anything a pad selects (slots, ranking rows, page tabs, buttons).
  - Slot presses pinch it. It re-reads its target when the page scrolls, and lets go of a slot scrolled out of view.
  - A rebuild of the card (another player, another page) only takes it off a slot, never off the row or button the
    pad is on.
- **No engine selection box anywhere**: every selectable wears an empty `SelectionImageObject`. Pad selection drives
  the same hover look (rows light their outline, buttons lift) plus the brackets and a `HoverHud` tick.
- **A rebuild keeps the pad's place.** Destroying the selected slot leaves a pad nowhere (the reference memory on grid
  rebuilds), so when the selection was in the card it moves to the new page's first slot, or to that page's tab.
- **LB / RB turn the card's pages** (Tabs mode, after the reveal), with the tab's press flash and thump.
- **Phones press, never hover**: `MouseEnter` is ignored on touch everywhere. A tap on a slot picks it (card and
  brackets) until the same slot, the card or anything else is tapped. Rows and buttons act on the tap.

Linted, compiled, built; **not replayed in Studio, and not tried with a real pad or phone**.


### Pad selection everywhere (2026-10-30)

- `pixelMotion`, `pixelSlab` and `focusBrackets` moved from `Survivors/Client/UI/Components` to
  `Global/Client/UI/Components`, so the lobby can draw the same brackets. Require them by the
  `StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts.GlobalClient.UI.Components` path.
- `cornerSelector` no longer draws the engine's 9-slice box. It returns an empty frame (the `SelectionImageObject` every
  button, grid item, text box and selectable scroll frame wears) and a `FocusBrackets` ScreenGui frames
  `GuiService.SelectedObject` with `focusBrackets` while that object wears it. A screen with its own marker (the
  inventory, the final stats) sets its own empty `SelectionImageObject` and is skipped, so nothing is framed twice.
- Linted and formatted; **not replayed in Studio** (lobby and run pad navigation both need a look).

### Review round (2026-10-30): what was optimised, and what is left

- **The race wrote everything every frame.** While anything moved, every row built three strings (`FormatShort` twice)
  and wrote ten properties, and the tick rewrote every button, tab, the title and both panels. Now:
  - A row compares rounded numbers before building any string.
  - Its position, scale and flash are written only when that spring stepped or that flash was lit (one more write as a
    flash ends, so it lands fully out).
  - Buttons write scale only while their springs move and flash only while lit; the title, the tab pop, the dim and the
    panels' slide likewise.
  - Stardust visibility is set once at show.
  - A layout (and a resize, which snaps the rows) redraws every row in full, because **a snapped spring reports no
    movement**: a resize that snapped rows to new places after the layout drew them would have left them where they
    were.
- **Moving a call into a function that sits above its definition is a runtime error, not a lint nicety.** `layoutAll`
  started calling `drawRow`, defined further down; Selene's `undefined_variable` caught it. Run Selene after every move.
- **Deleted:** the Scroll layout, `SetDetailsMode`, the story's dropdown, the row's string cache and `setText`.
- **Left, on purpose:**
  - **The file is ~2,150 lines in one constructor.** The clean split is the run card (pages, slots, the inspect card, its
    input and pad focus) into `runCard`, leaving the screen with the title, the race, the buttons and the brackets. It
    shares the brackets and the touch catch with the rest, so it needs a small interface
    (`FrameTarget(gui?)`, `OnPick`); do it as its own round with the bench open.
  - `newButton` (a text Slab button) and `placeLine` (a line fitted to a box) are still inside `finalScreen`. Each has
    one user; lift them with their second (the lobby will want the button).
  - The client's placement still floors to 0.01 and breaks ties by order, unlike the server's `computePlacements`.

## Last Wave: what the end screen rounds taught (2026-10-30)

Five rounds of screenshots, then a review. Linted, compiled and built every round; **never played in Studio, and not
tried on a real pad or phone**. The checklist below is on top of the inventory's (that section's table): run both
before showing a screen.

| # | The user said | The rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | "the first impression should be a ranking", "integrate everything without clutter" | **Stage a screen that has to say everything.** What everyone wants first (the ranking), then ONE player's detail at a time, picked from the ranking itself. A table of everyone's everything is what "clutter" means |
| 2 | "fix the build window" (slots drawn half a slot up and left) | **A component that centres its body inside its own button needs the button sized.** `inventorySlot.UI` is `size x size`; read how the component's first user places it before using it |
| 3 | "plenty of space at the bottom, make it bigger on x and y" | **Fit the unit to the screen, not to a cap.** Cap 6 per 1080, then the largest unit at which the whole column and both panels fit (bench 3 to 4, 1080p 5). Check five sizes in `lune` (1519x853, 1920x1080, 1366x768, 844x390, 2560x1440) |
| 4 | "on mobile the buttons are on top of the panels: header, middle, footer" | **The middle band is a hard box.** Compute the header's bottom and the footer's top first; panels live between and NEVER past them. When content does not fit, the content shrinks (rows 17 to 12 units) or scrolls; a minimum height that wins over the room is the bug |
| 5 | "the ranking's space on top and bottom looks awful" | **A list's panel is as tall as its list.** Filling a panel with three centred rows reads as empty. Only the panel whose content scrolls fills the height |
| 6 | "the ranking entries are not centred" | **Children of a Slab live in its WELL**, 4 units narrower than the body. Centre on the well |
| 7 | "FINAL RESULTS inside RANKING is unnecessary" | **A label that has said its piece goes.** The race names its category in the board's own TAB (popping per category), so it never needed a band of its own |
| 8 | "the little bar under the name, I don't know what it is" | **An unlabelled bar is noise.** If its meaning is not written next to it, remove it |
| 9 | "the level should say lvl, a bare number can't be read" (it was the score) | **Every number carries its word** (`22 PTS`, `LV 3/10`). The user misread an unlabelled score as a level: the bug is the screen's, not the reader's |
| 10 | "BEST and TOP look bad", then "no shadows, they should be IN it" | **A badge set into a row is an outlined plate in the row** (fill, lit row in its well, white letters with ink, no drop shadow), all badges one width, right against the value's text. At 7-unit rows a full bezel leaves no room for letters: make the row taller (9) or drop the bezel |
| 11 | "the damage panel has no stylised bars nor strokes round the images" | **Every image sits in a Slab of its kind's colour; every bar is a vitals bar** (ink outline, trough, fill with a lit and a shaded row). A flat Frame next to Slabs reads as unfinished |
| 12 | "the scrollbar doesn't go with the theme" | Inventory rule 9 again: the project's `scrollbar`, never the engine's |
| 13 | "padding just to name what you hover; hover effects are clipped and tell nothing" | **No hover that tells nothing new.** A hover earns its place only with information the screen does not already show; otherwise the thing takes no input. And keep a unit of air inside a scroll frame so a 10% lift is not clipped |
| 14 | "add hover information in the free space at the bottom left, fine with 5 players" | **An info card goes in a ZONE**: the free column, sitting on its bottom, growing up, never past the footer. When it does not fit (five rows), it rises over the list only while shown rather than shrinking the list for good. Say which trade was made |
| 15 | (round 4) cards for OTHER players | **Show what the run knows for everyone.** Live computed stats exist only for the local character; the run's damage per weapon and augment exists for all. Never show the local player's richer card for some and a poorer one for others without saying so |
| 16 | "controller navigation good, mobile presses, the inventory's selection arrows" | **Every selectable wears an empty `SelectionImageObject`** and shows its own hover look on `SelectionGained`; `focusBrackets` frame slots on hover / tap and anything a pad selects. **A rebuild under a pad moves the selection** to the new first item (or the page's tab) before the old one is destroyed. Shoulders turn tabs. Touch never hovers |

### What a screen like this is built from, now

- `pixelSlab` (Body, Tab, Letters, FitWidth, `Kinds`, palettes), `pixelFx` (Particles, Rings, Sheen, SideSparks),
  `pixelMotion` (springs, the clock), `inventorySlot` (slots, with their number in a gap), `inspectCard` (the info
  card, placed with `Show(entry, x, y, side, boundsHeight)` inside any zone), `focusBrackets` (the marker),
  `GlobalClient/UI/Components/scrollbar` (themed), `uiSound`.
- **Drawing only, fed by a wrapper** (`finalScreen` / `FinalStatsUI`, like `infoScreen` / `InfoUI`): the bench mounts
  the drawing with made-up data and the wrapper owns `DataCore`, localisation, avatars, `GamepadFocusController`
  and `gamepadScroll`.

### Process

- **Check the five screen sizes in `lune` after any layout change**, from the same formulas the layout uses. The phone
  overlap of round 3 came from a `fitUnit` estimate that no longer matched the layout; derive one from the other or
  re-check both.
- **The server may not have sent what the screen needs.** The game place never had the build; the leaderboard's
  snapshot already gathered it (`RunScoringService.GetSnapshot`). Look for the surface that already gathers the data
  before adding a gatherer.
- **Blink output is committed raw**: regenerate, restore the Meta files if their `.blink` did not change, never StyLua
  the generated files.
- **Never `git stash` to compare lint counts** in a tree holding the user's uncommitted work; diff the warning list of
  the changed files instead.


## Last Wave: the pings, the minimap's frame and legend, the keys and the debug readout (built 2026-10-30, unjudged)

Asked for: the last in-game pieces in the new style. The minimap needs only the new frame and the legend panel at its
middle right when open; the key hints (bottom right) and the debug readout (bottom left) stay WITHOUT a panel so
they do not take attention; the pings in the world and on the screen's edge get the real work. Bench `Stories/Pings`.
Linted, compiled, the place built with Rojo, the springs and the sizes at four screens checked in `lune`. **Not played
in Studio and not judged on the bench.**

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Components/pingMarker` (new) | One marker for both pings: a Slab in the pinger's colour (`FromColor`), the target's icon in the well, souls rising behind it in Blue (the souls colour), and a staircase pointer of Frames (ink rows 10, 8, 6, 4, 2 units wide, fill two narrower) on the side that faces the target. No rotation anywhere |
| `PingUI` | The world ping: the marker in a BillboardGui, scaled by one UIScale from the billboard's `AbsoluteSize`; it grows out of its pointer's tip and drops onto the target |
| `OffScreenIndicatorUI` | The edge marker (PingController and ArrowController both use it): the marker at a whole screen unit, the pointer on the side of the screen it is pinned to and slid along it toward the target, the body set back by the pointer's length |
| `Components/mapLegend` (new) | The open map's legend: a Grey Slab with a LEGEND tab, icon and name rows, coming out from behind the map with the rows popping in one after another and sparks off its far side |
| `MinimapUI` | The map's old 4 px black stroke is now a Grey Slab (unit 3, bezel 2, like the objective card under it) whose well the map fills; the legend is `mapLegend` |
| `KeyBindsUI` | Free Silkscreen words with ink outlines beside pixel keycaps (ink, Grey face with a lit row, a one-unit lip). While a key is held its cap goes into the lip and lights gold; the gold fades after the release. Pad glyphs squeeze while held. No CanvasGroup, no panel |
| `DebugUI` | Same place and lines, no panel: Silkscreen with ink outlines, the name dim and the number white, FPS green / gold / red (55 / 30). Same API; the setters are now functions |

### What the pings do

- **Arrival** (every time a marker shows, including an edge marker coming back on screen): from a third of its size to
  +14% and back (3.2 Hz / 0.45), from 8 units back (dropping from above in the world, sliding in from the edge on the
  screen), a white flash, and once it is nearly full size (0.1 s) a pair of rings and ten sparks.
- **Sonar**: two more rings 0.9 s apart, so it reads as a ping; the edge marker taps two units toward the target with
  each. Then the clock sleeps. Nothing loops for the ping's whole life, so ArrowController's long-lived markers
  (quests, altar reminders) do not keep a frame running.
- **Souls**: the fill rises on the reading spring (4.1 Hz / 0.72) in whole units with a lit top row that flashes
  white on a gain; filling it strikes (white flash, +8% thump, Blue rings, sixteen sparks) and turns the fill bright.
- **Leave**: `LeaveScale` over 0.22 s, inside the 0.25 s (PingController) and 0.4 s (ArrowController) the callers
  wait before destroying it.

### What was learned

1. **A billboard's size changes every frame the camera moves**, so a marker laid out in px from it would rewrite every
   piece every frame. Draw it ONCE at a fixed whole unit (4 px, a 160 px canvas) and scale the canvas with one UIScale
   (`fit.Scale = AbsoluteSize.X / 160`): one write a frame. Everything inside, `pixelFx` particles and rings included,
   then works in plain px.
2. **No CanvasGroup on a ping.** The old world ping and edge marker faded through a CanvasGroup, which renders at its
   own resolution and softens pixel art; the leave is a scale now.
3. **A pointer that must face any of four ways is four placements of the same rows, not a rotation**: each row is
   placed by (side, depth, width) round the middle of a side, `along` slides it in whole units.
4. **Callers that pin in raw px do not know the marker grows.** PingController pins 60 px and ArrowController 80 px
   from the edge, fixed; at 1440p and up the old marker already reached past the edge. The marker clamps its own
   middle 15 units in from every edge of its ScreenGui (body half 13 + 2), so it fits at any size without touching
   the controllers.
5. **A frame round something other UI hangs off goes INSIDE its box.** The objective card and the kill / soul chips
   are placed off the minimap's container, so the Slab fills the container and the map is inset into its well
   (`(1 + bezel) * p`); nothing that hangs off it moved. The map's window shrinks by that much; it is not stretched,
   except by under 2% on a non-square map.
6. **A line pushed every frame is rewritten only when what it SHOWS changes**: the debug velocity compares the value
   in tenths before building the string.
7. **Keep translation templates whole**: the debug lines still go through `F("FPS: {value}", ...)`, with the coloured
   number as the value, so the existing translations keep working.

### Not done / what else in the run is still the old style

`ChestUI`, `WinBoxUI`, `PlayersInfoUI`, `InteractableUI` (the prop prompt), `SelfReviveUI`, `RestartRadialUI`,
`PauseUI`, `KickUI`, `InformationUI` and `CursorUI` have none of the new kit. `TimerBarUI` (the pick glow) stays soft
on purpose (the user picked it). Ask before starting any of them: one element per round.

### Review (2026-10-30): what was optimised, and what is left

- **A ping is built new every time** (PingController mounts a fresh PingUI per ping, and a ping can fire every 0.25 s),
  so its instance count is a per-ping cost: the particle pool went 28 to 16 (the biggest burst) and the rings 3 pairs
  to 2 (a pair lives 0.52 s; arrival and sonar are 0.8 s apart). About 77 instances a marker down to about 61.
- **`draw` skips every unchanged write**: scale, position, flash, and the souls fill only when its whole-row count or
  look changes, its top row's colour only while it flashes. Before, about 12 writes every awake frame.
- **Left as is**: the edge marker reads the ScreenGui's and the camera's size each frame its position changes (three
  property reads, next to the Position write the old one already did). Reusing one world PingUI per player instead of
  building one per ping would remove the per-ping build, but it changes PingController (an adornee setter and the
  supersede path); do it if pings ever show up in a profile.

## Last Wave: the pause banner, the hold ring and the aim dot (built 2026-10-30, unjudged)

Asked for: `PauseUI` and `CursorUI` in the new style, as satisfying as they can be; then (round 2) the banner back to
the old one's shape and colour, the dot answering the fight, the hold ring remade as a pixel radial, and a story for
the dot. Benches `Stories/Pause` (banner and ring) and `Stories/Cursor`. Linted, compiled, the place built with Rojo,
the springs checked in `lune`. **Not played in Studio and not judged on the bench.**

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Components/pauseBanner` (new) | The banner, drawing only: a Grey Slab with a BIG pause mark in its middle (two inked white bars, 24 units tall), PAUSED under it and the line under that. Black, grey and white only. No divider. No uploaded art |
| `PauseUI` | Same API. Works out the line (host with keys, host on touch, not the host) and feeds it to the banner, top middle, 20% down |
| `Components/pixelRadial` (new) | The hold ring, drawing only: a real radial in pixel cells. An ink ring with a hard shadow and a dark track (row runs), and 192 cells that light clockwise from twelve, the outer ring lit, the inner shaded, the newest three white |
| `RestartRadialUI` | Same API plus `Complete()`, which PauseController and RestartController now call when a hold reaches full (both used to zero and hide it, the same calls as letting go, so the ring could not tell a finish from a release) |
| `Components/pixelCursor` (new) | The aim dot, drawing only: a white two-unit core in an ink plus with a hard shadow, 8 px at 1080p |
| `CursorUI` | Same API plus `Hit`, `Kill`, `Hurt`; CameraController feeds them |

### What they do

- **Pausing**: the card drops ten units from half its size to +10% with a white flash; landing, rings and sparks off
  its sides. The two big bars slam in one after the other (+23%), the second shaking the card +4%. PAUSED punches
  +22% and types out; the line types after it. While paused a sheen crosses the well every 3.2 s. **Resuming**: it
  pops away into white and grey bits.
- **The hold ring**: shows from half size to +10%. Cells light as the hold fills, a white head at the front throwing a
  spark every 0.05 s from outside the ink, a +4% thump at each quarter, and over the last quarter a shake that grows to
  a unit. **Full** (`Complete`): every cell flashes white, +11% thump, twenty sparks all round, a beat, then it pops
  away. **Let go**: the lit cells go grey and it drops away in 0.16 s.
- **The dot appearing / going**: unchanged from round 1 (arms snap in, ring, pop; arms fly out as it shrinks).
- **The dot in the fight** (only yours: EnemiesController checks the hit is the local character's):
  - **Hit**: the arms tick out of the dot two units long, flying out and shortening a unit at a time, gone in 0.2 s;
    the dot pops +5%. At most one every 0.1 s, never stacking, so a hundred hits a second read as a steady flicker.
  - **Crit**: the tick goes on the four DIAGONALS instead (round 3, the user's call), in the crit's colour
    (`FloatingNumbers.CritColor`, the same colours as the "!" numbers): each arm a staircase of two-unit blocks a unit
    apart, three long, starting 4 units out on both axes and flying 4 further. The dot flashes the colour and pops
    +12%. Crits have their own rate limit, so a hit and a crit together make an eight-pointed star. A diagonal in the
    pixel kit is always a staircase of axis-aligned blocks, never a rotated Frame (UI.md, "no rotation").
  - **Kill**: the dot's ink warms gold and it pops +9% (one every 0.1 s); five or more at once also throw a gold ring
    and sparks (one every 0.4 s).
  - **Hurt** (`HealthController.OnHealthChanged` going down): the dot flashes red and jumps a unit for a moment.
  - Nothing answers during its own appear / go gesture, or while it is hidden (mouse unlocked).

### Wiring

`EnemiesController.OnLocalHit` (new, fired with the crit stacks for the local player's hits and killing blows) and the
existing `OnLocalKill` are subscribed by CameraController, which owns the dot; the existing
`HealthController.OnHealthChanged` gives the hurt. **Why a new signal and not a direct call**: EnemiesController
calling CameraController would make it require CameraController, and CameraController waits up to 5 s at load for a
`Freecam` gui that only developers have; Rojo orders the `Actor` folder first, so for every normal player the enemy
listeners would have connected up to 5 s late. Subscribing from CameraController leaves the load order as it was.

### What was learned

1. **Ask what the old one did well before restyling it.** The user preferred the old banner's shape: the pause mark
   big in the middle, no line between title and text, and monochrome, which matched the world the pause turns grey.
   A restyle keeps the layout and the palette's meaning and changes the drawing.
2. **A screen that sits for minutes does nothing on most frames**: every write in the banner's and the ring's `draw` is
   guarded; the ring writes only the cells whose lit state or head changed, and all of them only while it flashes.
3. **A finish and a release must be different calls.** The ring's best moment (the burst) needs to know the hold
   finished; zero-and-hide could not say so.
4. **A per-hit reaction on something that never leaves the screen** is rate-limited, never stacks, and is gone in a
   fifth of a second, so the dot is back to only a dot between bursts.
5. **A new require between controllers can move the load order.** Check what the required module yields on at load
   before adding it to a hot controller.

### Not done / what else in the run is still the old style

`ChestUI`, `WinBoxUI`, `InteractableUI`, `KickUI` and `InformationUI` (`SelfReviveUI` and `InteractableUI` were done next, below).

### Review (2026-10-30): what was optimised, and what is left

- **`pixelFx.Rings` hid its edges EVERY frame**, live or not: 4 `Visible` writes per ring per frame for as long as the
  owner's clock ran. Each ring now remembers whether it is drawn (`IsDrawn`) and writes only when that changes. This is
  in the shared kit, so every element that throws rings got it (eleven users: the hotbar, status tiles, quest card,
  clock, XP bar, teammates, Color Dance, announcements, the banner, the dot, the pings), with no change to how anything
  looks.
- **The radial's finish flash fades in 6 steps** (`FlashSteps`), not a smooth value, so its 192 cells are recoloured
  about 6 times, not on every frame of the half-second fade. It also reads more like the kit, whose lights are stepped.
- **The dot recolours its arms only when the colour changes** (white for a hit, the crit's colour for a crit), not on
  every hit.
- **Readability**: the arm placement's `min(from * dir.X + from * dir.Y, ...)` is now a named `sign` with a comment,
  the crit / hit branch in `Hit` picks its numbers with `if` expressions, and three comments left over from the cyan
  banner (a header over 120 columns, "the hold ring's colour", "+14%" that `lune` measured at +10%) were fixed.
- **Left as is, and why**:
  - The banner keeps its clock awake while the game is paused, for the sheen. With the ring fix an idle frame writes
    nothing; it is a short Luau loop while nothing else in the run is moving. Sleeping between sheens would need a
    timer outside `pixelMotion`, which ignores the bench's time scale.
  - `EnemiesController.DamageEnemy` checks whether the hit is the local player's with two cross-module calls per
    `Damaged` event. That is once per event, not inside a loop (the batched event checks once per batch), next to the
    ECS lookups the handler already does.

## Last Wave: what the pause, hold ring and aim dot rounds taught (2026-10-30)

| # | The user said | The rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | "I liked the paused menu before: the icon big at the centre, no line, monochrome because the pause makes everything darker" | **A restyle keeps what the old one did well.** Before redrawing, write down the old layout (what is biggest, what is centred) and what its colours MEANT (monochrome = the world is paused), and keep both; change only the drawing. A new accent colour for an old screen needs a reason the user agrees with |
| 2 | "Yes, make the dot react to combat" (offered as optional) | **Something that never leaves the screen answers in ticks**: rate-limited (0.1 s and up), never stacking, gone in a fifth of a second, so it is only a dot between bursts. Take only the local player's events |
| 3 | "Remake the radial, but make sure it is still a radial" | **A shape's meaning survives the pixel style.** A radial stays a ring that fills clockwise; it is drawn as cells on the pixel grid (row runs for the static ink and track, one Frame per lit cell, sorted by angle), not turned into a bar |
| 4 | "I don't see a story of the cursor" | **One story per element, named after it.** A thing benched inside another element's story is not found. Each element gets its own `Stories/<Element>` with a flip per thing that happens to it, and a "running" toggle when it reacts to a stream (the dot's Fight) |
| 5 | "Is it the most optimized and readable it can be?" | **Review the shared kit, not only the new file.** The biggest saving this time (ring edges written every frame) was in `pixelFx`, paid by every element. When a component's idle frame is checked, read what its kit calls do on that frame too |

### Process

- **A finish and a release are two calls.** When a controller ends a gesture the same way on success and on failure,
  the drawing cannot celebrate the success. Add the call (`Complete()`) instead of guessing from the last value.
- **A new require between controllers can move the load order.** Ignis requires each folder's modules one after the
  other; a module that yields at load (CameraController waits up to 5 s for a developer-only `Freecam` gui) holds up
  anything that requires it. Before adding `require(X)` to a hot controller, read what X waits on; subscribe from X's
  side instead when it does. This is the one case a new signal with a single listener was the right trade, and the
  section above says why next to it.
- **Run StyLua on the files you changed, not on `src`**, when the tree holds someone else's work in progress: it
  reformats their files too. `stylua --check src` (which writes nothing) is the tree-wide check.
- **StyLua does not wrap comments.** Check the 120 columns yourself after writing long comments
  (`expand -t4 file | awk 'length > 120'`).
- **After a restyle, grep the file for the old look's words** (a colour's name, a percentage, "the line"): comments
  describing the old version are the first thing to go stale.

## Last Wave: the other players' cards (`teammateCard`, built 2026-10-30, unjudged)

Asked for: `PlayersInfoUI` (the column of other players down the left) in the new style, as satisfying as it can be.
Bench `Stories/Teammates`. Linted, compiled, the place built with Rojo, the gestures simulated in `lune`. **Not played
in Studio**; judged on the bench by the user over three rounds.

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Components/teammateCard.luau` | Drawing only: `Card(entry, pixelSize)`, `Column(registry, pixelSize, props)`, `Registry()` (sources per player, `Add` / `Remove` with a leave, setters that write only on change) |
| `PlayersInfoUI.luau` | The feeder, same API as before: ECS health / shield / maxes, `PlayerColorCore` colour, the headshot, the ultimate's charge polled at 10 Hz (a 0 to 1 share, not a ready flag) |

### What it does

- **The bezel is the player's colour** (`PlayerColorCore`: their character's outline, their minimap marker, their
  pings), so a card is matched to a body in the world at a glance. The headshot fills the well.
- **Health and shield are one inked strip** sharing the portrait's bottom outline: health three rows, an ink
  separator, shield two rows, on the vitals' springs (white band on a loss, green band ahead on a gain). No numbers,
  as before. No shield folds the shield rows away; the first Shield pick opens them.
- **A hit moves light only** (teammates are hit constantly): the band, a flash on the fill over 1.2%, a red tint on the
  face over 10%, a one-unit shake over 15%. Topping up to full dings the outline white (rate limited 0.35 s). A shield
  break flashes the row and throws small blue rings and sparks.
- **Low health** (under 30%) breathes three stepped red rings and the outline on the alarm's 1.15 s.
- **Down**: white flash, red tint, a 3-unit shake, red rings and sparks; the face turns to STONE (as the character
  does in the world) and the bezel walks to grey, a seeded crack runs down the face a row at a time, the skull pops in
  (+17%), and the red rings breathe on 1.6 s and never fade out while down. **Revive**: the crack retracts, colour comes
  back, the skull shrinks away, +9% thump, green rings and sparks, a sheen across the face.
- **One badge on the top outline**, its middle on the middle of the outline (y = p / 2), not on its outer edge. While
  the player is playing it is the ULTIMATE'S SQUARE (9 units): grey with a Violet fuse lighting clockwise from twelve
  as it charges (drawn on the spot, no clock), Violet with a lit hole and a glint when ready. Ready punches it (+28%)
  and throws small Violet rings; nothing else on the card reacts (someone else's ultimate).
- **It MORPHS into the word** (DOWN Red over VOTED Green over PAUSE Grey over PICK Blue) and back when the state is
  over: the box widens a unit at a time, the hole closes in two-unit steps (so it stays centred), the colours walk to
  the word's, and the word shows at 70% with a punch (+14%) and a flash; the way back hides the word at once, then
  narrows and reopens the hole. One spring at 1.8 Hz / 0.7: word ~0.17 s in, box landed ~0.26 s. A word swapped for
  another moves the width on its own spring and punches; the face clips, so a longer word never sticks out. With no
  ultimate and no word the badge shrinks away; one arriving from nothing pops in already as what it is.
- **Join**: pops in from half size rising 5 units, white flash, rings and sparks in the player's colour, a sheen; the
  bars FILL from empty; the headshot fades in when it arrives. **Leave**: `LeaveScale`, a puff, then the row closes
  (kept 0.6 s; a rejoin mid-leave keeps the card).
- Everything thrown leaves to the RIGHT, born past the alarm rings (the column is against the left edge).

### What the rounds taught

1. **`pixelMotion.Snap` moves the target too.** The first ultimate pip and status tab set their target to 1 and then
   snapped to 0 for the pop, so each flashed for a frame and sat at nothing ("I don't see their ultimate", "start
   picking doesn't work"). **Snap first, then set the target.** Grep every `Snap` in a new element and check the order.
2. **"Centred on the stroke" is the middle of the outline's unit (y = p / 2)**, not the box's outer edge. Pick the
   badge's height so it lands on whole pixels there: 9 units has its top at -4p at any unit. Its left is rounded
   (`round((side - w) / 2)`), so a width with an odd half sits half a pixel off centre rather than blurred.
3. **Two pieces that say "what this player is doing now" are ONE piece that changes shape.** A pip on the side read as
   stuck on, and a tab on the top was a second place to look. One badge that is the ultimate's square while the
   player plays and MORPHS into the word while a state applies keeps one place, and the morph itself is the juice.
4. **How a pixel morph stays pixel-hard:** one spring (0 square, 1 word) drives everything. The width steps a whole unit
