   at a time between the square's and the word's; the hole closes in steps of TWO units so it stays centred (5, 3, 1,
   0); the colours lerp; the word shows only once the box can hold it (70%) with a punch, and on the way back it hides
   at once, before the box narrows. A word swapped for another moves the width on its own spring, and the face clips,
   so a longer word never pokes out while the box catches up. A badge appearing from nothing pops in as what it already
   is, without morphing.
5. **Simulate a morph's frames, not only its peak.** At 3 Hz the word was in after 0.1 s, too fast to see the shape
   change at all; printing width / hole / word per frame in `lune` showed it, and 1.8 Hz puts the word at ~0.17 s and
   the landing at ~0.26 s.
6. **Someone else's events are quieter than yours.** A teammate's hit moves light only (band, flash, red tint, a
   one-unit shake only past 15%); their ultimate becoming ready punches its own badge and nothing else on the card;
   no sounds at all. Size is for joining, going down and a revive.
7. **Use the colour the world already gives a player.** `PlayerColorCore` is their outline, minimap marker and ping; as
   the card's bezel it links the card to the body without a name.
8. **Echo the world on the card.** A downed character turns to stone in the world, so the face turns to stone, the
   bezel walks to grey and a seeded crack runs down it (one ink run per row, seeded by the id, so each player cracks
   their own way).

### Cost: a lasting warning keeps the clock awake, so every write is guarded

- **The first build rewrote everything on every awake frame**: about 150 property writes a card (40 crack rows, 32
  sheen rows, both palettes, both bars, the badge, every size). That is fine for a 0.3 s gesture and wrong for a low or
  downed teammate, whose breathing keeps `pixelMotion` awake for as long as it lasts: four downed teammates would have
  been ~600 writes a frame for three rings changing.
- **Now `draw` is sections, each behind what it last wrote** (a `drawn` table: scale, position, card height, flash,
  stone, tint, crack rows, skull, sheen, alarm, edge, badge width / morph / charge / palette; bars keep their own
  `Drawn*` px). A breath frame writes the three rings' transparency and the two outlines' colour: five writes. Worked
  out by reading the sections, **not measured with a counter**.
- **Gate on EVERY input a section draws from.** The badge's first gate was width, morph and charge; PICK swapping to
  DOWN (same width, morph already 1) would have kept the blue. The word's palette is in the gate now.
- **Invalidate after a layout or a new palette**, and force booleans to the value that makes the next draw write
  (`IsSheenLive = true`, `IsWordShown = not isWordShown`), not flipped blindly. The ring positions are rewritten only
  when the alarm turns on or the card's height changes; a card height change resets the alarm's cache.
- **Quantize to what is drawn.** The fuse is 28 units round its 7-unit face, so the charge is floored to 1/28 before
  the gate; the feeder's 1/64 steps would otherwise redraw identical pixels on most pushes.
- **One more draw as a sheen ends**, so its rows are hidden (`IsSheenLive` remembers it was live).

### Readability

- **Keep references, not names**: `layout` looked bar rows up with `FindFirstChild("Light")` / `("Shade")`; `TBar` now
  holds `FillLight`, `FillShade` and `TroughShade`.
- **Drawing only, fed by a registry** (`Card`, `Column`, `Registry` in the component; ECS, colours, headshots and the
  ultimate's poll in `PlayersInfoUI`), like `infoScreen` / `InfoUI`: the bench mounts the drawing with made-up players.
- **Still copied, the old debt:** the arrival (scale and rise springs) and the leave (`LeaveScale`, a puff, the row
  closing) are the same shape as the other nine elements' (see "what the clock, toast and streak rounds taught"); this
  is the tenth copy for `pixelMotion.Presence` to replace. `Card` is one ~1,000-line constructor like the others; the
  natural split is the badge (its springs, frames, `drawBadge`, `refreshBadge`) into its own component if a second
  element ever wants a square that morphs into a word.

### Process

- **Another session can rewrite UI.md under you.** This section vanished once while a parallel session saved its own
  copy of the file (and `PlayersInfoUI` went back onto its "old style" list). Grep for your section before editing it,
  and fix it back without touching theirs.
- **A shared kit can change under you** (`pixelFx` was edited mid-round): re-check the functions you call against it
  before calling a round done.

### Sizes and open points

- Unit 3 design px: the card is 26 units wide (78 px at 1080p), the row 42 units with the shield. **On an 844x390
  phone the unit rounds to 1 (a 26 px card, smaller than the old ~33 px)**: check it on a phone.
- `SetDead` does not say downed or killed, so a teammate killed for good also reads DOWN.
- No sound: a teammate's events are not yours, and the world already speaks for them.
- PICK and PAUSE never show today: only the local player is marked picking (the column skips them), and nothing calls
  `SetPauseVote`.

## Last Wave: what a teammate is doing (`activityTag`, built 2026-11-05, unjudged)

Asked for: the spectator's arrow-pointed tag on every teammate card, saying in icons (not text) what that player is
doing; an altar hold with the altar's icon and the prompt's charge; on the spectated player it becomes the LIVE plate;
spectating is part of `PlayersInfoUI`, not a thing of its own. Benches `Stories/Teammates` (a Do flip per activity) and
`Stories/Spectator`. Linted, compiled, the Game place built with Rojo, the tag's states driven offline in
`tools/spectator/check.luau`. **Not played in Studio and not judged on the bench.**

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Components/activityTag` (new) | Drawing only: a 4-unit staircase point at the card and a 19-unit Slab with the icon; `Doing` (lasting), `Did` (a moment), pushed `Progress`, and the watched morph into the 60 x 21 LIVE plate |
| `Components/teammateCard` | Hosts it in the card's cell, 4 units right of the card (a unit clear of the alarm rings), on the portrait's middle; `Registry` gains `SetName`, `SetDoing`, `SetProgress`, `ShowDid` |
| `Components/spectateBar` | Arrows and RESULTS only; the name plate, its travel and its colour blend are gone |
| `PlayersInfoUI` / `PlayersInfoController` | Mount the bar; the controller turns each activity into a look (`SetChoosing`, `SetCharging`, `SetChargeShare`, `ShowPicked`, `ShowPaid`, `ShowLit`) |

### What it shows, and where it comes from

| Activity | Look | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Choosing a level-up / a reward | Drawn arrow on Blue / drawn star on the augment Teal; the bezel dims and its fuse is the pick's countdown (20 s / 25 s, `LevelsCore`), draining clockwise, green to gold to red at a half and a quarter (runClock's pick colours), the icon ticking on each phase and each of the last 3 seconds | `Rewards.Choosing` (new), closed by `*CharacterSelected` |
| Picked a level-up / a reward / a chest item | Its art in its rarity (items, upgrades) or its kind's colour (augments); pop, rings, sparks | `UpgradeCharacterSelected`, `AugmentCharacterSelected`, `ChestItemPicked`, `ChestLeftGrabbed` |
| Picked up a power-up | The drop's art on Green, as it reaches them (shards say nothing) | `DropsController`'s arrival loop |
| Holding an altar or a chest | The prop's icon on the prompt's white face; a gold fuse fills over the hold, the bezel dims, sparks off the fuse's front, a tremble over the last half; let go early, it drains grey | `Props.Hold` (new, client) relayed as `Props.Busy` |
| Paid souls without filling it | Souls motes pulled into the well, a blue wash, a gain punch | `Props.Busy` Fed (new, from `AltarServer` / `ChestServer`) |
| Opening a chest | The chest's icon filling over the server's 2.5 s window, bursting as it opens | `ChestOpened` |
| Lit an altar / began a quest | Gold: +10% thump, flash, sheen, rings, sparks | `Activated` (Altar only), `QuestStarted` / `ChallengeStarted` |
| Charging a quest circle | The quest marker on Gold (Red for a challenge), the fuse following the circle's share | `QuestCircleLoadProgress` + who stands inside, worked out in `QuestsController` |

- **One tag, three shapes.** Hidden, the icon square, the LIVE plate; the square and plate are one Slab whose width and
  height walk a whole unit at a time on the badge's morph spring (1.8 Hz / 0.7), the icon hiding at once and the
  plate's content showing at 70% (the teammate cards' lesson 3 and 4).
- **A moment beats a state, the plate beats both.** A pick shows for 1.7 s over what they are doing, then the tag goes
  back to it. The spectated player shows only LIVE and their name: their own screen is already on yours.
- **A timed fill that completes is done**: it bursts, waits 0.5 s for what follows (souls paid, a chest opening) and
  tucks away if nothing does, so a hold the server ignored (no souls) does not hang.
- **Quiet**: no sounds; size moves only for the big ones (a fill completing, an altar, a quest), as the cards' lesson 6.
- **The fuse is the prompt's, not a thinner one** (round 2): the whole bezel ring, as deep as the bezel, with the white
  head unit at its front. The first cut drew it one unit deep and read as a stroke, not the prompt's charge.
- **Centre a drawn glyph's ink, not its box** (round 2): `BuildGlyph` lays 7 x 7 texels in an 8-texel box (its shade
  row and column, invisible on the dark well), so a box centred in the icon put the ink half a texel up and left; and a
  texel of `floor(icon / 8)` px left a half pixel of slack. A texel is now a unit and the ink sits 2 units in, centred at
  every unit size. The choosing bob (a unit each way) was taken out with it: it read as off centre.

### Cost

- A settled tag sleeps. Awake: a countdown (the fuse writes when its run crosses a unit: 68 units over 20 s is about one
  write every 0.3 s; it sleeps once the time is out, until the server's pick for them arrives), a fill (fuse, stepped
  dim in eighths, sparks), LIVE's breath (two writes a frame). Every section is behind what it last wrote; the paint
  gate is on the palettes' identity, the morph and the stepped dim, not a string built every frame (the first cut built
  three hex strings a frame to compare).
- Sizes that depend only on the unit are set in `layout`, not in the draw that moves them (the fuse head's size was
  rewritten with every unit the fuse moved).
- `QuestsController` returns before its character query when a circle is at rest with nobody charging it: the server
  sends every waiting circle's share every frame, so the first cut queried every character 60 times a second per
  circle for nothing.
- The bar no longer reads a card's position: the plate is the card's own. It still reads the column's bounds every
  frame while shown (the arrows sit above and below it).
- Network: three new events (`Props.Hold` client, `Props.Busy` and `Rewards.Choosing` server); the highest
  server-to-client reliable id is now 235 of 255.
- **Not measured.** None of this was profiled; "cheap" above is from reading the code, not from the MicroProfiler.

### What this element taught (keep these)

1. **"Like the other one" means its exact geometry.** Asked for the interactable prompt's charge, the first cut drew a
   one-unit fuse, a smaller copy of an idea. Take the original's numbers (`propPrompt`'s `FUSE_PX` is the bezel's
   depth, `BEZEL_PX` the ring, a white head at the front) and scale only by the unit.
2. **Centre a drawn glyph's ink, not its box** (`pixelSlab.BuildGlyph` puts 7 x 7 texels in an 8-texel box for its
   shade; on a dark well the shade is invisible). Make a texel a whole unit, and check the slack either side is whole
   units at every unit size, or the icon sits half a pixel off at some of them.
3. **Idle motion on an icon reads as a layout bug.** A one-unit "thinking" bob looked like an off-centre icon in a
   still. A lasting state moves light and colour on the frame (the fuse), not the icon's position.
4. **A fuse that means time is that time's clock.** The choosing fuse first lapped forever; the player wanted the pick's
   countdown. Use the countdown the rest of the game already shows (`LevelsCore` seconds, `runClock`'s green / gold /
   red at a half and a quarter), drain it from full, dim the bezel under it so the run reads, and tick only the last
   seconds, quietly.
5. **A lasting state's clock runs whatever is shown.** A moment popped over a countdown pauses the drawing, not the time.
6. **Stop being busy when there is nothing left to draw.** A countdown at zero waits on the server; it should not keep
   the frame loop awake while it does.
7. **One check, in one place.** The controller first asked "is this the local player?" (a character lookup per call);
   the registry already drops writes for ids it has no card for, and the local player never has one.
8. **A spectator UI pinned to a HUD element should be that element.** The travelling name plate read the watched card's
   position every frame and had its own colour blend; as the card's own tag it needs neither.
9. **Per-frame network packets need an early out before world queries.** Decide from the packet (share 0, nobody
   charging) before touching the ECS.

### Process lessons

- **Mocks must use the real kit's constants.** The check script's slab mock had `Chrome = 4` (the kit's is 6); a
  centring check written against it failed for the mock's reason, not the code's. Copy constants from the module.
- **zsh does not split an unquoted variable.** `selene $F` with a list in `F` ran on one bad path and printed "1 error";
  run file lists through `bash -c` or an array.
- **Blink:** the local binary generated the main network fine this time; back up the three outputs, diff against the
  backup (new events renumber every later id), and never run StyLua on them (`.styluaignore` lists them).

### Open points

- The bench's activity flips use `task.delay`, real time, not the bench's time scale.
- A teammate's hold relays on press and on let-go; a finished hold relays nothing (what the interact does next is
  what shows).
- The countdown starts when the teammate's client hears `Rewards.Choosing`, so it can trail the server's by one trip.

## Last Wave: the self-revive card (`reviveCard`, built 2026-10-30, unjudged)

Asked for: `SelfReviveUI` in the new style, as satisfying as it can be. Bench `Stories/SelfRevive`. Linted, compiled,
the place built with Rojo, the springs checked in `lune`. **Not played in Studio and not judged on the bench.**

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Components/reviveCard` (new) | The drawing: a Gold Slab laid out as the old panel was (TAP RAPIDLY TO REVIVE in gold, the seconds big and white, a bar under them). 4 px units at 1080p, never under 2 |
| `SelfReviveUI` | Same API, except `Bounce` is now `Tap`, and a new `Complete` |
| `ReviveController` | Calls `Tap` on every press and `Complete` on `OnSelfRevived` (it used to zero the bar and hide it, the same as a pause, so the card could not celebrate getting up) |
| `LocalizationCore` | New string `REVIVED!` |

### What it does

- **Going down**: the card drops ten units from half its size, flashing white, with gold rings and sparks as it
  lands, and the title types out with a punch. A low `ChestJump`.
- **The bar**: whole units, the reading on the vitals' quick spring (4.1 Hz / 0.72). What the server has credited past
  the reading shows as a lit band, like the vitals' gain band. A white head column sits at the fill's front. Ticks at
  each quarter.
- **A tap** (every press, counted or not, at most one every 0.06 s): the card presses one unit down for about 0.1 s,
  the fill flashes, two sparks fall out of the card's bottom edge under the head, and `ClickHud` plays, pitched up with
  the progress (0.9 to 1.5). It moves the card, never its size: taps are the most frequent event there is.
- **Each quarter**: the bar steps up a colour, red, orange, gold, pale gold (the old bar's red to orange, carried on to
  the card's gold). A +4% thump, rings and side sparks in the new colour, `ChestJump` a step higher each time. Only
  upward, so a server correction across a line does not fire it twice.
- **The last quarter**: three stepped gold rings breathe round the card (0.9 s) and the ink outline warms gold.
- **The last three seconds**: the number turns gold and punches +10% on 3, 2 and 1, with a rising tick.
- **Getting up** (`Complete`, by filling it or by a teammate): the bar fills, everything flashes white, a +10% thump,
  white and gold rings, twenty side sparks and ten from the bottom, the title goes and the number becomes REVIVED!
  (punched +22%), a sheen crosses the well, `ScoreComplete`. After 0.6 s it pops away into gold bits.
- **A pause or the run ending** (`SetVisible(false)`): it drops away in 0.16 s, with nothing thrown. Resuming plays the
  arrival again.

### What was learned

1. **A success and a hide are two calls, again** (the hold ring taught it first). The old controller ended a revive the
   same way as a pause. Grep each `SetVisible(false)` for what it MEANS before restyling.
2. **The input itself is the most frequent event.** A mashing player presses ten times a second, so the answer is
   position and light (a unit's press, a flash, two sparks, a pitch), rate-limited and never stacking. The old 1.12x
   size bounce per tap is exactly what "frequent events move light only" rules out.
3. **Progress can be told in colour steps.** The old bar's gradient (red to orange across the bar) became a step per
   quarter, so the gradient's meaning (getting closer) is kept and each step is an event.
4. **A press spring has to be simulated for how long it SHOWS, not how high it goes.** At 6 Hz a one-unit press rounds
   to a moved card for only 0.06 s; 4 Hz / 0.55 with a 55 shove holds it about 0.1 s.

### Cost

The clock runs every frame while you are down (up to 30 s). Every section of `draw` writes only on change: the fill and
band by whole units (about 3 writes a second while it fills on its own), the number by tenths (`string.format` only
then), flashes and the breath in eighths. The fill's lit row, shaded row, head and flash are sized by scale, so a
growing fill is one write. Nothing reads `TextBounds`: the labels are fixed boxes, centred, refit only when the digits
become the word.

### Review (2026-10-30): what was fixed, and what is left

- **A reset value that is also a real value.** The draw cache is reset by setting every number to -1. Two fields could
  legitimately hold -1:
  - The title's visible count used -1 for "all of it". It now counts 0 to the title's length.
  - The number used -1 for "the word". The word is now -2.

  This was harmless today (each case skipped a write that would have changed nothing) and wrong the day it isn't.
  **When a cache is reset with one value, check that no field can ever draw that value**, and write the rule on the
  table.
- `SetProgress` called `pixelMotion.Wake` on every Heartbeat. The clock never sleeps while the card is shown, so the
  call was removed, with a comment saying why.
- The tier formula was written out three times; it is now `tierOf`. Two values that only `layout` used are no longer
  kept on the card.
- `SelfReviveUI` set a default revive time that the controller always overwrites before showing the card; removed.
- Two comments said "he". Comments say "you" for the player, or a role, never a guessed pronoun.
- **Left as is**: `pixelFx.Particles.Step` loops over its 48-particle pool every frame while the card is shown, even
  with none alive. It is a short Luau loop with no writes, it is in the shared kit, and every element pays it.

### Open points

- The thrown rings at landing and on getting up grow past where the side sparks are born, as on the pause banner. They
  are thin and fading, so it was left; check it on the bench.
- No key glyph: the title still says TAP, on every platform, as the old one did.

## Last Wave: the chest (`chestReveal`, built 2026-10-30, unjudged)

The run's chest, asked for "as satisfying and juicy as the level-up or rewards", with BeACastleLord's sword pull, gift
opening and seal opening and Megabonk's chest as references. `ChestUI` is now a feeder with the same API, so
`ChestClient` kept every call; the drawing is `Components/chestReveal`. Bench: `Stories/Chest`. Linted, compiled and
built; **not played in Studio and not seen on the bench by the agent that built it**.

### What the references gave, and what was taken

| Reference | What it does | Taken as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The sword in the Core | Three heaves, each a little further, then the yank; the blade's height out of the stone is the readout | Every rarity step is a heave; the gap between the doors is the readout |
| The gift | Two halves forced apart, gummed by threads that give from wisps to ropes; an echo of the shell thrown further each beat; ONE beat slips and slams back; the longest breath before the last; the halves thrown off; the thing inside swells and then spends itself, and only THEN the light comes, from behind it | Doors, threads, echo rings growing with the tier, the slip on roll tick 11, the roll's slowest tick last, doors thrown off, swell then rings and rays 0.1 s later |
| The seals | Something stands up within a tenth of a second of the press; nothing empty in front of the player | Light leaks from behind the slot on the rise (round 1 had a stepped shaft; round 2 replaced it, below) |
| Megabonk | Icons roll fast (0.06 s), the tiers climb with an effect each, a final effect, streams of light behind the item, the name and description shown after | The roll slows from 0.07 s to 0.27 s a tick (`ChestClient`, 2.8 s against the old even 3 s), the light streams (`lightRays`) |

Not taken: anything that moves the camera or the player (the gift and the sword hold the eye; a chest opens mid-fight),
words over the item before it opens (the seals' lesson: the thing and its light say it), and rotation (pixel art does
not turn; the gift's tumbling halves fly flat).

### What it is

- **The old layout, in pixels**: the item's Slab at the bottom middle (26 units), the name in the rarity's colour and the
  description over it, accept (green) right, banish (red, uses in a chip) left, skip (yellow) above the item while it is
  revealed, key glyphs where the old ones hung. New: the rarity's name in a tab on the slot, the climb's readout.
- **A stage, not a layout pass.** The billboard changes size every frame with the camera, so the stage is fixed design
  px (unit 6) under a UIScale of the billboard's height over 680. Units are uneven by a screen pixel at some distances;
  re-laying out every frame for exact units was the alternative and costs a pass per frame per chest.
- **The billboard grew to 24 x 17 studs** with the old 16 x 9.3 box in its middle, so what sat where still does and the
  light and thrown doors have room. Its `SizeOffset` is the old shift in studs over the new height.
- **One CanvasGroup round everything**, as before: BillboardGui text does not draw on some phones outside one, and its
  GroupTransparency is the pause/down fade.
- **The rarity look is the level-up card's**: `upgradeCard.Palettes` and `upgradeCard.Ornaments` are exported and read,
  not copied, so a tier reads the same on a card and in a chest. The chest says Godly, not Divine: Divine is the card's
  display name only.
- **No sounds in the component.** `ChestClient` plays the chest's in the world for everyone near it; a UI sound would
  play for every chest any player opens, everywhere. The bench plays them itself.
- **Hit areas are the old ones and always there**, so a tap behaves exactly as before (`ChestClient`'s mobile holds
  check the state themselves). The drawn buttons arrive and leave over them.

### The beats

| Call (`ChestClient`) | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `SetVisible(true)` | Rises 10 units out of the chest, popping up from half size, flash, a ring, and a thread of light leaks from behind it at once |
| `SetRarity` before it opens | A heave: everything takes the tier, the doors part to 0.35 units each a tier and are shoved past it, threads give, thump +2.3% (Common) to +4.9% (Secret), tab punch, an echo ring 4 + tier units out, more light leaking and a flare of it, a shake from Rare |
| `SetItemImage` (the roll) | The item drops a few units into the crack, the seam light flares, the doors strain a little further, light leaks off the top; the slot trembles harder each tick; tick 11 SLIPS: the doors slam shut, the slot is knocked in, and they come back further |
| `SetDecided(true)` | The doors are thrown off to either side and puff where they land, every rope goes, flash (black for Secret), thump +6% to +12.6%, the item swells +22%; 0.1 s later the rings, a burst, the full fan of light, a shake from Epic; the name types in and the buttons pop in after |
| `SetItemData` after it opened (a banish) | The banish mark stamps red over the item, which goes in a red puff; the new one drops into the well and lands with its own rings and rays |
| `SetVisible(false)` (taken) | The item swells, sticks, and is yanked up and away faster and faster with a trail, while the rest leaves (0.22 s, inside the 0.25 s before `ChestClient` unmounts it) |
| Hold progress | Sinks a unit onto its shadow, fills a unit at a time, squeezes, trembles and leaks sparks past 40%, strikes when full; an empty banish refuses |

Idle once open, by `upgradeCard`'s ladder: glow rings, breath, sparkles, sheen; Divine's columns rising off it;
Secret's black glow and rays, light pulled in, and the red/cyan glitch. The streams of light run at the tier's level
(round 2).

### What was learned

1. **The readout of a reveal is a SHAPE that changes, not a flash per step.** Five identical flashes say nothing about
   how far along it is; a gap that widens does (the gift's lesson). The climb's tab name is the second readout.
2. **One beat must go backward.** The slip is what makes the other heaves feel earned; it is the only one.
3. **The light comes a beat AFTER the doors**, not with them: the swell first, then the spend. Both on one frame read
   as one event.
4. **A world billboard is drawn on a stage, not laid out per frame**, and gets room around its old box for what flies.
5. **Read the rarity look off the shipped card**, never copy it; a second copy drifts on the next round.
6. **An idle element redraws only what changed**: the sheen skips once hidden, the text's transparency is cached.
7. **Particles**: the opening burst is born two units past the outermost glow and was flown in `lune` from the top
   edge at the slowest launch: it never comes back nearer than 12 design px above the slot.

### Open points

- Not seen. First things to look at on the bench: whether the doors' gap reads at Common (it opens least), whether the
  slip reads as a slip and not a glitch, the rays' strength over a bright floor, and whether 24 x 17 studs is enough
  room for the thrown doors at the closest camera.
- The roll's new pace is in `ChestClient`; if the user wants the old even 0.15 s back it is three constants.
- `ChestClient`'s anticipation shake and 1.5 s lid wait are unchanged, so the UI still appears 1.9 s after the press.

### Round 2 (2026-10-30): streams of light, and far fewer squares

Feedback, from a playtest screenshot: taking the item threw "a lot of particles", strange on a billboard; and the user
expected streams of light like Megabonk's chest or BeACastleLord's gift, not the round-1 stepped sunburst.

- **The squares were the take.** The taken item left a dot every frame of its flight (a dotted column up the screen),
  puffed where it ended, and both buttons puffed as they left, on top of the accept strike: some 40 squares at once.
  Now the item shrinks to nothing on its way up with no trail or puff, buttons leave without a puff when the whole
  chest goes (`SetShown`'s `isQuiet`), the strike throws 4 sparks, the leak and thread puffs are gone, and the
  opening's burst is 4 + 2 per tier. **A world billboard has no floor or frame for squares to belong to: they read as
  noise in the scene.** Keep particles on a billboard to the one moment that earns them.
- **The light is `Components/lightRays`**, a flat port of BeACastleLord's `Utils/Rays`, which is Megabonk's chest with its
  numbers: a bar of even width pivoted at the item (a taper reads as a spike), its light full at the base and gone
  before the tip, born, opening by a third of its life, held, closed (0.85 s +- 0.35), turning 34 degrees a second,
  bearings a golden angle apart, faint on its own (opacity 0.45 at most) so the fan is loud only where rays overlap.
  In the UI a ray is ONE Frame twice its length, centred on the item and turned with `Rotation`, the near half clear
  through its UIGradient, so it turns about its base with no holder. Rays are light, not shape, so they turn: the
  no-rotation rule is for pixel art.
- **How much light, when**: a thread leaks from the rise, more with every heave (and a flare) and every roll tick, NONE
  while the doors slip (the light is shut off with them), a burst and full fan for 0.8 s on the opening, then its
  tier's level (0.3 + 0.07 a tier of the rate) for as long as the chest is open; Secret's are black. They stop on the
  take and live out their life. The stepped shaft and the stepped sunburst were deleted.
- **Cost**: three writes per live ray per frame (size, turn, transparency); about 22 up at full, 8 to 19 idle by tier.
- Linted, compiled and built; not played.


### Review (2026-10-30): what was optimised, and what is left

- **An element that idles on its clock must not redraw on it.** An open chest never sleeps (its light and ornaments
  run while the player decides), so a `draw()` that rewrote everything every frame cost ~40 property writes a frame
  per chest for nothing. Now the tick works out `isMoving` (a spring stepped, the shake, a flash, the glitch, a leave)
  and only then rewrites the slot; the glow rings take their colour and transparency once in `paint` and only a
  breathing tier rewrites them; the buttons draw only when busy or dirtied (`holdButton`'s `isDirty`, set by a new
  fill or a pop back in).
- **When drawing is gated on "busy", the frame something SETTLES must count as busy.** `pixelFx.Shake.Step` reset
  its offset to 0 and returned false on that same frame, so a gated draw left the slot one shake-step off for good.
  Fixed in `pixelFx` (the settling frame now returns true), which also covers the eight other elements that shake.
  Springs already do this right: `pixelMotion.Step` returns true on the step that lands them.
- **Nothing string-shaped per frame.** The typewriter counted the name's and description's letters (a `gsub` over
  rich text) every frame, forever once done. They are counted once when the item is set.
- **A sub-component gets its own file when it has its own state and clock.** The hold button (fill, drain, tremble,
  strike, refuse, arrive, leave, count chip) was 300 lines inside the reveal; it is `Components/holdButton` with its
  own `Tune`, as `lightRays` is. It is the HELD sibling of `actionButton` (pressed): different gestures, so a second
  component rather than a mode on the first.
- **Cutting blocks out of a file by script: check the closing line.** A "from this line to that line" helper stopped
  one line short twice and left a stray `}` and `}\nend`; the compile caught both. Cut by exact text, or compile
  straight after.
- **Left as is**: `lightRays` writes three properties per live ray per frame (size, turn, transparency), which is
  what a moving ray is; `drawDoors` writes every frame while the doors are up, which is only during the reveal.

The chest's files now: `Components/chestReveal` (the reveal, about 1500 lines), `Components/holdButton`,
`Components/lightRays`, `ChestUI` (the feeder) and `Stories/Chest`.

## Last Wave: the prop prompt (`propPrompt`, built 2026-10-30, unjudged)

Asked for: `InteractableUI` (the prompt over the nearest chest, altar, barrel or box) in the new style, as satisfying as
it can be; then the key as its glyph image on every platform (as on a pad), and variants of the souls count, which the
user did not like as a tab; of four looks benched side by side the user picked Bare, and asked for the key to stay
still while nothing happens. Bench `Stories/Interactable`. Linted,
compiled, the place built with Rojo, the springs checked in `lune`. **Not played in Studio and not judged on the bench.**

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Components/propPrompt` (new) | The drawing, on a fixed 64-unit stage (4 px units): a white Slab (the old white frame) with the prop's icon in the well, the key's glyph standing on its top edge, the soul and the count under it with no box |
| `InteractableUI` | The feeder: one BillboardGui (8 studs, the Slab is the old 3-stud box) with a CanvasGroup (text on phones) and a UIScale fitting the stage to the billboard. Setters are plain functions now; `SetSouls(accumulated, needed)` and `Complete` are new, `SetHasHold` is gone |
| `PropsController` | Calls `Complete()` when a hold finishes or an instant prop is pressed (it used to set the progress to 1 and back to 0 in the same frame, so the prompt could not tell a finish from a release), and `SetSouls` with the cost |

### What it does

- **Walking up**: the Slab drops six units from half its size with a flash, rings and sparks as it lands; the icon,
  the key and the souls pop in one after another (0.04, 0.09, 0.14 s). Walking away drops it in 0.14 s.
- **Waiting**: a sheen crosses the icon every 3.5 s. The key does not move: an idle "press me" dip every 1.4 s was
  tried and the user disliked it. The key moves only when you press it.
- **A hold** (chests and altars, 0.5 s): the Slab sinks a unit onto its shadow, the key goes down and turns gold, the
  icon draws in, a gold FUSE with a white head eats clockwise round the bezel from twelve while the unlit bezel dims to
  grey, sparks fly off the fuse's front (never born on the key or the souls), a rising tick each quarter, and a tremble
  over the last half. **Letting go**: the fuse goes grey and drains back in 0.15 s.
- **Used** (`Complete`): the Slab jumps off its shadow, flashes, thumps +10%, the icon punches +22%, the key punches,
  gold rings and sparks, a sheen, `ChestJump`. A hide within a second after it (or with the cost full) is the prop used
  up: it pops away into gold (blue if paid in full) bits instead of dropping.
- **Souls paid**: motes fly from the count into the Slab, the fill rises in the well, its lit row and the count
  flash blue, the count rolls down a tick at a time with a `ScoreTick` per soul, pitched up as the cost fills. Full strikes
  in blue: flash, thump, rings, sparks, sheen, `ScoreComplete`.
- **The souls look, picked**: Bare, the soul and the count with no box under the Slab, as the old one. Lost: Tab (a
  blue tab joined under the Slab, the first build, disliked), Gauge (a bar under the Slab filling as souls are paid),
  Corner (a blue chip on the corner, like a stack's count). Deleted.

### What was learned

1. **The key is the glyph the game already has** (`KeybindsCore.GetImage`), on a keyboard too: a drawn keycap with the
   key's name was the first build and the user wanted the same picture as on a pad.
2. **A finish and a release are two calls, a third time** (the hold ring, the revive card): a controller that sets 1
   then 0 in one frame says nothing to the drawing.
3. **Souls flying INTO the Slab are the one particle allowed to cross what they fly into**; each is given the speed
   that its drag brings to rest at the target by the end of its life, `(1 - e^(-drag * life)) / drag` of it.
4. **A jump needs a softer spring than a press.** The press (6 Hz / 0.8) could not show a -45 shove at all (simulated:
   it never left 0 units); the drop's spring (3.2 Hz / 0.6) shows a unit up for 0.12 s.
5. **A box centred on the Slab keeps an even number of units**, or it lands half a unit off the grid.
6. **Something that never stops being shown does not move by itself.** A key that dips on its own reads as a press you
   did not make; idle life goes on light (the sheen), and motion answers the hand.

### Review (2026-10-30): what was fixed, and what is left

- **`Wake` every Heartbeat, again** (the revive card had it too). PropsController pushes the hold's share every frame,
  and `SetHoldProgress` called `pixelMotion.Wake` each time; `SetSouls` and `Complete` woke it too. The clock never
  sleeps while the prompt is shown, and each of those setters returns early or draws nothing when it is hidden, so only
  `Show` and `Hide` wake it now, with a comment on `step` saying why. **When a component keeps its clock awake while
  shown, grep it for `Wake` and keep only the calls that can come while it is hidden.**
- A timer check in `step` that kept the clock busy only while the prompt was shown, which it already was: removed.
- `soulsMiddle()` returned a constant through a function, and the souls' size was written out four times: they are
  `SOULS_PX` and `SOULS_MIDDLE` now.
- **Left as is**: the clock runs every frame the prompt is up, which is any time you stand near a prop, for the
  sheen every 3.5 s. An idle frame writes nothing: nine springs that return at once, four timers, the 48-particle and
  4-ring loops in `pixelFx`, and the draw's comparisons. Sleeping between sheens would need a timer outside
  `pixelMotion` that ignores the bench's time scale (the pause banner's trade). The billboard's fit writes one
  `UIScale` per frame the camera moves, as the pings do.

### Open points

- Holding with no souls to pay does nothing on the server, and nothing on the prompt says why. A refusal knock would
  need the local souls count in PropsController.

## Last Wave: the world bars (`worldBar`, built 2026-10-30, unjudged)

The two health bars hung in the world, the convoy's and the Greatshield dome's, moved off the old tweened `defaultBar`
onto the HUD's `vitalBar`. `Components/worldBar` hosts it; `Stories/WorldBars` benches both side by side.

| Bar | Style | What it keeps from the old one |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Convoy (`ConvoyClient`) | Slab in the convoy's blue (`pixelSlab.FromColor`), the low alarm, breaks at zero | The word CONVOY, now a pixel tab drawn OVER the bar, centred on its top outline row as the inventory and stats panels wear theirs (round 2: a folder tab standing on the outline read as behind the bar, and its letters were too small) |
| Dome (`GreatshieldClient`) | Neon in `vitalBar.Shield` (the dome is a shield), breaks at zero | No word, as before |

### What it does

- **Arrives**: drops 6 units onto its place on a 0.28 s decelerating curve while fading in, then throws two rings,
  pops the tab (+10%) and charges the bar up from EMPTY: the first `SetMax` seeds it at 0, and the landing calls
  `SetCurrent` with the latest value, so the heal's green band runs ahead, the sheen crosses and the refill dings.
  Damage that lands during the drop is kept and charged to.
- **Is hit**: everything `vitalBar` does (flash, white chip band, chunks, shake, the breathing low alarm on the convoy).
  The tab flashes white and shakes with it but never changes size: hits are frequent.
- **Leaves** (`Leave(kind, onDone)`; the caller unmounts in `onDone`, which is deferred):
  - `Broken`: a bar still above zero is emptied, so `Breaks` shatters it (rings, 28 chunks, thump, max shake); held
    0.45 s, then it falls 8 units on an accelerating curve while fading. The convoy at zero, and every dome end (the
    sphere bursts with it).
  - `Won`: gold rings, the tab pops +14%, 16 gold and white motes rise from above it; held 0.6 s, then it lifts away.
    A delivered convoy.
  - `Faded`: 0.2 s fade. A convoy that failed with health left, a quest cleanup, a dome cleared before a new one.

### What was learned

- **A billboard bar is sized in PX, not studs.** `vitalBar` lays out off its `AbsoluteSize`; a stud-sized billboard
  (or the prompt's stage-under-a-UIScale) changes that every frame the camera moves, and a UIScale over its pixel
  offsets scales them twice. `MinScale` (0.6) stops it shrinking past legible on a phone.
- **Round 3: 260 x 40 bar, a twelve-unit tab (~22 px letters at 1080p), `MinScale` 0.75.** On the bench the bars
  read tiny and the word was unreadable: the sizes were floored at 0.6 but the pixel unit was not, so on a small
  screen the tab got a ONE px unit and ~6 px capitals. The unit is now taken off the same floored scale and handed to
  `vitalBar` (`Unit`), so a small screen gets a thinner unit, never a smaller word. The tab wears the bar's Shade with
  its Fill as the lit row: white letters on the convoy's light blue washed out.
- **Cost**: the tab is in a CanvasGroup, which redraws its texture on any change, so it does not shake (the bar
  under it does) and every write in `draw` is guarded. `vitalBar` lays out only when its unit changes, not on every
  fade, and a bar that is only breathing (low) redraws 20 times a second, not every frame (HUD health too).
  `MaxDistance` 250 studs: the bar is px-sized and on top, so far away the arrow and the minimap marker carry it.
- **The chest's rarity tab** went from 5 to 7 units (~14 to ~19 design px letters on the 960 px stage): LEGENDARY is
  then about the slot's width and stays clear of skip.
- **No number on a world bar** (`vitalBar`'s new `IsNumberHidden`). BillboardGui text needs a CanvasGroup on some
  phones, and a group round the bar clips the chunks it throws. Only the tab's word sits in a CanvasGroup, with four
  units of room round it for its pop and shake.
- **The leave owns the adornee's lifetime**: the callers destroy it in `onDone`, so the bar plays its leave where the
  convoy stopped instead of vanishing with it.
- Particles: the win motes are born 8 units above the bar's top (the tab reaches 5, the win rings 7), float up under
  drag and never come back; checked with `lune` at the slowest launch. The longest mote (0.9 s) dies before the leave
  ends (0.95 s), so unmounting never cuts one off.

### Checked, and how

Linted (StyLua, Selene), compiled with `lune`, place built with Rojo, tab pops simulated (+9.9% / +13.8%), motes' worst
case simulated. **Not played in Studio** and not seen on the bench yet: judge it on `Stories/WorldBars`, then on a
convoy quest and a Greatshield ult. Whether `ClipsDescendants = false` lets the thrown pieces draw outside the
billboard's box is the first thing to look at in a playtest.


## Last Wave: the tutorial card (`tutorialPrompt`, built 2026-10-30, unjudged)

Asked for: the in-run tutorial (InGameTutorialController's prompt over the character and the stats tip at the side) in
the new style, as satisfying as it can be. Built, wired, benched (`Stories/Tutorial`); linted, compiled, the place
built with Rojo, spark reach and spring peaks simulated with `lune`. **Not played in Studio and not judged on the bench.**

- **One component, two hosts.** `Components/tutorialPrompt` draws a Slab card in real px at the pixel unit: a STEP n/3
  tab on the outline (TIP for the stats card), a square panel (the key's KeyImages glyph on a keyboard or a pad, a drawn
  keycap only for a key with no glyph, a pixel tap mark on touch, or the icon of what to find; the key never moves by
  itself, as on the prop prompt), the instruction, and while souls are gathered a count panel
  and a bar. `onResize` reports the card plus its margins, so the head billboard is OFFSET-sized (same size on screen
  at any zoom, on the pixel grid) inside a CanvasGroup, kept enabled (the mobile text rule). The side card is the same
  component in a ScreenGui, anchored left where the inventory opens. Each step has its own palette (Red, Gold, Magenta;
  violet for the tip). The head card has a bobbing pointer arrow under it.
- **Every change is a beat.** Arrival: drop and pop from 82%, flash, rings and side sparks once landed. A phase change
  (gathering -> search -> the key): flash, +4% thump, tab and panel punch, sheen. Souls: the bar fills on the reading
  spring, the count rolls down and punches, a rising ScoreTick; full strikes in blue (+10%, rings, ScoreComplete), and
  the controller holds the phase change 0.45 s (`SOULS_STRIKE_HOLD`) so the full bar is seen. A finished step is
  **stamped on the card**: green, DONE!, the tick popping into the panel, +9% thump, 22 sparks, then it pops away with
  a puff and the next step drops in. Anything set while the stamp plays (content, souls) waits for the next arrival.
  The "THE RUN CONTINUES" banner waits a second for the altar's stamp.
- **Width follows the text on a spring**, relaid only on whole-unit changes; the holder is sized to the wider of where
  the card is and where it is going so a shrink is not clipped.
- Not done: `tutorialPulse` (the arrows round a mobile button, shared with the lobby) is still the old look, and so are
  ArrowController's world arrows and indicators.

### What the Reel card does, beat by beat

- **Thrown out of the chest** face down (the chest's gold, an inset border, a big `?`), from the middle of the row
  outward, on cubics up out of the mouth and down into place, landing with a thump and dust.
- **Turns over**: narrows to its middle a unit a frame, flips, widens; the reel starts spinning (11 pictures a second).
- **The band climbs** Common upward: the card takes each tier (the level-up's palettes and ladder), thumps, throws an
  echo of its frame, ChestJump rising; the tease and Secret's breach are the level-up card's.
- **The reel stops** five pictures on (eight for the last card), easing out at the spin's speed, ticking each picture
  (`ObjectChange`, rising; `TicketTick` for tickets), always centred on a whole picture.
- **Lands**: bounce, flash, pop, rings, burst, the light's full fan (Epic and up keep a glow), shake from Epic, the
  name pops in, confetti; the ribbons slap in 0.22 s later, 0.14 s apart. Secret's band decodes from noise.
- **Order**: cards open lowest rarity first, 0.25 s apart, so the best is always last.

### Round 5 (2026-11-02): the snap, and a hand that fits the screen

Opening 50 boxes in the lobby, the user saw the cards appear off to the side and snap into the chest before flying out,
and the title and buttons huge with one card and tiny with 25 or 50, though the screen had room.

| What was wrong | The fix |
| --- | --- |
| The card's body waited **hidden at its slot** and was turned visible on the frame it was thrown; the engine drew the slot first (§3, "A frame turned `Visible`...") | Both card styles keep the body visible and park it at `PARKED` (off-screen) until `Deal`'s flight starts or `Land` draws it in place; `isThrown` replaces every `body.Visible` test |
| The chrome was `min(hand's unit, 0.7 of the cap)`, so it **followed the hand**: 10 px a unit with one card, 3 with fifty | The chrome has its own unit: `0.7 x cap`, and at most **7 px a unit per 1080 of height** (`ChromeHeightShare`). That keeps the run at 5 and the lobby at 7 for every hand |
| The lobby's canvas reads `PixelSize` at **~2.3x** (`setCanvasScale`), so the cap was 16 and only height stopped one card | The cap is also held to **10 px a unit per 1080 of height** (`CapHeightShare`), today's single-card size |
| `fitGrid` **floored** the unit to whole px and reserved the title and buttons at the hand's unit | It returns the exact fractional fit against the room the chrome leaves. The card's size follows it (`round(36 x q)`) and its pixel is `round(q)`. The card's insides already shrink to their room (`min(...)` against the inner height), so a card a few % under its grid still lays out |
| Gaps of 7 units between cards cost a big hand a column | A hand of **three rows or more** closes its gaps (`TightGaps`: 4 / 4 / 5 / 5 units) |
| The hand centred on the screen's middle, leaving a band under the title at fifty | The hand centres in the room **between the title and the buttons** |

## Last Wave: score, reward and sound feedback (2026-10-31)

The final stats needed audible satisfaction as points and currencies accumulated. Subsequent listening
rounds established that feedback needs a readable onset, appropriate weight and a restrained pitch climb.
Adding a valid asset ID is not enough. These are the UI lessons from that work; [Sounds.md](Sounds.md)
owns the full audio rules and combat-specific corrections so the two documents do not drift independently.

### Where the behavior lives

| Owner | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `src/Survivors/Client/UI/Components/finalScreen.luau` | Counter presentation, local-player tick cadence, independent pitch chains, show/hide/replay state |
| `src/Survivors/Client/UI/FinalStatsUI.luau` | Run data, canonical `RunStatsCore` labels and stats, avatars and input integration |
| `src/Global/Client/UI/Components/uiSound.luau` | Cached templates, bounded repeated voices, UI routing and edit-mode playback |
| `src/Global/Shared/Utils/pitchChain.luau` | Small consecutive-arrival pitch climb and reset behavior |
| `src/Survivors/Client/UI/Stories/FinalStats.story.luau` | Reproducible end-screen presentation bench |
| `Assets/Sounds/manifest.json` and `Feedback.model.json` | Current source files, uploaded IDs, template gains, rates, regions and SoundGroup references |

### A counter should sound like progress, then stop

- Sound follows the displayed increase for the **local player's row**, not every visible player's totals.
  Score ticks run during the active reveal, at most once per 75 ms. Do not play once per point crossed:
  a slow frame can skip many values, and replaying them all creates a backlog rather than satisfaction.
- Ticket and stardust gains share a 140 ms cadence, alternating when both advance. Separate pitch chains
  preserve their identities. Reopening resets all three chains and cadence state; leaving/hidden phases
  must not start more counter ticks. Test interruption during the count as well as a completed reveal.
- `PitchChain.Next` returns a multiplier: consecutive arrivals less than 0.45 s apart add 0.01, capped at
  14 steps (1.14). A gap resets the next multiplier to 1. Multiply the template's authored PlaybackSpeed;
  do not replace it. This is a subtle climb, not a progressively squeakier reward or an ultimate-power trick.
- `uiSound` debounces the same name within 30 ms, so several synchronized cards do not stack the same cue.
  ScoreTick, TicketTick and StardustTick each reuse four voices during play; other UI cues keep the existing
  one-shot path. A cycling voice may restart, so verify the real overlap before increasing pool size.
- The first ScoreTick file was a 49 ms menu-like clip and was inaudible in review. The corrected 131 ms
  coin blip reads better. Test the envelope and audible body alongside the actual animation and music;
  nonzero Volume and successful loading do not establish a usable tick.

The subtle chain logic came from **Anime Zombie Survival**'s coin controller; arrival batching/pooling ideas
also came from **BeACastleLord**. Borrow the logic, not those projects' audio files. Same-frame pickup arrivals
are batched so a crowd of drops does not create an uncontrolled stack of voices. Final-stats ticking belongs
to the local presentation; positional chest sounds remain with `ChestClient` so a UI mounted for another
player's chest does not produce a global duplicate.

### Choose and mix for the meaning of the event

- Reward confirmations may be tonal and positive. Dashes, impacts and combat ultimates need their own
  material and force; a little song, boing or alert does not become appropriate because it is retro.
- Use gain on the **Sound instances** to match files with different source levels. Keep source WAVs unchanged
  in project `Assets/Sounds`. Review against existing game audio: the first internally balanced additions
  were still much too quiet beside it. Consult the current manifest and balance reports before retuning.
- Preserve a power hierarchy. Small repeated ticks sit below completion/payoff cues; a stronger event needs
  appropriate body and attack, not just a longer tail or higher pitch. A visual's duration does not dictate
  the sound's duration. The user's latest Death Line direction is an initial massive boom and a silent ray
  continuation, superseding the earlier request for sustained audio.
- Keep sound and visible meaning together: landings/arrivals, completed reveals and server-confirmed claims.
  A sound added to a callback that also runs on stop can double an action. Audit the whole lifecycle and
  existing overlapping sounds before adding an activation cue or replacing a voice the user already likes.
- Every game Sound template and active clone needs the correct SoundGroup. UI ticks route to UI, combat and
  world effects to Effects, music to Music. Persist model references through Rojo and verify built instances.
  Active voices use `PlayOnRemove = false`; some original UI template paths intentionally play on removal,
  so do not globally rewrite every template flag or change `SoundsCore.Clone` to suppress those paths.

### Review without repeating the setup mistakes

1. Reproduce the exact count, claim or interruption in the real component/story. Cover replay, large jumps,
   simultaneous currencies, another player's row and closing mid-count. Check that cleanup stops new work.
2. Use the current source and manifest for expected values. Old reports and scratch probes describe their own
   revisions; do not restore an earlier candidate or assume an old expected gain is still current.
3. Check source formatting/lint against baseline, compile changed large modules, and build the affected
   places when code or assets change. Distinguish offline layout/assignment checks from a renderer or mix test.
4. For a controlled Studio probe, keep it temporary in StarterPlayerScripts. Tripwire's start ACK arrives
   before F5 cloning: wait for its unique client BEGIN log before deleting the edit-mode script. Read the
   completion log, clean up runtime objects and wrappers, and end the test you own. Do not enable loadstring,
   change saved data or reconnect Rojo to make a presentation test work. Disclose probes during user review.
5. Verify actual asset loading and the cloned voices' gain, rate and group. A loaded silent/wrongly cropped
   file can still fail. Numerical matching and controlled playback do not replace the user's listening review.

The previous audio pass recorded its controlled Studio checks and source/build evidence in
`Assets/Sounds/sound-rules-verification.json`; per-cue decisions are in `Assets/Sounds/RulesAudit.md` and
`rules-audit.json`. Those are dated evidence, not a blanket claim that every screen has been visually reviewed
or every input device tested. **This documentation update changes no runtime behavior and runs no playtest.**

the moving panel through its final settling frame. `inspectCard.SetPosition` updates only the anchor, preserving
the current reveal, text and sound state; unchanged anchors do no work. This fixes the tooltip staying at the
panel's offscreen opening position until selection moves. An offline regression reproduces the old behavior and
checks both panels at 30, 60 and 144 Hz without changing selection, including settled idle behavior. Formatting,
compilation, lint and the Game build checked; no Studio or physical-controller playtest was run for this fix.

## Last Wave: the settings menu (`settingsScreen`, built 2026-11-01, unjudged)

Settings is the first pixel-Slab screen that both places draw: the lobby puts it on the arcade `SurfaceGui` (a
1080-tall canvas), the run in a `ScreenGui`. The old menu sized its text with `TextScaled` and its key glyphs and
value box with `scaleNumber`, so the two hosts disagreed (canvas mode vs viewport mode, and a TextScaled line fits
its box, not the design). **The rule that fixes it: every size is a whole number of pixel units taken from the
screen's own `AbsoluteSize`** (`p = clamp(round(height / 1080 * 4), 2, width * 0.96 / 260)`), nothing reads
`scaleNumber`, nothing is `TextScaled`. A SurfaceGui reports AbsoluteSize in canvas pixels, so the lobby's canvas
and a 1080p window both get p = 4 and a 1040 x 992 panel. Any screen shared by both places should be built this way.

- `SettingsUI/init.luau` (wrapper) builds each tab's rows as plain `TRowSpec` tables (`Tabs/*`), owns the pad's
  Back / L1-R1 / Y stacks and focus restore. `Components/settingsScreen` draws the panel, tabs, list and BACK;
  `settingsRow` is one row; the controls are `settingsSwitch` (+ `settingsToggle` for one switch or a captioned
  pair), `settingsSlider` and `settingsKeys`. `settingsKit` holds the colours and the control contract. Bench:
  `Global/Client/UI/Stories/Settings` (time scale, reopen, next tab) mounts `settingsScreen` on fake rows.
- **The drawing must not require `GamepadFocusController`**: it indexes `Players.LocalPlayer` at load, which is nil
  in edit mode, so the first bench (mounting the `SettingsUI` wrapper) failed to load. A key slot's "B cancels the
  listen, Y does nothing" is a `Capture` callback the wrapper passes in; the bench passes a no-op.
- `pixelFx` and `uiSound` moved from `Survivors/Client/UI/Components` to `Global/Client/UI/Components` so the lobby
  can use them; every Survivors require now walks up to `GlobalClient.UI.Components`.
- **Juice, by event.** Open: the panel rises 4 units from 94.5% with the backdrop fading to 55%, rows rise in
  staggered 0.03 s. Tab: a gold plate slides to the tab, its leading edge on a quicker spring (it stretches to 72u
  over a 53u tab and snaps shut), flashes and throws rings; the new rows slide in 10 units from the tab's side.
  Hover / pad: the row lifts 0.6 u, turns gold with a white outline, and the inventory's focus brackets travel to
  it. Switch on: the knob stretches toward the far end (13u to 17.6u) and lands, the well flashes and turns green,
  the switch thumps +5.6% and throws green rings; off is a smaller, ringless thump at a lower click. Slider: every
  step ticks with a pitch climbing 0.82 to 1.3 across the range and flashes the cells it lit; the readout punches
  +8.7%; reaching either end thumps the track and throws rings. Key slot: listening breathes gold, a bound key
  flashes, punches +8.2% and throws rings. Off-default rows show a gold stripe and a reset key that grows in from
  40% to +12% and settles. All of those numbers were run through the real spring solver in `lune`.
- No particles: every place a spark could fly crosses a row, a reset key or a neighbour (checklist rule 1). Rings
  and flashes carry the light instead.
- Pad: one stop per row (the row itself for a switch or slider, each switch / key slot otherwise); Up / Down go to
  the nearest stop in the next row, BACK closes the loop. Held left / right on a switch or slider steps it with a
  0.32 s delay then every 0.075 s (polled with `GetGamepadState`, so a phone's pad cannot stick). The clock stays
  awake only while a pad rests on such a row, and a settled screen writes nothing.
- Pitfall hit while building: `pixelMotion.Snap` sets the **target** as well as the value. Snapping a pop to -0.6
  and shoving it left the reset key parked at 40% forever. Snap, then set `Target` back to rest.
- Pitfall avoided: a row's control holder left at ZIndex 1 draws under the row's opaque outline (Kick's portrait
  bug); it is raised to 7.

Checked: StyLua, Selene (no new diagnostics), every changed file compiles, both places build, unit / panel sizes
for lobby canvas, 1080p, 1440p, 768p, phone and 4K computed in `lune`, spring peaks simulated. **Not playtested or
seen in Studio, and not tried with a pad, touch or the Text Size setting.**

### Round 2 (2026-11-01): pad in the run, scrollbar, key glyphs

- **Focus did not land when opened from the topbar.** `SettingsUI` now uses `PushFocus` and re-asserts on every
  `SelectedObject` change while open (KickUI's `syncFocus` shape), returning to the last stop or the first row.
- **R1 jumped instead of cycling tabs**: `CharacterController` binds Jump (R1 on a pad) at `High`, above the
  default priority `PushCycle` used. The cycle is now bound at `High + 1` (lobby included; nothing there outranks it).
- **The right stick turned the camera.** `GamepadFocusController.PushMenu()` (new) sinks `Thumbstick2` through
  ContextActionService at `High + 1` while a full menu is open; the camera reads the stick through CAS, while
  `gamepadScroll` polls `GetGamepadState` and still sees it, so the list scrolls. Slider nudges use the left stick
  and DPad only.
- **DPad Right opened the inventory** (InfoController takes its key even when GUI navigation marked it processed).
  `GamepadFocusController.IsMenuOpen()` gates the run's Info, Map, Ping and Restart keys while Settings is open.
- Scrollbar now matches the inventory: ink track, gold thumb with a lit top and shaded bottom row.
- Key glyphs sit centred on the top edge of what they act on, as the old menu had them: B on BACK, Y on the reset
  key, L1 / R1 on the tabs they would switch to (they move with the plate).

Linted, compiled and built; **not played with a pad in Studio.**

### Round 3 (2026-11-01): binding anything, one slot at a time

- L1 / R1 are back at the left and right of the tab row, level with it. B and Y stay centred on their button's top
  edge.
- **A pad button never bound**: the listen dropped processed input, and every pad button is processed while a menu
  holds the selection. It now takes processed input. B and Escape still cancel.
- **Several slots could listen at once**: each row kept its own state. One module-level listen now ends the one
  before it.
- **Anything binds**: keys, pad buttons, mouse buttons (stored as `KeyCode.MouseLeftButton` / `Right` / `Middle`)
  and the wheel (no KeyCode, so `KeybindsCore.WHEEL_UP` 4096 / `WHEEL_DOWN` 4097, allowed by DatabaseService's
  SaveKeybind check; no schema change). `KeybindsCore.InputValue(input)` is what every reader now passes to
  `IsBound`; `BindableOf` gives ContextActionService a mouse button's UserInputType. A wheel notch is a press with
  no release, fired on `KeybindsCore.Wheel` by SettingsController: abilities, info, map, ping, zoom, unlock mouse
  and jump take it; sprint, slide, restart, pause and interact are held and ignore it.
- While a slot listens, a transparent shield covers the screen, so the click being bound does not also press what
  is under it; a listen cannot restart within 0.3 s of taking a key (the pad's A is both a key and "select"), and a
  DPad press that was bound puts the selection back where it was.

Linted, compiled, both places built; **not played.**

### Round 4 (2026-11-01): the top bar, for real

`IgnoreGuiInset = true` switches `ScreenInsets` from `CoreUISafeInsets` to `DeviceSafeInsets` (Roblox docs), and Vide
applies properties in hash order, so a ScreenGui listing both lands either way. Settings and Kick were under the
top bar; Info, Reward, Upgrade and FinalStats happened to apply `ScreenInsets` last. All six now set only
`ScreenInsets = CoreUISafeInsets`. Settings' and Kick's dims are their own `Backdrop` instances, mounted by
`TopbarController.overlayGuis` in a full-screen `ScreenInsets = None` ScreenGui one DisplayOrder below the panel's,
so the strip behind the top bar is dimmed. The lobby parents `settingsUI.Backdrop` to its SurfaceGui (ZIndex 9,
under the panel's 10). FinalStats keeps its overhanging dim; Info / Reward / Upgrade use the shared
`selectionBackdrop`, which is already its own full-screen ScreenGui. Linted, compiled, built; not played.

### Music switch hover ownership (2026-11-06)

Moving from a track's LOBBY / IN-GAME switch back onto the same setting cleared its gold row highlight. Each
`settingsRow` hit target reported its own `MouseLeave` as a leave of the whole row, although the parent row was
still hovered and would not send another `MouseEnter`.

- `settingsRow` owns the set of hovered hit targets and the current controller stop. Only leaving the last mouse
  target releases mouse hover; a late `SelectionLost` from another stop cannot clear the current stop. Controller
  focus and mouse hover retain each other when one ends. Disabling the row clears both.
- `settingsToggle.Pair` owns each switch's mouse and controller light independently, combining them for its caption
  and outline. Touch-generated mouse enters are ignored; disabling clears the light on both switches.
- Do not clear a row on every child's leave, share one boolean between mouse and controller events, or add coordinate
  hit tests. The same event ownership works on the lobby's SurfaceGui and the run's ScreenGui without polling.

Regression cases: row -> either switch -> row; parent leave while a child remains hovered; last child leave;
mouse enter/leave while selected; selection lost while hovered; new stop gained before the old stop loses selection;
disable/reopen; touch-generated enter; teardown. Hover must never save or change music preferences.

Checked with an offline Lune harness executing the actual row and pair modules against mocked input and drawing:
the earlier source fails eight checks, the fix passes all cases. Both modules compile, `stylua --check src` passes,
and changed-file Selene reports no diagnostics. Full-tree Selene still reports unrelated errors and warnings.
**Not playtested in Studio or verified with a physical controller.**

**The scrap, beat by beat.** Press: SCRAP sinks a unit (ClickHud is the slot's; SCRAP's own press has no sound so the
payout is the sound). Send: the counter holds its number. Server's new stash: the slot crunches (ChestBanish), SCRAP
flashes, thumps and throws lime rings, and 6 to 16 ticket pieces (one per 40 tickets) are thrown round the slot
against drag (k = 7), hang, and boomerang into the counter on placed landings, 0.42 s to 1.12 s, gaps closing from
193 ms to 38 ms. Each landing releases its slice of the number, swells the ticket (peak +5.5%, under 0.2 px a frame,
simulated) and ticks TicketTick on the pitch chain; the last strikes the "+N" and RewardBanked. A stack emptied
puffs apart and the surviving stacks close the gap in place (see the update below). A burst whose pieces were stolen by a newer one
pays out at 1.6 s; a hold nobody releases lets go at 2.5 s (a scrap the server refused).

Other events: opening rises 4 units from 94.5% and deals the slots down the grid (0.018 s each); a new category deals
in a column at a time from the side the carousel moved toward; a stack that grew strikes; slots a capacity purchase
unlocked strike; a locked slot shakes with BuyRefuse and the old toast; picking an item names it and its count / stack
cap between BACK and the amount, and SCRAP wakes from grey to lime with a thump and shows `SCRAP +N`.

Pad: the grid's links stop at its edges, the scroll follows the selection, L2 / R2 change category and the pad stays
on its slot (what is under it becomes the pick, as the old rebuild's refocus did), X scraps, Y opens the amount menu
(focus drops into it; B closes only it), B leaves. Touch: no hover; tap picks, a second tap within 0.35 s scraps; a
tap anywhere else closes the amount menu.

Pitfalls this round avoided or hit:

- A cross-module drawing that the bench must mount cannot require `GamepadFocusController` (no LocalPlayer in edit
  mode), so the dropdown split in two, like settings. `keyHint` / `scrollbar` are fine, through the live tree.
- LobbyUI writes the page's `Visible` and `Appear` writes it again on the same open: the show effect ignores a repeat,
  or every open dealt twice and pushed the pad's bindings twice. Selection and amount reset on hide, because the page
  is shown before `Appear` runs.
- The ticket sized at height / 10 left the old 54 x 27 top-bar chip a 9 px number; at height / 14 with the stub dropped
  when narrow it is about as readable as the old image chip, which is the real limit (the box is 54 px wide).
- `select` as a local name shadows the builtin (Selene `must_use`): `choose` / `selectTab`.

Benches: `Lobby/Client/UI/Stories/Stash` (capacity level, pad glyphs, reopen, scrap picked, next category, one more of
the first), `Global/Client/UI/Stories/TopBar` (picked tab, badge count, gain / spend / refused tickets),
`Global/Client/UI/Stories/Dropdown` (open, up / down, row height).

Checked: StyLua, Selene (clean on every changed file), every changed file compiles, both places build, layout at
1920, 1440, 2520 and 1280 x 720 canvases and 844 x 390, the ticket's number sizes and the payout's landing schedule
and swell worked out in `lune`. **Not playtested, not opened on the bench, and not tried with a pad, touch or the
Text Size setting.** The other lobby pages that now carry the new tab bar, ticket and dropdown have not been looked at.

### Scrapping updates in place (2026-11-06)

`stashScreen.SetCells` retains the slot pool and skips unchanged slot contents. A partial scrap updates only its
stack; an emptied stack moves the affected survivors along their row, with only row crossings popping into their
new cell, following BeACastleLord's `PackUI`. Replaying every trailing slot's entrance made a scrap look like a grid
rebuild. Full-grid entrances belong to opening and category changes. `StashUI` and the Stash story no longer pass
`shiftFrom`; the drawing compares stack names and counts itself. It snapshots changed input cells because the
story mutates its tables, and a second scrap starts a slide at the survivor's current position.

Offline checks of the actual reconciliation and clock functions cover unchanged syncs, partial/last/batch scraps,
row crossings, interrupted slides, slot identity, gains, capacity unlocks, full entrances and idle sleep. StyLua,
compilation and the Lobby build pass; full-tree Selene adds no diagnostics to its existing baseline. Not playtested
in Studio or on a physical controller.
