### Recipe: a readout every page shows, and the payout that flies into it

The tickets took four rounds (one shape per tab, then day 7 differing, then the look, then the dark middle). Each
correction below was predictable; do them up front for any currency, counter or status that more than one screen
shows.

**One of it:**
1. **Mount ONE instance above the pages** (`ticketsWallet`, mounted by LobbyUI), in one fixed spot, and let pages reach
   it through params: `TicketsBox` for a tab bar to keep clear of (`tabBar`'s `KeepClearOf`), `Counter` for a page that
   pays into it. A shared component that each page sizes and places itself still changes shape and jumps between
   tabs; the user reads that as different things.
2. **The same drawing, smaller, is still the same component** (`ticketsChip` for reward amounts wraps
   `ticketsCounter`). Search every caller (`grep -rn ticketsCounter src`) and look at each one at its real size,
   including the odd one out (day 7 is a bigger cell than days 1 to 6).
3. **One flight for every payout** (`ticketsFlight`). Screens throw it; none keeps its own pieces. The caller `Hold`s
   the counter before the balance changes, or the change rolls in ahead of the pieces.

**A pixel drawing that sizes itself from its box:**
4. **Fix the row count and take the columns from the box's proportions**, then the biggest whole unit that fits
   (`rows = 14; columns = round(rows * w / h); p = floor(min(h / rows, w / columns))`). Rounding the unit from the
   height and flooring the columns made one 2:1 box anywhere from 21 to 40 columns, so a threshold (the stubs) flipped
   with the size. Check it in `lune` across every size the callers use: every box of one shape must print one grid.
5. Any threshold on the grid (stubs, notches) is set so the shapes actually in use land on the same side of it.

**The look the user picked, and what they reject:**
6. **No dark well in the middle of a coloured object.** On the ticket it read as "a black box". Print the number on
   the object's own face, on a panel pressed in one unit (its Shade row along the top, its Light row along the bottom),
   white with the ink outline. Dark wells are for slabs and slots, not for a thing that is one colour.
7. **Picked:** gold over orange; on a gain, **both** the square side sparks and pixel glints round a soft bloom; the
   payout pieces as **glints**. **Rejected:** a pill with a hopping icon, idle twinkles on a resting readout, the
   pixel-ticket pieces and the cut gem chips.
8. **"Shiny particles like BeACastleLord's"** means UI.md 5j's collect pieces drawn with that game's sprites: the
   9 x 9 pixel glint (`ResampleMode = Pixelated`, a whole number of units so its art pixels stay square) with the glow
   dot behind it as a halo, a streak along its motion (a Frame with a `UIGradient` fading to its tail, rotated to the
   heading, half a streak back), an `easeOutBack` pop-in over 0.08 s, a twinkle, shrinking to 45% and whitening over
   the pull, and fading over the last 6%.

**BeACastleLord's art is usable directly:** both games upload under the same Roblox group (`ROBLOX_GROUP_ID` in both
`.env` files), so its asset ids work here with no upload. Where to find them:

| What | Where in `../BeACastleLord` | Id |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rune glint (4-point pixel star) | `Assets/effects/runes/images.json` (`glint`) | `105849311096915` |
| Glow dot (soft round light) | `Assets/effects/make_effects_rbxmx.py` (`GLOW_DOT_TEXTURE`) | `95624436217204` |
| Cut gem face (white, cut corners) | `src/Global/Client/UI/Components/facet.luau` (`FACES.Cut.Plane`) | `140261849228744` |
| Other rune sprites (ember, streak, spark sheet...) | `Assets/effects/runes/images.json` | |

The source pngs sit next to those files; composite them onto one dark sheet with PIL to see them before choosing.
The collect motion itself is in that repo's UI.md, "The shape of a satisfying collect" to "Building it so it stays
cheap"; this file's 5j is the same recipe.

**The bench, the way the user wants it (one round, not three):**
9. One story with **every axis as its own `UILabs.Choose`** (look, palette, gain burst, idle on or off, flight
   pieces) so they mix freely, plus `Do:` flips for gain, spend, refused and a payout that flies in, and a time scale.
   Show the readout where it really sits **and** every other size it is drawn at (the reward chips) side by side.
10. A look change rebuilds the bench and keeps the state (the balance). Vide's unmount only releases the reactive
    scope, so `root:ClearAllChildren()` after it, or the old drawing stays under the new one.
11. While options are on the bench they go through one `Style` table on the component, never a copy of it per look.
    Once the user picks: delete every losing branch, the `Style` type, its params on every wrapper, and the story's
    style controls; keep the story as the bench for the picked look.

**Before reporting, answer "is this the most optimized and readable it can be?" yourself** (it is asked every round):
12. No forward declarations, no field written onto another module's table afterwards; pass hooks into the
    constructor (`OnRolled`).
13. Build effects lazily on first use: most counters (reward amounts) never gain, so their sparks, glints, bloom and
    sweep are never made. Size every pool from the real worst case and say the number in a comment.
14. After trimming options, grep for comments that name what was removed (an old ticket size, "pieces" in a section
    name) and for locals selene now reports unused.

### Pixel fidelity: one bezel, and chrome derived from it (2026-11-02)

The user's rule: every border in the game is the same weight and is made of the same pixels. A Slab is an ink
outline one unit thick, a bezel `pixelSlab.Bezel` units thick (2, the Codex's, picked by the user), and the well. A
two-unit Slab must look exactly like a one-unit one drawn at double size. Never lose this in an edit:

1. **Lay every Slab out with `pixelSlab.Bezel`.** Never a literal, never a `Tune.Bezel` of the module's own. A part
   that draws its own bezel in Frames (`actionButton`, `abilitySlot`, `touchButton`, `statusTile`, `rewardCard`,
   `upgradeCard`, the thumbstick's knob in `MobileControlsUI`) reads the same constant. The only literal allowed is
   `0`, for a badge or chip that has no band at all (the tab bar's and carousel's count badges, the end screen's
   BEST / TOP chips, the kick list's Rail row).
2. **The lit row and the shaded row are the bezel's full thickness**, not one unit. At one unit on a two-unit bezel
   the shine is half the band and reads as half a pixel: measured off a screenshot at a 3 px unit, the top was ink 3,
   light 3, gold 3, and the sides gold 6. `pixelSlab.Body` does this; a self-drawn bezel must size its light and
   shade by `b`, the bezel in px.
3. **Never write the chrome as a number.** From a Slab's outside to its well is `pixelSlab.Edge` units (ink +
   bezel); across the well both sides add `pixelSlab.Chrome`. So a well is `w - pixelSlab.Chrome * p`, content on
   the Slab's body starts at `pixelSlab.Edge * p`, a panel sized to its content is `contentH + pixelSlab.Chrome * p`,
   and a tab's bottom in well space subtracts `pixelSlab.Edge * p`. Better still, lay out against the `wellW, wellH`
   that `Layout` returns. Every `4 * p` and `2 * p` that meant the chrome of a one-unit bezel broke when the bezel
   changed: the dropdown's panel came out short, and the carousel's word and arrows sat a unit low and right.
4. **A part with words or an icon in it grows; its well does not shrink.** A thicker bezel takes `2 * Bezel` units
   more from the well. Work out what the well held (text size, icon, a nested control) and add the difference to
   the part's height, not take it from the text. What grew for the 2-unit bezel: the quest card's claim plate and
   bar 9 -> 11 units, its badge 11 -> 13, the card 42 -> 46; the Settings row 24 -> 26 (its paired switches are 19
   units and would overlap an 18-unit well); the end screen's facts and page tabs 9 -> 11, buttons 14 -> 16, board
   rows 17 -> 19 (the rank square stays 13, which the row's width is built from), damage rows 14 -> 16. Every Slab's own
   size in units is a tuning value worth re-checking against its well when the bezel changes.
5. **What is NOT a bezel keeps its one-unit rows**, because there is no band to match: a fill's lit row inside a
   well (bars, sliders, the quest card's bar), keycaps (ink, face with one lit row, lip), the Codex's corner marks,
   the tickets counter's stepped ticket, the scrollbar's thumb, a tab hung over a Slab's edge.

**Checking a change**: grep for `.Layout(` calls ending in a literal (`, 1)`, `, 2)`), for `Bezel = ` in a `Tune`,
and for `4 * p` / `2 * p` beside a well or a Slab's body. A screenshot read pixel by pixel (Python, PIL) settles
whether a row is a whole pixel: walk one column down through the top edge and one row across the side.

### A pressed part moves as one (2026-11-02)

A pixel Slab's word is a **sibling** of its body (`pixelSlab.Letters` parented beside it, not inside it), and so is a
count badge, so moving `Slab.Body` moves nothing else. The tab bar's press set only `tab.Slab.Body.Position`: the
button sank a unit and the word stayed where it was, in every tab bar in the game. Hover still looked right because
the lift's clock moved all three, so it only showed on a held click.

1. **One function places a part's pieces from its state** (`placeTab` in `tabBar`). It reads the offset once
   (`local y = slabY(tab)`) and writes the body, the word (`y - Raise`) and anything hung on it (badge, icon). Press,
   release, hover, pad focus, the lift's clock and layout all call it. Nothing else writes those `Position`s. The
   other answer is to parent the word **inside** `Slab.Body` (`codexButton` does), so moving the body carries it.
2. **Store the word's raise from `pixelSlab.Fit`** (`tab.Raise`) at layout and reuse it. Never work it out again
   somewhere else: the lift's clock had its own `TextSize * 0.075`, which is not what `Fit` returns, so the word could
   jump a pixel on hover.
3. **Keep the move apart from the size.** Placing on a press writes positions only. Re-measuring text, `Layout` on a
   Slab and `Fit` belong to layout and to a change in content (`sizeBadge` runs on layout and when the count
   changes, never on a press).

**Checking a change**: grep the part for `.Position =`. Outside its place and layout functions there should be none.
Then hold a click on it and look at the word, not the button.

## Last Wave: the rarity ladder everywhere (`rarityLook`, `rarityImpact`, built 2026-11-01, unjudged)

Asked for after a review of how a player learns that Mythic beats Legendary: one rarity look on every surface, the
landing sounds as a scale, a hit on the whole screen that grows a channel a tier, top finds told to other players,
the Codex sorted best first, and the run's chest opening reused for the lobby's boxes. Bench: `Stories/Rarity`.
Linted, compiled, both places built, the grid and the stagger checked in `lune`. **Not played in Studio and not seen
on the bench.**

### One look, read everywhere (`Components/rarityLook`)

- The level-up card's palettes and ornaments moved out of `upgradeCard` into `rarityLook`, with the word a player
  reads (`Name`: Godly is Divine), the Slab palette for a slot or chip (`Slab`), the colour of a tier's NAME on a dark
  panel (`Word`: its light, but Divine white and Secret the void's violet, since their fills are near black), the
  note it lands on and its sample (`Note`, `LandSound`, `Chord`) and its screen hit (`Impacts`). Every colour goes
  through `pixelSlab.Show`, so the lobby's correction leaves it as drawn.
- Read by `upgradeCard`, `chestReveal`, both win box cards, `inventorySlot`, the inventory, the stash, the end screen,
  the Codex, the shop's drop rates and `chestPoolCache.RARITY_NAME_BY_ID`. **The three `rarityPalette` copies built
  their slab with `pixelSlab.FromColor`, which turned Divine (white) into the grey New slab again**: the exact report
  the level-up card was rebuilt for. They read `rarityLook.Slab` now.
- **A slot wears its rarity's glow** (`TSlotLook.Rarity`): the card's stepped rings, a ring a tier from Uncommon,
  three from Epic, white for Divine, black for Secret. Static frames under the slab, so dozens of slots cost nothing a
  frame. The strike's motes are born past the outermost ring (particle rule 2). Where slots sit 2 units apart (the end
  screen) the outer rings of neighbours overlap; judge it there first.
- The drop rates show each tier's slab fill edged in its word colour, and the name in that colour.

### The scale (item 5)

Every climb (level-up card, run chest, win box cards) steps ChestJump up a MAJOR SCALE from 0.9 (Common) to the
octave at Secret (`SCALE` in `rarityLook`; the old linear 1 + 0.05 a tier spanned six semitones and no key). The low
tiers share one landing sample, so it is pitched by the same scale (Common 1, Uncommon 1.12, Rare 1.26); Epic and up
keep their own. Over the top tiers a chord on ChestJump: Mythic a fifth, Divine a major chord and its octave, Secret a
LOW TRITONE (the interval that sounds wrong, for the tier that should not exist). `uiSound` takes `isLayered` so a
chord's three notes are not merged by its 0.03 s gap.

### The hit (`Components/rarityImpact`, item 7)

**Updated 2026-11-06:** rarity landings no longer pause animations; see "Rarity landings keep moving" below.
The hit-stop values and behavior in this original review are historical.

One new channel a tier, so the top differs in kind:

| Tier | Stage shake | Hit-stop | Edge vignette | Other |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rare | 0.6 unit | | | |
| Epic | 1 | | 1 band, 0.5 s | |
| Legendary | 1.5 | 0.07 s | 2 bands, 0.8 s | |
| Mythic | 2 | 0.1 s | 3 bands, 1.2 s, breathes twice | |
| Divine | 2.5 | 0.12 s | 3 white bands, 1.5 s | Columns of light up the whole screen; music dips 8 dB for 1.6 s |
| Secret | 3 | 0.16 s | 3 BLACK bands | Blackout behind the card (0.62), red/cyan tears, music CUT for 1.4 s |

- **The hit-stop is `pixelMotion.HitStop`**: every pixel element holds the frame it is on. It is scaled time, so a
  slowed bench holds it longer too. The vignette and columns are drawn in `Land` before the hold, so the held frame
  wears them.
- The vignette is stepped bands of four edges each (three units deep), never a gradient.
- **A frame writes only what moves.** A band's colour and which bands show, a column's place and size, are set once at
  the landing; a frame writes the bands' transparency, a column's shown quarters when the count changes and its fade
  over its last 40%, and the tears only while on or turning off. The first version rewrote ~190 properties a frame
  through a Divine landing.
- **The vignette keeps the landing it belongs to** (`vignetteTier`): a weaker landing inside it (a Rare card after a
  Mythic in a win box) shakes the stage but does not cut or redraw it. Checked with real Frames in `lune` (`@lune/roblox`):
  every tier ends hidden with the clock asleep and the stage back where it was.
- `rarityLook.Tint(rarity, text)` is the tier's word as rich text (its hex worked out once); the inventory, end screen,
  Codex and the lobby's chat line use it instead of building the tag by hand.
- **The caller owns the layer**: full screen, over the scene, UNDER what landed, so Secret's blackout darkens all but
  it. `Stage` is shaken in whole px round where it sits. Landings inside 0.2 s are one landing at the best tier, so a
  hand landed at once hits once, as its best.
- Where it is: `winBoxScreen` (its hand is now in a `Stage` frame, the impact layer under it), `UpgradeUI` (the
  Container moved into a `Stage` frame; `getOrderedCards` finds it with a recursive search), and the run chest, for
  the OPENER only, on a `ChestImpact` ScreenGui at DisplayOrder -1. **The chest's card is a world billboard, which draws
  under every ScreenGui, so its impact has no blackout** (`HasBlackout = false`) and no stage. Nothing moves the camera.
- `MusicController.Hush(depthDb, seconds)` drops the music on its own equalizer, so it never fights the duck or the
  volume setting.

### Rarity landings keep moving (2026-11-06)

The user rejected the animation stop on Secret and other box rarities because it reads as lag. `rarityImpact.Land`
no longer calls `pixelMotion.HitStop`, and `rarityLook.Impacts` no longer contains hit-stop tuning. This shared owner
covers the lobby boxes, run win box, run chests and upgrade cards. Keep the shake, vignette, columns, blackout,
tears and music behavior; never freeze the shared UI clock to emphasize a rarity landing.

Regression checks: land Legendary through Secret, open mixed-rarity hands and skip a hand; the cards, confetti and
HUD must keep advancing through each impact. Source checks only for this change; not playtested in Studio.

### The lobby opens boxes through the win box

`winBoxScreen`, `winBoxCard`, `winBoxCardSealed`, `lightRays`, `confetti` and `actionButton` moved to
`Global/Client/UI/Components`. `ShopBoxesUI`'s reveal is `winBoxScreen` over the carousel's own chest (its hooks drive
`carousel` the way `WinBoxUI`'s drive `chestViewport`). The rolls become cards in one place, `chestPoolCache.CardSpecs`,
for both. What the screen took on for the lobby:

- **Rows.** `fitGrid` picks the columns that give the largest whole unit, the fewest rows on a tie, each row centred.
  A win box hand (6 at most) lays out exactly as before. On the arcade's 1080 canvas: 10x is 5 x 2 at unit 6, 25x
  9 x 3 at 4, 50x 13 x 4 at 3 (108 x 150 cards).
- **Big hands share a budget**: the deal throws over at most 1.2 s and the climbs start over at most 2.5 s.
- **The skip is still sold.** `CanHurry` gates the press-anywhere (the lobby passes the pass's ownership) and `Skip`
  adds a Slab button while the cards open: gold SKIP lands every card, red UNLOCK SKIP prompts the pass. Auto skip is
  `Show(cards, isReroll, isInstant)` plus `PressContinue` 0.8 s after Continue arrives.
- `Dim` (the lobby passes 0.3 so the carousel chest and the cabinet glow still read), `SetTitle` (the box's name).
- The luck ribbon gets the roll's luck over the player's own, as the old card did.

**Not measured: a 50-card hand is about 13,000 Instances built in one frame** (a card is ~260: its 64-row sheen, 24
rays, 40 particles). Watch for a hitch on a 50x open first.

### Top finds are told (item 8)

- **Run**: every client already gets `OnChestOpened` with the opener and the item, so it needs no new event. When a
  chest that is not yours finishes opening on Legendary or better, `AnnouncementsUI` drops a banner: "MYTHIC FIND",
  "{player} found {item}", in the tier's word colour, for 4 s.
- **Lobby**: `ShopService` sends `RareFound` (userId, itemName, rarity) on the Meta network to everyone but the
  opener when a lobby open's best item is Legendary or better (the win box rolls tickets and is left out).
  `ShopController` writes it to chat 3 s later (about the opener's climb, so it does not spoil it): "{player} found a
  MYTHIC {item}!" in the tier's colour. **The Meta network must be regenerated** (`blink/generate.sh`) before either
  side loads.

### Small ones

- The Codex sorts items best first, like the inventory, and reads names and colours from `rarityLook` (Secret's white
  stroke is gone; its violet word reads on its own).
- `chestRevealCard` is deleted: nothing used it after the lobby moved.

### Open points

- Not seen. First on the bench: the vignette's weight on the Field backdrop, Divine's columns, Secret's blackout and
  tears, the 50x grid's first build, and the slot rings on the end screen's 2-unit gaps.
- The hit-stop holds the whole pixel UI, the HUD included, for up to 0.16 s. If that reads as a stutter mid-fight,
  drop it from the chest's impact (it is the only one that lands mid-fight).
- Item 3 of the review (a ladder strip during the climb) and item 2 (pips) were not part of this round.


## Last Wave: cashing out at the boss altar (`cashOutPrompt`, `spectateBar`, built 2026-11-01, unjudged)

Asked for: ending a run should end it only for you (a player report: one tired player at the altar ended a long
overtime run for the whole party), as satisfying as it can be, with a notice at the top saying who did it.

**The rule now.** The first activation of the boss altar **clears the run**: everyone in it wins. Every activation ends
the run for **that player only**, paid at their own run time (overtime multiplier included). The rest of the party
plays on and cashes out at the altar when they like; a teammate who stays and falls still finishes a win, scored at
the time they went down. Solo plays as before (the altar ends the run). **Updated 2026-11-04:** completing the altar's
hold now activates it immediately; the confirmation below was removed. See "Boss altar activation and blocked
reward buttons" below.

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Components/cashOutPrompt` | The "are you sure": a gold Slab over a dim, heading, a line on what leaving means, a gold leave button and a grey STAY. Rises 4 units from 94.5% (the kick menu's arrival). Confirm strikes before it goes: gold flash, thump, a ring, side sparks. A pad lands on STAY; B is Stay |
| `Components/spectateBar` | The strip a cashed-out player watches through: `<`, a blue Slab (a breathing LIVE light, SPECTATING, the teammate's name in their colour), `>`, and RESULTS. A switch slides the name in from that side with a flash, a sheen and a +6% thump |
| `Props/BossAltarClient` | Owns the altar's prompt (the hold opens the question) and `Game.PlayerCashedOut`: the altar's world cue and a camera shove on the clear, a sound and a banner for everyone else, and `HealthController.CashOut` |
| `FinalStatsController` | The end screen per player: a cash-out sees the ranking with the teammates still in the run marked FIGHTING (stats as they stand, no payout), SPECTATE instead of RESTART. RESULTS comes back to the screen **already settled** (`TRun.IsSettled`: no race, no fanfare). The party's screen replaces it when the run ends |
| `PlayersInfoController` | `AnnounceCashOut`: **RUN CLEARED!** (gold, 7 s, struck twice) with what it means for the others; **CASHED OUT** with the overtime bonus the player left with, read off the HUD clock |

### What was learned

1. **A screen that can come back must be able to open settled.** The ranking race is the payoff the first time and a
   chore the third; RESULTS from spectating opens on the final ranking with the card already out.
   **Settled rows must be drawn after snapping (2026-11-05).** `finalScreen.Show` creates rows at deal `-1`, and
   layout draws that hidden scale. `pixelMotion.Snap` changes spring state; `Step` then reports no movement, so the
   tick's conditional drawing cannot repair that scale. The settled path must finish scoring/ranking, snap each
   row's deal and final rank position, and explicitly redraw it. Keep `DealDelay = -1` to skip deal sounds too.
   Check first results, repeated Results -> Spectate -> Results with teammates still fighting, changed rank order,
   and the party's eventual final results. An offline check using production show/hide, drawing, scoring and ranking
   reproduced the hidden scale before the fix and passed 1,025 assertions afterward across 1-5 players and ten
   reopen cycles each. Layout and Instances were mocked; this fix has not been playtested in Studio.
2. **Say what the event means for the reader, not only what happened.** "X activated the boss altar" alone reads as
   "the run is over"; the banner says the others have already won and can stay or cash out.
3. **A number in a notice comes from the number already on screen.** The banner's overtime bonus is read off the
   clock's own value (`TimerController.GetCurrentOvertimeMultiplier`), so it never disagrees with it.
4. **Fit the longest line with room to spare.** At 128 units the longest prompt line filled all four lines at every
   size (checked in `lune`, Silkscreen advance 0.72); 144 units leaves a line for translations.

### Not done / open points

- **Not played in Studio, not judged on the bench.** `Stories/FinalStats` has a **Cashed out** outcome; the prompt
  and the strip have no story yet.
- The spectator keeps their own HUD (vitals and hotbar frozen at their last values; the clock, XP bar and map are the
  party's and stay useful). The map follows the teammate being watched.
- Switching teammates snaps the camera (the PlayerModule's subject change); a short blend would be nicer.
- XP needed per level still counts a cashed-out player who stays in the server (`LevelsCore` reads the player count).

## Last Wave: the Codex (`codexScreen`, `codexDetail`, `codexButton`, `loadoutPrompt`, built 2026-11-02, unjudged)

Asked for: the Codex in the new style, "the most satisfying and juiciest it can be". The old layout is kept (carousel
top centre, loadout cluster top right, a 4-column grid with the weapon / enemy stage under it on the left, the entry's
page on the right, BACK centre, the paint modes under the grid, EQUIP right); only the drawing and the feedback
changed. `CodexUI` went from 3,359 lines of Vide derives to a wrapper that feeds a drawing, like the stash.

| Piece | Where | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Drawing | `Lobby/.../MenuUI/Components/codexScreen` | Sizes from its own box (`p` from the height, 4 on the 1080 canvas, capped so 300 units fit). Pools one `inventorySlot` per entry of the biggest category and hangs four marks on each |
| Page | `.../Components/codexDetail` | Gold Slab: the entry's own `inventorySlot` (rarity glow included), kind word, a green EQUIPPED tab, the name (an item's in its tier's word colour), favorite / banish buttons, a scrolling page of rows |
| Button | `.../Components/codexButton` | The stash's bottom-row button made general: word or icon, pad glyph, lift / sink, `Lit` (its on palette + white outline), `Strike`, `Nudge`, `Refuse`, `SetEnabled` |
| Prompt | `.../Components/loadoutPrompt` | The cash-out prompt's shape for COPY (a row of loadouts to pick, ACCEPT grey until one is picked) and CLEAR (red confirm). Replaces the old `confirmPrompt` and the hand-built copy modal here |
| Wrapper | `MenuUI/CodexUI` | Data and rules only: sort, locks, discovery, the banish floor, paint modes, right click, double tap, the pad, rigs, loadouts. Builds `TCell`s and the page's `TRow`s and calls `refresh()` on every Core signal |
| Slot | `Global/.../inventorySlot` | Gained `ImageColor` (black for an undiscovered entry with no silhouette art), `IsDim` (banished) and exposes `Body` so a caller's marks ride its lift, deal and shake |

**Marks are played from state, not from the click.** `SetCells` keeps the last cell per slot; a cell with the same key
in the same place whose marks changed plays the change, anything else snaps. So a click, a paint drag, a right click,
the pad's held Y / X and a **loadout switch** all go through the one path, and a loadout switch ripples every changed
mark across the grid (0.025 s a slot, capped at 0.6 s). One sound per kind of change per refresh, however many slots.

| Mark | Where | On | Off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Favorite star | top-left corner cut-out | pops in (4.2 Hz / 0.42, shoved 7), gold motes | shrinks away |
| Banish cross | top-right cut-out | the slot crunches (squash + shake), the cross SLAMS in from 1.8x on a stiff spring, icon dims, ChestBanish | the slot strikes back to colour |
| Equipped tick | bottom-left cut-out, a 5 x 4 lime pixel tick | the slot strikes, lime motes | shrinks away |
| NEW | a green `pixelSlab.Tab` over the top edge, built the first time a slot needs one | pops in | pops out with a green puff (seeing the entry clears it) |

Other moments: opening rises 4 units from 94.5% and deals the slots down the grid, the stage flashes and the page
lands; a category deals in from the side the carousel moved toward; a new pick deals the page's slot in, flashes and
sweeps a sheen over the header, types the name, then slides each row in 4 units and types it after the row above
(260 graphemes/s, 0.035 s stagger), and pulses the stage's light. **Equip** is the big one: the Equip sound, the button
strikes with lime rings and side sparks, the whole surface thumps (+4%), the EQUIPPED tab pops onto the page, the
page's slot strikes, the stage throws rings and flashes, and the grid's tick pops in. A refused banish (the floor)
shakes the slot and the page's banish button with BuyRefuse. A paint mode lights its button and turns the grid's
frame its colour (red for banish) with a white outline, so it is plain the grid is painting.

The stage (weapon / enemy) is drawn in Frames: three stepped glow rectangles and a five-row stepped floor ellipse in
the kind's colour, the old stripe tile at 0.93, the rig on top. Its light is static and only written while a pulse
decays.

The tutorial still finds `CodexEntry_<name>` (slots are renamed per category), `TutorialCodexEquipButton` (its holder
is hidden when nothing can be equipped, which `isEffectivelyVisible` reads) and `TutorialCodexBackButton`.

Pitfalls this round:

- **A mote born above the top row is clipped by the grid's ScrollingFrame.** The marks' motes fly on the surface
  (unclipped), placed from the slot's AbsolutePosition over the surface's scale. They are born 7 units above the slot
  (past the NEW tab and a lifted slot) and rise under negative gravity, so they cannot come back down through it.
- The screen draws siblings by ZIndex (the lobby's SurfaceGui is `Sibling`): the header's flash and sheen sit in a
  clipping frame ABOVE the slot, words and buttons, or they draw under them.
- `select` as a local shadows the builtin; the wrapper's is `choose`.
- The old page rebuilt every row on every Core signal; the wrapper now compares a signature of the page and only
  re-shows it when something on it changed.

Bench: `Lobby/Client/UI/Stories/Codex` (pad glyphs, loadouts owned, paint mode, time scale; Do: reopen, next category,
favorite, banish, refuse a banish, equip, switch loadout (the ripple), see the NEW ones, copy prompt, clear prompt).

Checked: StyLua, Selene (clean on every changed file), every changed file compiles, both places build, the layout's
fit worked out at the narrowest the screen allows (300 units: the carousel and the loadout cluster keep 4 units
apart; BACK, the modes and EQUIP never touch) and on a phone's 844 x 390 (unit 2, 31-unit slots). **Not playtested,
not opened on the bench, not tried with a pad, touch or the Text Size setting.** First things to judge: the corner
marks' size on 4:3 (26-unit slots), whether the row typewriter is too slow on a long weapon page, the loadout ripple,
and the equip moment's weight.

### Round 2 (2026-11-02): what the user corrected

| Said | Was | Now |

| "I don't like how the equip moves everything" | The whole surface thumped +4% on equip, and the stage threw rings and flashed | No surface thump and nothing on the stage; the button's strike and sparks, the EQUIPPED tab, the page's slot strike and the grid's tick stay |
| "Make the line-by-line faster" | 260 graphemes/s, 0.035 s a row, 0.08 s before the first | 900 graphemes/s, 0.012 s a row, 0.03 s before the first, 0.1 s slide; the name at 140/s |
| "Leave the [viewer backdrop] that was before" | Stepped glow rectangles and a stepped floor in the kind's colour, pulsing on every pick | The old backdrop back as it was: near-black (5, 5, 5), the baked orange radial glow, the gold stripe tile at 0.88; no pulses. Raw colours, not `pixelSlab.Show` |

### Round 4 (2026-11-02): what was still wasted

A review for cost after the user's "is this the most optimized it can be":

- `setCells` built four small tables per slot per refresh to diff the marks, and a first fix put a closure inside the
  loop that captured loop locals (a `NEWCLOSURE` per slot, which the Performance Rules forbid). Now one
  `diffMark(view, mark, isOn, wasOn, delay, sounds, kind)` lives outside the loop: a refresh allocates nothing per
  slot. A hot path may take more than five parameters (CLAUDE.md).
- A mark that played looked up its slot's index with a linear search over every view; the view carries `Index`.
- The page's tick wrote the sheen's 48 rows and the flash every frame while anything else on the screen moved. Each
  is written only while it moves, and once more on the frame it ends.
- `cellOf` searched the category list for every cell; it takes the category.

Not measured in Studio. Cost that is left and accepted: every Core signal rebuilds the cell list (about 60 small
tables) and the page's rows to compare signatures. That happens per click, not per frame. The slots skip unchanged
paints through `inventorySlot`'s look key, and the page is only rebuilt when its signature changed.

### Recipe: a lobby page in the pixel style, in one round

The Codex took four rounds, and the stash took four before it. Almost every correction the user made was
predictable. Do these up front:

**Structure (copy the stash and the Codex):**
1. Split the page into a **drawing** (`Components/<page>Screen`, plain functions, takes words and callbacks,
   exposes `Set…` / `Play…`) and a **wrapper** (`<Page>UI`: Cores, rules, pad bindings, Vide sources). The bench
   mounts the drawing alone, because the wrapper needs a LocalPlayer.
2. The wrapper has one `refresh(reveal?)` that rebuilds everything from the Cores and calls the drawing. It is called
   from every Core signal. The drawing **diffs** what it is given (keyed per slot) and plays what changed, so
   clicks, drags, pad holds and server pushes share one path. Never play feedback from the click handler.
3. Keep the page's API (`UI`, `Visible`, `Appear`), the instance names other systems search for (the tutorial's
   `TutorialCodex…`, `CodexEntry_<name>`), and LobbyUI's open/close double write: the show effect ignores a repeat.
4. Reuse `inventorySlot`, `pixelCarousel`, `dropdown`, `scrollbar`, `keyHint`, `cornerSelector`, `cornerRibbon`,
   `pixelFx`, and `codexButton` (any word or icon button) and `loadoutPrompt` (any yes/no or pick-one question). A
   per-page decoration that must ride a slot's lift goes on `slot.Body`.

**Layout (the corrections, in advance):**
5. One spacing rhythm: **6 units from every screen edge and 6 between every block**. Carousel at y 6 (20 tall),
   panels from 32, bottom buttons 21 tall at 6 from the bottom (panels end 33 from the bottom), and 6 between
   columns and between stacked panels. Check every gap against the others before showing it; the user notices
   12 vs 7.
6. Panels start below `topbarClear.Below(root)` + 6 units, re-laid out on `topbarClear.Changed`. On a phone the
   Roblox menu, chat and voice buttons cover the top-left fifth of the lobby canvas.
7. The lobby canvas is **always 1080 tall**, so the unit is 4 on every device. A phone loses room to the platform's
   bar, not to a smaller unit.
8. Body text: **7 units** (headers 8). 5 units read as tiny, because Silkscreen's capitals are half the TextSize.

**Look:**
9. Every colour goes through `pixelSlab.Show`. In the lobby, near-greys lose their tint and get the corrected blue
   (no violet, no olive). Hand-picked tinted neutrals will read blue. Something the user already approved (the
   old viewer backdrop) keeps its raw colours.
10. A mark or badge on a slot is a **small Slab of its own** (outline, coloured bezel with a lit row, dark well,
    coloured glyph), overhanging the corner by 2 units. A glyph on a well-coloured cut-out vanishes against the dark
    panel.
11. Do not replace a backdrop or a look the user already had unless asked. The stepped "stage" glow was rejected for
    the old radial glow plus stripes.

**Motion:**
12. Frequent actions (equip, pick, mark) never move the whole screen: no surface thump, no stage flash. The element
    acted on strikes; the rest stays still.
13. Text reveals are fast: a row every 0.012 s at 900 graphemes/s. The first version (0.035 s, 260/s) was too slow.
14. A particle that must show above a scrolled grid flies on the unclipped surface, placed from the slot's
    `AbsolutePosition` over the surface's `UIScale`. The ScrollingFrame clips anything above its top row.
15. Per-refresh loops allocate nothing (no tables or closures per slot). A tick writes an effect only while it moves,
    plus the frame it ends on.

**Hover and focus (Codex rounds 5 to 7):**
16. The brackets go **only on what the hand is on**: the mouse's slot, else the pad's (`if hovered > 0 then hovered
    else padIndex`). Never fall back to the picked slot when the mouse leaves. The picked slot shows with its own
    white outline (`slot.SetLinked`). A fallback makes the brackets dash to the picked slot and back on every move.
17. **Keep the hover across the gaps between slots.** A slot's `MouseLeave` only releases the press; the hover (lift
    and brackets) stays on that slot until another slot's `MouseEnter` takes it, or the grid's ScrollingFrame fires
    `MouseLeave`. A callback that must know "over nothing" (the Codex's `props.Hover`, for the paint modes) still
    gets 0 in a gap. Keep the two as separate variables (`hoveredIndex`, `pointedIndex`).
18. **"NEW" (and any word across a corner) is `cornerRibbon`, across the TOP RIGHT**, never a tab or chip. Size it
    from the slot: a band of about 0.22 of the slot (at least 6 units), letters about 0.42 of the band, so a unit of
    fill shows above and below them (0.5 of a 5-unit band touched the ink). Corner badges move out of its corner.
    Build the ribbon's CanvasGroup only on a slot's first NEW: one per slot is a texture each.

**Data the drawing reads:**
19. A Vide `Visible` / `Label` function that reads state which is **not a source** (a Core getter, the shop's
    levels) re-runs only when a source it reads changes. Give it a version source, and bump that source from
    **every** signal that changes any input, including the load signals. The Codex's loadout menu re-read only on
    `LoadoutsCore.OnChanged`. It was built before the shop loaded, so it opened with no rows. The user reported it
    as "behind the descriptions": an empty `pixelDropdown` is just its 4-unit frame, which reads as a menu cut off.
    **On a "drawn behind" report, check that the thing has content before touching ZIndex.**
20. Size anything near the screen's top edge for its **highest** state: hovered and lifted, with a badge popped and
    its outline. The tab bar's count badge sits 3 units above its tab and lifts with it, and its outline went off
    the screen until the row moved a unit down (`tabBar`'s `UIPadding` on its tabs frame). `ticketsWallet` works
    out the tabs' height itself to sit level with them, so it moves with them by hand: change one, change both.

**From the Quests rounds (2026-11-02):**
21. **A page of many similar things is a grid, and a family of tiers is ONE card.** A list one item at a time was the
    complaint; 45 achievements grouped by `Metric` into 7 ladder cards (tier pips, the current tier shown) fit one
    screen, and a new tier adds a pip, not a row.
22. **A page of FEW things fills its panel.** Two or three cards at the grid's size in a big empty panel "look really
    strange": let the cards grow (up to 1.5x the panel's unit, full rows only, biggest card area wins) and centre a grid
    shorter than the well.
23. **Order is decided when a page or tab is dealt in, then kept while it is up**, so a claimed or changed item stays
    under the eye. Deal in again only when the set is not the same items.
24. **A number about a bar goes INSIDE it, centred**, white with the ink outline, as the vitals do. Beside it, the bar's
    length depends on the number's and no two bars match.
25. **Deal-ins use `pixelMotion.DealFrequency` / `DealDamping`** (+3.7% overshoot) on every page; no page tunes its own.
26. **Siblings of a `pixelSlab.Body` root need the root's ZIndex set**: the root is ZIndex 1, so a glow behind it at
    ZIndex z - 2 draws OVER it. On a "tint I cannot read through" report, check the layer order before the alpha.
27. **Do not show a counter nobody asked for** ("11/45 DONE" was removed): the footer is for the reset clock only.
28. **Lay out from `root.AbsoluteSize` as it is.** The open grow's `UIScale` sits on `surface`, a child of `root`, so
    `root` never carries it. Dividing by it made every layout run mid-grow ~6% too wide, and the settle does not
    change `root`'s size, so nothing fixed it (`pageSize` in the four screens).
29. **A modal on a page** (the gift picker): see "The gift picker and the lobby pages' size" at the end. Outside
    press cancels, inside press does nothing, the page under it is not `Interactable`, and the leave must end. The
    modal's own root goes `Interactable = false` the moment the leave starts, not when it reaches Hidden.

**Checking, in this order:** `stylua` / `selene` from the repo root, the `lune` compile of each changed file, both
`rojo build`s, then the bench. When the user sends a screenshot, measure it with PIL (sample the fills and walk a
column through a button) before changing a colour. The olive greys were found that way, not by eye.

## Last Wave: the scrollbar's skin, motion and touch reach (`scrollbar`, 2026-11-02, unjudged)

The user: "it doesn't belong where it's placed, it has a blueish part that really stands out a lot", "make it the most
satisfying and juicier it can be", then "too tiny of thickness... in phone it would be almost impossible to move it".
Everything is in `Global/Client/UI/Components/scrollbar`; the legacy path (`ThumbColor`, no `Palette`: Quests,
Options, Leaderboard, Profile, Kick, `list`, `grid`, `runView`) is unchanged.

| Report | Cause | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The blue part | Measured from the screenshot with PIL: a 1 px column of (1, 52, 95) beside the ink track. The track `Frame` turned its background on (`BackgroundTransparency = 0`) but kept the engine's default `BorderSizePixel = 1`, whose colour is (27, 42, 53), boosted by the lobby's correction | `BorderSizePixel = 0` on the track. Not a palette problem: the ink and well were already plain greys |
| Not juicy | A flat thumb that teleported with the scroll | See "the motion" below |
| Too thin for a finger | 2 units = ~3 pt in the lobby (canvas always 1080 tall, unit 4, 390 pt phone) and ~4 pt in the run (unit ~2). A finger wants ~44 pt = 30 lobby units, wider than any gutter | A wider invisible grab area (`Gutter`) and a thumb that swells under a touch grab. The bar stays 2 units drawn |

**The motion** (`pixelSkin` inside the module, numbers in its `Tune`, worked out in `lune`):

- The thumb follows the scroll on a spring, 11 Hz at 0.82 damping (a wheel step settles in ~0.07 s), 18 Hz while
  dragged so it stays under the hand.
- It smears along a fast move: the trailing edge stretches 0.008 px per px/s, capped at 2 units (only a fling hits
  the cap).
- Reaching an end squashes it against that end (pop 36: a unit, rebounding a third of one) while a 1-unit white cap
  flashes there. The squash keeps the thumb pinned to the end it hit, so it never leaves the track.
- Grab: a white flash and a small squash (pop 18), lit (Light body, white top row) while held; release flashes half.
- A three-line grip (Shade, half a unit tall, a unit apart) on thumbs 9+ units tall.
- A touch grab widens the thumb a unit out of each side of its groove (6 Hz, 0.5 damping) until release. The track
  needs a unit free on each side for it; every caller has at least that.
- A bar that appears or is resized is **placed**, not slid in from where it was.

**Sound:** a soft HoverHud (1.05, 0.35) on hover; ClickHud on grab (1.05, 0.6) and release (0.86, 0.45); HoverHud
ticks every 1/12 of the range while dragging, pitch 1.3 at the top to 0.82 at the bottom (the slider's range); the
first notch is the grab's own click and the end notches are left to the end click. An end click (1.22 top, 0.8
bottom) plays **only after a player's scroll**: a drag, or a wheel / touch pan in the last 0.35 s (the scroll frame's
`InputChanged`). A category change or rebuild that resets the scroll slides silently. Gamepad stick scrolling is not
detected, so it bumps without the click.

**Touch reach:** `Gutter = { Left, Right }` in units, the empty space beside the bar the grab area may cover,
default 1 + 1. It must stop at the list (or it steals the list's taps) and at the clipping well (input is clipped
too). Codex grid, Codex page and stash pass 2 + 2, Settings 2 + 3 (its well does not clip; the right side is the
panel edge, which takes no input). On an 844 x 390 phone: ~9 pt in the lobby screens (was ~3), ~10 pt for Settings in
the lobby and ~14 pt in the run, ~8 pt for the end and info screens. Phones still scroll mainly by dragging the list
itself; the bar is the backup. If that is still too small, the next step is a thicker drawn bar, which means wider
gutters on every screen.

**How it is built, for the next control like it:**

1. Fixed layout and motion are separate functions. `layout()` writes what hangs on the track's size (rows, grip and
   cap sizes) once per resize; `place()` writes the thumb's position / size only when it lands on a different
   pixel (and the grips only when the height changes); `paint()` writes colours only on a state change or while a
   flash fades. A settled bar writes nothing, and the stepper sleeps.
2. One stepper on `pixelMotion`, woken by a scroll, a grab or a release; it returns busy while any spring or flash
   moves.
3. Input stays in the outer function (drag math on the true geometry, never the animated thumb), the look in the
   skin; the outer calls `Move` / `Hot` / `Grab` / `Release` / `Drag`.
4. A Vide binding and a stepper must not both write a property: the thumb's `Position` / `Size` bindings are left
   off when the skin drives them.

Checked: StyLua, Selene clean, every changed file compiles, both places build, spring peaks and phone sizes worked
out in `lune`. **Not playtested: not tried with a mouse, a finger or a pad, and not opened on a bench.** Judge the
hover sound (maybe one sound too many) and the end squash (`Tune.BumpPop`).

## Last Wave: the Quests page (`questsScreen`, `questCard`, built 2026-11-02, unjudged)

Asked for: the lobby's Quests page in the new style, "the most satisfying and juicier it can be", and a fix for "a list
showing one by one, that takes a LOT to see the quests" (45 achievements now, more to come). Built on the stash /
Codex recipe: `QuestsUI` is now the wrapper (data, order, tabs, pad, clock), `Components/questsScreen` the drawing,
`Components/questCard` one card, `Stories/Quests` the bench. The tab bar (`tabBar`, already pixel), BACK, REROLL, the
reset clock, the confetti, the toast and the badges are kept.

**The list became a grid, and the achievements became ladders.**

- Cards stand three to a row (two on 4:3), 42 units tall. Worked out in `lune` at 1920 x 1080: a 464 x 201-unit well,
  147-unit cards, four rows visible. The old list showed about four cards; this shows twelve.
- Every challenge with the same `Metric` is ONE card (`LADDER_ORDER` in `QuestsUI`; an unlisted Metric still gets its
  own card, after these). The 45 achievements are 7 cards and fit on one screen (148 units of 201). A new tier is a new
  pip, not a new row, so "more achievements" no longer means more scrolling.
- A ladder card shows its **current tier**: the first ready one, else the first open one, else the last. It has a pip
  per tier (gold done, green ready, dark open, white outline on the one shown) and `3/7`. The mouse over a pip shows
  that tier (name, bar, reward) until it leaves the pips. A tap shows it, and a second tap goes back.
- **Order is decided when a tab is dealt in** (ready, then open by how near, then done) and **kept while the page is
  up**. A claimed card stays where the eye is. A set that is not the same quests (a reroll, a new day) is dealt in again.

**Three states, three kinds of look:** open (grey bezel, gold bar, `45/100` rolling up beside it), ready (green
bezel, white outline, a three-ring stepped green glow, and a CLAIM plate where the bar was), done (grey, darker well,
muted name, a green bar reading DONE, a green tick badge over the top right corner, rewards at half).

**Motion:**

| Moment | What plays |
| --- | --- |
| Open | Panel rises 4 units from 94.5%; cards deal in 0.035 s apart (max 0.4 s); each bar fills from empty 0.14 s after its card lands, its count rolling with it |
| Tab | Cards deal in from the side the tabs moved toward, a column at a time |
| Hover | Card lifts a unit, white outline, brackets (only on the hand's card, kept across the gaps, Codex rule 16-17) |
| Press a ready card | Plate sinks and greys while the claim is out (3 s at most); tickets counter held |
| Server confirms | Card flash, +9% thump, rings, 14 sparks rising INSIDE the card's well (gold among them for stardust), tick badge pops, `ticketsFlight` from the ticket glyph into the wallet (its own chime, so `RewardBanked` is no longer played on top), confetti and the toast as before |
| Ladder moves on | 0.3 s after the strike: the claimed pip pops gold (+24%), the next tier's name types in (140/s), its bar refills from empty |
| Press an unfinished card | One-unit shake, BuyRefuse at half. A done card does nothing |
| Idle | Ready cards catch a sheen in turn every 2.6 s (light only; a `task.delay` chain, the clock sleeps between) |

**Pitfalls avoided, for the next grid of cards:**

- **Sparks thrown off a card's sides cross its neighbours** in a grid and blink (the particle checklist, point 1). The
  first draft did that; the sparks now rise inside the card's own well from just above the bottom row, under drag and
  upward float, so they cross one background and are clipped by the well.
- **The card's hit button sits UNDER its body** (ZIndex below), so the pips (TextButtons in the body) take their own
  presses; the card still hears MouseEnter over them, because the engine sends it to every button under the cursor.
- **The pad's A glyph is one `keyHint`** made with the screen, parented to the plate of the card the pad is on. A
  card is built outside any Vide scope (from a refresh), so it cannot make its own.
- **The footer is placed on its own.** The clock rewrites it every second; laying out the whole grid for that would
  re-fit every card's title.
- A card slot is reused across tabs, so `Set` with a different key drops the pip preview and a pending claim.
- On hide, `activeTab` goes back to Daily, so LobbyUI's Visible-then-Appear double write never deals the last
  visit's tab and then Daily over it.

Bench: `Lobby/Client/UI/Stories/Quests` (Tab; Time scale; Do: reopen, claim the first ready (a ladder moves on),
progress everything (cards turn ready in place), reroll (a new set deals in), empty tab).

Achievements (7 cards, no full-row layout fits) keep the panel's unit, 3 columns. The first rule (biggest unit first) gave a phone three small cards in a row; area is the right score |
| "The bounciness on changing tabs is a lot, the same for the stash and Codex; one level for every UI, less" | Slots and cards dealt in on 3.4 Hz / 0.52: +13.9% overshoot (simulated) | One spring in `pixelMotion` (`DealFrequency` 3.4, `DealDamping` 0.7): +3.7%, within 1% in 0.3 s. `inventorySlot` (stash, Codex grid and page) and `questCard` read it; do not give a page its own deal spring |
| "Some numbers go inside the progress bar; maybe inside it at the centre, like the health / shield bar" and "some bars differ in size" | The count sat right of the bar and the bar was the card's width minus the count's, so every goal length gave a different bar | The bar is the bottom row's full width and height (9 units, the claim plate's size), the count centred in it, white with the ink outline (DONE in green when claimed) |

Checked: StyLua, Selene, compile, both places build; the deal spring and the fill layouts at 16:9, 4:3 and a phone's
canvas worked out in `lune`. **Not playtested.**

### Round 3 (2026-11-02): no counter, and a review for cost

The user: "remove the counter of quests" (the Achievements footer, "11/45 DONE"), then "is this the most optimized
and readable it can be?". The footer is empty on Achievements now (it only ever says the reset clock). The review found
one bug and four costs:

| Found | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| **Bug:** a ladder moving on after a claim waits 0.3 s before typing the next tier's name, by starting `typeAge` at -0.3. The tick only advanced it `if typeAge >= 0`, so it never counted up and the name stayed blank | A separate `isTyping` flag; the age's sign no longer says whether typing is on. **Never use a negative value of a timer as both "waiting" and "off"** |
| Every card is ticked while ANY card moves (a sheen on one wakes the clock), and each tick drew the whole card: the scale, the bar, a count string formatted every frame | A card draws only while it is busy, plus the one frame it settles on (`wasBusy`) |
| The sheen's 64 rows were written (`Visible = false`) on every draw while no sheen ran | Written only while it sweeps, hidden once when it ends (`isSheenDrawn`) |
| Every claim refreshes the whole tab, and every card re-laid out (title re-fitted by `TextFits`, bar, pips) | `isUnchanged` compares the tiers (key, state, progress, goal, reward, title) and skips a card nothing changed on |
| `barX` / `barY` lived across calls but were only used inside `place` | Gone |

Left as they are, on purpose: each refresh builds the tab's cell tables (a few dozen small tables per server push,
never per frame), and `linkSelection` makes one closure per card per layout (layout only, like the stash).

### Round 4 (2026-11-05): the weekly preview matches the live count

The Quests story now shows three weekly cards, matching the server's updated count. `questsScreen` already sizes
cards from the received list, so the count change needed no drawing or layout rewrite. Keep stories aligned with
the real data shape before using them to judge spacing. The touched UI files compile and pass changed-file
StyLua/Selene. **Not playtested or visually reviewed in Studio.**

Use the game's name **quests** for quest-circle activities. In daily/weekly descriptions, add "during runs" or
name the quest directly to distinguish what is being counted: "Complete 3 quests during runs" or "Complete Color
Dance once". Calling them "events" introduces a name the game does not use.

Achievement ladders use a data entry's optional `Group`, falling back to `Metric`. Different modifier or weapon
families can share the same win metric while keeping separate, readable cards. Reuse the existing ladder drawing
and tier ordering rather than merging unrelated win conditions into one long row of pips.

### Achievement hover gaps (2026-11-06)

`questCard` owns tier previews. Keep the last hovered tier across the gaps between pips; restore the current tier
only on `pipRow.MouseLeave`. Clearing on each pip's `MouseLeave` flashes the default tier between every pair of
squares. Check both sweep directions, leaving the row above/below or at either end, and touch's tap-again toggle.
Source checks only; not playtested in Studio.

## Last Wave: what the Quests rounds taught (2026-11-02)

The general lessons, on top of the recipe's new items 21 to 27 (in "Recipe: a lobby page in the pixel style").

**Reading a lot at once**
- The complaint "it takes a LOT to see the quests" was about **how many things one screen shows**, not their style.
  Count what fits before drawing: the old list showed ~4; the grid shows 12, and grouping tiers into one card made
  the 45 achievements 7 cards. Look for the data's own families (here `Metric`) before inventing categories.
- A ladder card needs: the tier being worked on (first ready, else first open, else last), a pip per tier with three
  colours plus a white outline on the shown one, and `3/7`. The hand over a pip previews that tier; a tap toggles it,
  since a finger has no hover.
- The opposite failure is real too: a grid built for 45 looks broken with 2. **Design the layout for the smallest
  and the largest count the page will ever hold**, and check both in `lune` at 16:9, 4:3 and a phone's canvas.
  Score fill layouts by card AREA: "biggest unit first" picked three small cards in a row on a phone.

**Layers and colour**
- A wash over a card that "needs to be more transparent" was three glow rings drawn on top of it. The kit's
  `pixelSlab.Body` root has no ZIndex of its own (1); anything hung beside it inside the same parent must set it.
- The card's hit button sits UNDER its body so the pips (buttons in the body) take their own presses, and the card
  still hears MouseEnter over them (the engine sends it to every button under the cursor).

**Motion**
- The user judges bounce across pages, not per page: one deal spring for every page, in `pixelMotion`. +13.9%
  overshoot was "a lot"; +3.7% is the level now. Simulate overshoot and settle time in `lune` before changing it.
- Sparks for an item in a dense grid stay INSIDE the item (its own well clips them). Thrown out of its sides they
  cross the neighbours, which the particle checklist forbids.
- A delayed step (type the name after the strike) needs its own on-flag; see the round 3 bug.

**Cost** (the round 3 table, as rules)
- Per card in a shared clock: draw only while busy, plus the settle frame.
- A multi-row effect (sheen) writes its rows only while it runs, and hides them once.
- A refresh from a server push skips items whose data did not change; compare fields, do not build signatures.
- A once-a-second readout (the reset clock) gets its own placement function, never the whole page's layout.

**Process**
- Two screenshots answered two questions this round: one showed the wash was a layer (the whole well was green, not
  the edges), the other that bars differed because of the text beside them. Read the screenshot for the CAUSE before
  answering the words ("more transparent").
- A request to remove something ("the counter") also removes what fed it (`achievementsDone`, `challengeCount`) and
  updates the bench to match.

## Last Wave: the shop (`shopScreen`, `shopCard`, `priceButton`, `shopBoxes`, `ticketsSpend`, built 2026-11-02, unjudged)

Asked for: the lobby's Shop in the new style, "the most satisfying and juicier it can be". Built on the stash / Codex /
Quests recipe. The old layout is kept: BOXES / DEALS / TOOLS / PREMIUM tabs on top, the boxes tab's 3D wheel of chests
with the name on top, arrows either side, pity lines under it, drop rates bottom right and the buy bar along the
bottom; the other tabs a grid of cards; BACK left, the deals' REROLL in the middle and their reset clock right.

| Piece | Where | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wrapper | `MenuUI/ShopUI` | Catalog, prices, levels, ownership, purchases, the pad. Builds `shopCard.TCell`s per tab and calls `refresh()`; every Controller signal queues ONE deferred refresh |
| Page | `.../Components/shopScreen` | Tabs, gold panel with a scrolling card grid (up to 4 columns, 100-unit minimum), BACK / REROLL / footer, `BoxesHost` for the boxes tab |
| Card | `.../Components/shopCard` | Title, picture on a soft glow-dot light, description, level pips + `3/8`, price row; a deal wears its kind / rarity palette and a `pixelSlab.Tab` over its top edge; owned = one green OWNED plate, quiet well, green tick badge |
| Price | `.../Components/priceButton` | Gold slab + ticket glyph + amount, green slab + Robux glyph, or an icon slab (the gift, magenta). Lift, sink, rolls to a new price, `Feed` swell, strike, refuse, OWNED |
| Boxes chrome | `.../Components/shopBoxes` | Name plate that slides the way the wheel turned, staircase arrows (`codexButton` now exposes `Well`), pity lines, drop rates Slab, buy bar (multiplier + pixel dropdown, tickets, Robux, gift, auto skip) |
| Spend flight | `Global/.../ticketsSpend` | `ticketsFlight` backwards: glints thrown out of the wallet against drag, hang, boomerang into the price; each landing feeds it and ticks the pitch chain |
| Bench | `Lobby/Client/UI/Stories/Shop` | Tab, time scale, balance; Do: reopen, buy the first with tickets / Robux, free throws arrive |

`ShopDealsUI` is deleted (its rules moved into the wrapper). `ShopProductsGridUI` stays: the leaderboard's donation
grid still uses it. The 3D carousel, the reveal (win box screen) and every purchase / pity / luck rule are unchanged.

**A purchase, beat by beat.** Press: the price sinks, ClickHud. Not enough tickets: checked on the client first, so the
price and card shake at once with BuyRefuse and the wallet stings (`OnInsufficientTickets`); the server still has the
last word. Sent: the wrapper remembers what it paid with (`pendingByKey`, 6 s for tickets, 120 s for a Robux prompt).
Server confirms (`OnPurchaseSuccess` for tools / premium, `OnDealPurchased` for deals): `screen.Bought` HOLDS the card
(`shopCard.Hold`), so the deferred refresh's new level waits; if paid in tickets, 5 to 12 glints (one per 150) fly from
the wallet into the price over ~0.35-0.7 s, each swelling it; on the last, `Release` plays the held change (the bought
level's pip pops +24%, the price rolls to the next level's, OWNED arrives) with a flash, +9% thump, rings, 16 sparks
rising INSIDE the well, the picture jumping 3 units, and RewardBanked. Robux and gifts strike 0.05 s after the answer.

**Why Hold / Release:** the Controller fires the state signal (`OnUtilityChanged`) BEFORE the success signal, so a
refresh played on the state signal would pop the pip before the tickets landed. All refreshes are deferred one frame;
the success handler runs synchronously and holds the card first. Keep that order if the signals change.

Other moments: opening rises 4 units from 94.5% and deals the cards; a tab change deals them in from the side the tabs
moved; the hand onto a card lifts it, whitens its outline and sweeps a sheen once; a box change slides the name plate
and nudges that arrow, prices roll; the multiplier nudges; free opens arriving on the shown box strike its price.

Layout: one rhythm (6 units from edges, panels 32 / 33). Rows that all fit the well stretch up to 1.9x (four deals
are four tall cards, premium's two rows fill the panel); more rows keep 88 units and scroll; a short last row is
centred. The drop rates sit level with the buy bar, or over it when the bar reaches under them (4:3).

Pad: L2 / R2 tabs, the pad walks the prices row by row (left / right through a card's prices then the next card's,
up / down to the same price above / below), Y rerolls deals, the right stick turns the wheel. Names the tutorial finds:
`TutorialShopBackButton`, `TutorialFreeThrowButton` (the tickets price while free opens are held).

Checked: StyLua, Selene, every changed file compiles, both places build; grid and bar fits worked out by hand at
16:9, 4:3 and a phone's canvas. **Not playtested, not opened on the bench, not tried with a pad or touch.** First to
judge: the spend flight's length and count, the card's picture size at 88 units, the deals' tall cards, the drop
rates over the bar on 4:3, and whether `TextBounds` reads right on a card's first layout (a label not yet drawn may
report 0; the card then reserves one line, which could let a long title touch the picture until the next refresh).

## Last Wave: the shop's new shelves (BUNDLES, deals' extras, run boosts, VIP; built 2026-11-02, unjudged)

Asked for: "try everything" from the shop ideas round except skins and the season pass, VIP with +10% stardust too, "the
most satisfying and juicier it can be", in the pixel style. References were three top Roblox shops (one a wave game):
banners that list their contents as coloured "+ ITEM" chips, a "-50%" / "x4 VALUE" sticker, section titles inside one
scroll, a currency grid whose biggest pack takes the whole row, a free claim with a timer, a weekly stock.

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| BUNDLES tab (welcome offer, featured, bundles, ticket packs) | `ShopUI` (`BUNDLES_TAB`, premium items with `Shelf = "Bundles"`, `ShopCore.TICKET_PACKS`) |
| DEALS: free box every 4 h, box milestones, weekly special, then the daily deals | `ShopUI.refresh`, `ShopService` extras section, `ShopCore` constants |
| TOOLS: UPGRADES then RUN BOOSTS (potion, Revive Token, Head Start, Lucky Run) | `Data/Shop/Utilities` (`Shelf = "Boosts"`, `RunBoostCharges`, `Boost`) |
| PREMIUM: VIP first | `Data/Shop/Premium/VipPremium`, `VipChatController`, `RunScoringService` |
| Card: wide banner, chips, sticker, countdown, progress bar, claim button, drawn ticket pile | `shopCard` (new `TCell` fields) |
| Screen: section titles, wide rows, row-based pad walk, `SetClock`, payout flight | `shopScreen` |
| Bench | `Stories/Shop` (BUNDLES is the default tab; "Do: claim the first claim") |

**The card's new parts.** A `Header` on a cell is a section title the screen draws over it (gold word, a one-unit rule to
the edge) and starts a new row. `Wide` is a banner a row to itself, 76 units tall: picture left (up to 22% of the well),
name in 11-unit letters, the countdown under it in the warn red, then the chips (one column up to three, two from four),
the description if room is left, prices stacked in a right column 64-96 units wide with the gift left of the bottom one.
Chips are an ink box, a fill with a lit row, white words with ink, 9 units tall, on what they give: tickets gold, a box its
kind's colour (Items magenta), boosts green, potions blue. A strike pops them one after another (0.045 s apart). The
sticker is `cornerRibbon` across the top right (band 9 units, its middle 15 in, so ~42 units of run for 5-unit letters),
its CanvasGroup made on the card's first sticker, hidden once owned. A claim is the tickets button gone green saying
CLAIM; before `ReadyAt` it is grey and counts down in place; `IsClaimLocked` greys it with the word (a milestone short of
its opens). `Progress` / `ProgressMax` is a bar over the prices with the count inside it (recipe item 24). `TicketStack` 1
to 5 draws a pile of the tickets glyph as the picture, a cell a twentieth of the picture.

**Moments.** Every claim and pack goes out as `ShopExtras.Claimed` BEFORE the server grants, on the Meta network like the
tickets change, so the wrapper holds the counter first; the card strikes, then `ticketsFlight` throws the payout from the
struck price into the wallet. A bundle with tickets does the same off `OnPurchaseSuccess`, but `PremiumGifted` rides the
main network and the tickets the Meta one, so their order is not guaranteed: worst case the number rolls in early.

**Checked:** StyLua, Selene (the generated Meta network gains four `Value is not defined` errors, the same Blink quirk the
existing empty-data events already show), every changed file compiles, both places build, the wide card's fit worked
out by hand at 16:9 (text column ~270 units) and 4:3 (~170 units). **Not playtested, not opened on the bench, not tried
with a pad or touch.** First to judge: the wide card at 76 units, the sticker over a wide card's top price on a short
banner, chip text shrinking at 4:3, the pile's size in an 88-unit card, the claim countdown in the button.

### Weekly deal (2026-11-06)

The weekly slot belongs on **DEALS**, after the free claim/milestones: one revealed permanent unlock, two Lucky Runs,
and one Revive Token, for **4,500 tickets or 99 Robux**. `ShopCore.WEEKLY_BUNDLE` owns prices, product ID and boost
counts. The old `1/1` stock chip repeated permanent ownership and was removed; do not restore it. The bundle says
**PURCHASED** only after its whole payload was bought and **NEXT BUNDLE IN** for its rotation. `shopCard.OwnedWord`
changes that card's disabled price label; ordinary permanent unlocks still say OWNED. The Shop story mirrors the
same shelf, rewards, currencies and purchased label.

The earlier move to BUNDLES was rejected: that shelf is hidden for players with paid random items disabled, and the
weekly offer needs to participate in the Deals reroll. The revealed weekly purchase uses the same client/server
Robux rule as daily deals (including the existing optional revealed-deal kill switch), rather than the random-item
bundle gate. Its availability badge and confirmed ticket-purchase feedback also belong to DEALS. Moving a guaranteed
offer to a restricted shelf must not silently make that offer unavailable to those players.

The existing Deals reroll refreshes daily offers and an unbought weekly feature, excluding the old feature when
another eligible unlock exists. It preserves the weekly reset date and purchased flag. A pending weekly Robux
checkout retains its saved feature independently while the displayed weekly offer rerolls. The reroll remains
unavailable to players with paid random items disabled; buying an already revealed offer and paying to generate
a new offer are separate entry points.

The player-facing name is **WEEKLY DEAL**, including its section, receipt, preview and Roblox product name, with
**NEXT DEAL IN** on the countdown. It still includes the featured unlock and boosts. Internal persisted names such
as `WeeklyBundlePending` stay stable. Two cases previously left the weekly offer unchanged: the server skipped
rerolling it whenever a saved checkout existed, and `Stories/Shop` regenerated its same fixed weekly item. The server
now rerolls the displayed feature while keeping the original checkout snapshot; another checkout cannot overwrite
that unresolved snapshot. The story alternates featured items and preserves its purchase flag and rotation date.

Weekly bundle prices sit **side by side** on the right: `HorizontalPrices` opts this banner into the card's existing
horizontal price layout, whose row height fits both buttons and their gap inside the price area. The previous
vertical pair was too cramped. Keep this option in the live wrapper and Shop story; other banners retain their layout.

`ShopService` retains each player's existing rotation date and purchased flag when upgrading the old single-unlock
offer. An unbought featured unlock acquired elsewhere is replaced without restarting the week. A stale displayed
name/date is refreshed before charging tickets. A completed collection has no new eligible weekly unlock.

Robux checkout persists the revealed offer in `WeeklyBundlePending` before acknowledging the prompt. That rotation
stays pinned across a disconnect or delayed receipt until payment or Roblox's cancelled-dialog event releases it;
buying with tickets also releases the pending checkout. A paid receipt grants the saved bundle and records the receipt
with the boosts/purchase flag. If that unlock became owned during checkout, or another payment already bought the
bundle, the extra paid receipt receives a fixed credit of **four Lucky Runs and two Revive Tokens**, recorded with the
receipt. It never rolls an unseen replacement after payment or awards lootbox currency/free throws as compensation.
`ShopCore.WEEKLY_BUNDLE.CreditRunBoosts` owns this credit, and `PurchaseUI` lists exactly those boosts.
The new checkout field has a migration; legacy purchases are not reopened or credited boosts retroactively.

Owners: `ShopUI` builds the banner and routes its purchase feedback on DEALS; `ShopController` mirrors extras and
waits for the saved-offer acknowledgment; `PurchaseUI` lists the actual Robux grant. Price fields are `PriceTickets`
and `PriceRobux`, so shared reward-line builders never mistake the bundle's cost for tickets awarded to the buyer.

The weekly card is built directly from its content data and shared reward lines. Do not build a daily card first:
that formats an item description and checks permanent ownership only to overwrite both results. The purchase helper
clones the saved offer and changes `Purchased`; its unchanged content fields need no repeated assignments. The ticket
listener delegates document validation to the existing matching/grant guards instead of fetching it again between them.
Before/after comparisons covered 32 card states; runtime performance has not been profiled.

Regression cases: ticket and Robux purchase, repeated requests/receipt replay, insufficient tickets, stale card,
featured unlock acquired elsewhere or during checkout, exhausted collection, cancellation/reconnect, receipt delayed
past the weekly boundary, legacy purchased/unpurchased offers, Deals badge and both buttons on a narrow card,
restricted-player visibility/direct purchase, the revealed-deal kill switch, weekly reroll before/after purchase,
pending checkout during a reroll, and the fixed boost-credit receipt.
Checked offline behavior, migration, reward presentation, lint, compilation and Rojo builds. **Not playtested in Studio.**

### VIP: two rerolls a chest and a second free box (2026-11-08, unjudged)

Asked for: VIP's free reroll had used up the paid one ("the VIP cannot reroll again by paying"), a FREE label on the
reroll button, and a second free box every 4 h on DEALS for VIP, shown to everyone so it sells VIP.

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Two rerolls a chest: VIP's free one first, then the paid one | `ShopService` pending `RerollUsed` (paid) + `VipRerollUsed` (free), carried onto the rerolled pending; `ShopBoxesUI` `isFreeRerollUsed` / `isPaidRerollUsed`, `pushReroll` |
| FREE tag on the reroll button | `actionButton` `Tag` / `TagColors` (new, generic); `winBoxScreen.SetReroll(isOffered, isUsed, isFree?, left?)` and `Words.Free` |
| VIP FREE BOX card beside FREE BOX | `ShopUI.vipFreeCell`, kind `VipFree`; `ShopExtras.ClaimVipFree`, `ExtrasLoaded`'s last `vipClaimAt`, `ShopCore.CLAIM_VIP_FREE`; save `ShopVipClaimAt` (migration v20) |
| Receipt line | `PurchaseUI.perkRows`: "FREE BOX EVERY 4H" (chest glyph, green) |
| Benches | `Stories/WinBox` Reroll "Free then paid"; `Stories/Shop` DEALS has the non-VIP card |

**The reroll, beat by beat.** The tag is a plate as tall as the count chip, straddling the TOP edge the way the chip
straddles the bottom, green, white Silkscreen with ink, inside the button's body so it rides the entrance, lift and
thump. It pops in from 40% with a few motes, hops ~2 units every 1.6 s while up (80 on a 4 Hz spring: 1.9 peak, settled
in 0.2 s, simulated), and on the free press flies 10 units up while it swells and shrinks away (`pixelMotion.LeaveScale`)
in a puff of green motes. The chip counts what the chest has left: 2 for a VIP whose free one is up and the box has a
reroll product, punching to 1 on the press; the button stays grey until the new hand is up, then comes back with 1 and
no tag, for the paid prompt. The free one is tracked on the client, not read back from `vipRerollDay`: the server
sends the rerolled hand BEFORE the extras with the new day, so reading the day would offer the free one twice.

**The card.** An owner sees VIP FREE BOX in VIP's gold with a VIP tab and a CLAIM on its own 4 h clock; its claim is a big moment (the lobby's confetti, like a flash deal), so
the perk feels paid for each time, and a ready one counts on the DEALS badge. Everyone else sees the same card with a
red VIP ONLY sticker and VIP's Robux price, which prompts the gamepass; the clock has never run for them, so the box is
ready the moment the receipt closes. It does NOT count on the badge for non-owners (shown, never nagging). Policy-
restricted players never see it and the server refuses the claim: a Robux gamepass paying out box opens is paid random
items, the same gate as the free reroll. Analytics reuse the `ShopClaim` source.

**Which box (2026-11-08, second ask).** Not the free one's Items Box: the server picks at CLAIM time, at random, among
the boxes that can still give the player something new (`ShopCore.GetNeededBoxes`: a tickets-priced box whose pool,
less `Hide` entries, holds a name not in `UnlockedNames`; items unlock on their first roll too, so all five boxes can
complete), and among every box once all are complete (`ShopCore.PickVipClaimBox`). Picking at claim, not when the
clock comes up, means nothing is saved and an unlock in between can never make it give a finished box. The owner's
card lists the possible boxes (its short text drops the list when it would not fit), `ShopExtras.Claimed` carries the
picked box's name ("" for every other claim), and `NotificationUI` says YOU GOT A FREE WEAPONS BOX with the strike.
The everyone-else card sells it as "always one you still need". The plain free box stays the Items Box.

**Checked:** StyLua, Selene (only the generated Meta network's empty-event `Value` quirk is new), every changed file
compiles, both places build. **Not playtested, not opened on either bench.** First to judge: the tag's size beside the
chip at the win box's 5 px unit, whether the hop reads as alive or as nagging, the tag overlapping the card row above
on a short screen, and the two FREE cards side by side on a phone.

**Slot caps.** `ShopCore.CAPPABLE_UTILITIES` (WeaponSlots, PassiveSlots, AugmentSlots). Save field `UtilityCaps` (sparse map,
**migration v15** seeds `{}`); Meta Blink `ShopExtras.SetUtilityCap(name, u8)` and `ShopExtras.UtilityCaps(string[], u8[])`
(sent whole on load and change). The server clamps the cap to what was bought and drops it when it equals that.
`ShopService.GetActiveUtilityLevel` = min(bought, cap); `RewardsService` reads it for the three slot bonuses. On the card:
`-` and `+` either side of the pips, pips past the cap go dark brown, the label reads `active/bought`, a step pops that pip
when the server answers. Shown on a maxed (OWNED) slot card too, and reachable with a pad.

**Blink note:** the local `blink` regenerated the main network with a different formatting (13k-line diff) although
nothing in it changed; those three files were restored from git. Only `NetworkMeta` (client and server) carries the new
