### What the shop rounds taught (2026-11-02), as rules for the next page

Layout and sizes:
- **Buttons in one bar are one height.** The boxes bar's prices stood 30 units over a 21-unit row and read as a
  different control. Make them the row's height, and let the face's aspect set the width.
- **A symbol is one size across a page.** The price glyph had been sized to its own number, so a 2-digit price wore a
  double glyph next to 3-digit neighbours. Now it is always a texel per cell; only the words grow.
- **A section title clears what stands over the next row.** Cards wear tabs 5 units over their top edge. The title
  sits 3 units up into the gap above its row, and every section after the first gets 8 more units of air.
- **Too much text gives up words, not the picture.** A card whose description only fits shrunk or cut shows its
  short form (`ShortDescription`: an item's stats without the flavour line). Shrinking it let the text eat the icon.
- **Icons come with different empty margins: crop to the visible rect.** `imageBounds` reads an image once through
  an EditableImage, finds the texels with alpha 48 and up, and the card shows only that rect. It scans in from each
  edge to the first solid texel, not every texel. An image the experience cannot read stays whole.
- **A picture whose size waits on a measure stays hidden until the measure is in.** `imageBounds` answers at once
  from its cache but yields the first time (`CreateEditableImageAsync`). The card used to show the whole image while
  it waited and then snap it to the trimmed rect, so every icon on a tab jumped in size a moment after the first visit,
  and never again (the cache was warm). Now `shopCard` sets `ImageTransparency = 1` before asking and 0 in the answer
  (trimmed or not), and drops an answer for an image it no longer shows. `ShopUI.Appear` warms every picture the shop
  can show (`warmPictures`), so the wait is spent while the player is still on the first tab. Same rule for any
  layout that waits on something async (a texture's size, a text measure, a headshot): don't show it until the answer
  is in, and ask for it early. A "first time only" bug means a cache filling up.

Feel:
- **One thing, one celebration, at the moment it arrives.** The lobby burst its confetti when the server answered,
  before the spent tickets had flown, and the card struck after. The open shop now plays the purchase (tickets fly,
  land, the card strikes) and bursts the confetti on the strike. `ShopUI.WillCelebrate` tells the lobby to hold its
  own burst. Anything the shop does not play still bursts at once.
- **Skip means fast.** A skipped or auto-skipped box reveal holds 0.1 s after the last card lands, not 0.45 s, and
  brings Continue 0.08 s after that, not 0.47 s. Every wait on a skipped path is a wait the player asked to drop.
- **A premium shimmer is slow and stays close.** Hover twinkles are a 1.5 s round. The pair sits at an angle round
  the face that wanders at most 0.7 rad per round. Jumping anywhere on each round read as a fizz.
- **"Random" by `seed * constant` is not random.** Stepping a seed by 1 and taking `(seed * K) % perimeter` walks the
  outline in one fixed stride, so the twinkles came back to the same few spots. They also sat on the bounding box,
  floating off the plate's cut corners. Pick from the shape's own outline texels.
- **Remake an old screen in the kit, keep its job.** The gift picker kept its API (`Show`, `Refresh`) and its
  behaviour (filter, live joins and leaves, B cancels). The drawing moved into `giftScreen` and its bench.

Code:
- **A clock writes only what moved.** `pixelMotion.Step` returns true on the frame it snaps to rest, so "write when
  Step is true" never misses the last frame. A panel at rest then writes nothing. The gift picker's tiles write only
  while they deal in, and the gift writes only when its bob reaches another whole pixel. A sheen is drawn while it
  sweeps and once more as it ends, to clear its rows.
- **No closures made per frame.** Helpers a per-frame draw calls are module functions, or factory functions taking
  what they need as parameters, never `local function` inside `draw`.
- **A question does not change anything.** `WillCelebrate` first spent a flag, so asking twice gave two answers. It
  now compares against the last deal played (`celebratedDeal`), and stays true however often it is asked.
- **One formula, one place.** The plate's chamfer and the ticket's notch (`chamferOf`, `notchOf`) feed both the
  silhouette and the brackets' `Shape`, so the two cannot drift apart.
- **A component made after the screen gets its own Vide root.** codexButton registers `Vide.cleanup`, and a gift
  tile is made when a player joins, long after ShopUI's root ran. Each tile is made inside `Vide.root` and keeps
  the destroy function.
- **Tooling: zsh does not split `$files`.** `sed -i ... $files` handed sed one long path. Pipe through `xargs`.

## Last Wave: the gift picker and the lobby pages' size (2026-11-02, linted, not playtested)

What the user reported: the Quests, Codex and stash pages ran off the right of the screen (the lobby and the shop
fit); the gift picker let the shop's buttons hover through its dim; a press anywhere closed it; and after any close,
by CANCEL or outside, no button on the shop worked, so the picker could never open again.

| Report | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pages wider than the screen | `unscaledSize()` divided `root.AbsoluteSize` by the open grow's `UIScale.Scale`, but that UIScale is on `surface`, not `root`. A layout during the grow (on open, or `AbsoluteSize` arriving on the first visible frame) laid the page out at 1/0.945 of its size, and the settle never changes `root`'s size, so `onResize` never ran again. The shop had the same bug and only looked right because it is re-laid out later | `pageSize()`: `root.AbsoluteSize`, rounded. Before dividing by a scale, check **which frame the UIScale is parented to** |
| Every shop button dead after the picker closed | `giftScreen`'s tick set `isPanelMoving = true` for the whole `Leaving` phase, even after the panel was gone, so `isBusy` never went false and the phase never reached `Hidden`. The root stayed `Visible` with its full-screen `Active` dim, transparent, sinking every press | Moving only while `leaveAge < 1`. **Any "Hidden when nothing is busy" gate: make sure each busy source can end.** A leaving popup that never finishes is invisible and still eats input |
| Hover through the dim | The lobby menu is a **SurfaceGui**: buttons under an Active dim still get `MouseEnter` | `giftScreen`'s `Covering(isCovering)` prop; `ShopUI` sets `screen.UI.Interactable = not isCovering` (true on open, false when the leave starts) |
| The shop ignored presses for ~0.5 s after the picker closed | The shop went `Interactable` when the leave started, but the picker's own `Active` dim and `PanelCatcher` stayed over it, sinking every press until the leave ended and the root went `Visible = false` | `close` sets `root.Interactable = false` as the leave starts, `open` sets it back to `true`. **A leaving popup is only a picture: turn its input off when the leave starts, not when it hides** (linted, not playtested) |
| A press inside the panel closed it | The dim cancels (wanted: "like the codes UI"), and the panel was a plain Frame, so a press on its empty parts fell through to the dim | A handler-less, transparent `ImageButton` (`PanelCatcher`, ZIndex 0) under the panel's Slab, as `CodesUI` does. Tiles and CANCEL sit above it |

How it was checked, and what did not work:
- **Tripwire's `simulate_mouse_input` does not reach the lobby's SurfaceGui** (tried with and without the 58 px
  inset): clicks never fire. To drive a pad-closable modal from a probe, call its bound action:
  `ContextActionService:CallFunction("GamepadFocus_Back", Enum.UserInputState.Begin, nil)` runs the same `dismiss`.
- A probe in the user's live playtest is in front of them: it forced `ShopUI.Visible` and opened the picker on its
  own. Delete it (`delete_instance`) as soon as the user takes over, and tell them to restart the playtest.
- `tw.py <tool> @file.json` fails (it `json.loads` the argument before checking for `@`); load args from a file with
  a small wrapper that imports `tw` and calls `tw.post`. A RunContext value is
  `{"type":"EnumItem","enum":"RunContext","item":"Client"}`.

  left holding a 7 x 7 pixel glyph (tick, cross, "!") drawn in Frames with its shade a unit down-right.

  0.9 of the canvas), and the toast is as wide as its longest line (40-unit minimum column).
- **The arrival**: pops from half size dropping 3 units onto its row under a white flash; on landing the glyph
  punches in from nothing (4.2 Hz / 0.42, about +23%), rings are thrown, a sheen crosses the well, Good throws side
  sparks (6, plus 3 per detail line), Bad shakes the glyph only, Warning breathes on three stepped rings while it shows.

  `Clear()` (the Ascension) destroys them at once with nothing thrown, as the old one emptied its list.

Checked: stylua, selene, lune compile, both Rojo builds. **Not played in Studio and not judged on the bench.**

**Round 2 (2026-11-02): the gift wears the gift.** Gift received and gift sent pass the shop's gift picture
(`rbxassetid://88621624412481`, the one ShopUI / ShopBoxesUI / GiftPickerUI use and LoadingScreen preloads) as
`image`: it takes the glyph's place, 10 units square in the 12-unit panel (a unit each side, as the run's toasts), and
bobs a unit on 1.6 s in whole units like the gift picker's gift. It punches in on the same spring as a glyph. A gift
that FAILED or was blocked keeps the red cross: the picture says "a gift", the cross says "it went wrong", and a
failure must read as a failure first. The merge key is message + variant + image.

Numbers, checked in `lune` with a scratch copy of the wrap and layout (not kept; copy `wrap` and `layoutToast`'s sums out of the module to redo it):

| Toast | 1920 x 1080 (unit 4) | Bench 640 x 360 (unit 2) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BUILDERMAN JOINED | 1 line, 444 x 72 px, 7% of the height | 222 x 36, 10% |
| GIFT TO ... COULDN'T BE DELIVERED, 3 ... GRANTED | 3 lines, 668 x 136, 13% | 19% |
| Premium gift (heading + 3 rewards) | 5 lines, 524 x 188, 17% | 26% |

The pop lands 0.12 s after the push (peak 1.06x); the glyph peaks 1.22x and the count badge 1.19x.

**What this round taught:**

1. **A picture the player already knows beats a glyph.** The gift button's picture says "gift" before a word is
   read; a tick only says "good". When a notice is about a THING with its own icon (a gift, later a box or a
   currency), pass that icon; keep the glyph for notices about an outcome (joined, refused, warned).
2. **Outcome before subject on a failure.** A failed gift keeps the cross, not the gift, so red plus picture never
   reads as "you got a gift".
3. **A draw gate only saves something if the value moves slower than a step a frame.** The warning's breath was first
   gated in hundredths: it moves ~2.7 a second at its fastest, more than a hundredth a frame, so every frame still
   wrote. Gated in twentieths (stepped light anyway), it writes ~35 times a second. Work out the value's fastest
   rate before choosing the step.
4. **Two offsets on one Frame share one gate.** The mark's shake and bob are folded into one number
   (`shake * 4096 + bob`) so the position is written once when either reaches another pixel, not by two gates
   that each think the other's write is theirs.
5. **Wrap with the generous advance, then size to the longest line.** Wrapping at `Advance` 0.72 guarantees a line
   fits, so no label ever shrinks (a shrunk line is unreadable on a phone); sizing the toast to its longest wrapped
   line keeps short notices short instead of every toast being the widest.
6. **Read nothing back from an Instance per frame.** The bar first read `Track.Size.X.Offset` every frame (a
   reflection call); the layout now keeps `TrackW` in the toast's table.
7. **A clean-screen clear is instant.** A suppression meant to keep a ceremony clean must not play leaves and puffs
   over its first quarter second.

**Cost, as it stands:** one `pixelMotion` stepper, alive only while a toast or particle lives (the bar keeps it awake
for a toast's 5 s). At rest a toast writes its bar on each whole unit, a picture's bob on each unit, and a
warning's rings on each twentieth; the pop, flash, sheen, rings, shake and badge write only while they move (cached
`Drawn*` fields, and the sheen's last frame clears its rows). About 60 Instances per toast (sheen rows, 8 ring
edges, up to 26 glyph texels), built per push and destroyed when it leaves: notices are rare, so they are not pooled.
Per-toast closures are the three input connections, made once.

**Readability, what is still open:** a stack of three tall notices (Premium gifts) takes about half the screen's
height under the tab bar; if that shows up in play, cap the stack by height as well as count. Words are Silkscreen 7
units (heading) and 6 (details) at the lobby's unit 4, about 10 pt on a 390 pt-tall phone. Not checked on a device.

### Review before playtesting (2026-11-04)

### Navigation focus and centered scroll hints (2026-11-04)

Category switches preserve the region the controller is navigating. Codex keeps the selected carousel arrow;
Quests and Shop keep selection in their tab bar and move it to the newly active tab after the reactive drawing
updates. Settings does the same for L1/R1 and preserves header focus when its values or input platform rebuild the
rows. Switching categories from content still lands on the new category's content anchor. Deferred Shop/Quests
focus checks the current category and visibility before applying; Shop also yields to a reveal.

The shared tab bar exposes its selected state through `NavigationSelected`, independent of which tab the controller
is browsing. `selectionLinks.SelectedIn` reads the actual engine selection, and `ActiveTab` ignores hidden or
unselectable controls. Options and Profile had equivalent unconditional content-focus effects; these now preserve
their category indicator. Their effects live below the header construction so they can use its actual instance.
Stash and Leaderboards already retain header focus on category switches and were left unchanged.

Scroll glyphs are centered on the scrollbar thumb again. `scrollbar.attachHint` draws them in a transparent overlay
above every clipping ancestor of the track, within the same page's hierarchy. This lets the glyph overlap the panel
stroke without being cropped or shifted left. Absolute thumb geometry is mapped to the overlay using scale shares;
the glyph follows layout/resize events, hides with any hidden ancestor or disabled layer, and removes its overlay
and connections when the scrollbar or Vide scope is destroyed. It uses no additional frame callback.

against the 335-diagnostic baseline. These changes have not been rendered or controller-tested in Studio. No Studio
probe was installed.

### Navigation implementation review (2026-11-04)

The scroll hint separates hierarchy setup, layer placement and visibility updates. Only an ancestry change rebuilds
its ancestor listeners; hiding/showing a panel, changing clipping or enabling/disabling its GUI reuses the existing
connections. Hidden hints skip geometry work, unchanged positions are not rewritten, and showing a hint refreshes
the position it missed while hidden. Reparenting replaces the cached ancestor list and detaches the old listeners.

The tab bar changes `NavigationSelected` on just the previous and new active buttons inside its existing selection
transition, rather than rewriting every tab's attribute from the reactive reader. An unchanged selection writes none.

Checked: 280 offline assertions, all 23 accessibility files compile, both Rojo builds pass, formatting/whitespace
checks pass and Selene remains at 335 baseline diagnostics with no new ones. Source/GUI stand-ins measured five-tab
attribute writes going from 5 to 2 on a switch and 5 to 0 when unchanged. Six visibility/clipping updates registered
54 replacement hint listeners before this review and zero afterward. Additional checks cover skipped hidden/unchanged
position writes, refresh on show, ancestor replacement, detach/reattach, layer changes and cleanup. These counts are

## Controller and touch contract for Last Wave

Consolidated 2026-11-04. Read this before changing navigation, selectable controls, scrollbars, category tabs,
animated overlays or touch actions. These are the accepted behaviors from the controller corrections above;
earlier implementation notes are history. Verify the current source before applying the recipe to another screen.

### Trace the whole input path before editing

A selectable button is only one part of controller support. Trace the wrapper's category changes, reactive rebuilds,
focus effects and deferred callbacks, the drawing's directional links, the visible selection marker, and the shared
scroll/input owner. Making a control reachable can expose a later wrapper callback that immediately moves focus
away. A navigation-only unit check will miss that callback; a source-only check will miss renderer clipping.

| Owner | Start with |
| --- | --- |
| Actual controller focus, modal return targets, Back and cycle bindings | `Global/Client/Controllers/GamepadFocusController.luau` |
| Card rows, directional links and content/header bridges | `Global/Client/UI/Components/selectionLinks.luau`; lobby `Components/shopScreen.luau` |
| Active tab state and category arrows | `Global/Client/UI/Components/tabBar.luau`, `pixelCarousel.luau`; each page's wrapper |
| Shared visible corners and the moving face they frame | `Global/Client/UI/Components/cornerSelector.luau`; lobby `Components/codexButton.luau`, `priceButton.luau` |
| Stick polling, explicit scroll ownership and shared fallback | `Global/Client/UI/Components/gamepadScroll.luau` |
| Scrollbar skin, hint placement, clipping and cleanup | `Global/Client/UI/Components/scrollbar.luau` |
| Box reveal focus and chest return to rest | lobby `ShopBoxesUI.luau`, `Components/shopBoxes.luau`; global `winBoxScreen.luau` |
| Touch gesture cancellation and favorite/banish actions | lobby `CodexUI.luau`, `Components/codexScreen.luau` |

Paths above are relative to `src/`; lobby page wrappers/drawings are in `Lobby/Client/UI/MenuUI/` and shared UI is
in `Global/Client/UI/`. Reuse these owners instead of adding parallel focus, gesture or scroll systems. Require
modules that pull Ignis controllers through the live `script.Parent` tree: a StarterPlayer require can create a
second controller copy. Follow the module's existing singleton path for `cornerSelector` and `scaleNumber`.

### Navigation must follow the drawn layout

- Wire explicit `NextSelection*` links. Roblox consumes DPad navigation when `GuiService.SelectedObject` is set;
  a ContextActionService DPad binding is not a substitute for the GUI's links. Keep focus inside the active page or
  overlay, with intentional self-links at boundaries. Hidden, closing, owned/unavailable or policy-hidden controls
  must not remain selectable unless they still represent an available action, such as gifting an owned product.
- Shop navigation has structure: controls inside a card, cards inside a drawn row, and rows inside sections.
  Use the layout's row information through `selectionLinks.LinkCards`. Up/down visits the current card's other
  control band first, then the immediately adjacent row with available controls. A wholly inactive row can be skipped.
  Alignment breaks ties within that search; a globally aligned button farther away must not bypass a nearer row.
- Horizontal movement stays in the drawn card row. Gift is left of the price buttons, including when the neighboring
  card is owned. A stepper above a price must not steal a left/right move intended for the neighboring card.
  An owned card can center its gift/owned group, so test it separately from the unowned layout.
- Rebuild links after layout, resize, ownership, content or policy changes. Reuse existing focused controls when
  refreshing data. Before destroying a focused target, replace/repair its current and saved return targets using the
  focus controller. Empty pages need a valid category/back target. Snapshot geometry once per calculation and skip
  unchanged link writes; recalculate only the selected control's links on a simple focus change where appropriate.

These exact paths are regression cases, not optional layout preferences:

| Starting selection and input | Required next selection |
| --- | --- |
| Premium/Bundles: owned card's Gift, Right | Nearest Gift on the card to its right, before that card's Robux price |
| A card's Robux price, Left | Its own Gift when Gift is the adjacent visible control |
| A slot card's minus, Down; its Gift, Up | Its own Gift; its own minus |
| A slot card's Robux price, Up | Its own plus |
| A slot card's Gift, Left | A control to its left in the card row, rather than plus above it |
| Deals: Free section, Down | Weekly Deal before Daily Deals |
| Tools: third upgrade row, Down | The centered final upgrade row before Run Boosts |
| Bundles: Arsenal, Down toward ticket packs | The nearest smaller-pack row before the lower 50k pack |

### Category changes preserve the region being navigated

- Read `GuiService.SelectedObject` through `selectionLinks.SelectedIn(header)` when deciding whether the player is
  in the header. A remembered content index or desired focus alone does not tell you where native navigation moved.
- Activating a tab/arrow manually keeps focus in the header. Never unconditionally focus a grid item after changing
  categories, rebuilding rows or loading values. Audit every `SetFocus` call on that path, including deferred ones.
- If header focus is active, L2/R2 category shortcuts move it to the newly active tab. Settings uses L1/R1 for its
  categories. A carousel with stable arrow/indicator controls keeps that selected control as its category changes.
  If focus was in content, a shortcut can retain the content index or land on the new content anchor as that page
  already specifies. Opening a page and changing a category are different focus events.
- `tabBar` publishes the active button through `NavigationSelected`. `selectionLinks.ActiveTab` finds a shown,
  selectable active tab after the reactive drawing updates. The selected category and the tab currently being
  browsed are different states. Update the old/new active flags only; unchanged selections write none.
- `selectionLinks.AttachHeader` bridges Up from the first content row and Down back into content. Preserve a valid
  exact return target, or find a shown replacement. Restore temporary Up/Down links on exit and teardown without
  overwriting links installed by a newer owner. Dropdowns, key capture, prompts and nested modals keep their focus.
- Deferred focus must recheck visibility, the current category, and modal/reveal ownership before applying. A stale
  callback from the preceding tab must not overwrite the latest selection. Repair Settings header focus on value
  or platform rebuilds too. Test manual activation and shortcuts through the actual wrapper, not just the tab drawing.

The audit covered Codex, Quests, Shop, Settings, Options and Profile, which needed header-preserving behavior.
Stash and Leaderboards already preserved it. Recheck them if their wrappers change; do not generalize from one page.

### Reachable controls must have visible selection feedback

Every focusable control needs its intended controller corners and selection feedback: prices, Gift, minus/plus,
dropdown triggers and rows, auto-skip, previous/next chest arrows, category tabs, category arrows and empty-page
fallbacks. `Selectable = true` alone is incomplete.

For the shared traveling corners, set `SelectionImageObject = cornerSelector.Image`. An arbitrary empty Frame
suppresses the engine image but also opts out of the shared selector. Earlier historical advice to use an empty
selection image must be read with this distinction. A screen intentionally drawing its own focus marker can keep
that marker; do not blindly replace it. If the hit stays still while its slab lifts/sinks, add the `FocusFrame`
ObjectValue pointing to the visible face so the shared corners follow that face. Check SelectionGained/Lost feedback
and pressed feedback as well as the links. Confirm it visually on the actual selected control.

### One stick action has one visible owner

- Poll live gamepad state through `gamepadScroll`; event-cached stick values can miss release on mobile controllers.
  Explicit handlers retain precedence even while temporarily gated, so a fallback cannot bypass a prompt or slider.
  The shared scrollbar fallback has one frame callback for all registrations and targets the focused list. Reuse it
  instead of adding a frame callback per bar. Manual scrolling must update the focus controller's scroll-position
  baseline (`TakePosition`) so the next focus move does not snap the canvas back.
- A hint promises an action. Do not show the same right-stick glyph on two bars while only one responds. Codex's
  accepted split is left-stick entry navigation with automatic grid scrolling, and right-stick detail scrolling.
  The entry grid passes `GamepadScrollEnabled = false`, which suppresses both its fallback and its hint; the detail
  handler remains available while an entry is selected. Rigs and open loadout prompts temporarily own the stick.
  Mouse/touch can still drag either scrollbar. Boxes uses the right stick horizontally to cycle chests.
- The scrollbar glyph stays centered on its thumb, above the panel stroke. Moving it inward to avoid clipping was
  rejected. Raising ZIndex cannot escape an ancestor's `ClipsDescendants`: use `scrollbar.attachHint` to draw above
  the clipping ancestors, inside the same page's layer hierarchy so unrelated overlays retain their ordering.
- Project the absolute thumb center into the hint overlay using scale shares. ScreenGui/SurfaceGui coordinates and
  a parent's opening UIScale must not be mixed with unscaled pixel offsets. Check both thumb ends, resize, page
  entrances and canvas changes. Do not change the accepted visual placement to conceal a layering bug.
- A detached hint must hide with any hidden ancestor or disabled GUI and be destroyed with its scrollbar/scope.
  An ancestry change rebuilds cached ancestors/listeners; visibility, clipping and layer changes reuse them. Hidden
  hints skip placement, unchanged positions skip writes, and showing a hint catches up to its current position.
  Test reparenting, detach/reattach and idempotent cleanup. No new frame callback is needed for hint placement.

### Reveal focus follows visible phases, not guessed delays

1. Remember the actual opening control. Preserve that original return target across rerolls.
2. Hide/disable the shop chrome and clear its focus. Focus Skip from its actual `Shown` callback, when it becomes
   selectable. Its entrance can exceed the focus controller's retry budget; requesting focus at reveal start failed.
3. Focus Continue when the reveal makes it available. Hidden or scheduled buttons must not remain selectable.
4. Continue clears selection immediately while the reveal leaves and the chest returns. Do not show corners on
   hidden controls or restore shop focus when only the faster overlay/opening blend has finished.
5. Wait for the carousel's terminal `IsResting()` state, restore chrome, then restore the opening control. If the
   target has disappeared or become unavailable, choose an intentional shown replacement. Cancel outdated waiters
   with the reveal token on close/cleanup. A hidden shop must still finish its in-progress chest return motion.

Test skip, auto-skip, continue, reroll, leaving the page mid-return and rapid reopen. Reuse modal focus cleanup
handles (`PushFocus`, `ReplaceFocus`) where applicable; a shared panel's return state belongs to its wrapper.
Animated leaving states must terminate and hide/destroy their input roots. A transparent Active backdrop can still
intercept every button underneath it after its artwork has vanished.

### Touch scrolling must never paint actions across entries

Favorite/banish modes commit from a resolved tap on the intended entry. Touch InputBegan, TouchMoved and incidental
hover while panning must not favorite/banish each entry the finger crosses. Track the originating InputObject, the
touch's initial position and the list's canvas position; permanently cancel that tap once it is a pan, even if the
finger returns to its origin. Reject activation from another finger or after the list has moved.

The current Codex guard uses more than 12 screen pixels of touch travel or more than 1 pixel of canvas movement;
verify its source before reusing these thresholds. Test movement out and back, inertia/list movement and another
finger as well as a stationary tap. Preserve intentional mouse drag painting and held controller marks. Touch
must not inherit persistent mouse hover.

### Regression review before reporting a controller fix as tested

| Check | Cases to include |
| --- | --- |
| Card geometry | Owned/unowned Gift; all three slot steppers; centered owned controls; mixed button sizes; wide rows; incomplete centered rows; hidden/policy-restricted controls; empty rows |
| Row order | Free/Weekly/Daily; thirteen upgrades at four columns; smaller ticket packs before 50k; repeat at one through four columns and after resizing |
| Header behavior | Enter header from content, visit tabs/arrows, activate manually, cycle both ways with shortcuts, return Down; repeat on every affected page and with empty/read-only categories |
| Scroll ownership | The hinted bar responds once, no second list scrolls, explicit handlers remain authoritative, next focus move preserves manual scroll, modal/rig/input switches release the stick correctly |
| Selection rendering | Corners on every newly reachable control, including chest arrows/dropdown/auto-skip; moving faces and clipped list edges; no focus on hidden controls |
| Hint rendering | Centered on the thumb above the stroke at both ends; narrow/phone canvases, opening scale, ScreenGui and SurfaceGui; hidden pages, disabled layers, reparenting and destruction |
| Reveal lifecycle | Skip when visible, Continue when ready, clear on exit, restore after actual rest, original target across rerolls, leave/reopen during motion, cleanup |
| Touch actions | Stationary tap acts once; scroll up/down, cross entries, return to origin, moved canvas and another finger do not paint; mouse/controller marking still works |
| Lifecycle | Close/Back, nested overlays, reconnect/input switching, joins/removals where relevant, resize, rapid category changes and stale deferred work |

Build meaningful checks against the current layout and wrapper callbacks, with real ownership and section variants.
Earlier checks used simple aligned fixtures and covered reachability without the visible marker or wrapper reset;
they passed while the player's failures remained. Keep UI Labs stories synchronized with the live drawing and
include the state that actually failed, rather than a simpler catalog that avoids its final short row.

Run the repository's formatting/lint checks, compare Selene against its existing baseline, compile changed large
Luau files for the local-register limit, and build both places for shared changes. These verify source/build health.
Offline GUI/input stand-ins verify modeled sequences and operation counts. Studio rendering, physical controller
input, phone gestures and actual frame-time profiling are separate evidence. Verify that connected Studio contains
the edited source before testing; a successful Rojo build does not synchronize a running playtest. Preserve the
user's playtest/session, and disclose any temporary probe instead of quietly changing what they are observing.

Do not call an offline check a Studio/controller playtest, or claim "most optimized" from assignment counts.
The latest recorded source pass had 280 offline assertions, 23 accessibility files compiling, both builds passing
and no added Selene diagnostics against 335 existing ones. It did not establish rendered/controller/phone proof or
frame-time gains. Those counts are dated evidence, not a permanent baseline to assume in another session.
Scratch harnesses under `/tmp` are not durable project tests; this contract and the source are the handoff.
If hardware/Studio testing is unavailable, finish the authorized implementation and available checks, report that
limit explicitly, and leave the concrete manual cases above for verification rather than inventing confidence.

## Last Wave: watched-player spectator view (2026-11-04, source checked; Studio proof pending)

Historical implementation round. Its top-strip layout, duplicate teammate mirror, 100-byte camera format and
validation status were superseded. Use the [current contract](#spectator-ui-and-replication-contract-for-last-wave)
before making changes; the history below records what was built at that time.

This supersedes the spectator limitations in the 2026-11-01 cash-out entry. Spectating now has its own
`SpectatorService`, `SpectatorController` and `SpectatorUI`; the existing final-stats controller still owns the
teammate list, entering/leaving spectate, Results and controller focus. The spectator's frozen HUD hides while
read-only copies of the watched player's drawing APIs play. These use the actual run components and responsive
layout, rather than sending screenshots or letting the spectator issue the watched player's actions.

### Coverage and presentation ownership

| Watched state | Presentation |
| --- | --- |
| Camera | Actual position, rotation, zoom and FOV; interpolated camera samples. Player view is the default; the strip/F switches to Orbit view. Samples include a pre-shake pose so the viewer's screen-shake preference still works. The existing camera/AOI path and server replication focus follow the watched world. |
| Vitals and combat HUD | Health, shield/overshield, ability icons, charges, cooldowns, locks, descriptions and press/shine feedback; buffs/timers, XP/level, kills, souls, streak, revive progress, and cursor hit/hurt/kill feedback. |
| Progression | Level-up and augment/ability hands, rarity/roulette presentation, source stat previews, new/owned state, favorites, synergy/conflict artwork, counts, banish state, rerolls, skips and confirmed selections. Late viewers receive the current hand and immediately land its cards so a near-deadline choice remains readable. |
| Watched selection | A separate instance of the shared focus brackets follows the source control's descendant path, visible face and scroll clipping. The viewer's own selection remains on the spectator strip. Reward/upgrade confirmation artwork also follows the source selection. |
| Other run UI | Watched inventory/stats, formatted values and inspect cards, inventory scrolling, chest contents/reveals and accept/banish holds, world interaction prompts/holds, quests, color-dance state, announcements, countdown remaining time/pulse, teammate vitals/ultimates, run/overtime clock and map expansion/legend state. Blur, saturation and the shared reward/inventory backdrop follow the watched presentation. |
| Exit and lifecycle | Results stops the mirrored HUD/camera immediately. Switching targets destroys the old scope before accepting the new source; late packets from another source and old camera sequences are ignored. Disconnect, finish, run end and restart release subscriptions, UI and camera state. |

Reward previews carry the source's display data. Recalculating them against a remote player's partial client ECS
can silently change the before/after values, favorites or synergy icons. `UpgradeOption.Describe` builds serializable
drawing data on the source; `Draw` consumes that data on the viewer. Augment spawns carry the same sort of icon and
favorite snapshot. Gameplay callbacks are replaced with inert functions. Read-only drawings skip their input bindings,
disable native button/scroll interaction, and reassert that restriction after updates that would normally make a
control selectable. Only the viewer's spectator controls own focus and Back. The inventory mirror does not change
mouse-lock ownership; Left Alt remains the player's manual toggle.

The spectator strip sits at the top, with the watched clock and quest/announcement column below its actual bounds.
On narrow windows it wraps into a name/arrow row and an action row; text retains a minimum pixel unit and actions
retain their height. Controller links follow the drawn rows, and hidden controls immediately release interaction.

### Replication and cost boundaries

- New events use the Meta Blink network. The server validates that the viewer finished and the target is still in
  the run, then keeps per-target viewer sets. It sends presentation only with `Fire(viewer, ...)` to those subscribers.
- The first subscriber enables the source; the last subscriber disables and disconnects its capture loop. With zero
  viewers there is no spectator JSON encoding, camera capture or spectator upload. The source retains current UI
  arguments locally for a future join; that bookkeeping is part of the existing drawing calls.
- Camera uploads target 20 Hz; HUD changes flush at 10 Hz. Unchanged values coalesce, transient feedback expires,
  new viewers receive a targeted snapshot, and existing viewers keep receiving deltas. Source generations reject
  obsolete uploads; monotonic sequences reject reordered unreliable camera packets.
- Camera packets are 100 bytes. Presentation batches cap at 128 calls and 48 KiB. The server caps a source at
  256 KiB/sec, 40 presentation packets/sec and 30 camera packets/sec. These are configured bounds, not measured
  live bandwidth or frame-time results. The generated Meta receive guard also accommodates these snapshots;
  its previous 4 KiB guard rejected valid large hands before the spectator handler ran.
- No gameplay outcomes, rewards or saves are accepted from this cosmetic stream. Instance/function references do
  not cross it; source GetCard functions become inert display data. Backdrop replay accepts only the known owners,
  and replay scopes do not record a second stream through the shared drawing APIs.

### Enemies/drops freeze and verification

The win chest used to force `TimeCore` to zero when a player cashed out, even while the party continued. Removing
that unconditional pause from `WinBoxController` leaves final run-end pausing with `FinalStatsController`. An offline
probe against the real controller and TimeCore reproduced the old live-clock freeze and verified that the current
code preserves live, slow, ended and manually paused clocks, including a second reveal and Continue.

`lune run tools/spectator/check.luau` currently passes **165 offline assertions**. It loads the production codec,
recorder, relay service, generated client/server Blink transport, receiver, controller, strip and upgrade-preview
module with explicit runtime/drawing stand-ins. Cases include zero-viewer traffic, targeted late snapshots, unchanged
setters, collection cleanup, consecutive reward hands, nested replay isolation, source-only preview data, the old
large-packet rejection, camera ordering, target switches, teardown and read-only controls after Appear. Strip geometry
and navigation are checked at 1920x1080, 844x390, 390x844, 320x568 and 240x320.

Source checks: Blink regeneration, `stylua --check src`, the harness formatting check, compilation of the 93 listed
changed/new Luau files, both Game and Lobby Rojo builds, and `git diff --check` pass. Full-tree Selene has **no added
diagnostics** against the captured worktree baseline (10 errors/325 warnings before, 10 errors/322 warnings after).
The existing diagnostics remain; this is not a clean full-tree lint result.

`Survivors/Client/UI/Stories/Spectator` is the review bench, using the real strip, vital bars, ability slot, level bar,
reward card, chest reveal and focus brackets. It defaults to watched reward choices, with controls for gameplay/chest
states, watched/confirmed selection, banish mode, vitals, teammate switches and rerolls.

**Not playtested or visually judged in Studio.** The connected places did not contain the new spectator controller;
no playtest was restarted or source silently replaced. Builds and offline GUI/input stand-ins do not establish Roblox
rendering, physical controller/phone behavior, live packet costs or frame-time gains. After syncing, verify with at
least two clients (and two viewers for routing): cash out while another keeps fighting; join mid-hand/mid-hold; reroll,
banish, skip and confirm; inspect/scroll inventory; expand the map; resize/change input; switch targets; exit through
Results/Back; then finish, disconnect and restart. Confirm enemies/drops keep moving, source corners follow the actual
animated face, the viewer cannot operate watched rewards, and only active viewers receive the additional stream.

## Last Wave: spectator layout, hover, left controls and camera corrections (2026-11-04)

Historical correction round. The [current contract](#spectator-ui-and-replication-contract-for-last-wave) consolidates
these decisions with the subsequent retention, decoding and cache fixes.

The user's review rejected the top spectator strip displacing the clock and announcements, the quest column above
ordinary reward hands, missing mouse-hover corners, gameplay key hints in spectate, and the offset/jittery camera.
This entry supersedes those layout/camera details in the preceding spectator round.

- **Reuse includes the containers.** `Components/runHud` now builds the clock ScreenGui and quest column for both
  the live wrappers and spectator receiver. The clock keeps its drawing's position and Timer layer 14; quests keep
  the actual `0.5, 0.07` column, padding, inset policy, active/pinned stacks and normal layer 4 below Choices 9.
  The source's brief held-result layer 10 is mirrored when it actually applies. No spectator control moves either
  top HUD element. The quest lock warning uses its existing drawing too. Overtime bonus state stays separate from
  the readout so coalescing a clock update cannot discard the multiplier or strand its unfold animation.
- **Keep the actual teammate cards.** Spectating uses the existing `PlayersInfoUI` instances and public vitals;
  the duplicate watched teammate registry is no longer streamed or drawn. Each portrait becomes an individual
  selectable control, with a watched accent, shared corners and pressed feedback. Up/Down arrows sit around the
  column; View and Results sit with it. Cards and controls use Spectator layer 16, above level-up/augment hands.
  Short windows place the actions in a footer row; navigation follows that row. Target removal repairs focus before
  disabling its old control. Geometry follows the column's actual animated content height, while unchanged geometry
  and navigation skip rewrites. The story uses this same teammate drawing and selection wiring.
- **Make a target change feel like a target change.** The newly watched card flashes in its player color, throws
  a restrained ring and five sparks, and gives a centered spring thump. The name travels vertically with the switch;
  buttons retain Slab lift, press/sink, flash and click feedback. This is one event per changed watched state, not
  recurring motion on every vitals update. Long names truncate while text retains a readable minimum size.
- **Mouse hover is separate from pad focus.** Source buttons report mouse enter/leave to the local recorder.
  Touch does not leave a mouse hover behind; pad selection remains available. The existing Blink focus payload
  carries the control path and layout order, so a swapped/rerolled card does not depend on sibling insertion order.
  The viewer draws the shared corners on the actual animated face and drives the reward/upgrade drawing's own
  hover state. Hovering an action such as Reroll frames that action without also hovering a card with the same order.
  Hidden, removed and cleared controls release their old hover. Watched controls remain inert.
- **Hide gameplay hints.** The viewer's bottom-right keybind panel hides and restores with the local HUD. It is
  registered as local-only presentation and never appears in a spectator snapshot. Map toggles also defer to the watched source while spectating.
- **One ordered camera pipeline.** The live shoulder/shake pass runs at Camera + 1, watched playback at Camera + 2,
  and watched-source capture at Camera + 3. Local FOV tweens do not overwrite a watched camera. This follows
  [Roblox's explicit render-order API](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/RunService#BindToRenderStep).
  Samples carry the source's final pose, pre-shake pose, FOV, focus and character origin. Playback blends source
  offsets and follows the viewer's rendered target between packets; it does not restart from the viewer's already
  translated world camera or use an invented focus twenty studs ahead. Unanchored/scriptable source cameras retain
  their absolute pose. Camera samples are now 128 bytes, still 20 Hz, uploaded once per watched source and relayed
  only to its viewers. The existing sequence, generation and budget checks remain.
- **No new Roblox metadata protocol.** The client read-only marker is a local registry in `cornerSelector`, cleared
  on scope teardown. Player/card identity stays in Lua tables. Neither needs Attributes or CollectionService tags.
  The spectator server has no attribute/tag writes; all additional presentation traffic uses generated Blink.
  Existing client kit metadata such as `FocusFrame`/`FocusCut` remains where the shared selector already needs it.
