## Last Wave: spectator retention, cached focus and protocol cleanup (2026-11-05)

Implementation evidence for the [current contract](#spectator-ui-and-replication-contract-for-last-wave). Counts and
profiling limits below describe this particular worktree and test run; remeasure them in a later session.

The follow-up review found avoidable history and repeated work despite correct subscriber routing. These changes
preserve the preceding round's layout, layers, controls and feedback. They add no Roblox Attributes or instance tags;
additional client/server traffic still uses Blink.

- **Bound retained history on both ends.** Removed entries are deleted from retained source state. A removal needed
  by existing viewers lives only until the next flush, never enters a late-join snapshot, and is discarded when capture
  stops. Transient feedback is likewise retired after sending. Per-entry dirty keys clear with their state, ordinary
  flushes iterate dirty entries, and full retained-state scans are reserved for snapshots. The receiver drops removed
  ability-id mappings and their per-entry revisions. Events use a scalar revision watermark rather than retaining a
  key for every hit/press. Repeated collection clears always advance, including a second clear after new entries.
- **Explicit operations and types.** The serialized call envelope identifies Remove, Clear and Event operations,
  allowing bounded receiver cleanup and replay rejection. The server validates that operation field. Call, argument,
  focus-path, binding, retained-record, view and camera-sample types describe the boundaries; dynamic drawing APIs
  and heterogeneous argument contents remain explicitly dynamic. Camera interpolation now uses typed From/To samples
  and elapsed time. Shared camera format offsets, rates and protocol limits live beside the codec.
- **One viewer decode.** The controller decodes and inspects the received call array, then passes that array to the
  receiver. The receiver no longer decodes the same buffer again. Snapshot chunks are serialized once and shared
  between simultaneous recipients. JSON strings are batched directly, without an intermediate buffer for each call.
- **Cache identity; keep geometry live.** Source focus paths retain their identity while unchanged, so unchanged focus
  is not serialized. Structural and name/order changes invalidate them; an unrelated descendant change that leaves
  the path unchanged does not create another focus payload. New-viewer focus can be sent just to that viewer.
  `Utils/spectatorFocus` caches the receiver's target, hierarchy, layer, focus-face reference and scrolling ancestor.
  Replacement/reparented controls invalidate the cache. Each rendered frame still reads visibility, the current
  face and its geometry, so moving/hidden cards and scroll clipping remain correct. Cache listeners disconnect on
  invalidation and teardown. Only active bonus clocks are stepped instead of searching every view for one.
- **Avoid repeated preference reads.** Each camera packet reads the screen-shake preference once, outside its
  twelve-component decode loop. Source-side billboard metadata lookup is limited to the world prompt/chest kinds.

The durable `tools/spectator/check.luau` harness passes **582 assertions** in this round. Concrete operation evidence:

| Case | Before review | After this pass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Empty collection after 250 unique add/remove pairs while idle | 250 obsolete removal calls in its late snapshot | No removed entries retained; only live entries are snapshotted |
| 2,500 watched add/remove operations with a flush between batches | Removal history could grow until a clear/destroy | Only the live entry remains after sending pending deltas |
| One HUD packet on the viewer | Controller decode plus receiver decode | One controller decode; no receiver decode |
| 1,200 unchanged focus checks / receiver frames | Repeated path construction and child enumeration | No child enumeration after resolution |
| 100 unchanged source flushes after initialization | Focus serialized on each flush and compared as text | Zero JSON encodes |
| Simultaneous new viewers | Snapshot calls serialized for each recipient | Shared encoded chunks |
| Shake preference per received camera packet | Twelve reads | One read |

Cases also cover removal delivery to existing viewers, no removal replay to joiners, remove/re-add in one flush,
repeated clears, stale add/event rejection, local-only hints, cache rebuild after layout changes/rerolls, live moving
geometry, hidden layers, malformed focus and complete listener/marker cleanup. These are production-module tests with
runtime/drawing stand-ins; their work counts are not FPS, memory-byte or live-bandwidth measurements.

The connected Game place contained the edited modules. A temporary F5 UI probe passed **22 real-engine assertions**
at 1919x1080, including the existing layout/layer/read-only checks and replacing the reward hand while retaining
correct watched corners without another focus packet. The probe was deleted from StarterPlayer immediately after
starting, cleaned its runtime HUD, and the controlled playtest was stopped. Existing missing/type-mismatched boot
asset warnings remained; the probe emitted no spectator runtime errors.

Available source checks passed: repository and harness formatting, compilation of the 111 listed changed/new files
in the current mixed worktree, both Rojo builds, diff whitespace checks, and no added Selene diagnostics against
10 errors/322 warnings. No commits or publishing occurred. Real two-client latency, physical input and device CPU/
GPU profiling remain separate evidence; this pass establishes the concrete work reductions above, not an absolute
claim of maximum runtime performance.

## Last Wave: loading, reward and map reliability (2026-11-05)

A three-player Studio test reported a repeated ability offer whose timer granted nothing, then a client with no
minimap icons or altar highlights. Treat these as possible live-game failures, not an avatar-cloning quirk. The
reward timeout defect and map failure paths were reproduced with source-based runtime stand-ins; the exact cause
of the reported Studio runs was not captured in their logs. The separate opening ability picker passed a
three-player offline check before the changes. If the report referred to that opening choice, its exact failure
remains unconfirmed.

### Reward expiry must grant an actual offered reward

- In `Survivors/Server/Services/RewardsService`, the old `autoPickAugment` considered only augment IDs, even when the
  hand contained abilities. An ability-only hand could acknowledge selection and close without granting anything.
  A mixed hand always auto-picked an augment. An unfilled ability slot could therefore appear in later offers.
- Timeout selection now draws from the combined offered ability and augment IDs. Ability binding, the character's
  ability-to-weapon mapping, tier advancement and broadcasts go through the same `tryApplyAbilityPick` /
  `applyAbilityPick` path used for a manual choice. Initial ability expiry reuses this path too.
- **Never equate dismissing the hand with granting its reward.** Confirm the binding/tier change before recording
  selection. Validate manual choices against the offered IDs before calling the shared binding helper. Tier zero
  is a valid first-slot choice; only a missing tier is absent. Preserve the initial-picker-before-Head-Start order
  in `GameplayService.StartGame` so queued level-ups cannot take over its moment state.

### Opening choices must release each player independently

A follow-up three-client report used one active player and two AFK opening pickers: choose the first ability,
grant test souls and rapidly activate two altars. The old opening-choice routine waited for the whole party before
clearing any player's server moment. The active player's UI had already closed, but their altar rewards queued
behind that opening moment. Its final cleanup then cleared the moment without draining the queued rewards, so
they could remain stuck even after the AFK players timed out. This defect can affect ordinary multiplayer runs;
it does not depend on Studio clients sharing an avatar.

- `AltarServer.Interact` queues an augment/ability reward on **every completed altar activation**. There is no
  minimum elapsed-run-time or activation-speed gate in that reward path. Soul funding and the shared maximum
  activation count still apply. Every second activation also spawns elites; this does not replace its reward.
- `OpenInitialAbilitySelection` now tracks only unresolved opening pickers. Once a player chooses or times out,
  remove them from that local set and call `finishMomentForPlayer`, which clears their opening state and drains
  their own queue. The function can still wait for other opening pickers before `StartGame` grants Head Start.
- **Never bulk-clear shared reward tables when the last opening picker finishes.** An earlier picker can already
  own a later altar hand. Teardown must affect that player's opening choice once, without touching their next
  hand's offered IDs, tier or selection state. Track opening completion separately from `PlayersPickedReward`,
  because normal moment completion resets that flag for the next reward.
- Active quests deliberately defer new moments through `questBlocked`; unblocking drains retained rewards.
  Downed players also retain queued rewards until revived, and finished players leave the reward flow. Keep these
  rules distinct from an accidental wait on AFK teammates. Multiple altar rewards must remain in FIFO order.

The follow-up ran **15 offline lifecycle assertions**, using the production opening routine, queue/drain/finish
functions, manual pick handler and ability binding helpers with mocked ECS/transport and a simplified normal-hand
opener.
The old source failed the first fast-picker assertion. The fixed source covered two rushed altars, rewards queued
before opening cleanup, later ability selection across the other players' timeout, AFK auto-selection, quest
deferral, departure, run end, solo and no-option players. This does not establish a Studio multiplayer playtest;
the connected Studio session had no live playtest server when checked.
The follow-up passed full-tree StyLua, changed-file Selene, Luau compilation, the Game Rojo build and diff whitespace
checks. Full-tree Selene remained at its captured 10 errors/322 warnings, with no added diagnostics.

### Discovery and prop readiness cannot depend on image availability

- The old `IconsCore` swallowed image-fetch errors; `MinimapUI.AddPropMarker` returned immediately when the icon was
  absent. This discarded the marker's cell/discovery bookkeeping as well as its pixels. The discovery callback
  that enables an altar's highlight could never run. An absent log was not evidence that registration succeeded.
- **Register the marker and its discovery callback even with no image.** `MapDot.icon` is optional. Prop/drop pixel
  drawing tolerates nil icons, while cell membership and discovery continue normally. A later icon paints the
  existing dot; a failed image must not prevent an altar highlight, arrow or discovery state from progressing.
- `IconsCore.CacheRegularIcon` coalesces requests for the same ID, retries failures, bounds each attempt and warns
  when attempts are exhausted. Successful images remain cached; a failed ID can be requested later. Activated
  marker images use this same loader rather than a separate unbounded fetch.
- A delayed icon completion must match **both the current dot object and its current image ID**. Removal, a new run
  or activation can invalidate it. Never resurrect a removed marker, write into a replacement dot, or overwrite an
  activated altar/chest icon with an older initial-image request. Destroy late editable images rejected by a load
  deadline so their memory does not remain allocated.
- `GeneratorController.tryAddProp` waits for the existing replicated prop ID **and** `PrimaryPart`, in either arrival
  order. Its waiting/deduplication entry is not proof of completed registration. Readiness listeners disconnect on
  registration or removal, already queued callbacks cannot register twice, and a removed pending model can be
  re-added. Keep this metadata scoped to the existing prop integration; do not invent another Attributes protocol.
- Restart invalidates deferred prop registrations as well as completed handles. `GeneratorController` advances its
  prop generation on `OnGameRestarting`; a queued callback or a listener waiting for attributes from the old map
  must never restore a handle after `PropsController.Reset`. Check both ID/PrimaryPart arrival orders, removal,
  pending work across restart and exactly-once registration on the new map.
- Server prop preparation has the same generation boundary. `PropsService.Reset` cancels old player-data waits
  and yielding init hooks; footprint indexes and template bounds belong to one map. `RestartService` waits for
  `PropsService.WaitForMap` before resetting characters and starting gameplay. Restart chest counts use the
  currently connected players. An offline harness ran the production restart/prop functions through ten restarts,
  with one to five players, and checked counts, overlap, ECS cleanup and interrupted generation. This is not a
  Studio multiplayer or replication-order playtest.
- `MinimapController.RemovePropMarker` also removes queued marker/discovery work before the UI exists. The UI
  constructor already generates its images: do not immediately call `Generate` again from the controller and
  allocate another set of editable images.

### Cosmetic loading has a budget; essential readiness has a failure path

**`pcall` catches a returned error; it does not impose a deadline on a yielding request.** A retry count also does
not help when the first request never returns. Apply a wall-clock deadline to each yielding operation, and decide
explicitly what happens after it expires.

The two loading screens now use [preloadAssets](src/Global/Shared/Utils/preloadAssets.luau), which retains completion
as state rather than relying on a one-shot signal. The old screens started workers before calling
`OnCompleted:Wait()`: immediate completion or an immediate error could fire the signal before a waiter existed and
leave the screen stuck after all batches had been counted. Check empty, immediate, failed and slow requests; never
assume that an async API must yield before returning.

The shared preloader runs at most eight workers with batches of fifty instances. It counts returned requests even
when they fail, reports failed requests, and stops scheduling more work on timeout or the lobby's skip. Requests
already in the engine may finish in the background. The lobby preserves its existing skip and warning flow; the run
loading screen moves optional minimap icon caching into the background so it cannot hold up spawning.

[awaitWithTimeout](src/Global/Shared/Utils/awaitWithTimeout.luau) bounds operations such as editable-image requests,
font-metric warmup and avatar loading. It preserves nil/multiple results and returned errors. A timed-out operation
can still complete later: ignore that result for readiness, and use its late-result cleanup for owned resources.
The helper is a deadline on waiting, not a guarantee that Roblox canceled the underlying request.

[loadingTimeouts](src/Global/Shared/Utils/loadingTimeouts.luau) is the source of the shared deadlines. Snapshot at
this change; read the source before tuning or quoting these values:

| Stage | Deadline / interval | Outcome on failure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cosmetic texture preload | 15 seconds overall | Continue loading without blocking on optional assets |
| Editable image / optional terrain atlas | 5 seconds per attempt | Retry/cache warning or continue without the optional atlas |
| Font metrics | 3 seconds per weight | Finish the warmup attempt so menu mounting and its concurrent waiters can proceed |
| Settings response | 10 seconds by default | Use defaults for now; a late response can still apply |
| Client terrain readiness | 45 seconds after entering that stage | Give the affected player a rejoin error; never report a floor ready |
| Server player join/data readiness | 120 seconds from that player's join hook | Disconnect only the peer whose own readiness is incomplete |
| Avatar API | 30 seconds | Fail that player's avatar load without blocking other avatar requests |
| Character setup after avatar load | 35 seconds | Fail that player's missing final character identity |
| Character acknowledgements | 30 seconds, retry every 3 seconds | Retry missing peers, then disconnect peers that still cannot acknowledge |
| Client party/game-start wait | Derived: join + avatar + setup + 15 seconds, currently 200 seconds | Outlast server recovery before reporting a remaining start failure |

Do not independently shorten the client's party wait below the server's recovery budget: that would disconnect a
healthy player while the server was still removing or recovering an unhealthy teammate. These are configured
budgets checked in code, not measured Roblox service response-time guarantees.

A missing texture normally does **not** make `PreloadAsync` wait for successful download forever: Roblox processes
failed assets too. A request that remains pending is a different case, and still needs the application deadline.
`SurfaceAppearance` texture packs are not supported by `PreloadAsync`; they stream at runtime. Queuing that instance
is not proof that its PBR textures are ready. See the
[ContentProvider contract](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/ContentProvider).

### Terrain and multiplayer handshakes must remain safe under failure

- `LoadingState` remembers terrain/game-start success and a failure message. Waiters check stored state and their
  deadline, so success before subscription is not lost and failure never masquerades as readiness. Loading text
  identifies the map-build and party-wait stages. An unrecoverable failure gives a rejoin message through Roblox's
  disconnect UI; it does not silently remove the overlay and drop a player into an incomplete run.
- Terrain construction retries once. Set the build mode before construction so a failed partial first build is
  cleaned on the retry. A second failure records a loading failure and retains the gravity clamp until that client
  leaves. An in-run regeneration failure also disconnects the affected client instead of leaving it without a floor.
- Report terrain ready **after a successful floor build**. A cosmetic minimap repaint error is caught separately
  and cannot prevent a usable floor from becoming ready. Conversely, a texture deadline must never force the
  terrain-ready flag. The optional atlas and settings waits have their own bounds before generation proceeds.
- Both server startup gates require every currently connected client's floor-ready signal, even when the expected
  party count has already been reached. The old early-start branch could satisfy the expected count while another
  connected client was still loading. A failed peer must leave before the remaining ready party proceeds.
- Avatar API calls run independently for each player and have a deadline. A second watchdog waits for that player's
  final character identity: an API returning successfully is not proof that all character setup hooks succeeded.
- Install the expected acknowledgement set **before broadcasting the character**. Track the actual expected peers;
  duplicate/unexpected replies cannot satisfy another player's slot. Disconnect cleanup removes that player only
  when still pending, rather than decrementing a counter again after an earlier acknowledgement.
- Retry only missing acknowledgement peers. The client re-acknowledges an already assigned ID without initializing
  that character again. A departed player stops its wait; a missing replicated character has a deadline. Server
  timeout handling identifies unresponsive peers, checks the owner still exists and owns the same character, and
  does not grant an identity to an owner that never became ready.
- The join watchdog checks each player's own load/data/teleport-fetch state. A healthy player merely waiting for
  teammates must not be treated as failed because the party has not spawned yet. Readiness and retries continue
  using the existing generated Blink traffic and the existing GameLoaded integration.

### Regression cases and evidence from this change

Before editing these paths again, retain or recreate these cases with the production functions:

1. Ability-only, augment-only and mixed reward expiry; tier zero; invalid choices; consecutive ability slots; three
   initial pickers, including one fast picker and two AFK peers. Activate two altars before the peers finish;
   assert independent FIFO delivery and preservation of the fast player's later hand when the peers time out.
   Assert the granted binding/tier, not merely a closed modal or a selected message.
2. Missing, failed, nil, delayed and permanently unavailable icons; discovery before image completion; activated
   image overtaking an initial request; removal/restart while an image is pending; shared fetches and late cleanup.
3. Prop ID before primary part and primary part before ID; duplicate readiness callbacks; removal before readiness
   and subsequent re-add; marker removal while UI creation is still pending.
4. Empty, immediately successful, immediately errored, failed-status and stalled preload batches; early skip; no
   new batches after the budget expires; font warmup with multiple waiters; settings that arrive after fallback.
5. Terrain success, partial first-build failure, both attempts failing, cosmetic minimap failure and regeneration
   failure. Assert that a failed floor never fires GameLoaded and that the gravity clamp follows the real floor.
6. Immediate, duplicate, unexpected, retried and missing character acknowledgements; peer/owner departure; one
   avatar API stalling; setup hooks failing after API success; stalled data/teleport fetches; a healthy teammate
   waiting through another player's recovery. Check the client/server deadline inequalities too.

The reward/map pass ran **23 offline regression checks**. The loading pass ran **52 offline regression checks**,
including the later font/concurrent-menu-waiter case. All thirteen files touched by the loading pass compiled and
passed targeted StyLua; both Game and Lobby Rojo builds and diff whitespace checks passed. Full-tree Selene gained
no diagnostics against its captured **10-error/322-warning** baseline. At the loading pass's formatting check, a
concurrently edited `SpectatorUI` file prevented claiming a clean full-tree StyLua result; those unrelated changes
were not reformatted by this work.

The source-extracted probes were temporary files under `/tmp/ballarc-multiplayer-fix` and `/tmp/ballarc-loading-fix`,
not a committed regression suite or CI checks. They may disappear; the cases above are the durable recipe. No
commits or publication were made in these fixes.

**No Studio multiplayer playtest or visual/device approval was established by these fixes.** Follow up in Studio
with three clients, including delayed/failed assets and one missing readiness reply; confirm the healthy party can
start, the affected client receives the intended rejoin message, reward expiry grants the selected slot, and altar
highlights/discovery work while an icon is unavailable. Repeat disconnect and restart cases. Offline mocks,
compilation and Rojo builds do not establish live replication timing, renderer behavior or physical input handling.

## Spectator UI and replication contract for Last Wave

Consolidated 2026-11-05 from the user's spectator reviews. Read this contract first; the dated rounds preserve
implementation history and evidence. This contract takes precedence over their rejected layouts and older validation
status. Verify the current code before assuming that a path, tuning value or recorded check count remains current.
These decisions are settled requirements, not choices to reopen every session.

### What the user means by spectating

The default Player view follows what the watched player sees and decides: camera position/rotation/zoom/FOV, vitals,
abilities/charges/cooldowns, XP/level, counters, buffs, revive state, quests/notices, inventory/inspection, interactions,
chests, rewards and level-up hands, hover, banish/reroll/skip state, confirmations, map state, clock and visual overlays.
Preserve responsive layout and the viewer's accessibility preferences. This is read-only presentation driven through
the same drawings, not a video stream and not permission to operate another player's actions.

Show the watched player's actual preview data. Their formatted stats, owned/new state, favorites, synergy/conflict
icons and before/after gains cannot be reconstructed reliably from the viewer's incomplete remote-character ECS or
own favorites. Serialize display data from the source; do not send executable functions, Instances, rewards, save
mutations or client-decided gameplay outcomes. Source GetCard callbacks become inert card data on the viewer.

### Reuse the whole layout contract

Using the same card/clock drawing is insufficient if a new wrapper changes its parent, inset policy, anchor, scale,
column layout, clipping or ScreenGui layer. Trace the live wrapper and compare the complete container hierarchy.
Extract a shared container when both owners need the same one; do not copy its properties into a second wrapper.
Reuse an existing live HUD instance when its public data is already available locally.

| Surface | Required behavior / current owner |
| --- | --- |
| Clock | `Components/runHud.Clock` is shared by TimerUI and the receiver; keep the live drawing's position, inset policy and Timer layer 14. Never move it to make room for spectator controls. |
| Kills, souls and streak | `SelfStatsUI` follows the minimap's left edge. Measure the position after mounting the counter ScreenGui; preserve the shared inset policy and the expanded-map freeze. See the mounting rule below. |
| Quests and announcements | `runHud.Quests` shares the live column at `(0.5, 0.07)`, active/pinned stacks, spacing and insets. Normal layer 4 stays below Choices 9. Mirror layer 10 only while the source actually holds a finished quest result there. Keep the existing quest lock warning drawing. |
| Players and spectator controls | Keep the existing left `PlayersInfoUI` cards and public vitals, not another streamed teammate list. Make each eligible portrait individually selectable. Put Up/Down cycling and Results with that column, mounted by `PlayersInfoUI` itself (`spectateBar`); the watched player's own side tag (`activityTag`) morphs into the LIVE plate with their name (2026-11-05: the tag that travelled between cards is gone). There is no orbit/player view toggle (removed 2026-11-05): the mirrored camera is the point of spectating. Cards and controls use Spectator layer 16 above reward/augment hands, so decisions cannot hide the only way to switch or leave. |
| Narrow/short windows | Follow the column's actual animated height. Use the compact footer when vertical space runs out, link navigation according to its drawn rows, keep usable action height and minimum text sizes, and truncate long names instead of shrinking them into illegibility. |
| Gameplay hints and map | Hide/restore the spectator's bottom-right gameplay keybind panel; it is local-only and never transmitted. While watching, map toggles defer to the source. |

The layer numbers above are the verified current values in `RunUILayers`; read that module instead of introducing
parallel magic numbers. Keep the live clock/quest `IgnoreGuiInset`, `ScreenInsets`, clipping and scale rules. A correct
ZIndex inside a child cannot repair the wrong ScreenGui DisplayOrder or an ancestor's clipping.

### Measure cross-GUI positions after mounting (2026-11-05)

Switching spectated players rebuilt `SelfStatsUI` while the minimap already existed. Its `task.spawn` ran the initial
position calculation immediately, before the new counter ScreenGui was parented. `WaitForChild` returns immediately
for existing children, so those calls did not delay setup. The unmounted GUI origin was `(0, 0)`; after mounting it
was `(0, -58)` in the controlled Studio viewport. The cached position then put kills, souls and streak **58 pixels
above the minimap**, until another minimap movement recalculated it. A cold first mount can hide this race because
waiting for the minimap happens to yield.

Keep the coordinate conversion in `SelfStatsUI`: subtract the mounted parent's `AbsolutePosition` from the
minimap's `AbsolutePosition`, then apply the pixel gap. The fix uses `task.defer` for the initial lookup/follow,
matching the existing minimap-override path. This works because the current callers parent the returned ScreenGui
synchronously before deferred work resumes. If a future wrapper delays parenting, measure at its explicit mounted
point instead. A defer here crosses the mounting boundary; it does not promise a rendered frame or fix every stale
layout problem described elsewhere in this document. Never hard-code the observed 58-pixel offset.

This correction schedules one setup callback per HUD creation and keeps the existing minimap-position listener and
its cleanup. It adds no per-frame polling, extra listener, network message or layout implementation. Keep the short
comment explaining why setup must defer. More abstractions or repeated render-step corrections need a demonstrated
requirement; this fix was not CPU/GPU-profiled and is not evidence of maximum possible performance.

To reproduce and verify, mount the production counters while a minimap already exists, then destroy and rebuild the
real `SpectatorUI` receiver repeatedly, as target switching does. After mounting, assert matching counter/minimap top
coordinates and the intended gap at the counter's right edge; assert teardown destroys the previous counters. Keep
cold creation, viewport resizing, expanded-map parking and collapse in future regression coverage as well. Read both
GUI origins when diagnosing a displacement, rather than compensating in the drawing's local positions.

The preceding fix was reproduced in Studio before editing and then passed **24 engine assertions** across four
direct counter mounts and four real receiver rebuilds. The temporary probe removed its runtime HUDs and its
StarterPlayer template was deleted. The **582 offline spectator checks**, full-tree StyLua, changed-file Selene,
Luau compilation, Game Rojo build and scoped diff whitespace check passed; full-tree Selene added no diagnostics
against the captured **10-error/322-warning** baseline. These are that round's results, not checks rerun by this
documentation edit. Actual two-player switching, device coverage and performance profiling were not established.

### Hover, input ownership and feedback

Mouse hover, controller selection and confirmed choice are three different states. Capture mouse enter/leave even
when `GuiService.SelectedObject` is nil; tracking only controller focus does not satisfy the hover requirement.
Touch must not leave a persistent mouse hover. Send control identity/path and layout order so swapped cards do not
rely solely on insertion order. Frame the source's hovered action itself; hovering Reroll must not also light a reward
card with the same LayoutOrder.

Use a separate instance of the shared focus brackets for watched hover. It follows the actual visible `FocusFrame`
face, movement, current shape and scrolling clip. Drive the existing reward/upgrade hover state as well. The viewer's
own shared selector stays on the spectator controls. Clear watched hover when the target hides, disappears or changes;
move/repair the viewer's focus before disabling or destroying a selected player control.

Copies must skip input bindings and gameplay callbacks. Disabling native interaction alone does not stop every hover
callback, and an Appear/count/enabled update can make a control selectable again. Keep explicit read-only drawing
paths and reassert inert native buttons/scrolling after updates. Transparent/hidden/leaving controls must release
input. Preserve the user's manual mouse/camera ownership: inventory/stat visibility must not silently change it;
Left Alt remains the explicit mouse toggle. Results/Back and target/run lifecycle changes must tear down immediately.

Make meaningful events satisfying with the existing pixel Slab vocabulary. Target changes use the player color,
centered thump, brief flash, ring and bounded sparks; the current card uses five sparks and an impulse smaller than
revival. Buttons retain hover/lift, press/sink, corners, flash and existing UI sounds. Do not restart those effects for
every vitals update or make ordinary hiding sound like success. Pool recurring effects, let hidden/settled effects
sleep, and anchor UIScale effects around the visible center. Derive switch motion from a fixed layout baseline;
adding an offset to the previous frame's position causes drift. Preserve existing audio choices; consult Sounds.md
before selecting/replacing voices. Actual feel and visual taste require review, not a compiler pass.

### Network and state ownership

All additional server/client communication uses Blink. Never use server Attributes or CollectionService tags as an
unserialized side channel. Prefer ordinary Lua tables for client bookkeeping too. Read-only roots are registered in
`cornerSelector`'s local map, and portrait identity stays in Lua tables. Existing client kit integrations such as
`FocusFrame`/`FocusCut` remain where required; they are not an excuse for new metadata-driven protocols. ECS tags are
ordinary ECS state, separate from Roblox instance tags.

The server owns eligibility and per-target viewer sets. Clients send presentation only while requested; the server
checks source generation, membership, size/rate bounds and camera validity. Send only to that source's subscribers.
The first subscriber enables capture; the last disables/unbinds it. Zero subscribers means no additional spectator
camera capture, JSON encoding or uploads. Local current-UI bookkeeping may remain for a future join; normal game/AOI
replication still exists and must not be described as zero network traffic.

New viewers receive targeted current snapshots; existing viewers receive changes. Encode shared snapshot chunks
once for simultaneous recipients. Read the current format/rates/limits from `spectatorCodec` and the Blink schemas:
currently camera 20 Hz with 128-byte samples, HUD flushes 10 Hz, and at most 128 calls / 48 KiB per presentation batch.
Preserve the server byte/packet budgets and generated receive guard. A bounded schema buffer can still be rejected
by an older, smaller outer transport guard: the original Meta 4 KiB guard dropped valid reward snapshots. When a
schema changes, regenerate both Blink networks and verify actual generated transport in both directions. Keep cold
spectator events on Meta and respect Blink's per-network 256-event limit.

### Keep history bounded; cache work without freezing presentation

- Retain current state for snapshots, not the entire command history. Remove commands needed by existing viewers
  survive only until sending; late viewers need no removal for an entry they never had. Discard pending removals and
  expired feedback when capture stops. Removing/clearing state also clears its dirty keys. Ordinary flushes iterate
  dirty entries; reserve full retained-state scans for snapshots.
- Bound both ends. The source once snapshotted 250 removal commands for an empty collection. The receiver could also
  retain every removed ability-id mapping and event revision key. Remove per-entry mappings/revisions, use bounded
  revision watermarks for transient events, and reject stale replay. Test long-lived churn, not just a clean first hand.
- Repeated clears are state transitions even when their arguments are identical: Add, Clear, Add, Clear must deliver
  both clears. Preserve remove/re-add-in-one-flush semantics and the revision ordering of snapshots versus deltas.
  The typed Remove/Clear/Event envelope fields are serialized protocol data, not Roblox instance metadata.
- Decode a received HUD buffer once, then pass the decoded calls to presentation. Do not decode in both controller
  and receiver. Do not serialize unchanged hover merely to compare the resulting JSON strings. Read preferences once
  per camera sample, not inside each of its twelve component reads. Avoid intermediate per-call buffers when batching.
- Cache the focused control's identity, path, layer, focus-face reference and scrolling ancestor. Invalidate on relevant
  tree, name/order, reparenting, replacement and teardown events. A reroll must find the new card without requiring the
  source to move its mouse again. Disconnect cache listeners and release references when replacing/destroying scopes.
- Keep visibility, the current face, geometry and clipping live every rendered frame. Caching geometry indefinitely
  would make moving corners wrong. An unrelated tree mutation with the same resulting source path should not trigger
  another identical network payload. Keep normal packets and animation metadata out of the history/cache dictionaries.
- Use explicit protocol/binding/view/record types and shared tuning constants. Keep genuinely heterogeneous drawing
  arguments at a clear dynamic boundary. Group related camera sample state instead of many unrelated-looking globals.
  Do not trade clear ownership for speculative micro-optimizations or promise maximum performance without profiling.

### Snapshot state, terminal feedback and reused screens (2026-11-05)

A player revived less than a second before another player started spectating them. `SelfReviveUI` retained
`SetVisible(true)`, but `Complete()` was an `Event`: it was discarded without subscribers and excluded from late
snapshots even with subscribers. The receiver replayed the old show and kept "Tap Rapidly to Revive" on an alive
player. Waiting for feedback expiry or increasing its lifetime cannot correct that cached state.

**Classify a method by the state it leaves behind, not its name or its animation.** `SelfReviveUI.Complete` ends
the downed state, so it shares the retained `Visibility` key with `SetVisible`. Existing viewers run the completion
animation; a fresh hidden `reviveCard` receives only `Complete`, whose existing hidden-card guard makes it a no-op.
The old show cannot return in a snapshot. `Tap`, cursor hits, ability shines and Color Dance's short `Safe` hold
are transient feedback. `propPrompt.Complete` is also feedback: it leaves the prompt shown until its owner hides
or suppresses it. Do not change every method named Complete to a visibility setter.

**A new cycle invalidates every cached setter that its drawing resets.** `write` suppresses unchanged arguments;
that is correct only while the relevant state survives. A pooled quest can finish twice with the same arguments,
but a new `Show` resets it to running. Without invalidation, the second finish is silently suppressed. Read the
actual implementation of Show/Appear/Clear and its callers, including setters made before the opening call.
Use the binding's existing `ClearKeys` to forget those retained calls and their dirty keys at the reset boundary.
This removes old snapshot state and lets an identical later setter produce a new revision.

The audited reset boundaries are:

| Owner | Binding rule and why |
| --- | --- |
| `QuestActiveUI.Show` | Clear `SetRemaining`, `Finish` and `SetOut`: pooled cards start a new quest with a fresh duration and outcome. |
| `RewardUI.ClearOptions` / `UpgradeUI.ClearOptions` | Clear `SetBanishActive`; collection clearing already forgets confirmed selection and per-option state. |
| `RewardUI.Appear` | Clear confirmed selection, button visibility, action visibility and banish mode: Appear resets them itself. |
| `UpgradeUI.Appear` | Clear confirmed selection, button visibility and banish mode. Preserve `SetActionsVisible`, which the controller sets before Appear and which this drawing does not reset. |
| `ColorDanceUI.SetRound` | Clear the previous `SetCheck` and `Clear` result. Keep `SetOnColor`, which survives the round change. `SetRound` and `Hide` share visibility; `Safe` is an event so every passed round produces feedback without replaying it to late viewers. |
| `ColorDanceUI.Clear` | Retain the final result as ordinary state. It is not a collection clear; `{ Clear = true }` has collection-removal semantics, regardless of the method's name. |
| Inspection `Show` in `Components/infoScreen` | Clear `Refresh` and `SetPosition`: Show supplies the new card data and coordinates. Unit size survives. |

**Related values that seed or clamp one another need a complete state call.** Keeping the latest call per method
and sorting by revision does not preserve every dependency. For example: max 100, current 50, then max 200.
The source correctly holds 50/200. A fresh receiver replaying the retained current before the retained maximum
lets the bar's first-max seeding overwrite it with 200/200. A current value above the default maximum can also
be clamped before the correct maximum arrives. Do not fix this by turning off deduplication, replaying history,
adding a per-frame correction, or guessing the source values from the viewer's ECS.

`vitalBar.GetValues()` reads the drawing's actual maximum, current value and overshield, including its seeding and
clamping. Health and shield bindings use `Prepare` after the original live setter, `Group = "Vitals"`, and
`Method = "SetVitals"` to record that complete state. `Method` changes only the recorded replay method; the source
still calls the original setter once. The mirror seeds maximum before current, includes overshield for shield,
and skips an unchanged maximum so current-only updates do not restart its maximum-change animation. Its first
current/overshield application is instant, so joining does not invent a damage or gain celebration. Health sends
two values; shield sends three. Each retains one Vitals call and ordinary identical states still coalesce.

Prefer these explicit binding rules over a new service, delayed hide, longer event lifetime, periodic resend or
unbounded command history. There is no additional timer, render callback, server request or polling loop for these
fixes. ClearKeys walks a fixed list only when its owning method runs; vitals reuse the existing captured argument
table. This describes the code's bounded work, not measured maximum CPU/GPU performance.

For future changes, exercise both an existing viewer and a fresh snapshot with zero subscribers beforehand. Cover
join immediately after completion, join after event expiry, join during a real down/hold, target switching,
Show/Finish/Hide/Show/Finish with identical arguments, repeated reward control changes, and maximum/current updates
in different orders. Verify reset setters made before opening as well as those made afterward. Retained outcomes
must survive while current; transient celebrations must repeat live and must not replay in a late snapshot.

`tools/spectator/check.luau` loads the real revive/vitals wrappers and production capture/codec, and evaluates the
other owners' actual binding declarations against stateful drawing stand-ins. It checks cache invalidation and
transport semantics; those stand-ins do not prove the renderer or physical input. Keep this distinction when
reporting results, and compile large edited modules for Luau's local-register limit.

This audit passed **619 offline assertions**, full-tree StyLua, changed-source Selene, compilation of all nine
edited runtime modules and the harness, both Rojo builds, and scoped diff whitespace checks. Full-tree Selene
added no diagnostics against the freshly captured **10-error/322-warning** baseline. The new regression cases
were also run against the pre-audit sources and reproduced the repeated quest/reward changes, stale Color Dance
feedback/deadline, stale inspection state, and health/shield snapshot-order failures. These counts describe this
round; future edits must rerun the checks rather than copy them as an acceptance threshold.

After verifying the nine edited modules matched Studio, a controlled client probe passed **13 engine assertions**
with the real health/shield wrappers, bar drawing, capture and codec. It checked maximum-before-current snapshots,
overshield, subsequent current updates, real `43/237` then `35/237` readouts, and GetValues after a maximum decrease
clamped current. The probe's HUDs were released and its StarterPlayer template was deleted. This is not proof of
two-client timing, the other screens' renderer/input behavior, physical controllers or performance profiling.

Two probe setup pitfalls are part of that evidence: the bridge's start acknowledgement can precede the client
copying StarterPlayerScripts, so use a client-start marker before deleting the template as soon as the test is
actually running. Wait for the controlled test to stop before starting another; a stop acknowledgement can also
precede teardown. A probe that disables its ScreenGui can leave its readout at the default `Label` because layout
has not run. For an invisible geometry/readout check, keep the test GUI enabled and park its drawing offscreen;
do not change the live HUD to satisfy the probe. The corrected offscreen probe produced the 13 passing assertions.

### Camera and clock integration rules

Use explicit render priorities, not unordered PreRender callbacks, for camera writers/sampling: live shoulder/shake
at Camera + 1, watched playback at Camera + 2, and watched-source capture at Camera + 3. Capture the final source pose,
pre-shake pose, FOV, focus and character origin. Blend source-relative offsets while following the viewer's rendered
target between packets, so character replication timing does not add movement twice or make follow motion wait for
20 Hz camera samples. Keep absolute behavior for an unanchored/scriptable source. Local shoulder offsets, shakes and
FOV tweens must not fight watched playback. Respect the viewer's screen-shake preference. Preserve actual source focus;
do not invent a point twenty studs ahead. Sequences reject reordered camera samples; source generations reject stale
uploads; teardown restores camera, map and local HUD state.

The win-chest reveal must not independently zero TimeCore when someone cashes out while others keep playing. The
final party run-end path owns that freeze. Test live, slow, ended and manual-pause clocks plus repeat reveals/Continue.
For the timer drawing, overtime bonus state and run/pick readout are separate retained values. Reset must remove the
old bonus, while a current bonus keeps receiving the drawing's animation updates between network changes; otherwise
coalescing can lose the multiplier or leave its unfold pending forever.

### Start from these source owners

Paths below are relative to `src/Survivors/` unless stated otherwise.

| Responsibility | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Subscription eligibility, forwarding, budgets, stop lifecycle | `Server/Services/SpectatorService.luau`; `blink/Client/Spectator.blink`, `blink/Server/Spectator.blink` |
| Capture enable/disable, packet decode, camera playback, viewer lifetime | `Client/Controllers/SpectatorController.luau` |
| Current UI state, dirty entries, pending commands, source hover | `Client/Utils/spectatorCapture.luau` |
| Read-only factories/adapters, watched hover, scope cleanup | `Client/UI/SpectatorUI.luau`; `Client/Utils/spectatorFocus.luau` |
| Protocol types, codec, camera format and shared limits | `Shared/Utils/spectatorCodec.luau` |
| Live containers and layer ordering | `Client/UI/Components/runHud.luau`; `Client/UI/RunUILayers.luau`; `Client/UI/TimerUI.luau`; `Client/Controllers/QuestsController.luau` |
| Real teammate cards, eligibility/selection, spectator buttons and final-screen routing | `Client/UI/PlayersInfoUI.luau`; `Client/Controllers/PlayersInfoController.luau`; `Client/UI/Components/teammateCard.luau`; `Client/UI/Components/activityTag.luau`; `Client/UI/Components/spectateBar.luau`; `Client/Controllers/FinalStatsController.luau` |
| Source-derived previews and card hover | `Client/UI/RewardUI.luau`; `Client/UI/UpgradeUI/`; their reward/upgrade card drawings |
| Shared selector and read-only registry | `src/Global/Client/UI/Components/cornerSelector.luau` |
| Game-time freeze ownership | `Client/Controllers/WinBoxController.luau`; `Client/Controllers/FinalStatsController.luau`; `Shared/Core/TimeCore.luau` |
| Bench and durable offline checks | `Client/UI/Stories/Spectator.story.luau`; `tools/spectator/check.luau` |

The `blink/`, `tools/` and explicit `src/Global/` entries are repository-relative. Shared helpers belong to what they
are, and a page/view-specific element belongs to its owning view. Keep dependencies one-way; no new peer service or
controller merely to split a large file. Avoid duplicating controllers through StarterPlayer and PlayerScripts paths;
the existing recorder/selector singleton redirection is deliberate.

### Before reporting completion in a future session

1. Read this contract, AGENTS.md and the current owners. Record the live worktree and lint baseline. Preserve unrelated
   work, current UI decisions and active Studio/Rojo sessions; use explicit paths for edits/staging. Do not commit or
   publish without the user's authorization.
2. Audit the integration, not just the new drawing: shared containers, all input routes, live versus read-only ownership,
   packet format/outer guards, source and receiver retention, lifecycle cleanup and late viewers. Correct known
   redundant work and readability problems before calling the feature optimized; do not wait for another review to
   inspect the corresponding receiver or long-session state.
3. Keep the story on the real components and the state under review. Cover rewards open with the left controls visible,
   long names, all eligible players, five viewport shapes, moving/clipped corners and the compact footer. Simple aligned
   fixtures or first-open-only tests miss wrapper resets, hidden focus, final short rows and reroll replacement.
4. Run meaningful checks: `lune run tools/spectator/check.luau`, `stylua --check src`, harness formatting, Selene against
   the fresh baseline, compilation of changed large Luau files for register limits, `git diff --check`, and both Rojo
   builds for shared changes. Regenerate Blink when schemas change. Historical assertion/diagnostic counts are evidence
   snapshots, not acceptance thresholds to copy into a new reply.
5. Verify that Studio has the edited modules before testing. Disclose a temporary probe before it can appear on the
   user's screen, delete its StarterPlayer template as soon as the test starts, clean its runtime HUD and stop only the
   controlled test. Preserve an existing user playtest. A controlled UI probe does not prove two-client camera timing.
6. Exercise the actual failure cases: first/second viewer, targeted late snapshots mid-hand or mid-hold, final viewer
   exit, direct portrait selection and cycling, View/Results/Back over rewards, card/action mouse hover, pad/touch/input
   switching, banish/reroll/skip/confirm, hidden/replaced controls, inventory scroll, map state, zoom/rotation/movement,
   both shake settings, target finish/disconnect, restart, and repeated add/remove/clear churn with reused ids.
7. Report source checks, offline operation counts, Studio engine assertions, visual/listening review, physical input,
   real multi-client latency/bandwidth and device CPU/GPU profiling separately. Do not equate lint/build success,
   assignment counts or a synthetic GUI test with rendered correctness, FPS gains or "the most optimized possible."
   Finish authorized implementation and available checks, state the remaining evidence precisely, and leave concrete
   manual cases when hardware/multi-client testing is unavailable.

The dated retention/protocol round above recorded 582 offline assertions, 22 controlled
Studio UI assertions, both builds and no added diagnostics against that run's baseline. Real two-client camera timing,
physical controller/phone behavior, taste approval and device profiling remained unverified. No current test was rerun
merely to consolidate this document. The counter-mounting round has separate evidence in its section above. Future
sessions must verify their own source and evidence instead of repeating these numbers as fresh results.

## Last Wave: the daily rewards (`dailyScreen`, built 2026-11-05, linted, not playtested)

Asked for: the Daily Rewards modal in the pixel style, "the most satisfying and juicier it can be". Built on the gift
picker's modal shape (Slab over a dim, PanelCatcher, leave turns input off at once) and the Quests claim recipe. The old
layout and colour meanings are kept: title and subtitle on top, days 1 to 6 three across in two rows with day 7 a tall
tile on the right, green for today (day 7's rainbow), grey with a green tick for claimed, grey with its rewards under a veil for locked, the
streak bonus as a green badge on the corner, box throws as chips in their box's colour, the shield bottom left, BACK
(red) bottom centre, the reset clock bottom right.

| Piece | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Drawing | `Lobby/.../MenuUI/Components/dailyScreen` (`new`, `Locked` / `Today` / `Claimed`). Takes `TDay`s (state, tickets, stardust, bonus %, chips), `SetShield`, `SetClock`, `Claimed(day, tickets)`, `Refused()`, `PressToday()` |
| Wrapper | `MenuUI/DailyRewardsUI` (same `UI` / `Visible` API). Reads ProgressionController, builds the chips (shop's box palettes), sends the claim, the toast, the 1 s clock and the midnight rollover, the pad (PushFocus on today, PushBack, PushCycle) |
| LobbyUI | Passes `Tickets = wallet.Counter`; the wallet now stays shown while Daily Rewards is open and is raised to ZIndex 101, over the modal's dim (100), so the claim has somewhere to land |
| Bench | `Lobby/Client/UI/Stories/DailyRewards` (claimed day, can claim, streak cycles, server delay, time scale; Do: reopen, claim today, claim refused, midnight, day 7 next) |

**Moments** (all from state or the server's answer, never from the click):

| Moment | What plays |
| --- | --- |
| Open | Dim, panel rises 4 units from 94.5% with a flash and a sheen, the heading gift pops then bobs; the seven tiles deal in 0.045 s apart on the one deal spring; today pings (flash, +4%, ring) once it has landed |
| Idle | Today: white outline, three-ring stepped glow, a sheen every 2.6 s; day 7 cycles the rainbow on its bezel. One `task.delay` chain at 0.2 s, only while a day is claimable |
| Hover / pad | Tile lifts a unit, brackets on it (mouse via `cornerSelector.Marker`, pad via `SelectionImageObject`), the pad's A glyph on today's tile only |
| Press today | Sinks, pulls in 4% and the light crosses (the motion vocabulary's "raise" charge); the wallet is held |
| Server confirms | Flash, +9% thump (+13% and a 0.05 s hit-stop on day 7), rings, ChestJump; the tickets break into glints that fly into the wallet (`ticketsFlight`, its own banked chime); the rewards wink out in a puff; 16 sparks (26 on day 7) rise inside the emptied well; day 7 opens its gift on a flaring, spinning sunburst for 0.42 s first. Then the tick stamps down from 2.4x (lands in 0.09 s, squashes to 84%), the tile shakes a unit, turns grey, ring, ObjectPick; 0.3 s later tomorrow's tile winks |
| Refused | Charge lets go, a one-unit shake, BuyRefuse at half; the wallet is released at once |
| Locked tile pressed | One-unit shake, BuyRefuse at half. Claimed: nothing |
| Midnight while open | The new day pings (flash, +4%, green ring) |
| Streak bonus / shields change | Badges pop; the shield Slab pops with a ring on a gain, knocks on a loss |

**Choices worth keeping:**

- **The refresh waits a frame.** ProgressionController fires `OnDailyRewardsChanged` before `OnDailyRewardsClaimResult`,
  so a refresh on the change would snap the day to claimed before the claim could play. The wrapper defers one queued
  refresh; the result plays first, then the refresh finds the day already claimed (the shop's Hold / Release rule).
- **One sheen and one particle pool for the seven tiles**, lent to today's tile (`adopt`): only it sheens, charges and
  strikes. Seven of each was ~800 Frames, nearly all never drawn.
- **Day 7's sunburst keeps one colour per state.** `pixelBurst.SetColor` repaints every texel, and the rainbow moves 5
  times a second; only the bezel and glow cycle.
- **Sparks stay in the struck tile's emptied well** (UI.md "Particles: the checklist"): the rewards go under the strike's
  flash, so the sparks cross one background. Worst case worked out in `lune`: they climb 16 units, under day 7's gift and
  inside a small tile's 49-unit well.
- **The panel's sheen row grows with the panel** (`ceil(wellH / (112 p))` units, the shop card's rule): the panel is 180
  rows tall at 1080p.

Sizes (units, `lune`): panel 320 x 186 (unit 4 at 1080p, 67% x 69% of a 16:9 screen, 89% wide on 4:3), small tiles 63 x
55 (as tall as the most chips any of days 1 to 6 shows), day 7 98 x 115 with a 42-unit gift. Unit 3 at 1280 x 1080 and

## Last Wave: UI lifetime and cleanup (2026-11-05)

Applies to runtime UI, spectator copies and UI Labs stories. The earlier note "Vide's root frees STATE, not
INSTANCES" applies in gameplay too: `Vide.mount` / `Vide.root` teardown releases the reactive scope and its
registered cleanups; it does not automatically destroy Instances created with `Vide.create`.

### The failure and its owners

A player without Greatshield saw two dome health bars left behind after the Greatshield owner had finished and
was spectating. Both `GreatshieldDomeBillboard` instances were still enabled in that player's `PlayerGui`, with
`Adornee = nil`. The dome cleanup released its Vide scope and destroyed its anchor, but left the billboard alive.
The misplaced bars were leftover UI; moving the anchor or changing its height would not fix their lifetime.
Dome visuals are shown to all clients, so cleanup must work for teammates as well as the weapon owner.

| Owner | Lifetime and required cleanup |
| --- | --- |
| `Survivors/Client/UI/Components/worldBar.luau` | Registers destruction of its BillboardGui, or its root Frame when used without a billboard. This covers both Greatshield dome and convoy bars. The caller waits for `Leave` to finish, unmounts, then destroys the world anchor. |
| `Survivors/Client/UI/AnnouncementsUI.luau`, `MountPinned` | Owns the returned panel, including Color Dance's Frame. Unmount releases its scope and defers panel destruction so the animation callback that requested unmount can finish. |
| `AnnouncementsUI.Mount` / `Unmount` | Retains the scope's teardown handle. Unmount captures the old controller and handle, clears module references, releases the scope and destroys the controller's banners and both stacks. Clearing references alone leaks the root. |
| Announcement entry finalizer | Marks the entry gone, invalidates its auto-dismiss token, removes it from the registry, releases its scope and destroys its owned UI. Repeated finalization is harmless. |

Paths in the table are relative to `src/`. Keep cleanup in these existing owners; do not add a polling controller
to search for orphan UI or patch Vide globally to destroy everything it creates.

### Rules for future UI work

- **Name the owner before creating the UI.** Register root destruction with `Vide.cleanup`, or pair the returned
  scope teardown with explicit instance destruction in the owner. A mount that returns only an unmount handle must
  register cleanup for the owned UI it promises to remove. Destroy only owned roots/layers, never a borrowed parent
  or shared ScreenGui. An external owner may instead destroy the containing model or GUI, as chest reveals do.
- **Treat anchors and drawings as one lifetime.** Keep an anchor alive through the exit animation. Destroy the
  billboard before destroying its anchor. A temporary world bar left in `PlayerGui` with no `Adornee` after its
  leave is a cleanup failure, even if it is hidden or its data stopped updating. A persistent shared prompt may
  intentionally clear its target while idle. Check the outer BillboardGui's class and `Adornee`; an inner Frame
  may share its name without being a second billboard.
- **Finish callbacks safely.** If an animation callback requests its own unmount, release its scope and defer
  destruction of the panel it may still touch. Do not add arbitrary delays or frame waits. Cancel pending tasks or
  invalidate their generation tokens on teardown; stopping a reactive scope does not cancel ordinary `task.delay`.
- **Release resources and references too.** Stop active motion, disconnect external subscriptions, release each
  independently mounted root, and clear cached handles. Make public teardown safe to call again. Capture the old
  handles before clearing module state so a rebuild cannot destroy the replacement. Snapshot a registry before
  invoking teardown callbacks that remove their own entries.
- **Keep reuse deliberate.** Persistent HUDs, the shared interaction prompt and quest-card pools retain their UI
  intentionally. Hiding or returning a view to a pool preserves it; permanent removal releases its resources and
  destroys it. Dynamic list entries need their own cleanup when removed, even while the enclosing screen survives.
- **Keep the fix at lifetime boundaries.** Registration happens at mount; release happens at removal/unmount.
  These fixes add no per-frame scans or watchdogs. Clear ownership takes priority over speculative pooling or
  micro-optimizations. Do not claim maximum performance from source inspection or offline checks.

### Regression checks and evidence

For future changes, check normal completion, interruption, replacement, owner finish/disconnect and restart on
both the owner and another client. Repeat mount/remove cycles and story rebuilds; inspect retained Instances,
reactive roots and active callbacks after deferred cleanup. Cover same-turn mount/unmount, repeated teardown,
removal before an auto-dismiss timer fires, and an animation callback unmounting its own panel. Removing one panel
must preserve its siblings and any supplied parent. Verify pooled views can be reused after hiding.

Evidence from this fix: the user's affected-client dump confirmed two enabled billboards with nil anchors.
An offline Lune check using the installed Vide implementation and production announcement mount/unmount/finalizer
code, with simplified stack drawing, reproduced the pinned-panel leak before the fix. Afterward, 20 cleanup cycles,
same-turn teardown, sibling preservation, repeated teardown and cancellation of delayed auto-dismiss passed.
Changed modules compiled, `stylua --check src` passed, and Selene gained zero diagnostics against the captured
full-tree baseline. These are lifecycle/source checks. **The permanent fixes have not been playtested in Studio;
rendering, real two-client timing and CPU/GPU performance were not verified.**

## Automatic team pings (2026-11-05)

`ChestServer` and `AltarServer` call `PingService.PingAutomaticProp` only after souls were actually deposited and
the cost remains unpaid. Chest tanks remain per-player; altar funding remains shared. `QuestsService` calls
`PingAutomaticQuest` once per alive character per idle quest/challenge circle when they enter its charging radius.
This does not change the two-second, one-player activation rule. Automatic pings use the existing per-player ping
slot, six-second expiry, player colour, sound and off-screen indicator. Only the server can generate the Quest kind.
Both automatic entry points require more than one connected player; manual pings remain available in solo.

`PingService` retains automatic target identity separately from the manual cooldown. Funding completion and quest
start/removal clear callers for that target, preserving newer pings at other targets and manual replacements.
Expiry, disconnect and restart release the retained identity and timer. Standing in a circle cannot re-ping every
Heartbeat; each circle owns its set of characters already announced, including after leaving and re-entering it.
Check that set before resolving the character's player, so announced characters skip the lookup on later frames.

`PingUI` reserves camera-space clearance above the shared chest/altar prompt's anchor: half its 8-stud stage plus
one stud of air, then half the ping's current spring size. Use the animated size for both placement and sizing;
a fixed world-Y offset can overlap at different camera angles or distance tiers. Keep ordinary floor/drop pings
on their existing placement. The quest symbol is shared through `PingCore.QUEST_IMAGE`.

Offline checks exercised the actual ping service, circle-loading function and deposit branches with mocked engine
dependencies: partial/full deposits, personal/shared funding, repeated circle entry, multiple callers, manual
replacement, expiry, disconnect and restart. Changed modules compiled, full-tree StyLua passed, Selene gained no
diagnostics against the captured baseline, and the Game Rojo build passed. **Not playtested in Studio: actual
billboard spacing, mobile rendering and multiplayer timing still need in-game review.**

## Last Wave: the box chest's motion (`chestMotion`, 2026-11-05, simulated, not playtested)

Asked for: the chest's movement in the win box and the lobby shop as satisfying as it can be, before the 3D model is
swapped for an animated sprite (`Assets/ChestSprite/`). The old motion was a random jitter every frame (`SetShake`)
and an eased lift: no wind-up, no pop, nothing when the cards left, and a close that eased down. Megabonk's chest
(its `Open` and `OpenedBounce` clips) was the reference: a 0.42 s squash to 0.79, the lid and a stretch to 1.25 on
the 0.083 s frame, settled by 0.75 s, and a 0.73 -> 1.25 -> 0.92 -> 1 bounce per item thrown.

`Components/chestMotion` is the chest's whole body as numbers: `Lift`, `X`, `Roll`, `Pitch`, `Scale`, `Squash`. It
does not draw anything. `chestViewport` (the run), the lobby carousel (one per chest) and the `WinBox` bench's
stand-in all draw from it, and **the sprite should read the same channels**: Lift/X to px, Roll to `Rotation`, Scale
to size, and Squash on the height with the width divided by its square root. The 3D model cannot squash, so its Scale
is a dolly along the camera's ray through its base.

| Beat | Called by | What the chest does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enter | `WinBoxUI` on a fresh box | falls in from 2.6 studs on `inQuad` and lands with a thud |
| Charge | `winBoxScreen`'s new optional hook, `OpenAt` (0.4 -> 0.6 s) before the lid; a reroll's 0.4 s before it reopens | crouches and leans back on a `t^0.8` draw, rattling at ~11 Hz (two sines a channel on their own phases), building to the lid. Animations.md §1's dip and strain |
| Knock | `winBoxScreen`'s optional `Knock(rarity, share)`, one per tier from Common to the hand's best, 0.16 s apart, the last 0.18 s before the lid (Megabonk's buildup by tier); each tier above Common holds the lid 0.16 s longer | jumps, squashes and kicks to alternating sides harder each tier, rattles up to 1.6x, looms toward the viewer (up to +14%, Megabonk's camera push), and the pop after is up to 1.6x bigger. The screen plays ChestJump on the tier's note (`rarityLook.Note`) and leaks the tier's colour out of the shut lid; the lobby flashes the cabinet glow in it. Simulated: Common 0.6 s, 4 degrees, pop x1.13; Secret 1.7 s, 12 degrees, loom 1.16, pop x1.35 and stretched 1.49 |
| Open | `Open(secondsToDeal)` | released out of the crouch: up past its 0.8 lift to about 1.08, stretched to about 1.29, scale +13%, a 6 degree kick, then a smaller rattle building with the light until the throw |
| Deal | `Deal(count, stagger)` | recoils down and squashes as the hand leaves, then a spit per card, never closer than 0.08 s apart, so fifty cards do not buzz |
| Rest | the title's strike | a small hop |
| (open) | | hovers: a slow bob and sway, faded in |
| Close | the lid shutting | bites down and tips toward the viewer |
| Drop | `WinBoxUI` 0.8 s after Close (inside its 1.55 s dismiss hold); the lobby after its 1.1 s hold | falls on `inQuad` in 0.2 s, lands squashed with a bounce and a knock |
| Hop | the lobby carousel's newly picked chest | hops as the wheel brings it round |

- **Kicks are written as the peak they reach** and turned into a launch speed from the spring's own response, so a
  number in `Tune` is what is seen. Simulated in lune: every peak lands 0.07 to 0.08 s after its kick and is within

- **The lobby wheel turns on a spring** (1.7 Hz, 0.62): ~8% past the box and back, about 6 degrees on five boxes.
- A reroll's wind-up crouches from the lift it is at, not the floor.
- `IsResting` is settled to the eye (0.01). The lobby's controls come back 0.73 s after the drop instead of 0.45 s.

### Round 3 (2026-11-05): the chest's look, its shadow, the light handoff, and the best card in the middle

**Sprites were dropped for the live 3D chest.** The baked sprites in `Assets/ChestSprite/` (Animated-v4 three-quarter,
v5 front-facing, 48 spin steps) are kept, but the user wants players to believe they see the 3D model through a pixel
filter. A sprite cannot give that: hiding the steps of the shop's ~52 degrees a second spin needs ~360 frames, the
roll / scale / squash springs rotate and stretch a sprite's own pixel grid (a real filter keeps the grid fixed on
screen while the model moves under it), and pitch and the tilt-to-open blend cannot be baked without a combinatorial
explosion. So the chest stays a model in a ViewportFrame and every motion stays in code.

`Components/chestLook` dresses a chest viewport, and both `chestCarousel` (its `Look` param) and `chestViewport.Build(look)`
take one; nil draws as before. `chestLook.Picked(edgeColor)` is the look the user picked on the bench, used by
`ShopBoxesUI` (edge `(14, 4, 6)`) and `WinBoxUI` (edge black, over winBoxScreen's black dim):

| Setting | Picked | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pixel filter (`PixelFactor`) | Off | A CanvasGroup stretched N times past the viewport with the viewport scaled back inside it, so the group's texture hits its size cap and draws at lower resolution. The pixel size is the engine's choice (graphics level, memory cap), and the forum reports the upscale as blurred, not chunky. Kept on the bench only. For a crisp, fixed grid the remaining route is a Luau rasterizer into an EditableImage |
| Light (`Lighting`) | Now (the viewport's own: white ambient, warm key) | "Soft" (BeACastleLord's modelPreview: grey 200 fill, warm key hung off the camera over its left shoulder) was tried and turned back |
| Shadow | On, 0 x 10 px, 0.25 transparent | BeACastleLord's silhouette: a second ViewportFrame with a clone of every chest, Ambient, LightColor and ImageColor3 black, offset in screen px. See below |
| Edge colour (`EdgeColor`) | The colour behind the chest | A ViewportFrame blends its edge pixels toward its BackgroundColor3 even when it is transparent; the default draws a light line round the model |

How the shadow follows a skinned, animated chest:
- **Clone the chest before any clip plays and take the AnimationController off the clone**, then copy from the real
  chest each frame: the pivot, every Bone / Motor6D `Transform` (paired by walking both `GetDescendants` in the same
  order, checking name and class), and the primary part's `Transparency` (the carousel fades its back chests).
- **Copy in PreRender / RenderStepped, after the frame's PivotTo.** The Animator has not stepped yet that frame, so the
  Transforms read are the ones the frame draws with, and the shadow is on the same pose, not a frame late.
- **Write only what changed** and skip a chest at transparency 1. A closed chest's joints never change, so outside the
  clips the copy costs a read per joint. What it cannot save: the shadow is a second render of every chest (10 in the
  shop instead of 5), the same price BeACastleLord pays.
- Shadow and chest sit under one holder (one CanvasGroup when the filter is on), so they share a pixel grid.

**The front chest's light now hands over instead of jumping** (`chestCarousel`). It was placed once at the front slot,
so the rays stood still while the chests slid past, and then snapped to the new chest. Now there are two `lightRays`
that ride a chest each (projected from the camera every frame, written only when a pixel changes): on a turn the one
on the leaving chest stops emitting and its rays live out their life on it, the other starts with a burst on the
chest coming round. Three presses inside a ray's life (~1.6 s) reuse the fading one, which then jumps.

**The best card lands in the middle, under the chest** (`winBoxScreen`, both the run's win box and the shop's boxes):
the player is looking at the chest when the hand comes out, so the payoff goes where the eye already is. The grid's
places are sorted nearest the hand's middle first (ties: upper row, then left), the cards best rarity first, and card
k takes place k; that same ranking is the throw order (middle outward). Cards still open lowest rarity first, so the
last and biggest reveal is the centre card. A row of 4 has no centre: the best takes the left of the middle two.

Bench lessons (`Stories/ChestLook`, the wheel with a look beside the shop's now):
- **UI Labs can play a model's clips outside play.** Roblox does not step Animators in edit mode, which is why
  `ChestFloor` says "the lid only moves in play". `Animator:StepAnimations(dt)` is plugin-only and a story runs as a
  plugin, so the carousel's `ShouldStepClips` steps them each frame; the story sets it to `not RunService:IsRunning()`,
  since in play the engine steps them too and doubling plays them twice as fast. Never set it in game code.
- A slider for a pixel offset (`UILabs.Slider(def, min, max, step)`) beats a dropdown; a pick from a set stays `Choose`.

Linted, compiled; **not played in Studio.** Not known: the shop's real backdrop colour behind the chests (the bench's
gradient was used), and whether the black shadow reads on the shop's near-black backdrop or under the floor (the
floor is drawn in the chest viewport, over the shadow).

| Open | Dim, panel rises 4 units from 94.5% with a flash and a sheen, the heading's ticket pops then bobs; rows deal in 0.06 s apart on the one deal spring with rising ticks, each mark hopping as its row lands |
| Idle | Every 2.4 s the next row still to claim catches a sheen, taking turns down the list; stops when all are claimed |
| Hover / pad | Row outline white, CLAIM lifts (codexButton), brackets on the hand, the pad's A glyph on the focused unclaimed row |
| Prompt up / claim sent | The row pulls in 4% and its light crosses every 0.35 s until the answer (a sent claim gives up after 4 s) |
| Like, first press | Mark hops, row nods, a ring, the "LIKE THE GAME FIRST!" toast |
| Server confirms | Row flash, +9% thump, rings in the mark's colour, CLAIM strikes, ChestJump; the tickets break into glints that fly into the wallet (`ticketsFlight`); the ticket winks out in a puff and 18 sparks rise in the row's well (left of CLAIM, worst case 13 of its 22 units); the heading ticket jumps. 0.12 s later the tick stamps down from 1.4x where the ticket was, the row shakes a unit and greys, CLAIM turns grey CLAIMED, ObjectPick |
| Last claim | 0.3 s after its tick lands: panel thump, gold rings off the whole panel, flash, sheen, 0.05 s hit-stop, the heading ticket's biggest jump, ChestJump 1.35, and the subtitle turns to "THANKS FOR SUPPORTING THE GAME!" |
| Refused / prompt failed | The row lets go, shakes a unit, CLAIM shakes, BuyRefuse at half; the wallet is released at once |

Sizes (units, `lune`): panel 252 x 163 (unit 4 on the lobby canvas: 1008 x 652 px, 53% x 60% of 1920 x 1080), rows 234 x
28 with a 22-unit well, CLAIM 58 x 17, the row ticket 26 x 12 (the daily tile's, so it draws the same grid), the tick 16.
"FAVORITE THE GAME" needs 98 of the label's 108 units at 8.
