### Round 2 (2026-11-16): play-time and invite rows (linted, not playtested)

Asked for: free tickets and stardust for playing 15 and 30 minutes and for inviting a friend, after a reference with a
PLAY 30 MINUTES row counting down on its button and a gold INVITE FRIENDS row, "the most satisfying and juicier it can
be". The three one-time rows are unchanged; under them an **EVERY DAY** caption (gold, left) with **NEW IN 11H 44M**
(muted, right) stands over three daily rows.

| Row | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| PLAY 15 / 30 MINUTES | A cyan badge holding a 7 x 7 **pixel clock** drawn in Frames (rim, a texel of shade under it, a hand that steps a quarter every second: nothing turns), a bar under the label filling to the nearest unit, and a grey button counting down (`12M 40S`). When the time is up the row **rings in** (flash, hop, rings, half the sparks, the button striking green, `AbilityReady`), then the clock rattles every 1.6 s until claimed. Claimed: the tick, and the button counts to the reset |
| INVITE FRIENDS | The featured row: gold bezel, a warm well, a bigger badge (22 units, the Envelope glyph), 32 units tall, a note under the label (`+50 FOR SENDING AN INVITE`, `A FRIEND JOINED!`, `FRIEND REWARDS FULL TODAY`). Its button is a gold INVITE; with friends waiting it turns into a green CLAIM paying all of them at once. It pays again and again, so on a claim its tickets **come back** 0.45 s after the strike with a pop instead of a tick stamping down |

How it fits: rows 28 -> 24 units and gaps 6 -> 4 so six rows, the caption and the taller invite row stay at unit 4 (panel
252 x 249 units, 1008 x 996 px; the lobby canvas is always 1080 tall). Label room is 110 units on a row, 104 on the
invite row; the longest label (FAVORITE THE GAME) needs 98, the longest note 90 at 5 units (`lune`).

What the drawing now takes: `TRow.State` ("Claim", "Go", "Wait", "Claimed") and `Button` replace `IsClaimed`; the wrapper
decides every word on a button that is not CLAIM. `SetRows` repaints a button only when its state or words change (the
wrapper pushes once a second), and a row turning to Claim with the panel up is what plays the ring-in, so a friend
joining with the modal open rings the invite row too. "All claimed" (the thanks and the panel strike) skips the invite
row, since it never finishes.

With the modal shut, `FreeTicketsUI` toasts `PLAY REWARD READY!` or `A FRIEND JOINED!` once when either happens (and on
arriving back from a run with one due). The FREE button now hides only when everything for the day is taken.

Server: today's play time is `LoginStreakService.GetPlaySecondsToday` (both places; written into the save by a
`document:OnceBefore("Close")` hook, so lobby and runs add up across teleports). A friend is credited once ever, up to
`FriendsPerDay` a day, when they join the player's lobby by invite (`ReferredByPlayerId`) or by following them in (a
friend arriving without a teleport); a party coming back from a run is not a join. The invite itself is paid on trust
when the platform's prompt closes with someone picked, once a UTC day.

First to judge: the clock badge, the ring-in's strength next to a claim's strike, whether the 1.6 s rattle is too busy,
and the gold invite row against the gold panel. **Not opened on the bench, not playtested; the invite prompt and the
friend join were not run.**

## Last Wave: the skill tree (`skillTreeScreen`, `skillNode`, `skillWires`, `skillCard`, built 2026-11-05, unjudged)

The Constellation page remade in the pixel Slab kit, with everything that translated from BeACastleLord's tree (§4, 5c,
5j, 5o). `SkillTreeUI` keeps the rules (optimistic buys, pending counts, node ascends, the tree's ascension hold, the
paid restart, the skip pass, held syncs) and hands `Components/skillTreeScreen` a state; the drawing diffs it and plays
what changed (recipe item 2). Bench: `Stories/SkillTree.story` (the real tree from SkillTreeCore, fake points, a `Do:`
flip for the open, +points, ascend, restart and a branch wave). The old 4,000-line UI is in git history.

What came across from BeACastleLord:
- **Colour is what is bought.** An unbought star is a grey Slab (dim, or fully lit when the points cover it); it takes
  its branch's colour only once bought. A star the points cover breathes gold light round it (three stepped squares, 4
  levels a 2 s breath, so 4 writes a breath); an owned one pools its branch's light, and the light of two neighbours
  meets in the gap. Stars one link past the frontier are grey ghosts with a black icon.
- **The cost is thrown.** A level point leaves the gold readout as a chip (0.3 s, bent path, speeding into the star),
  an ascension point leaves its orbit pip round the centre (0.5 s). The level lands when the chip does.
- **A purchase is a sequence.** The square knocks (in to 0.9, overshoot +6%, +12% on MAX, simulated), throws two rings
  and 10 sparks (22 on MAX) from outside its edges, prints a receipt rising off it ("+0.1% DAMAGE", "MAX!",
  "ASCENDED"), and light pulses back through every owned wire one hop every 0.05 s. A first level runs its wire in texel
  by texel (0.225 s); the dotted lines then run out to what it opened and those stars pop in when their line arrives.
- **The map builds itself on every open**: the centre, then ring by ring (0.13 s apart, x0.78 each ring, floor 0.045),
  each ring's wires running out and its stars landing on their ends, one rising note per ring.
- **Three answers under the hand**: a coverable star lifts 2 units, a reachable one 1, a ghost none. The lift is
  critically damped, the press is its own fast spring. A refusal is one jolt of 2 units with a red flash and BuyRefuse.

Links are **pixel staircases**, not turned frames (§4: a turned frame is resampled): Bresenham on a 2-unit texel grid,
528 texels for the whole tree (lune), never touching a star's face. A link is hidden, dim (every third texel), crawling
(two lit, one dark, walking toward the star it opens; gold when the points cover that star) or solid in the child's
colour. **A push that keeps a link's look leaves it alone**, or the points settling mid-purchase would cut the run-in.

Input: the mouse buys on click and a hold repeats (first after 0.38 s, then 0.16 s shrinking x0.85 to 0.06 s), the
level-up pitch climbing with the streak. A drag pans (it cancels the hold and the click), the wheel zooms by a share
(x1.12 a click) about the pointer, eased. Touch: a tap picks the star and shows its card; a tap on the picked star
buys. The pad keeps the reticle (left stick), right stick pans, triggers zoom, A buys (hold repeats), Y holds ASCEND,
X restarts, R1 toggles skip. The card is read-only and starts its quick exit when the mouse leaves the star,
even toward the card, then parks off screen once the fade finishes (round 8).

ASCEND is a 1 s hold: a fill grows across the button, the orbit spins up and the map shakes more and more. The
ceremony keeps the old beats (glide home, drain swept round the centre like a clock hand, held breath with the music
ducked, detonation) in the kit: a white flash, three pixel rings out of the centre, 70 sparks, every star lighting again
in a wave outward, then the "ASCENSION IV" title typed in. RESTART asks with `loadoutPrompt` (red), then unlearns the
stars from the rim inward, each throwing its point home. **A page that leaves mid-ceremony finishes it** (the
wrapper's Detonate and Done still run), or `IsAscending` would stay true and the held sync would never apply.

Checked: StyLua, Selene (no new warnings), the `lune` compile of every changed file, both Rojo builds, the springs and
the wire geometry in `lune`/Python. **Not playtested and not opened on the bench.** First to judge: the node size (20
units) and map scale (0.24 units a data unit), the gold breath's strength, whether click-to-buy should become
click-to-pick on desktop, the reveal note (Hover3 pitched up) and the ceremony's length.

### Round 2 (2026-11-05): hover that holds, nothing hovered through the chrome, room for the links

- **The hover was being undone by a coordinate check.** A mouse move cleared the hover when the pointer was "far" from
  the star, measured by turning `InputObject.Position` into page px. On the lobby surface that is the wrong space (§3),
  so the next move after every hover cleared it: the sound played, the lift, brackets and card never showed. The hover
  now lets go only on GUI events: a star's `MouseLeave` releases it 0.25 s later unless the mouse reached the card or
  another star first (recipe 17). No coordinates. The wheel's zoom anchor now reads `GetMouseLocation()` (window px)
  and the pinch adds the inset to its touches.
- **Nothing is hovered through the chrome.** The bottom row's hits, the level bar, both readouts and the card count
  the mouse in and out (`overChrome`, `isOverCard`); a star does not take the hover while either is set, and entering
  the chrome drops it. The bar, the readouts and the card are `Active`, so a click on them never reaches a star.
- **The points hang from the top edge** (6 units), centred, clear of the platform's buttons; the card and the reticle
  still stop below the readouts or the topbar, whichever is lower.
- **Room for the links:** map scale 0.24 -> 0.34 (closest stars 9 -> 21 units of air), link texels 2 -> 3 units, links
  start 3 units off a face, dim and crawling links brighter, and the owned light 2 -> 3 units a step so it still meets
  across the wider gap. 665 texels in all (Python on the data). The map is now about 1936 x 1708 px at zoom 1.

Checked: StyLua, Selene (no new warnings), the `lune` compile, the lobby build. Not playtested.

### Round 3 (2026-11-05): centred squares, bigger wells, the links back to two units

- **A star read as off centre in its own light.** Measured from the screenshot: the slab's ink shadow made a 5 px dark
  band on the right and bottom only, inside light that is even on all four sides. Stars carry no drop shadow now (the
  light already gives them depth). The icon was also half a unit off: an odd number of units in an even well cannot
  sit in its middle, so the icon now takes the well's parity.
- **"Bigger" meant the squares, not the links.** Links are back to 2-unit texels. Squares 20 -> 26 units (centre 28 ->
  34), the icon 0.78 -> 0.88 of the well: a rung's icon goes from 10 to 16 units. Map scale 0.34 -> 0.4 keeps at least
  11 units between any two squares (Thorns and Evasion Extended), room for one's level tab and the other's ascend tab.

- **The centre is the galaxy, not a square.** No slab, no square light: the galaxy drawn at 1.5x the centre's size

- **The ceremony, closer to the old one.** Holding ASCEND spins the galaxy up. The drain leaves each star and its links

  stars falling into it from the dark. The detonation bursts it back past its size on a loose spring (0.32 damping),

### Round 7 (2026-11-06): one click from level 1 to the last ascend, and skip means no hold

- **ALL takes a star all the way.** A press takes up to the picked count of steps on the star. Each step is what the
  card offers at that moment: the star's ascend once its buyable levels are full (`CanUpgradeCap` requires level ==
  max), else a level. So ALL runs it from its first level through every ascend the points cover. The client judges
  each step on the star as it will be (`withPending` on both levels and caps). The server takes the steps by the same
  rule in one request (`SkillTreeBuyMany`, which replaced the levels-only `SkillTreeLevelNodeMany`). A one-step buy
  still uses the single events.
- **The stream lands in order.** Each point leaves at least 0.045 s after the one before and lands at least 0.04 s
  after it, so a star's ascend (a spiral) lands before the levels it opened. Spirals after the first take 0.6 s, not
  1.3 s. Simulated: a full star (10 levels, then 5 ascends of 10 levels each) lands in 4.65 s, in order. The flight
  pool is 128, because one star is at most about 111 steps and a reused flight lands early and out of order. A late
  ascension point leaves the galaxy, since the orbit pip it was aimed from is gone by then.
- **ASCEND takes the count too**: as many tree ascensions as the level pays the toll for, in one ceremony
  (`SkillTreeAscendMany`; the title names the last). **With skip on, a press of ASCEND commits; there is no hold.**
- **One push per buy.** `spend`, `applyLevel` and `applyAscend` no longer push. The press pushes once after its loop,
  and each landing pushes once, because a push rebuilds every star's view and ALL can be a hundred steps in a frame.

Checked: StyLua, Selene, the `lune` compile, both Rojo builds, the Meta network regenerated, stream order simulated
in `lune`. Not playtested.

### Round 10 (2026-11-06): hover through descriptions, stable fade hierarchy

- **A read-only description must allow input through**, including while fading. `skillTreeScreen` no longer makes
  the card Active or rejects a square's MouseEnter through `isOverCard`. That guard discarded the enter event;
  moving the description away later did not give the stationary pointer a second enter. Real controls and readouts
  still block the map. `skillCard`'s holder, content and compositor are explicitly inactive.
- **Do not restore opaque descendants during fade cleanup.** The reported end-of-exit flash was not a spring
  overshoot: alpha uses a clamped smoothstep. The old cleanup moved the card off screen and reparented opaque
  contents out of the transparent CanvasGroup in the same frame. That is a rendering-boundary suspect, similar to
  the stale-layout flashes documented in §3; offline property checks cannot establish the renderer's cause.
  Keep one padded CanvasGroup for this single tooltip, and keep its contents parented there. At the end it stays
  fully transparent and parks; reopening restores alpha in place. No Visible toggles, per-exit reparenting or group
  destruction. This deliberately differs from staging many panels only during their entrance (§ staging panels):
  stable composition is needed here, and there is only one description.
- Regression cases: cross a fading description onto another square; stop over the covered square without moving
  again; hover/click through an open description; complete the fade at 30/60/144 FPS; re-enter during it; resize or
  switch to a longer card; close/reopen mid-fade. Check the final rendered frames in Studio for the reported flash.

Checked: source event guards, offline hover/fade/lifetime checks, changed-file StyLua and Selene, Luau compilation,
repository lint comparison and the lobby build. Not playtested; the renderer fix still needs visual verification.

### Description idle work (2026-11-06)

`skillCard` writes scale only while the scale spring or exit moves. Placement caches the last drawn UDim2 and skips
unchanged writes; both parking paths invalidate it so reopening at the same location still places the card.
Typewriter character counts use `pixelSlab.Characters` once per line on Show (cached in a reused array), and the
typing clock stops when every visible row finishes. Rich-text markup does not count toward the reveal; the row
stagger and rate stay the same. A completed row is fully revealed, including when its text refreshes in place.

Offline before/after instrumentation: 120 settled Tick/Place calls went from 120 scale writes and 120 position
writes to zero of each. A short single-row description went from 12 grapheme writes in its first 0.2 s to one.
Regression checks cover longer text, rich text, row stagger, changed placement, parked-position cache invalidation,
fade completion and re-entry. Changed-file StyLua/Selene, compilation, full formatting/lint comparison and the lobby
build were checked. These are mock UI/source checks, not measured Studio frame-rate gains or renderer proof.

### What the skill tree rounds taught: read before remaking any lobby page

Seven rounds went into this page, and most of them fixed one of the mistakes below. Check each one before showing a
remake.

**Hover and input**
- Hover is MouseEnter/MouseLeave on each element, never distance maths against `InputObject.Position`. On the
  lobby's SurfaceGui canvas the input and the page are in different spaces, so a coordinate hover drops on the next
  mouse move (§3). For a point in the window, use `GetMouseLocation()` and convert it once, through
  `pageFromWindow`.
- Nothing is hovered through interactive chrome. Bars, readouts and menus over the map are `Active`, and
  MouseEnter/MouseLeave counters (`overChrome`) gate the map's hover. The skill description allows input through:
  release its hover immediately on the square's MouseLeave, including when the pointer moves onto the description.
  Starting dismissal immediately means no grace period: animate the drawing out before parking it.
- A menu over the map (`pixelDropdown`) folds away on a press anywhere else. Track the mouse with enter/leave
  counters. A touch fires no MouseEnter, so for a touch use `GetGuiObjectsAtPosition`.

**Sizes and centring**
- "Bigger" for a box means the inside: a bigger well and a bigger icon, never a thicker stroke or line. Ask which
  part if it is unclear.
- A square on a grid is only centred if all of these hold:
  - no drop shadow (it makes a dark band on two sides);
  - the icon has the same odd/even parity as its well;
  - the centre sits on an even unit;
  - a two-unit line is drawn on a grid shifted half a texel.
  Check the centring in Python or `lune` on the real data before saying it is centred.
- A link joining two boxes reaches under both (here, half way in), so it still meets a box drawn smaller (a drain,
  a press, a pop). Never end a link at the edge with air.
- The page's special object (the galaxy) is free, not boxed: no slab, a soft glow, its own motion.

**Style**
- In the pixel UI, nothing round and nothing big goes behind the content. Soft round nebulae were rejected: they
  drew the eye off the skills. Pixel-art planets would only be acceptable in the kit's own style, and are probably
  still too much.
- Particles take the page's theme sprite: the tickets' glint and glow for a constellation, not square dust. Run
  "Particles: the checklist" (§ vitals) on every spawn.
- A shared idea wears its shared component. The tree's XP is the run's `levelBar` strip (moved to Global, with a
  `Unit` prop for canvases `scaleNumber` does not measure), not a new bar.
- Keep the old page's layout and its signature gestures (memory: restyle keeps the old layout):
  - the level and ascension in the right-hand corner, with the actions centred, so nothing reads as off-centre;
  - the spiral of an ascension point;
  - the swirl of the drain.
- A drained or disabled box keeps its outline, in its own colour darkened (lerped 0.62 toward black). It does not
  go black.
- Text never leaves on `Visible = false`. It fades, rises and swells (here, shedding stars). The same goes for any
  title or banner.

**Sound**
- A clip that loops is never played through `uiSound` (that plays it once, so a looped clip runs its whole length).
  Clone the page's own copy, play it only while the thing it voices moves, and fade it out on landing.

**Bulk actions and skip**
- Any repeated purchase gets a count picker (1, 5, 10, 25, ALL) beside the actions:
  - send one request per press, with a byte count;
  - on the server, run the normal single validated purchase that many times and stop at the first that fails;
  - on the client, predict each step with the pending counts and stream the feedback in landing order;
  - push the state once per press, not once per step.
  A burst of single requests is dropped by the server's 0.05 s buy guard.
- When a step can change what the next step is (a star's ascend opening ten more levels), the count runs across
  both kinds by the same rule on both sides. The count was not limited to one kind.
- "Skip animations" skips the gates too: no hold to confirm and no ceremony wait. A pool or stream sized for a
  typical buy is sized for the largest one instead (a full star is about 111 steps).

**Before calling a round done**
- Simulate timings and geometry in `lune` or Python on the real data: link offsets, landing order, how long a
  stream takes.
- Read the source the user compared against (BeACastleLord) in full for what it does beyond the obvious: its
  depth-correct parallax, drifting layers, pointer lean, the building reveal, the vignette. "Take everything you
  can" means every one of those.

## Last Wave: the codes modal (`codesScreen`, built 2026-11-05, linted, not playtested)

Asked for: the Codes UI in the pixel style, "the most satisfying and juicier it can be". Built on the free tickets'
modal (gold Slab over a dim, PanelCatcher, input off at once on the leave, rise from 94.5% with a flash and a sheen). The
old layout is kept: title and subtitle on top, the code field, REDEEM (green, pad A) and BACK (red, pad B, not a stop).
New: three sealed reward sockets under the field, and the answer is shown in the panel instead of closing it for a toast.

| Piece | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Drawing | `Lobby/.../MenuUI/Components/codesScreen` (`new`; `Granted(rewards, toast)`, `Refused(message)`, `FocusTarget`, `Submit`, `SetCode`). Owns the TextBox and the waiting state, so a second redeem cannot go while one is out |
| Wrapper | `MenuUI/CodesUI` (same `Visible` API). Turns the Blink answer into `TReward`s (ShopCore names and images, the Quests stardust icon) and the old messages; mounts the confetti in its own ScreenGui |
| LobbyUI | Its codes confetti listener is gone: the burst now flies in CodesUI's ScreenGui, over the dim, at the payoff |
| pixelSlab | `ScreenPalettes`, `ScreenMuted`, `ScreenTicketColor` / `Light`: the kit's colours for a lobby **ScreenGui** |
| Bench | `Lobby/Client/UI/Stories/Codes` (answer, reward set, server delay, time scale; Do: type a code, redeem, reopen) |

**Why it is still a ScreenGui, and what that costs.** A TextBox on the arcade SurfaceGui makes the mobile keyboard pan
the view off-screen (white screen), so the modal stays in screen space. But the kit's `Show` colours undo the
SurfaceGui's Brightness 2 and the place's colour correction, which a ScreenGui does not get: gold (255, 190, 40) is
written as (143, 120, 72) and reads as mud (`lune`). **A lobby ScreenGui paints with `pixelSlab.ScreenPalettes`**
(the lobby's plain greys, no correction). Darks are unaffected either way (well 24 -> 25, ink 14 -> 17), so the Slab's
own ink and wells and `codexButton`'s ink are fine; `codexButton.SetEnabled(false)` (corrected GREY / MUTED) is not used.

**Moments** (from the server's answer, never from the click):

| Moment | What plays |
| --- | --- |
| Open | Dim, panel rises with a flash and a sheen, the gift pops; the sockets deal in 0.06 s apart, each "?" hopping; the subtitle types in |
| Idle | Light only (nothing moves on its own): the sealed "?" marks breathe towards white in a wave along the row, three colour steps, repainted only on a step. The gift is still between its jumps (free tickets' ticket bobs; this one does not) |
| Typing | Each key lights the field (light only, it is frequent) and lifts two motes off the end of the code, a tick rising in pitch with the length; a paste (4+ letters at once) lights it brighter and sweeps it; a delete is a lower tick |
| Redeem, empty field | The field and REDEEM shake a unit, a soft refuse, and the field takes focus |
| Redeem sent | The field pulls in 4% with its light crossing every 0.35 s, the sockets hop one after another with rising ticks, "CHECKING" counts its dots. The answer is held until 0.35 s of this has been seen; none in 8 s gives up with "NO ANSWER, TRY AGAIN" |
| Granted | Field flash, +9% thump, green rings and sheen, the code turns green, REDEEM strikes, the gift jumps, ChestJump; 0.14 s later the code puffs away. From 0.24 s each socket breaks open 0.16 s apart: the "?" puffs, the reward stamps down from 1.4x (lands 0.092 s), its count rolls up from +0, flash, rings in its colour, ObjectPick rising per card. 0.22 s after the last lands: panel thump, gold rings, flash, sheen, 0.05 s hit-stop, the gift's biggest jump, RewardBanked and the confetti |
| Refused | The field shakes two units and turns red, red rings, REDEEM shakes, every sealed "?" shakes and reddens for 1.2 s, BuyRefuse at half, and the reason types in red. Changing the code calms it all |
| Closed before the answer | The wrapper (or `Missed`, for an answer held during the charge) sends the old notice instead, with confetti on a grant |

Reward colours: tickets gold (the kit's ticket glyph), stardust blue, potions magenta, throws green; boxes have no
`ImageId`, so throws draw a 7 x 7 chest glyph. Up to six cards share the row (60 units wide at most).

Sizes (units, `lune`): panel 220 x 137 (880 x 548 px at 1080p; 440 x 274 on an 844 x 390 phone, where the unit floors
at 2), field 202 x 24 with code text at 9, cards 40 tall, buttons 76 x 17. The longest refusal ("DISCORD CHECK ON
COOLDOWN, TRY AGAIN IN 3 MIN") needs 194 of the status line's 202 units at 6. The typing motes are born at or below the
well's middle: the fastest climbs 7.6 units, the well gives 8.5 before its top, so none is cut by the clip.

Checked: StyLua, Selene (clean on the changed files), the `lune` compile of each, both Rojo builds, the numbers above in
`lune`. **Not playtested and not opened on the bench: not tried with a mouse, a finger or a pad, and the mobile keyboard
pan was not re-checked.** First to judge: the sockets' breath and hops, the hold of 0.35 s before the answer plays,
whether keeping the panel open (instead of closing for a toast) is wanted, and the screen palettes beside the canvas.

## Last Wave: the invite modal and the invitation card (`inviteScreen`, `invitationCard`, built 2026-11-05, linted, not playtested)

Asked for: `InviteUI` and `InvitationUI` in the pixel style, "the most satisfying and juicier it can be". The old layout
and colour meanings are kept: a gold modal titled INVITE with one row per player in the server who is not in the party,
the platform's friend invite (was "+", pad X) and close (was "X", pad B); and a gold card under the top right corner with
the sender's portrait and name, a green ACCEPT and a red DECLINE. Blue is the colour of inviting (the envelope, INVITE,
INVITE FRIENDS); green is a join.

| Piece | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Modal drawing | `Lobby/.../MenuUI/Components/inviteScreen` (`new`; `SetPlayers`, `UpdatePlayer`, `Joined`, `Press`, `PressFriends`, `FocusTarget`). Rows are plain Instances keyed by UserId, made and destroyed by `SetPlayers`, so they can arrive after the screen's Vide scope |
| Card drawing | `MenuUI/Components/invitationCard` (`new`; `Show`, `SetWaiting`, `UpdateImage`, `Accepted`, `Declined`, `SetHeld`) |
| Wrappers | `MenuUI/InviteUI` (same `UI` / `Visible`), `MenuUI/InvitationUI` (same params, still returns the Instance LobbyUI parents) |
| Bench | `Lobby/Client/UI/Stories/Invite` (players 0-12, time scale; Do: reopen, invite first, first joins, one leaves / arrives, invite friends, receive invitation, accept, decline; tutorial hold) |

**The server sends no answer to an invite** (`Invitation.Send` has no reply, and `LobbyService` silently drops a repeat
from the same sender to the same lobby until the recipient accepts or leaves). So the row says SENT for the request, and
the only confirmed success is the player turning up in the party: `InviteUI` sees an id that was on the list become a
`LobbyController.HasMember`, and that row plays JOINED. Thumbnails never gate a row or an invitation (the old code dropped
both when the thumbnail call failed); the initial shows until the portrait loads.

**Moments:**

| Moment | What plays |
| --- | --- |
| Modal opens | Dim, panel rises 4 units from 94.5% with a flash and a sheen, the heading's envelope badge pops then bobs; rows deal in 0.045 s apart (capped at the 8th) on the one deal spring, each portrait hopping as it lands |
| Hover / pad | Row outline white, gold bezel, hot well, lifts a unit; brackets on the hand (FocusFrame on the row's Slab) |
| INVITE pressed | Row nods (+4%), flash, blue rings, the face pops and greys to SENT with a light bar draining over the old 3 s; an envelope pops out of the face (1.35x, ease-out-back), then sweeps up and out past the panel's top right corner, faster as it goes, shrinking, with a blue / white / gold spark trail and a puff where it vanishes; the heading envelope hops. ClickHud + ObjectPick, a faint HoverHud pip on the vanish. When the bar runs out the face pops back to INVITE |
| Player joins the party | Row strikes green (flash, +6%, rings, sparks rising in its well, portrait punch, JOINED! face), ChestJump 1.2 + ObjectPick; it holds its place 0.85 s, then pops away in a green puff and the rows below slide up |
| Player arrives / leaves the server | Deals in at its sorted place (rows below slide down) / pops away in a grey puff |
| Nobody else here | NO ONE ELSE IS HERE YET, INVITE YOUR FRIENDS! in blue, and INVITE FRIENDS catches a sheen every 2.4 s (light only) |
| Invitation arrives | Card slides in from past the right edge on the open spring, flash, sheen, portrait punch, envelope hop, MenuIn; on landing gold rings and a nod. While it waits the envelope bobs and a soft gold ring leaves the card every 3.2 s |
| Another queued behind it | The `+N` badge (small gold Slab over the top right corner) pops, the card nods, the envelope hops |
| Accept | ACCEPT strikes, card flash, +9% thump, green rings, sparks off its left and bottom edges (the right is the screen's edge), ChestJump 1.25; 0.3 s later it pops away in a green puff |
| Decline | DECLINE nudges, the card shakes a unit and slides back out to the right, MenuOut soft; the next one slides in, and the pad goes to its DECLINE as before |
| Lobby tutorial | Held out of sight (as before); slides in when the tutorial reaches the Ready step |

Sizes (units, `lune`): modal 216 x 223 (864 x 892 px, 45% x 83% of 1920 x 1080; the old was 50% x 85%), five rows of
26 before it scrolls, fewer on a short screen; card 124 x 65 (496 x 260 px), hung at 0.115 of the height like the
notices, 6 units from the right. "INVITED YOU TO THEIR PARTY" would have shrunk to 4.6 units in the card's 86-unit text
column, so the line is "INVITED YOU TO PLAY" (5.5 units).

## Round 3: marks that load, a star, air in the badges, tickets bought fast

- **Codex marks that start on.** A slot built already ticked, banished or favourited went through `snapMark` straight
  away and never built its glyph (they were built lazily, only on a change), so the badge showed an empty well until
  the mark was toggled. Every mark change now goes through `setMark`, which builds the glyph first. Each `TMark` carries
  its own `Rows`, `Palette` and `Glyph`.
- **One star.** `pixelSlab.StarRows` (the codes screen's star, moved into the kit). The codex's slot star, its banish
  and favourite buttons (bottom row and the entry page) and the shop's Codex Favorites / Codex Banishes cards all draw
  the kit's star and cross instead of the old images. `codexButton` takes `Glyph` + `GlyphPalette` (its own colours
  unlit, white over the lit palette's shade when lit); `shopCard` cells take `Glyph` + `GlyphPalette`.
- **Air in badges.** `pixelSlab.WellTexel(wellW, wellH, unit)` sizes a glyph with a unit of air on every side. Shop,
  quest and codes badges are 16 units (well 10 at Bezel 2), the codex marks at least 14 (well 10 at a 1-unit bezel);
  freeTickets' 18-unit badge already had room.
- **Shop tools all "bought" on first visit.** The level pips are made by the layout, which runs after `paint`, so new
  pips kept their creation colour (lit gold) until the next repaint. `ensurePips` paints what it makes.
- **Tickets bought fast.**
  - `ticketsCounter` holds stack (`Hold` counts, `Release()` ends one) and every flight pays its own slice
    (`Pay(amount)`). Before, the first purchase's last slice let go of the one shared hold, so the second's change rolled
    in ahead of its pieces and its own slices did nothing.
  - "+N" and "-N" add up while still on screen, with a +9% re-pop.
  - `ticketsFlight` lands a piece taken by a newer throw instead of dropping it, so payouts finish in order.
  - In the shop, a second press on a card before the first was answered overwrote the first's record, so one purchase
    played with no spend and the wallet waited out its 2.5 s deadline. Presses now queue per card, a repeat press prices
    the next level and checks the balance less what is already in flight, the card strikes once per purchase with the
    level that came in for it, and the banked chime climbs a pitch chain.
- **Follow-ups the user caught (2026-11-06):**
  - The Favorites star sat low: its description was estimated at one line and drew two, growing up into the picture's
    room. `shopCard` now measures drawn titles and descriptions (`remeasure`) and lays out again on a miss.
  - Glyph sizes differed by a whole step between cards: a shop glyph may now reach into the gaps round its room.
  - A half-texel anchor shift (to centre the drawing, not the box) was tried and **reverted**: it put badge ticks off
    the unit grid (1.5 units of air on one side, 0.5 on the other). Centre the box.
  - `shopCard.set` split into `set` (the hold queue) and `apply` (showing a cell), so `Release` applies the held state
    directly instead of working round `set`'s hold check.
- The lessons are in §3: "Lazy parts and late text", "Pixel glyphs", "Tickets in quick succession", and the symptom
  table.

Checked: StyLua, Selene, `lune` compile, both Rojo builds. **Not playtested and not opened on the bench.**

### Round 3 (2026-11-06): the scrollbar flashing on open and close

What the user saw: opening or closing Invite with a short list showed a wide gold line at the right of the panel that
then went away; with a long list, a strip of empty track at the bar's end that closed up as the panel opened.

| Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| The list's ScrollingFrame had the engine's default 100 x 100 size until the screen's first layout, so a hidden screen's list "overflowed", and the bar (also at its default 100 px, so a unit of 50 px) unrolled and rolled up again as the open laid it out | `inviteScreen` creates the list at 0 x 0. In `scrollbar`, a window with no height never needs a bar |
| `scrollbar` compared `AbsoluteCanvasSize` with `AbsoluteWindowSize`, and under a screen's open / close `UIScale` they do not shrink together: the close's shrink made a short list "overflow", and mid-open the thumb was the wrong length | **In the kit**: a list sized in offset with an offset canvas (every pixel screen) is measured from its own `Size` and `CanvasSize`, which a UIScale does not touch; anything else (automatic canvas, scale-sized window) keeps the absolute pair as before. A drag now sets `CanvasPosition` against the same unscaled range |

**Rule for any scroll-dependent drawing:** never compare two engine `Absolute*` sizes of a frame under a moving UIScale.
Read both from the same space, preferably the offsets you wrote. Checked: StyLua, Selene, `lune` compile, both builds.
**Not playtested.**

### Review (2026-11-06): what was cut, and the rules it left

- **The list exists only while the modal is up.** `InviteUI` publishes only while `Visible`, fetches a portrait the first
  time a player is on the open list (cached after), and `inviteScreen` frees every row once its leave has ended. Before,
  every lobby state change (ready, gear, ...) re-sorted and re-laid out a list nobody had opened, and a 30-player server
  kept ~1,500 Instances alive all session. A cooldown outlives its row in `sentAt`, so SENT survives a quick reopen.
  `Open` now expects `SetPlayers` first (the bench re-sends on reopen).
- **Idle life never keeps the clock awake.** The card's envelope bob and its idle ring, and the modal's envelope bob,
  run on a 0.2 s `task.delay` chain (bob in eight whole-unit steps over 1.6 s, ring every sixteenth); only a ring or a
  sheen wakes the clock, for its own half second. An unanswered invitation used to step every frame for as long as it
  waited.
- **`inviteRow`** is its own module (Kick's `kickScreen` / `kickRow` split): plain functions over a row table, one shared
  `TEvents` table for every row instead of reaching into the screen's state. `inviteScreen` went from ~1,630 to ~1,030
  lines.
- **`pixelSlab.EnvelopeRows`** is the one envelope, beside `TickRows` / `CrossRows`; the modal and the card both draw it.
- The card's `tint` skips a colour it already has (70 sheen rows were recoloured on every answer); `scrollbar` measures
  once per layout on a `task.defer` instead of once per changed property.

Checked: StyLua, Selene (clean on the nine files), `lune` compile, both Rojo builds. **Not playtested.**

### Last Wave: fitting the reworked tool and ticket icons (2026-11-06)

The shop box reveal's reroll glyph was too large for its well. `actionButton` still allowed the image-era minimum
of 12 units across: with the shared 6-unit chrome it could leave only 6 units for an 8-texel glyph. Flooring the
texel scale and clamping it to at least one unit then overflowed; clipping only hid the drawing that did not fit.

- `actionButton` now reserves chrome + glyph + one unit of air on each side before choosing its pixel size, and
  sizes with the same `WellTexel` rule as the shop's owned badge and Codex corner marks. This covers both lobby
  and run box reveals, level-up actions and augment/ability rewards. At the reported 70 px / requested 5 px
  unit, the resulting unit is 4 px, the well is 46 px and the glyph is 32 px, leaving 7 px per side.
- `touchButton` had the same minimum-one-texel issue at its 14-unit limit. Controls that accept a glyph now reserve
  its full bounds too, even while showing an image, so changing the interact prompt to Skip keeps its geometry.
  Image-only controls retain their sizing. The existing square skip buttons (`codexButton`) have at least
  17-unit outer sides; their 8-texel glyphs fit with air. Shop tool pictures retain their approved allowance into
  the surrounding gaps; their owned badges and Codex marks already use `WellTexel`.

Regression cases: reveal a box in lobby and run, reroll/spend/disable and quarter-turn the action, open level-up
and augment/ability hands, resize to small/large screens, switch the mobile prompt from image to Skip, view shop

### Daily Rewards: day 7 must show before hover (2026-11-06)

`dailyTile.Apply` can receive data before the first layout, while `GiftSide` is zero. `paintTile` then hides both
the gift and its sunburst. `Layout` calculated their room but never refreshed visibility; hover or closing the
screen called `SetHovered` and finally repainted them. `dailyTile.Layout` now paints after placing its contents.
Keep size-dependent visibility synchronized at layout boundaries, including resizing a resting tile; do not
depend on a hover, a close, or continuous repainting to reveal initial content.

Audited the other `pixelBurst` owner (`shopCard`) and quest, inventory, action, price, reward and upgrade cards.
Their corresponding visibility or drawing paths already handle initialization/layout; no matching defect found.

Regression cases: data before layout, open without hovering, day 7 locked/today/claimed, resize until the gift has
no room then restore, and hover enter/leave. An offline Lune probe ran the actual tile module with mocked drawing
dependencies: it reproduced the missing gift/rays before the fix and passed those cases afterward. Full-tree
StyLua passed; changed-file Selene is clean, full-tree Selene retained the same 10 errors / 324 warnings, and
`dailyTile` / `dailyScreen` compiled. **Not playtested or visually verified in Studio.**

## Last Wave: the loading screen and the warning (`loadingScreen`, built 2026-11-06, linted, not playtested)

Both places' `LoadingScreen.client` scripts now drive one kit component, `Components/loadingScreen`, required from
ReplicatedFirst by its `StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts` path (the same path every screen uses, so it is the same
module). The scripts keep their asset lists, deadlines, skip rule, `LoadingFadeStarted` attribute and kick paths.

- **Title**: LAST (white) WAVE (gold), one holder per letter with an ink copy a unit down and right. Letters fall in
  12 units, decelerating, 0.07 s apart, and land with a flash, a +10% punch and a `HoverHud` tick climbing in pitch.
  Once all have landed a one-unit wave runs through them. The title measures its letters with `GetTextBoundsAsync`
  (prefix widths, so the space survives) inside a 1.5 s deadline, and falls back to Silkscreen's 0.72 advance.
- **Bar**: a grey Slab with a gold fill (lit row, shaded row, white leading edge), a stepped sheen every 2.2 s, and
  sparks born two units above the bar off the leading edge as it gains. The reading is the 4.1 Hz / 0.72 spring. A
  phase fills `From` to `To`; with no progress reported it creeps toward 92% of its end so a long wait still moves.
  `preloadAssets` takes an optional `onProgress(share)` for this. Run: LOADING 0-55%, BUILDING MAP 55-85%, WAITING FOR
  PLAYERS 85-100%. Completing pays off: flash, two rings, side sparks, thump, "READY" in gold, `ScoreComplete`.
- **Warning** (lobby): the bar puffs away and a gold Slab deals in (scale 0.4 to 1, thump, rings, `MenuIn`) with
  WARNING on a `pixelSlab.Tab`. The body types in at 110 characters a second; the 4 s auto-continue starts only once
  it is all shown, drawn as a gold drain under it. Three stepped gold rings breathe on the 1.15 s cosine.
- **Skip**: the prompt rises in after 2 s, worded for the device (key, button or tap), and breathes; a press flashes
  and punches it.
- **Exit**: content pops away on `LeaveScale` (letters staggered, each with a puff), then the black is cut into 9 rows
  of blocks tiled from one rounded number per edge, each shrinking to its middle in whole units on a delay that grows
  from the screen's centre out (about 0.95 s in all). `LoadingFadeStarted` is set when the exit starts, as before.
- **Colours**: a ScreenGui, so `ScreenPalettes` and the new `pixelSlab.Seen` (the lobby's plain greys only), never
  `Show`.

- **Bench**: `src/Global/Client/UI/Stories/Loading.story.luau` plays the real component through either place's flow
  on fake timings (Flow, Stop at Loading / Warning, Load seconds, Loop, Time scale, replay, skip), over a stand-in
  "THE GAME" so the exit has something to reveal. `loadingScreen.new` draws straight into any non-PlayerGui parent
  for it, and `Destroy` tears it down mid-flight.

### Structure (2026-11-06): one folder, one piece per file

`Components/loadingScreen/` is one ModuleScript to Rojo (same require path). `init.luau` owns the clock, the order the
pieces start in (`begin`, the mark handing to the title, an arrival handing to the bar), the cover and exit blocks,
the dust and the public API; it fills ONE `TFrame` a frame (`Clock`, `Dt`, `P`, `Leave`, `ExitAge`) and hands it to
every piece's `Step`. The pieces are `title`, `mark`, `bar` (with its stage line and percentage), `warning`,
`captions` (skip prompt, teleport banner) and `blocks`; shared numbers are in `Tune`, types in `Types`, curves in
`ease`. Each piece hides itself once `ExitAge` passes `Tune.LeaveSeconds`, and keeps `Drawn*` copies of what it last
wrote so a settled screen writes nothing but what is meant to keep moving (the title's wave, the dust, the skip prompt
and warning rings breathing, the sheen). Add a new element as a piece with `Layout(view)` and `Step(frame)`.

### Round 2 (2026-11-06): bigger, the studio mark, and teleports as one screen

- **Bigger**: the user's screenshots (795 px tall) showed the warning body at 12 px. The unit is now 4 px at 1080p
  (was 3), the warning body 7 units, its tab 12 units, the panel 200 units wide, and the teleport words 7 units.
- **The studio mark** (lobby, fresh join only). Round 2 morphed Silkscreen letters into the logo's blocks; the user
  disliked it (two drawing languages, so it read as a swap, not an assembly). Round 3: LUVIK INTERACTIVE is drawn in
  the logo's OWN block style (`GLYPHS`: Frames in logo pixels, cap 50, stroke 8, every face extruded three steps of
  (-1, +2) in navy, which reproduces Luvik64.png's extrusion), so the word's L IS the logo's L. Beats: blocks pop in
  one by one with their extrusion stepping out and a rising tick; everything but L and the I of INTERACTIVE falls away
  from both ends; the L and I are pushed together (ease past and back) and the I clacks in; the I squashes into the
  i with an overshoot and throws the dot up, which lands; the mark powers up to full size a whole px per step (crisp at
  every step, a tick each) and thumps with a navy-to-blue flash, rings, sparks and `ChestJump`; holds; pops away into
  the title. A render of the font and the assembled mark against the PNG was checked offline before shipping.
- **Teleports** (`Controllers/TeleportCoverController`, both places): `Player.OnTeleport` (RequestedFromServer or
  Started) puts up a `Cover` screen: the blocks of the exit run backwards, growing in from the edges, born gold and
  cooling to black, then LAST WAVE deals in over "ENTERING THE RUN" / "RETURNING TO LOBBY" / "REJOINING". Once it is
  up, `Snapshot()` (a still clone: no particles, rings or cells) goes to `SetTeleportGui`; a plain black GUI is set
  at start so an early teleport never shows Roblox's own screen. A failed teleport plays the normal exit.
- **Earlier triggers**: two old black covers went up BEFORE the teleport and hid the new one (playtest, 2026-11-06):
  the lobby's `MenuUI/LoadingUI` ("Loading...", at the countdown's 0) and `FinalStatsController`'s "Returning to
  lobby..." overlay (Main Menu, DisplayOrder 2000). Both are gone; those moments call
  `TeleportCoverController.Cover(words)` and their give-up paths (`StopCountdown`, the 10 s watchdog) call `Uncover`.
  Any new flow that knows a teleport is coming should call `Cover` the same way, never draw its own black.
- **Arrival**: both `LoadingScreen.client` scripts parent `GetArrivingTeleportGui()` to PlayerGui before removing the
  default screen, and open in `Arrive` mode: drawn UNDER the frozen copy (DisplayOrder 999) until its own title is
  laid out, then the copy is destroyed; the words hold 0.6 s and pop away as the bar deals in where they stood.
- **Bench**: `Stories/Loading` flows are Lobby join (with the mark), Lobby / Run arrival, Run join, and Teleport to
  run / lobby, which covers the stand-in, holds 1.5 s for the teleport, then hands over to an arrival under it.

Checked: StyLua, Selene (clean on every changed file), the `lune` compile, both Rojo builds. **Not playtested or
visually judged in Studio, and the story has not been opened in UI Labs.** Teleports cannot run in Studio, so the
`OnTeleport` timing (whether the cover is up before the client leaves) and `SetTeleportGui` taking a GUI set
mid-teleport are unverified until a published test.

## Last Wave: the AFK zone (`afkScreen`, built 2026-11-06, linted, not playtested)

Asked for: the AFK UI in the pixel style, "the most satisfying and juicier it can be". The old layout and colour
meanings are kept: AFK ZONE (blue, the lobby's AFK colour) and its subtitle on top, TIME AFK, the stardust and tickets
this stay has earned side by side (stardust left, tickets right, each "+N" rising off its outer side), the rate line, and
a red EXIT AFK with the pad's B at the bottom. It is still a page on the lobby's SurfaceGui (no dim; the lobby's glow
stays up behind it and still pulses on each grant, from LobbyUI), so it paints with `pixelSlab.Palettes`.

| Piece | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Drawing | `Lobby/.../MenuUI/Components/afkScreen` (`new`; `SetElapsed`, `SetTotals`, `SetRate`, `Granted`, `Open`, `Close`) |
| Wrapper | `MenuUI/AFKUI` (same `UI` / `Visible` / `SetInitialValues`). Keeps EnterAfk / LeaveAfk pairing, the 18-minute rejoin, the config observes, the 1 Hz clock, PushBack and PushFocus(nil) |
| Kit | `ticketsFlight(counter, { Colors, TickSound })`: optional, so the same flight carries stardust (blue pieces, `StardustTick`) |
| Bench | `Lobby/Client/UI/Stories/AFK` (interval, payout, stardust rate, grant delay, resume seed, time scale; Do: reopen, reopen as a resume, pay now, skip to the next minute / hour) |

**New: the NEXT PAYOUT bar.** The old screen showed nothing between payouts (5 minutes at the live config). The server
restarts its count when the zone is entered and after each grant (LobbyService's `Accumulator`), so the bar fills from
the open and from each grant, with the time left inside it. Full before the grant arrives, it reads PAYING OUT with
counting dots and the fill pulses; the strike waits for the server. A bar that stays full 4 s past its length with no
grant (a payout of 0 never fires one) starts its next count, as the server has.

**Moments** (the payout from the server's grant, never from the bar):

| Moment | What plays |
| --- | --- |
| Open | Panel rises 4 units from 94.5% with a flash and a sheen, the moon pops; clock, bar, tallies and rate deal in 0.06 s apart on the one deal spring with rising ticks |
| Idle | All on one 0.1 s `task.delay` chain, so the clock sleeps: the moon bobs 1.5 units on whole units, a Z leaves it every 1.6 s drifting up and left (away from the words, inside the well), the fill grows a whole unit at a time and its words count down. Only the fill's sheen (every 3.2 s) wakes the clock, for its 0.55 s |
| New minute / hour | The clock lights gold and fades (light only; a readout does not bounce). An hour also thumps its block, throws gold rings and plays ObjectPick |
| Payout | Bar flash, +9% thump, gold rings, sparks off its right end, the moon jumps, a panel sheen, ChestJump; the fill drains back over 0.32 s while the tickets fly out of its end into the tickets tally (`ticketsFlight`, held and paid a slice per landing, strikes with "+N"); 0.14 s later the stardust flies into its tally (swell per landing, then flash, thump, blue rings, sparks off its left side and "+N" rising off its left edge), so the two banked chimes do not stack |
| Resume after the rejoin | The totals and the clock open where they were, with no strike |
| Exit / B | ClickHud on a press of EXIT AFK, MenuOut, the panel pops away on `LeaveScale`, input off at once; any flight in the air settles |

Sizes (units, unit 4 at 1080p): panel 236 x 165 (944 x 660 px), inner width 218, bar 218 x 19, tallies 40 x 18 each, 12
apart, clock 16, heading 11 with a 16-unit moon (7 x 7 glyph at two units a texel). The longest line, the subtitle,
needs 186 of 218 units at 6. The stardust number is fitted for "9.99K" (5 characters) so a total that gains a digit never
overflows its 22-unit room.

Checked: StyLua, Selene (clean on the four files), the `lune` compile of each, both Rojo builds. **Not playtested and
not opened on the bench: not tried with a mouse, a finger or a pad, and the rejoin teleport cannot run in Studio.**
First to judge: the Zs (drift, pace, whether they read as sleep), the bar's PAYING OUT wait on a slow grant, the two
tallies' sizes beside each other, and whether a payout every 5 minutes deserves the panel sheen on top of the bar's
strike.

### Review (2026-11-06): the tally split out, and idle steps that only write what moved

| Found | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `afkScreen` was 1,424 lines holding two things: the screen and a tally | `Components/afkTally` (`new`, `Layout`, `Step`, `Counter`; a plain record and module functions), as `dailyTile` is to `dailyScreen`. The screen is 1,134 lines |

**Moments:**

| Moment | What plays |

## Last Wave: the run options page (`optionsScreen`, `optionsCard`, `runSummary`, built 2026-11-06, linted, not playtested)

The Options page (difficulty, modifiers, run summary) moved off `commonButton`, the `ticketShape` chips and
`TextScaled` labels onto the pixel kit, keeping the old layout: the tabs at the top (L2 / R2), the cards on the left,
the RUN SUMMARY column on the right, BACK at the bottom left. `OptionsUI` is the wrapper (LobbyController,
ProgressionController, the Cores, notices, the pad); `MenuUI/Components/optionsScreen` is the drawing, built on the
Quests page's skeleton (one rhythm, `topbarClear`, the hover kept across gaps, the grid's own selection links). LobbyUI
now passes the wallet (`TicketsBox`, `Tickets`) as it does to Quests. Bench: `Lobby/.../Stories/Options`.

**The cards** (`optionsCard`, one module for both kinds). Five states: `Locked` (dark well, padlock glyph and
"BEAT HARD" on the bottom row), `Unpaid` (the shop's `priceButton` ticket face on the bottom right), `Off`, `On`
(slab painted in the option's own colour via `pixelSlab.FromColor`, white outline, three stepped glow rings, a sheen
every 3.2 s), `Blocked` (a modifier that needs a party: faded rewards, "2+ PLAYERS"). A difficulty shows threat pips
(its place on the ladder, filled in its colour), its ticket and stardust multipliers, and the corner tick badge when it
is the pick. A modifier shows its bonus ("+0.20", red when it is a cut such as Infinite's), its soul cost when it is not
x1 ("SOULS x2"), and a pixel switch whose knob snaps across (5 Hz / 0.55, a little overshoot) with the colour filling
behind it. Shapes are per tab: difficulties 58 units tall, at least 96 wide, three a row (the old grid); modifiers 46
tall, at least 74 wide, four a row, so all ten fit a 16:9 screen without scrolling (4:3 drops to three and scrolls 13
units; checked in `lune` at 1920, 1440 and 2340 by 1080 and the bench's sizes). An unbought difficulty hides its
stardust: the price takes that room, and at 106 units the row would overflow.

**What plays, and when.** Every outcome plays on the server's answer, never on the click (the click only sinks, ticks
and, for a buy, holds the wallet):

| Event | Card | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A modifier turned on, or a harder difficulty picked (a gain) | Flash, +9% thump, rings and in-well sparks in its colour, knob snaps, badge pops | A chip with the bonus ("+0.20", "x2.40") and 9 motes fly out of the card's ticket on cubic paths (5j: shares of the trip, S and C mixed, landings placed on a closing curve, the chip last at 0.96 s). The plate is HELD at its old total, swells under each landing (smoothed pressure), then rolls up with a ScoreTick count pitched by the value, strikes (flash, +9%, gold rings, sparks rising off it) and RewardBanked |
| Turned off, an easier pick, Infinite (a cut) | -4% nudge, glow off | No flight: the total rolls down with a red sting and a small shake |
| A pick that changes the difficulty | | The name pops (a size, 3.6), each stat rolls to its value a beat after the one above, its row flashing red if it went up and green if down |
| A modifier added to the list | | Its row slides in from 8 units right and flashes its colour; past the room, "+N MORE" |
| A purchase confirmed | The price stays up (`Hold`) while `ticketsSpend` throws the tickets out of the wallet into it, then strikes gold (+10%, 22 sparks), confetti and RewardBanked; the card swaps to its switch / pick | |
| Refused (no tickets), locked, blocked, not the owner | Shake, BuyRefuse, the old notices | |
| Page opens | Panel rises from 94.5%, cards deal in along the grid, the summary a beat after | The plate counts up from x0.00 silently (a reveal, not a gain: no strike, no ticks) |

The flight is called BEFORE the summary that carries the new total (`OptionsUI.throwGains` diffs the lobby state
against what it last saw), so the hold is in place when the total arrives. A non-owner sees the owner's changes fly too.
A card not on the shown tab throws nothing and the total simply rolls.

**Summary content.** SOUL COST is now the run's real cost, the difficulty's multiplier times every enabled modifier's
(`ModifiersCore.GetEnabledSoulCostMultiplier`, what the altars and chests charge); the old line showed the difficulty's
alone. The tickets total uses `ModifiersCore.GetEnabledTicketsBonus`, so a dashboard-disabled modifier no longer counts.

**Pitfalls this round already hit (fixed before showing):**
- A summary row built in `Layout` and filled in `Set` showed x0.00 when `Set` came first: rows are made in `Set`.
- Any refresh (a tab change) re-ran `rollTickets` and turned the opening count-up into a fake gain with a strike; only a
  changed total rolls now.
- The chip was timed to land at 0.86 s while the last mote landed at 0.90 s: the plate rolled before the stream ended.

Checked: StyLua (`--check src`), Selene clean on the changed files, the `lune` compile of each, both Rojo builds, the
layout at five screen sizes in `lune`. **Not opened on the bench and not playtested.** First to judge: whether the
flight is too much for the owner flipping many modifiers in a row, the plate's tick count while it rolls, the switch's
look next to the price, and the summary's "+N MORE" cut at 6 rows on 1080p.

**From SpecialDelivery's dialogue** (`typewriter` / `DialogueUI` there), in this kit:

- **The line is one label pair per letter**: an ink label with the outline under, a fill label over, each on its own
  layer so an outline never covers the letter before it. Silkscreen is not monospace, so each character's advance is
  measured once with `GetTextBoundsAsync` (the printable ASCII set as the module loads, anything else in parallel when a
  line needs it; `Present` may yield, at most `MeasureWait` 2 s). The card wraps at whole words to the text column and
  centres each row itself; its height follows the rows it laid out.

  and settles, fading in; the rise is drawn in whole units (`lune`: 3, 2, 1, 0, -1, -2, -1, 0). A skip pops the rest in at
  once.

  running while one is on screen (writes only on a whole-unit change); `hideGlyphs` stops it when the card leaves.

## Last Wave: the Robux purchase receipt (`purchaseScreen`, `PurchaseUI`, built 2026-11-06, linted, not playtested)

Asked for: buying something with Robux felt flat (the card's strike and the lobby's confetti, the same as a tickets
buy, and only confetti when the shop was closed or on another tab). It should be "the most satisfying and juicier it
can be", looking at the win box's card drops. Bench: `Stories/Purchase` ("Receipt" picks one of ten made-up receipts;
`Do: hurry`, `Do: two in a row`). **Not opened on the bench and not played.**

### What plays, beat by beat

| Beat | What | Numbers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Charge | The dim falls (0.72). A floor shadow grows where the card will land, the light leaks and three notes climb | 0.34 s; shadow 25% -> 90% of the card, 3 units tall; ChestJump 0.78 / 0.92 / 1.08 |
| Drop | The card falls from above the screen, faster and faster | 0.16 s, `t^2` |
| Slam | Hit-stop, squash, dip, flash, two rings, dust puffing sideways off its feet, a burst and full fan of rays, confetti, the price tier's `rarityImpact`, the box landing sample and its chord | hit-stop 0.06 s; squash -10% then +2.5% (thump -3.2 at 2.9 Hz / 0.4); dip 2.5 units (125 at 4.5 Hz / 0.38); confetti 30 + 5 a tier |
| Stamps | THANK YOU (or GIFT SENT!) pops over the card's top edge; the name stamps from 1.8x; the subtitle types | +0.1 s, +0.2 s (0.09 s, `t^2`), +0.32 s at 0.018 s a letter |
| Lines | Each line slides out from UNDER the card to its place (ease-out-back, growing from 55%), thumps, rolls its count up with ticks, then stamps on the next note of a major scale, sparking off its sides. The line of tickets then flies into the wallet (`ticketsFlight`) | first at +0.62 s, gaps 0.42 s closing x0.9 to a 0.2 s floor; roll 0.32 s + 0.06 a digit, 8 ticks |
| Ribbon | A permanent perk slaps on FOREVER (a deal: NEW) across the top right corner | +0.22 s after the last line |
| Finale | 60 confetti, ScoreComplete, rays pulse, a thump and a sheen | +0.25 s |
| CONTINUE | AWESOME! pops in; the pad lands on it. Idle: the card bobs a unit, a sheen every 2.6 s | +0.35 s |

A 7-line bundle has CONTINUE up at 4.2 s (`lune`). A press anywhere, a key or a pad button lands everything at once
(the win box's hurry rule); B does the same, then closes.

**Its own gesture** (the reveal rule): the box throws cards up OUT of a chest, the codes break sockets open; this one
DROPS onto a shadow and PRINTS lines out from under itself. It borrows the rarity look (the slam hits as the price's
tier: under 100 R$ Epic, under 400 Legendary, else Divine with its shafts and music dip; a deal hits at least as its item's
rarity) and the kit's rays, rings, sheen and paper confetti.

### Where it lives

| Owner | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `ShopController` | Marks the Robux prompt in flight (`beginRobuxPurchase`, keys `Premium:` / `Utility:` / `Deal:` / `Pack:` / `Gift`), spends it on the matching grant (`isRobux` on `OnPurchaseSuccess` and `OnDealPurchased`), and answers `IsRobuxDialogUp` (Roblox's dialog is taken as up until PromptProductPurchaseFinished / PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished, never under the box reveal's 1.5 s floor). A grant over 120 s after its prompt is not taken as Robux. `GiftSent` no longer fires `OnPurchaseSuccess` |
| `MenuUI/PurchaseUI` | Builds a receipt from the catalog (bundles' rewards, perks' fields, an upgrade's level, a boost's charges, a potion's runs, a pack's tickets and bonus, a deal's content, a gift sent), holds the wallet in the grant's handler (the server sends the tickets right after), queues receipts, waits for the dialog (at most 10 s) while keeping the wallet's hold alive, owns the pad (no cursor during the reveal, B hurries then closes, L1/R1/L2/R2 blocked) |
| `Components/purchaseScreen` | The drawing, steps on `pixelMotion`, plays its own sounds |
| `LobbyUI` | Mounts it at ZIndex 105 in `MenuContainer`, raises the wallet to 106 while it plays, makes the lobby and the shop deaf under it (a SurfaceGui dim does not stop hover) |
| `ShopUI` / `NotificationUI` / lobby confetti | Step aside for a Robux purchase: the card does not strike (its pending press is dropped), no "YOU GOT X" or "YOU GIFTED" toast, no global confetti. A pass bought outside the game still gets the toast |

### Pitfalls this build hit

- **Multiplier suffixes use the same small x as the stash and shop.** `purchaseScreen` draws a count's `x` at 0.65
  of its fitted TextSize, including while rolling, stamping, hurrying and resizing. Layout counts the x as 0.65 of
  a character and measures the final count before adding rich text, keeping the next label still during the roll.
- **A line placed this frame has a stale `AbsolutePosition`.** A hurried line is moved and its tickets thrown in the same
  frame, so the flight's start is worked out from the screen's own numbers, not read off the frame.
- **Dust thrown down crosses the floor shadow and the subtitle** (checklist rule 1): it puffs out sideways off the card's
  feet instead. **A line's sparks would be overtaken by its own stamp swell** (+6.9%, rule 6): they start that much further
  out, simulated at 4.6 units clear at worst.
- **The leave's confetti kept the lobby deaf for up to 4 s**: `Left` is told when the dim and the card are gone; the paper
  finishes falling over a lobby that has its input back.
- **A UIStroke draws with its text transparent**: the name's outline is hidden with it until the stamp.

### Open

- Not seen or heard: the drop's speed and the slam's weight, the line rhythm on a 7-line bundle, AWESOME! as the word,
  the FOREVER ribbon in red on gold, Divine's shafts and music dip on a 499 R$ VIP.
- The confirming state on the card while Roblox's dialog is up, the avatar's cheer and the chat line for big purchases
  were proposed with this and are not built.
