## Last Wave: readable reset and availability timers (2026-11-06)

The selected countdown format uses at most two adjacent units: `5d 9h`, `23h 29m`, `29m 30s`, then `30s`.
Omit leading zeros and a trailing zero unit (`23h`, `1m`). Days replace accumulated hours on weekly/monthly resets.
Seconds appear below an hour. This is for time remaining; elapsed run/profile/AFK clocks retain their clock format.

- `GlobalShared/Utils/Functions/formatCountdown` owns the duration text. Positive fractions round up to a second so
  an available-in timer cannot display `0s` before its deadline. Longer spans drop the precision below their second unit.
- `GlobalClient/Utils/countdownText` owns the caption treatment: existing muted words, the kit's gold light on the
  duration, the kit's warm red light in the final minute, and green for an available action. The palette already goes
  through `pixelSlab.Show`. This adds no animation clock, per-tick sounds, particles or scale kicks.
- Quests and resetting leaderboards say **RESETS IN**; daily deals say **REFRESHES IN**; daily rewards say
  **NEXT REWARD IN**, or green **READY TO CLAIM** while `CanClaimDailyRewardToday()` is set. The daily caption updates
  on the existing state refresh as well as the one-second timer, so a confirmed claim changes it immediately.
  Expired reset captions say **RESETTING...** / **REFRESHING...** while waiting for refreshed data. Zero alone never
  marks a reset as complete or grants a reward. AllTime leaderboards and achievements still have no reset caption.
- Shop offer, weekly-deal and claim-button durations use the same formatter. Their existing offer flash, last-minute
  heartbeat and confirmed claim feedback stay with the cards. Ordinary long-duration ticks stay quiet.
- These labels enable RichText; fitting must count visible characters through `pixelSlab.Characters`, never markup
  bytes. Daily rewards now fits its clock to its own footer room again whenever the text changes. The three existing
  DailyRewards / Quests / Shop stories use the real helper and have a **Seconds left** control for reviewing unit
  changes and the final minute. DailyRewards' **Can claim** control previews the green state.

Checked: all 13 touched Luau modules compile (including the large ShopUI and LeaderboardUI), 19 duration boundary
examples and an exhaustive week of duration/precision checks pass in Lune. Caption highlighting, expiry and ready
strings were checked with mocked palette/dependency inputs; that is not a renderer check. `stylua --check src` and
`git diff --check` pass. Selene is clean on these 13 files; the full-tree comparison gained no diagnostics (the existing
11 errors and 322 warnings remain). Both lobby and game Rojo builds pass. **Not playtested or visually reviewed in Studio.**

### Review (2026-11-06): what was cut

- `runSummary.Set` returns at once when the new summary draws the same (`isSameSummary`): every lobby update (a
  teammate readying) rebuilt it and re-fitted all its text.
- The card works out its colours (`pixelSlab.FromColor`, the glow, the badge) only when its colour changes; a hover
  goes through `paintHover` (outline and the switch's light) instead of a full repaint; the ticket's parts are listed
  once and the fade is written only when it changes.
- The summary's frame writes are guarded (row flashes, row slides, the plate's sting, scale, shake, outline, flash):
  a row at rest writes nothing. A layout resets what it overwrote (`DrawnSlide`, `drawnShake`) so the next frame
  reapplies a slide or shake in flight; a new flash resets `DrawnFlash` so its colour is written.
- `pixelSlab.TextUnits(text, textUnits)` is the kit's one text-width estimate (the same advance `FitWidth` uses); the
  five copies of `chars * 0.72 * size` in the options components use it.
- Left as is: each card's `settingsSwitch` runs its own `pixelMotion` stepper while it moves. Driving it from the
  page's clock would mean changing the Settings component; it costs nothing at rest.

### Round 3 (2026-11-06): one copy of the shop's looks, and tidier timing

- `Components/shopLook` holds what the shop, the receipt and the daily rewards each kept a copy of: the box and kind
  palettes, the type labels, the tools drawn as glyphs, `Image`, `WithCommas`, and `Rewards` (what a bundle gives, in the
  shop's order). ShopUI's chips and the receipt's lines are both built from `Rewards`, so they cannot drift apart. The
  donate heart is `DonationsCore.HeartImage`.
- CONTINUE's time is kept outside the event list (`buttonAt`), so a hurry runs every event and only brings it forward.
  The roll's length is one function used by both the schedule and the line.
- `ticketsCounter.Extend` restarts a hold's deadline; the receipt calls it while it waits for Roblox's dialog (it used
  to call Hold and Release back to back).
- Not changed, on purpose: putting the idle bob on a slow timer would save nothing. While CONTINUE is up the idle ray
  glow keeps the clock running (lightRays paints at 15 fps), and the bob only writes when its pixel changes.

### Round 5 (2026-11-06): the cleanup pass

Asked: "is this the most optimized and readable it can be?" It was not; this pass changes no look or timing except the
wave's step rate.

- **`Components/dialogueLetters`** is the typewriter, lifted out of the card (as SpecialDelivery keeps its typewriter
  apart): measuring, reading, the wrap, the pop, the fall, the wave. It also owns the one letter count (`Letters`, a
  `<br/>` is a letter) and the punctuation pace (`Hold`), which `DialogueController` and the bench now share instead of
  each keeping a copy. `dialogueCard` is the card only (813 lines, from ~1,300).
- **The wave runs on its own `task.delay` chain at 12 steps a second** (it moves in whole units, so it needs no more)
  and stops once no highlighted letter is up, so the card's clock sleeps between moments again, as the idle rule asks.
- **The pointer follows on events**: in a layer it is re-placed on the target's `AbsolutePosition` / `AbsoluteSize`,
  `Visible` on it and every ancestor up to the layer, its list's window and the layer's position. Nothing is read per
  frame but its own animation.
- **Small ones**: a letter's `IsMoving` flag replaces a `table.find` per reveal; `Measure` yields on the measurements'
  completion instead of polling a frame at a time; the loading-screen wait listens for the attribute instead of polling.
- **`DialogueController.Talk`** reads as its steps: `waitForLoadingScreen`, `UI.Present`, `typeLine`, `offerNext`, with
  one `listenForPress` for both presses. The NEXT press is handlers only; the old per-frame `Heartbeat:Wait` loop on a
  spawned thread is gone. `parseCommands` counts a `<br/>` as a letter, like the card.

Checked: StyLua, Selene (clean on the eight files), `lune` compile of each, both Rojo builds; the letter split, word
ends, highlighted words, punctuation holds and `<speed>` command positions run in `lune` on the shared code. **Not
playtested.**

## Last Wave: the leaderboards (`leaderboardScreen`, `leaderboardRow`, `leaderboardFilter`, `donateScreen`, built 2026-11-06, linted, not playtested)

Asked for: the Leaderboards page in the pixel style, "the most satisfying and juiciest it can be", without the MODE
filter (Survivors is the only mode; the wrapper sends mode 1), and a FRIENDS filter that works. The old layout is kept:
the board carousel top centre, the filters in a column on the left, the board on the right, BACK left, DONATE centre
(Donator board only) and the reset clock right along the bottom. `LeaderboardUI` went from 2,509 lines of Vide derives to
a wrapper that feeds a drawing, like the Codex and Quests.

| Piece | Where | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Drawing | `Lobby/.../MenuUI/Components/leaderboardScreen` | Sizes from its own box (the lobby rhythm: 6 units from edges and between blocks). Pools one `leaderboardRow` per place, the pinned row, the filters and the menu hosts |
| Row | `.../Components/leaderboardRow` | Rank badge (gold, silver, bronze for the podium, sheen every 3.4 s), up to five overlapping portraits (rbxthumb), name over details with the weapon and trait icons first, value right. The player's own row is gold. A placeholder state (`SetSkeleton`) with three shimmering bars |
| Filter | `.../Components/leaderboardFilter` | Name over a slab with the value and a chevron; gold and the chevron up while its menu is open; a picked value pops in with a flash |
| Donate | `.../Components/donateScreen` | Gold modal: beating hearts beside DONATE (a lub-dub every 1.4 s), six tier tiles (Green, Blue, Magenta, Red, Orange, Gold), each with a heart and a `priceButton` Robux face. Replaces the old `ShopProductsGridUI` popup (which nothing uses now) |
| Wrapper | `MenuUI/LeaderboardUI` | Filters (one `dropdown` each, rows 12 units; PLAYERS, REVIVES and MODDED open upward), fetching (debounced 0.6 s, a 10 s give-up that offers RETRY), the run card (`runView`, unchanged), pad bindings |
| Bench | `Lobby/.../Stories/Leaderboard` | Board, rows, the player's place, own best off the board, each empty state, reload, next board, find me, donate |

What it does, and why:
- **A board loads as placeholders, not "LOADING..."**: up to ten rows of three bars, a wave of transparency running down
  them in four steps (writes only on a step). When the board arrives the rows deal in on the deal spring, sliding in from
  the side the carousel moved toward (12 units), a soft tick per landing for the first eight, rising in pitch.
- **The podium lands with a badge pop and a ring in its medal colour; the player's own row lands with a flash, a +6%
  thump, rings and gold sparks and an `ObjectPick`.** Only the player's row is voiced: filters change often (UI.md recipe
  item 12, frequent actions never move the screen).
- **The player's row is pinned under the board** on a band of the well's colour whenever it is out of view, or when they
  are not on the board (then it shows their own best for this board, rank "-"). Pressing it (or the pad's X) scrolls the
  list to their row on a critically damped spring and strikes it there; off the board, it opens their own run card. The
  list's canvas has the band's height of extra room, so the last row can be scrolled clear of it.
- **Empty boards say why** and offer the next step: Friends "NO FRIENDS ON THIS BOARD YET" with INVITE FRIENDS (the
  platform invite, now `GlobalClient/Utils/promptGameInvite`, shared with the invite modal), Personal "FINISH A RUN TO SET
  ONE", a board that never answered RETRY.
- **Column titles** (#, PLAYER, and the board's value: TIME, OVERTIME, DAMAGE, KILLS, DONATED) over a one-unit line, and
  the filters panel has a matching FILTERS title, so the two panels start their contents level.
- Donator rows show the tier the total has reached (PATRON, LEGEND...) where the run rows show their details.

The friends board, and why it "did not work great": the backend's `/api/board` never read the `friends=` parameter the
game sent (it only scopes Friends for a signed-in web session), so FRIENDS showed the global top 50. And the friend
list came from the client. Now the server reads it (`Player:GetFriendsWhoPlayedAsync`, falling back to the first pages
of `Players:GetFriendsAsync`, at most 200, cached for the session, re-read after 10 minutes, retried after 60 s on a
failure) and **puts the player on the board with their friends**, so a player always sees where they stand. The
backend honours `friends=` only on the game's bearer token (`BackendService.GetBoard` signs the request when it has
one) and binds the ids as one JSON parameter (`json_each`), since D1 allows 100 bound parameters. The Blink event lost
its `f64[]`. **The backend must be deployed** for the friends board to scope; before that it shows the global board,
as it always did.

Pad: L2 / R2 walk the boards, Y opens DONATE (Donator), X finds the player's row, B goes back. Filters walk up and down;
right from a filter goes to the board, left from the board to the filters; up from the top of either reaches the
carousel through `selectionLinks.AttachHeader` (skipped while a menu is open). A row going away under the pad (a reload
turns them to placeholders) moves the pad to the first filter.

Checked: StyLua, Selene (clean on every changed file), the `lune` compile of each, both Rojo builds, Blink regenerated
(only `FetchFriendsLeaderboard` changed). Not opened in Studio, the bench not run, the backend change type-checked only.
**Not playtested.**

## Last Wave: Stardust packs, and the readouts that open the shop (2026-11-07, linted, not playtested)

Asked for: Stardust packs in the shop "just like the tickets bundles", the lobby's tickets opening the shop's BUNDLES tab
and **smoothly** scrolling down to the ticket packs, the constellation's two points doing the same for the Stardust
packs, "the most satisfying and juicier it can be", the developer products made through the API with the packs' own
pictures as their icons.

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Packs: 1,500 / 4,500 / 12,000 / 30,000 / 75,000 Stardust at 79 / 199 / 449 / 899 / 1,799 R$ (the ticket ladder at 1.5x, same +19% to +119% stickers) | `ShopCore.STARDUST_PACKS`, `STARDUST_ROBUX_RATE` (one level = 1,000, so the top pack is 75 levels: an ascension and a half) |
| Grant: `Claimed` kind 6 (`CLAIM_STARDUST_PACK`, amount = the Stardust) before `AddSkillTreeXP`, never through a run's multipliers | `ShopService` (end of file), `ShopController.PromptStardustPack` (key `Stardust:N`) |
| Card: `DustStack` 1 to 5, one big sparkle (two cells a texel) and smaller ones round it, on a **Magenta** card with magenta rays (blue rays hid the dust too) (the user: on Blue the dust was invisible; gold under orange tickets is the pattern) | `shopCard` (`DUST_SPEC`, `placeDust`); `Assets/Shop/build.py` exports the same spec as the product icons |
| Section STARDUST last on BUNDLES; a policy-restricted player sees BUNDLES with only this section (Stardust buys nothing random) | `ShopUI` (`stardustSection`, `isBundlesHidden`) |
| Receipt: STARDUST, EXTRA STARDUST, the CONSTELLATION LEVELS it rolls in (from the tree read in the grant's handler, before the bank), ASCENSION READY when it crosses the 50-level toll, a LEVEL UP! ribbon | `PurchaseUI.stardustReceipt` |
| Opening onto a section: `ShopUI.Appear("Bundles", nil, ShopCore.SECTION_*)` | `LobbyUI.openShopOnto` |
| The glide, its ticks and the arrival | `shopScreen.FocusSection` |
| Products | `tools/shop/create_packs.py` (idempotent by name, ids checkpointed in `tools/shop/icons.json`) |

**The open, beat by beat.** A press on the tickets (or a point slab) lifts, swells 6-7%, squeezes 8-9% while held and
bounces on release (`ClickHud`); the shop opens on BUNDLES; after 0.3 s (the panel's grow) the cards glide down on an
ease in-out cubic, 0.34 s plus 0.22 s per well's height travelled, capped at 0.85 s (worked out in `lune`), with a
`HoverHud` tick each time a row passes the top, climbing 0.06 a tick, never closer than 40 ms; on arrival the section
title flashes white back to gold over 0.6 s and punches 6% on a bouncy spring (`RewardBanked` 1.2), then each card of
the section beckons in turn 0.09 s apart (the claim's beckon, now `Beckon(delay, pitch, true)` for any card: flash,
ray flare, thump, picture jump, ring, its price strikes, `ChestItemCycle` climbing). Already there: no glide, straight
to the arrival. A wheel or a touch during the wait or the glide hands the scroll back at once. The pad's first focus is
the section's first card, and `ensureVisible` stands aside while the glide owns the scroll.

**Decisions to carry:**
- **No "+" badge on the readouts.** One was built (a green cross on the wallet's and each point slab's corner, so a
  touch player could tell they are buttons) and the user rejected it on sight; the component was deleted.
- The Stardust receipt card is Magenta with the dust in Blue (`TReceipt.GlyphPalette`), matching the shop card.
- A restricted player's tickets open **DEALS** (no ticket packs to show them).
- The Stardust bought counts toward lifetime `TotalStardustEarned`, as Robux tickets count toward the tickets' total.
- The wallet is deaf (no hover, no press) while a modal it is raised over is up (`IsPressable`).

**Products** (production universe `8896795837`, made 2026-11-07 with `ROBLOX_OPEN_CLOUD_KEY`, read back: names, prices,
for sale, no regional or managed pricing, icons attached): `3729145303`, `3729145315`, `3729145332`, `3729145347`,
`3729145361`. The test universe has none, like the ticket packs.

**Checked:** StyLua (whole tree), Selene (no finding in any changed file; the tree's 11 errors are the generated Meta
network's `Value` quirk and TopbarPlus), the `lune` compile of every changed file, both Rojo builds, the prices, stickers,
level wording, receipt level maths (toll crossing, cap) and glide timing in `lune`, the pack art in a PNG beside the
ticket packs'. Benches: `Stories/Shop` ("Do: open onto TICKETS / STARDUST", the Stardust shelf), `Stories/Purchase`
("Stardust pack (1799)"), `Stories/SkillTree` and `Stories/Tickets` (the press feel). **Not opened on the
bench, not played, no purchase made, not tried with a pad or touch.** First to judge: the glide's speed and ticks, the

## Last Wave: the lobby's boost rack (`lobbyScreen`, 2026-11-08, linted, not playtested)

Asked for: a new counter for the run boosts (the lobby only counted the Stardust potion, as a line of words under the
party bonus), with each boost switchable on and off, "the most satisfying and juicier it can be". The potion line is
gone; every boost and potion held is a tile on a rack at the top left, mirroring the promo and FREE stub at the top right.

- One tile per boost held, in the shop's `Order`, the promo's size (24 units x the bottom row's fit `k`), 5 units apart.

  (grey when off), and the boost's own line, or "Saved for later" when off. A touch has no hover, so a toggle shows it
  for 2.5 s. It deals in line by line; switching flashes and thumps the title.

## Last Wave: what a quest puts away, and what it refuses (`questStow`, 2026-11-08, linted, not playtested)

Asked for: when a quest (or a challenge) starts, nothing may stay open without its rewards and protections, so the open
level-up / reward closes with an animation and comes back after the quest, and an opened chest closes and refunds its
souls (round 2: it does NOT reopen on its item later); the players who had something open are told so; and while it runs, chests and altars say no (a chest refunds every soul paid into it, an
altar keeps its souls and wakes after the quest). "The most satisfying and juicier it can be."

- **Server.** `RewardsService.SetQuestBlocked(true)` puts each unpicked choice back at the front of its player's queue
  (`IsResumed`: no second heal, no second level-up analytics) and fires `Rewards.MomentRetracted`; a pick already in
  flight finishes. `QuestsService.OnBlockChanged` (fired after RewardsService is told) drives `ChestServer`, which
  shuts every opened chest (`Props.ChestClosed`): the item is gone, the opener gets back what it cost
  (`computeRefundForOpener`, so their later chests' costs are corrected as for a grabbed one) and the chest is closed
  again, rolled anew by whoever opens it after the quest; and `AltarServer`, which holds a filled altar and runs the
  whole activation (Luck, Difficulty, boss, augment) when the last quest ends. One altar waits at a time: each altar's
  cost counts the activations before it. A refusal is `Props.QuestRefused`, sent before the refund's `PropSoulsChanged`.
- **The put-away** (`UI/Components/questStow`, fed by `QuestsController`): each card's rect (`GetCardShots` on both
  choice screens) folds as a white sheet down into a parcel (a 16-unit Slab in the card's
  rarity / kind palette with its icon), pops in with sparks thrown from outside it, is thrown sideways against drag,
  hangs, and is pulled on a boomerang cubic into the red warning ribbon, shrinking and going white. Landings are ranked
  before the throw with the gaps closing (simulated at 1080p: 0.92, 1.15, 1.32 s; every pull 0.33 s or more), each one
  strikes the ribbon (`QuestLockWarningUI.Pulse`: white flash, a jolt, +5% / +9% thump on the last, gold side sparks)
  with a LockChest clunk and a rising tick. The cards pop away under their parcels as on any close. A shut chest's card
  leaves with its item, the lid slams (the Close track) and the chest hops; its prompt, cost and minimap mark come back.
- **The notice**: one gold banner per quest start, coalesced in the frame, only for players who had something open:
  `SAVED FOR LATER` "A quest started! You get your {level-up and reward} back when it ends[, and your chest gave its
  souls back]", or `SOULS REFUNDED` when it was only a chest.
- **The no** (`propPrompt.Refuse`): a red cross stamps down over the Slab, the bezel flushes red and fades, the prompt
  shakes its head three times in 0.6 s, red side sparks, BuyRefuse + a low LockChest; a chest's refund throws the souls
  from outside the Slab's sides into the count, which rolls back up. One red `AFTER THE QUEST` banner says why and is
  struck again on a retry instead of stacking.
- The client banks a level for a retracted level-up it already counted (`BankedLevelUps`), so the reopened one does not
  level the bar twice.

Benches: `Stories/Quests` ("Do: quest takes a level-up hand"; start a quest first) and
`Stories/Interactable` ("Quest running"). Checked: StyLua, Selene, `lune` compile, the landing timings simulated, every
particle spawn against the checklist. **Not opened on the bench, not played.** First to judge: whether the parcels read
as "kept" rather than "lost" (the cards still pop with their rarity puff under them), and the head-shake's size on a
far billboard.

## Last Wave: the style meter (`styleMeter`, `StyleUI`, built 2026-11-12, played once by the user)

A DMC / ULTRAKILL-style meter for the run: a rank Slab and a feed of loud words for the moments the player **chose**.
The user's brief: beside the player, not in a corner ("the current streak is far from the eyes"), a setting to fade it
out completely, loud flavour words ("plain labels sounds boring"), and the most satisfying and juiciest it can be.

| Piece | Owner | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rules | `Survivors/Shared/Core/StyleCore` | Moves (label, palette, points, per-unit points, headline flag, cooldown), ranks D DEADLY to SSS LAST WAVE with a drain per rank, freshness, hit loss. Both sides read it |
| Scoring | `StyleService` (server, a leaf) | Gauge, drain on the entity clock, freshness heat, the run's total (`GetTotal`, for the F-to-S end grade still to build). Batches a frame's awards per move into one owner-only `StyleAwarded`, hits into `StyleHurt` |
| Hooks | `EnemiesService` `styleKills` beside `updateStreak` (same ability test), its lifesteal and nuke / charm / frost sweeps; `DropsService` grabs; `CharacterService` dodges, enemy hits, ally revives | Only chosen moments: plain auto-attack kills, regen, Speed / Jump / Magnet / Health pickups earn nothing |
| Drawing | `Components/styleMeter` | The rank Slab (STYLE tab, letter panel, word, gauge bar) and up to five feed lines from a fixed pool of six |
| Screen | `StyleUI` | The meter's ScreenGui, its near edge up to 120 units from the screen's centre on its side, tab top at 0.25 of the height; 104 units wide. A second full-screen ScreenGui for the screen hits (`rarityImpact` bands in the rank's colour, SSS confetti). The opacity and the side |
| Wiring | `RewardsController` | Mounts it at module level, owns both Blink listeners, follows `StyleMeterOpacity` and `StyleMeterOnRight`, kicks the camera through `CameraController.Jolt`, resets on restart. Not `StatsController`: CameraController's requires already reach StatsController, so it could not take the jolt |

**Juice, as built.** A new line stamps in (its word at 1.7x, 2x for a headline, springing to rest at 3.6 Hz, damping
0.6), flashes white to its colour, slides in from the player's side (-12 units) and wipes its backing across; points
roll up from 0. The same move again merges (count punch, flash, points roll, life reset): the reference's "SICK! x3".
Headline moves (OVERKILL, MASSACRE, SLAYER!, CLOSE CALL, KABOOM, MIND GAMES, ICE COLD, TIME OUT, INVINCIBLE, SAVIOR)
use a bigger word, throw sparks off the line's right edge and thump the rank Slab. A stale move (freshness step 4+)
greys. A rank up slams the letter (2.4x, 3x for SSS), flashes the Slab in the new rank's palette, throws rings and side
sparks, lands a win-box-style screen hit of the matching rarity (D Common to SSS Divine) in the rank's colour, kicks
the camera (a quarter strength at D, full at SSS: Kick 4, Shake 1.5, 0.3 s) and plays the meter's own stinger a step
higher per rank; SSS adds 70 confetti. A rank down sinks the letter; a hit flashes red and shakes. The bar breathes red
under 15% of the rank. SSS's letter cycles hue at the ambient step rate. Lines leave by fading, sliding away and
`LeaveScale`; the Slab pops away with a puff.

**Numbers going up (2026-11-12, "a lot more dopaminic").** Under the word, the run's style score (gold, with commas)
rolls toward its total. Every award throws its "+points" out of its line: a pop, then an ease-in pull (u²) on a sine
arc of 12 units into the score, white turning gold; it lands with a punch, the score lighting white and settling back to gold, and a
`StyleScore` tick climbing through `pitchChain`. A repeat inside 0.12 s adds to the number in the air instead of throwing another; with
all ten in the air the oldest lands early, so no points are lost. Each award beats the letter. From S the Slab sheds
embers (5 / 9 / 16 a second at S / SS / SSS); from SS the letter trembles a unit on its own ambient gate.

**Decisions to keep.**

- **Words of 10 characters or fewer.** At 104 units a line holds about 10 characters at headline size beside a count
  and points; longer words were fitted down and read SMALLER than the ordinary ones ("OBLITERATED", "SUPERCHARGED",
  "GIANT SLAYER", "UNTOUCHABLE", "BLOODTHIRSTY", "DEEP FREEZE", "FREEZE FRAME" were renamed for that).
- **A stamp's damping is 0.6.** At 0.42 the headline stamp sank 30% under rest and read as a wobble.
- **The word draws over its count and points** (ZIndex 14 against 13): a stamping word swells across them.
- **Every line moves down for a new one, the leaving ones too**, and gaps close only once a leaving line is gone, so a
  pushed line never lands on one still fading.
- **The opacity is a CanvasGroup only between 0 and 100%.** At 100% the meter sits in a plain Frame; at 0 both
  ScreenGuis are off and `RewardsController` drops the server's updates. The group carries 30 units of margin because
  it clips the sparks.
- **Left of the character by default, right as a setting** (Visuals, "Style Meter On Right", `StyleMeterOnRight`).
  The user's call after the first version touched the character. The camera holds the character LEFT of the screen's
  centre, its body reaching about 87 units out at the closest zoom (playtest screenshot, 2026-11-12), so a fixed
  offset that clears it on the right does not on the left. The near edge aims for 120 units off the centre and the
  meter never enters the screen's outer strip on its side: 100 units on the left (the teammate column), 118 on the
  right (the objective panel reaches about 113 units in). At 1920x1080 the left meter spans x 300 to 612, about 88 px
  clear of the character; the right one ends at x 1566. On a narrow screen it gives up offset, not the strip. Lines
  arrive from the player's side and leave away from it, whichever side it is on.
- **Nothing in the feed reaches the backing's slant.** A line's points end `SlantSteps + LinePadUnits` units from its
  right end: placed at the plain pad they sat over the slant's short columns and read as touching the edge (the user
  caught it). The word column keeps 4 units clear each side, so a long score shrinks before it reaches the Slab.
- **Harder difficulties climb slower.** Every style point is multiplied by the difficulty's `StyleGain`
  (DifficultyCore, config-tunable): Easy 1.25, Normal 1.12, Hard 1 (StyleCore's tuning baseline), Infernal 0.88,
  Nightmare 0.78, Psychopath 0.7. GameplayService hands it to `StyleService.SetDifficulty` when the run starts
  (StyleService cannot require GameplayService: GameplayService reaches it through EnemiesService). The user's ask;
  the saturating kill units already stop denser waves from paying more.
- **Its own sounds, not the win box's** (Sounds.md, "Style meter"). The first version played the chest landings and
  chords per rank; the user: that "makes the actual things that come out of the chest have less value". The screen
  hit borrows the rarity look only.
- **Embers are born above the meter and only rise** ("Particles: the checklist"). The first ones were born inside the
  Slab's top edge as blinking (`isSteady = false`) pieces and rose through the light STYLE tab: the user saw them
  flicker. They now start 2 units above the tab's top as drawn this frame (a thump swells the body about its middle),
  fade in and out smoothly and live 0.6 to 0.9 s; a `lune` run of the strongest thump (2.4) against the slowest ember
  keeps it at least 1.4 units above the tab. The score landing's gold puff was born in the well and floated up
  through the bezel, so it became a white flash of the score itself.
- **Draw what changed, not every frame.** The drain keeps the meter's clock awake for as long as a rank shows, so the
  Slab redraws only on a frame where a spring, flash, sheen, shake, warning breath, tremble or the leave moved (or a
  rank or layout marked it dirty), and a feed line only while its springs move or it leaves. Its wipe and fade are
  written only when they change, its colours only while it flashes.
- **The score's punch spring is declared before the list that steps it.** It was declared after, so the list held nil
  and the score never punched. A spring missing from a step list fails silently.
- The old streak meter stays where it was: its souls bonus belongs with the souls chip. The feed's WRECKED line is the
  ability-kill count beside the player.

Bench: `Stories/Style` (Backdrop, Time scale, Auto demo, a 20 s fight on a loop, Opacity, Side, and a "Do:" flip for
every move, two hit sizes and a reset; the screen hits draw in the widget). It runs StyleCore's scoring itself, so freshness, drain and ranks behave as in a run.

### Seeing a story offline with `rur-native` (rur 0.8.0, worked 2026-11-20)

From rur 0.3.1 `rur-native` mounts the Rojo project itself. Name the file with `--rojo`: there are two project files
in the root, so it will not pick one. Run it from the repo root with `RUR_ROBLOX_CONTENT` set to Vinegar's content
folder (rur does not read `ROR_ROBLOX_CONTENT`):

`rur-native render --headless --offline --rojo game.project.json --story src/Survivors/Client/UI/Stories/Style.story.luau --viewport 1920x1080 --scale 1 --time 3.3 --dir <dir>`

The output folder is `--dir`, not `--out`. It prints the services it mounted first. The symlink root and the empty
placeholder folders that 0.1.0 needed are gone. If a story indexes something only Studio holds, it fails with "X is
not a valid member", and that still needs a placeholder.

`--time` runs the story's own clock to that moment (about 0.2 s a render), so a loop over times gives a video
(`ffmpeg -framerate 30 -i %05d.png`). Fonts fall back from Silkscreen and group images do not load, so judge layout,
sizes, overlaps and motion there, not the look of the letters.

Checked: StyLua, Selene (no new findings), `lune` compile of every changed module, both Rojo builds, the Blink ids
(242 of 256), the bench rendered offline frame by frame (first version). The 2026-11-12 user round played it on Hard
and Infernal (placement, padding, too-easy SSS, chest sounds); the fixes after it are linted and built only.

## Last Wave: the pixel keycaps (`Assets/ui/keys/authorkeys.py`, 2026-11-16, in game as `KeyImages`)

The Kenney key images (white caps, the letter a hole, `KeyImages.luau`) are being replaced: the user disliked that
they need a backdrop and that they are off-style. Every key, button and stick is authored instead, as two layers of
colour INDICES so the UI can push it: **body** (ink outline, the lip under the face, the dark hole the face sinks into)
and **cap** (face, bevels, legend). A press moves the cap `Press` texels into the lip and lerps it to a lit palette; a
mouse or a d-pad moves only its button or arm (`Part`). The picker page is a scratchpad build of
`authorkeys.py preview` poured into `Assets/ui/keys/keybench.template.html` (artifact R8zin2AKmbPoDHKjVJNkaM), pressed by the real keyboard, mouse and pad.

**Picked:** the **Chunky Square** look: Chunky (bevelled all round, two-texel lip, legend with a shadow) with hard
corners and letter caps 15 x 15, square like the old corner-hint caps; pad shapes stay Chunky's. It is the one the game
ships; Chunky and Chunky Light (the same cap in pale plastic) stays on the bench. Lost: Slab (today's corner-hint cap), Ivory,
Night. The push look is **Full** (Thump + Burst over Sink; the bench page's JS is its reference).

### What the rounds taught

1. **Centre inside the bevels, not on the shape.** Lit and shaded edges are not face: a legend centred on the whole
   face sat against one of them. Measure the plain face between the bevels and keep one plain texel round every
   legend texel (`is_clear`); a shadow only has to land on plain face.
2. **Exact centring is a parity rule.** A legend centres only when its width and the clear width share a parity, and
   the same for height. A face bevelled on four sides has the same parity both ways, so a 4-wide letter can never
   centre in a circle. Stretching the circle a row to make it fit was rejected: **circles stay round**.
3. **One font, one width: `FONT5`.** Silkscreen's letters are 1, 3, 4 and 5 texels wide, so "1", "L" and "M" keys
   came out three sizes. Every letter and digit is now 5 x 5 (words use it too, a texel apart); symbols are 5 wide.
4. **A family looks alike.** All face buttons (Xbox and PlayStation, View and Menu) are one 11 circle, sticks one 13
   with one ring on the face's centre (not the legend's), the d-pad's four arrows one size (arm = 7 plain texels plus
   its bevels), shoulder pairs one size. A legend that does not fit its family's size is an error, never a bigger
   button: the fit search once quietly grew some face buttons to 13.
5. **Draw circles by row widths, by eye** (`CIRCLES`). A computed circle reads as an octagon once outlined; 11 is
   `3 7 9 9 11 11 11 9 9 7 3`. A computed ellipse comes out pointed.
6. **Centre a shape on its visual middle.** The PlayStation triangle is four rows over a blank one, so it sits half a
   texel high (its middle is a third of the way up). No single apex pixel on top.
7. **The light twin is the same drawing**: identical geometry and shadows, only `Colors` differ (dark legend over a
   soft shade, coloured legends on pad buttons).

8. **Real proportions on a composite.** The controller guide (`authorpad.py`) was judged against photos: the DualSense
   d-pad is as big as the face cluster opposite, sticks are big. A check (`check()`) refuses any part that leaves the
   shell or comes within a ring and a texel of another, seats and rings counted.
9. **Shapes from the hardware.** The DualSense d-pad keys are rounded outside and pointed inside (square ends read as
   blocks); the mouse wheel is one texel (three read as a fourth button).

### In game

Every picture is uploaded twice, idle and held (cap down `Press`, lit), at 8 px a texel, and `KeyImages.luau` is
generated (`authorkeys.py luau`; README in `Assets/ui/keys`). Every existing caller got the new art through the same
names. The tutorial shows the controller guide (`controllerGuide`, right edge) to a pad player at each ability prompt
and at the altar, swapping to the held picture while the button is down.

**The Full push in game is `pixelKey`** (`src/Global/Client/UI/Components`). Pixel-by-pixel effects (the legend landing
late, the sheen, the dithered ring) cannot come from two pictures, so `push_atlas` splits each key into layers (body,
cap idle and lit, a white shine mask, legend idle and lit, three ring steps), packs the distinct ones into one atlas at
2 px a texel, and `KeyImages.GetPush` hands them out. Stacked ImageLabels then play the bench's numbers: the lit layer's
transparency steps in quarters (that IS the glow lerp, over the same silhouette), the shine sits under the legend so a
flash or sheen never covers it, the sheen is a UIGradient band, sparks and dust are texel Frames. The corner hints
(`KeyBindsUI`) draw pixelKeys at 2 px a texel on keyboard and pad; a picture taller than the 15-texel row (a d-pad
is 23, a stick 17) drops to the biggest whole unit that fits instead of spilling over its neighbours, never a
fractional scale. `keyHint` callers still show the static pictures.

## Kill All The Monsters: a gun drawn as its model, and the hotbar's one slot (`GunPicture`, `Hotbar`, 2026-11-21, rendered in rur, not playtested)

The hotbar slot and the weapon card draw the gun's own model over a black copy of it as its shadow, instead of a white
glyph. What the round cost:

- **Fit the leaned picture, not the flat one.** A picture fitted to the gun lying flat and then turned by `Rotation`
  is wrong for any gun, and badly for one as tall as it is long: the pistol (1.17 : 1) came out 86 px tall in a 96 px
  slot and 10 px left of centre. Roll the camera to the lean and fit the leaned bounds (`GunPicture.stand`); keep
  `Rotation` for the gestures on top.
- **The shadow is part of what is centred.** A 6 px drop left every gun 2 to 5 px low. The fit takes the drop into
  the height and centres the gun and its shadow together.
- **Measure placement from the model files.** `lune` reads `Assets/models/Guns`, and the picture's maths runs on the
  parts' boxes: size in the slot and the four gaps for every gun, before any Studio round.
- **One fit, two copies.** The shadow has to be a second ViewportFrame; the camera is worked out once and given to
  both.
- **Derive a gesture's clock.** `state.Now` ticks for every coin that lands. A gesture read straight off it re-ran
  every binding in the slot on those frames; behind a `derive` it holds one value at rest and nothing downstream runs.
- **Do not build what cannot show.** Four slots nothing can sit in were a card, two springs and a dozen bindings
  each. The row is the gun's slot until a second thing can be carried; placing several is then a rank in a centred
  row and a spring on its x.
- **rur draws nothing for a Plastic part offline** (the viewport worker cannot find the Plastic atlas, and the error
  is only in `manifest.json`). Bench stand-ins are SmoothPlastic.

## Kill All The Monsters: a bought Gold pack on the HUD (`Hotbar`, `Upgrades`, 2026-11-21, rendered in rur, not playtested)

The stamp over the money block, the block's strike and the bought slab's flash (VFX.md 38 has the world's half; the
beats are in `Assets/effects/items/README.md`).

- **The receiver was already right.** The money block's pulse is restamped by every rise of the counter, so thirty
  landings a second hold it swollen instead of kicking it (5j's smoothed pressure, for free). The pack adds one strike
  on the last landing and nothing per coin.
- **The amount is said once, where it lands.** "+$1,000" is stamped over the block the frame the coins leave the
  buyer, never faded in (its first frame is its white one), and drops INTO the plate on the last coin. No banner: the
  squad's banner is for what changes the squad's run.
- **A piece timed to a sound reads the sound's clock from its owner.** The strike's time is `CoinFlight.Shower.LAST`,
  the same constant the coins land by and the cue was baked to, not a second number in the HUD.
- **A swelling button is anchored at its centre first.** The pack slabs were placed by their corner; they are placed
  by their centre now, so the bought one grows from its middle.
- **The show's length keeps the clock running.** `stamp` only holds `Now` for 1.6 s; a longer gesture raises
  `motionUntil` itself (`Hotbar.GOLD_PACK_SECONDS`).
